x: The manual has one chapter for each module of the program, in the order the modules appear in the menu, and one section for each page. Each page section tells you what the page is for, where to find it, what every box means, how to do each task step by step, what the program records in the books, and the messages you may meet. Opening the manual from the program Every page has a Help button with a question-mark icon at the right end of its title bar. It opens this manual at the section for that page. The whole manual is also in the user menu: click your name at the top right of the screen, then User's Manual . The log-in page has a User's Manual link, so you can read the manual before you log in. How the manual is written Words you see on the screen are in bold, exactly as the program shows them: Save & New , Customer:Job , Receive Payments . A menu path such as Customers > Create Invoices means: click Customers in the menu on the left, then click Create Invoices . Boxes marked Note , Tip , Important and Example give extra information, shortcuts, warnings and worked examples. The construction chapter uses the sample contractor, Sample Builders & Development Corp., and its projects. The accounting chapters (the modules under Accounting in the menu) describe each page with examples of a trading business, such as the customer ABC Trading Corp. and the item LAP-001 Laptop; the pages work the same way for a contractor, with projects as classes. Amounts are in pesos, for example ₱12,500.00. What you see depends on the access your role gives you (see "Access: what you can open and do" later in this chapter). Note If the manual describes a button or a menu entry that you do not see, your role does not allow that action. Ask your administrator if you need it.

You need: A computer, tablet or phone with a current web browser, such as Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. The address of your company's GSMaRT Construction System, for example http://server/accounting-system/ . Your administrator gives it to you. Save it as a bookmark. A username and a password. Your administrator creates your account in System Administration > User Accounts . If your company works with a Company Code, you can also create your own account from the log-in page and wait for approval (see Your Company: Company Owner and Employees ).

The log-in page is the first page you see. It shows the program's name and, under it, the name of your company. Step by step: log in Open the address of GSMaRT Construction System in your browser. Type your Username . Type your Password . The letters are hidden as you type. Click Log in , or press Enter. The Home page opens (see Home Dashboard ). If you log in with a temporary password, or your password has expired, the Change password page opens first (see "Your password" below). Right after you log in you may also see: A pop-up headed Maintenance due that lists the preventive maintenance tasks that are due, if you may open Preventive Maintenance. Click Later to close it, or Open Preventive Maintenance to deal with them. It comes back after each log-in, when a new day starts, and when the list of due tasks changes. A blue message saying that a memorized transaction was entered automatically, for example Memorized transaction "Office rent" was entered automatically for 09/27/2026. Memorized transactions set to be entered automatically are recorded on their due date, the first time anyone opens the program that day. Note As the log-in page says, every log-in, every failed attempt and every action is recorded in the audit trail, with the user's name, the time and the computer's network address. Messages on the log-in page Message What to do Invalid username or password. Check the spelling and that Caps Lock is off, then try again. Invalid username or password. 3 attempt(s) left before the account is locked. The password was wrong. Type carefully: the account locks after the last attempt. Too many failed attempts. The account is now locked. Ask an administrator to unlock your account. This account is locked. Only an administrator can unlock it. Ask an administrator to unlock your account in User Accounts. This account is inactive. Contact your administrator. Your account was switched off. Ask your administrator. Your registration is waiting for approval by your Company Owner. You can log in once it is approved. You joined with the Company Code. Wait for the Company Owner to approve you. Your registration was not approved. Please contact your Company Owner. Your request to join was rejected. Speak to the Company Owner. Your company's access is currently suspended. Please contact your Company Owner. The whole company was switched off on the platform. Too many failed log-in attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again. Too many unknown usernames were tried from your computer. Wait 15 minutes. You were logged out after a period of inactivity. Your session timed out. Log in again. You have been logged out. You used Log out . When the program runs several companies When several companies are kept in GSMaRT Construction System, the log-in page says Log in to your company instead of showing a company name. You still type only your own username and password: the program finds your company from your username, and you can never reach another company's records. A New employee? Join your company with its Company Code link appears under the form; it is explained in Your Company: Company Owner and Employees . The Super Admin, who manages the companies, logs in on the same page and lands on the platform pages (see Super Admin: Managing Several Companies ).

Your password protects your work and your name in the audit trail. Never tell it to anyone, and never let another person work under your log-in: every entry you save carries your name. Password rules Your administrator sets the rules in Company, Security & Closing Date . The Change password page always shows the rules in force. As delivered, a password must have: at least 8 characters, upper-case and lower-case letters, a number, a symbol, such as @ # ! or %, and it must not contain your username. As delivered, a password expires after 90 days, and a new password must be different from the current one. Changing your password Where to find it: click your name at the top right > Change password . Field What to enter Current password The password you logged in with. New password Your new password, following the rules under the boxes. Confirm new password The new password again, to rule out a typing mistake. Click your name at the top right, then Change password . Type your Current password . Type the New password . Type it again in Confirm new password . Click Change password . The program says Your password has been changed. and opens the Home page. Use the new password from your next log-in. Message What it means Your current password is incorrect. The first box does not match your password. The new passwords do not match. The second and third boxes differ. Type both again. Choose a password different from your current one. The new password is the same as the old one. The new password must have at least 8 characters, a number. The message lists the rules the new password breaks. Temporary passwords and expired passwords When an administrator creates your account or resets your password, you get a temporary password. At your first log-in the Change password page opens with the message Please replace your temporary password before continuing. Until you change it, every other page brings you back here. Only Log out still works. When your password is older than the number of days set by the administrator, the program shows Your password has expired. Please choose a new one. and opens the same page. Forgotten password and locked account The program does not send passwords by e-mail. If you forget your password, or your account is locked after too many wrong passwords (5 as delivered), ask an administrator. In User Accounts they can unlock your account and give you a temporary password, which you then change as described above. A successful log-in sets the count of wrong attempts back to zero.

t: Logging out and the automatic time-out
x: To log out, click your name at the top right, then Log out . Always log out when you leave a shared computer. The program also logs you out by itself when you have not opened or saved a page for a while (30 minutes as delivered; the administrator sets the time). The next time you click, the log-in page opens with You were logged out after a period of inactivity. Important Typing in a form does not count as activity. Only opening a page or saving does. If you spend a long time on one form, save it before the time-out runs out, or what you typed is lost when you finally press Save .
After you log in, every page has the same frame: a dark bar across the top, the menu of modules on the left, and the page itself on the right, with its title bar at the top.

Part What it does GSMaRT Construction System Click the name at the top left to go back to the Home page from anywhere. Company name The company you are working in, beside the program's name. Search box Type a name, document number, reference or barcode and press Enter. The Search page lists what matches. Find Opens the Find page, which looks for transactions in every module with any combination of filters. Bell Shows how many preventive maintenance tasks are due, in a red circle. Click it to open Preventive Maintenance . Your name Opens the user menu. The search box, Find and the bell appear only for users who may open the pages behind them. When no maintenance task is due, the bell is an outline without a number. The user menu shows your role (for example Administrator ) and the entries Change password , User's Manual and Log out . A Company Owner sees Company Owner before the role names. Note When the Super Admin works inside a company, a yellow strip under the top bar says so, and the user menu has Back to the platform instead of Change password .

The menu on the left lists the modules: Home , Financial Set-up & Reports (called Chart of Accounts before version 29), Fixed Assets , Customers , Vendors , Inventory , Point of Sale , Banking , BIR Reports , System Administration and Company . Click a module to open its list of pages; click it again to close it. Opening one module closes the one that was open. The module of the page you are on opens by itself, and the page you are on is highlighted. Inside a module, the pages are grouped under small headings such as TRANSACTIONS , LISTS and SETUP . The reports of a module are folded away under REPORTS with their number in brackets. Click REPORTS to unfold the list of reports. Large modules divide their reports under grey sub-headings, such as Customer and Receivables Reports and Sales Reports . Click REPORTS again to fold the list away. Note The menu shows only the pages you may open. Two users with different roles therefore see different menus. A module you have no page in does not appear at all.

t: The title bar of a page
x: Under the top bar, every page starts with a title bar. On the left is the page's name, for example Home , New Invoice or Invoice INV-00001 . On the right are the page's own buttons, such as New , Export , Edit , Print or Report Center . At the right end is the Help button, which opens this manual at the section for the page.

t: Messages at the top of the page
x: After you save, void, delete or change something, a coloured message appears above the title bar: green for success, for example Your password has been changed. blue for information, for example a memorized transaction that was entered automatically, yellow for a warning, for example You were logged out after a period of inactivity. red for a problem that stopped the action. Click the small cross at the right of a message to close it. The message goes away by itself when you open another page. When a form cannot be saved, a red box with a warning sign appears above the form and says why, for example Choose an item for every line that has a description or amount. Everything you typed stays on the form. Correct what the message asks and save again.

Home. Where you start. The Home Dashboard shows your key figures, reminders and a button for every transaction you may enter. The Report Center lists every report you may open. Memorized Reports and Saved Report Layouts keep reports set up the way you like them, and Find looks for transactions in every module at once. See Home, Finding Things and Working with Reports . Financial Set-up & Reports. The general ledger: the list of accounts, the Class List, Employees & Other Names, Memorized Transactions, Set Up Budgets, Make Journal Entries (including opening balances), Module Default Accounts (the accounts each module posts to) and Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists. Its reports are the financial statements and the ledgers: Trial Balance, Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Statement of Cash Flows, General Ledger, Journal, Subsidiary Ledger, Schedule of Accounts, the budget comparisons, the statements by class, and the comparative income statements and balance sheets by month, quarter, year and your own ranges or dates. See Financial Set-up & Reports: Chart of Accounts and the General Ledger . Fixed Assets. The Fixed Asset Register, Run Depreciation, Dispose of Assets, Asset Maintenance (repairs paid through a bill, a check or a cash voucher), Preventive Maintenance (tasks that fall due by date or by meter and remind you through the bell), Asset Categories and Asset Locations, with reports on depreciation, additions and disposals, and maintenance. See Fixed Assets . Customers. Everything you sell and collect: the Customer Center, estimates, sales orders, invoices and batch invoices, sales receipts, statement charges and statements, finance charges, the sales forecast, customer payments, and credit memos and refunds. Its reports cover receivables (aging, balances, open invoices, collections) and sales (by customer, item, sales rep and site). See Customers and Receivables . Vendors. Everything you buy and pay: the Vendor Center and Bill Tracker, purchase orders, receiving, bills, supplier debit memos, Pay Bills, and Receipt Management, which turns photos and e-mails of receipts into bills. Its reports cover payables (aging, balances, unpaid bills) and suppliers. See Vendors and Payables . Inventory. Items and stock: the Inventory Center, the Item List, sites, units of measure, processing formulas, transfers between sites, quantity and value adjustments, assembly builds, disassembly and processing, physical counts, and item prices and price levels. For convenience the Inventory menu also shows Create Purchase Orders and Receive Items . Its reports cover quantities, valuation, stock status and processing. See Inventory . Point of Sale. The counter: the POS Register, cashier shifts with cash drops and X and Z readings, POS receipts, returns and voids, and the POS terminals, with sales reports by item, category, cashier, payment method and hour. See Point of Sale . Banking. Write Checks, Cash Voucher (petty cash and revolving fund payments), Use Register, Make Deposits, Transfer Funds and Reconcile, with the reconciliation reports and the Check Register. See Banking . System Administration. For administrators: user accounts, roles, page access, effective access, the company details, security settings and closing date, data utilities, imports from CSV files, backups, and the one-time Multi-Company Setup. Its Audit Reports include the Audit Trail, Transaction History, voided and deleted transactions, user activity, log-in history and access changes. See System Administration . Company. Company Profile & Code, Employees & Users and Join Requests: where the Company Owner hands out the Company Code and approves the employees who join with it. While the program runs a single company, Company Profile & Code only says that there is no Company Code yet. See Your Company: Company Owner and Employees . The Super Admin's platform pages, which create and manage the companies, are not in this menu; they are described in Super Admin: Managing Several Companies . The Appendices at the end of the manual hold reference material.

Every transaction in the program (an invoice, a bill, a check, a journal entry, an inventory adjustment) is entered on a form. The forms work the same way everywhere. The picture shows a new invoice as an example.

From the menu: most document pages, such as Customers > Create Invoices , open on the list of that kind of transaction; click New in the title bar for a blank form. Some pages, such as Customers > Receive Payments , open on the form itself. From the Home page: the Quick actions buttons open the page, and for the common documents (estimates, sales orders, invoices, sales receipts, statement charges, credit memos, bills, purchase orders, checks and journal entries) they open a blank form directly. To change a saved transaction, open it and click Edit .

Dates are shown as month/day/year, for example 09/27/2026. Type the date or click the calendar button in the box to pick it. A new form starts with today's date. Amounts are typed without the peso sign. You may type commas (12,500.00) or leave them out (12500). The program keeps two decimals. Number boxes that show a greyed-out number with (auto) , such as INV-00014 (auto) , fill themselves in when you save. Leave them empty unless you need a number of your own. Boxes whose label says what happens when they are left blank, such as Due date (blank = from terms) , can be left empty.

Any drop-down with more than four choices (customers, suppliers, items, accounts, classes, terms and so on) is a box you can type in. It shows Type to search until something is chosen. Click the box, or move into it with the Tab key. The list of choices opens under it, with the current choice highlighted. Type any part of what you are looking for. The list narrows with every letter. Several words may be typed in any order: every word must appear somewhere in the choice. Choices that begin with what you typed come first, and the matching letters are marked. Click the choice you want, or move to it with the Up and Down arrow keys and press Enter. Good to know: After you have typed, leaving the box with the Tab key takes the highlighted choice. Esc closes the list and keeps what was chosen before. To empty a box, delete the text and leave the box, or open the list and click the first entry (for example Clear this box ), which appears when something is chosen. If nothing matches, the list says Nothing matches followed by what you typed. The part in brackets at the end of a choice, such as an account code or the kind of name, is shown in lighter letters. Short lists, such as a status or a yes-or-no choice, stay ordinary drop-downs. Example On the invoice, click Customer:Job and type abc . The list shrinks to ABC Trading Corp. and its jobs, such as ABC Trading Corp.:Office Renovation Project. Press Enter to take the first one.

The middle of most forms is a grid of lines, one for each item, service or account. Choose the Item (or the account). The program fills in the description, the unit, the price (the cost on purchase forms) and the tax code from the item, and a quantity of 1. Amount is worked out as Qty times Rate , less the Discount . The discount is either a percentage ( % ) or an amount off the line ( Amt ): choose which in the small drop-down beside the discount box. If you type the Amount yourself, the Rate is worked out from it. The tax of each line comes from its tax code. Prices on sales and purchase forms are VAT-exclusive: the VAT is added on top. Click Add line for another line, or Add 5 lines or Add 10 lines to add that many empty lines in one click. The new lines are lit up for a moment. To put a line in between two others, click the small square plus button at the end of the line that should come after it: an empty line is inserted just above that line, and the lines keep that order when the form is saved. Click the red cross at the end of a line to remove it. On forms with a site at the top ( Default site for items on bills, item receipts and purchase orders, Inventory site on sales forms), the site chosen there is copied onto every line, including the lines added later, so you do not have to choose it on each line. A line can still be given another site. Changing the site at the top afterwards moves every line that still had the old one, and leaves alone the lines you changed yourself. There is no set limit to the number of lines: a bill or an invoice of several hundred lines is saved whole, and editing it later keeps every line. Long forms are sent to the server in one package for this reason. The Subtotal , Tax and Total under the grid add up as you type. A negative total is shown in brackets, for example (1,250.00).

The buttons at the foot of the form stay in view while you scroll: Save records the transaction and shows it as saved. Save & New records it and opens a blank form, so you can enter the next one straight away. It appears only if you may create transactions on the page. Cancel leaves without saving. If something is missing or wrong, nothing is saved and a red box above the form tells you what to correct. If a very long form shows the message "This form has more fields than the server accepts at once (...), so nothing was saved", the page was opened before the program was updated: press Ctrl+F5 to load it again, enter the lines and save. Nothing was saved by the attempt.

t: Stock below zero: the Yes / No question
x: When Allow selling or moving stock below zero (with warning) is switched on (see "Stock below zero" in Inventory ), saving a sales invoice, a sales receipt, a batch of invoices, a POS sale, an inventory adjustment or an inventory transfer that would leave an item below zero at a site is not done straight away. A window headed Stock will go below zero says "Saving the transaction will lead the inventory to a negative balance." It lists each item with its site, the quantity On hand and the quantity After saving , and asks Do you want to continue? Click Yes to save the transaction. The same button you pressed is used again, so Save & New still opens a blank form afterwards. Click No to go back to the form. Nothing has been saved; change the quantities, or cancel the transaction. A yellow box above the form repeats the items while you decide. When the setting is switched off, there is no question: the transaction is refused with "Not enough stock: ...".

t: Memorize Transaction and Load Memorized Transaction
x: A transaction you enter again and again (a monthly retainer invoice, the rent check, an accrual journal entry, the regular order from a supplier) can be kept as a pro-forma and loaded into a new form whenever it is needed. The forms that have it: Create Estimates, Create Sales Orders, Create Invoices, Create Batch Invoices, Enter Sales Receipts, Enter Statement Charges, Create Credit Memos, Enter Bills, Supplier Debit Memos, Create Purchase Orders, Receive Items, Receive Items and Enter Bills, Write Checks, Cash Voucher, Make Journal Entries and Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand. To memorize what is on the form: Fill in the form as if you were going to save it. Click Memorize Transaction at the right of the save buttons. In the box, type a name in Name it , a Group if you use groups, and choose the Reminder : Don't remind me keeps it on the list until you load it; Remind me when it is due (or Enter it automatically ) asks for Every , Next due and Remind (days before) . Click Memorize Transaction in the box. The form is checked as for saving; the message "Memorized as "...". It is on the Memorized Transactions list ... This invoice itself was not saved." appears and the form stays filled, so you can still save it. To fill a new form from it: Open the form for a new transaction and click Load Memorized Transaction in the title bar (it shows how many there are for this form). Type part of the name to find it, and click Load . If you had already typed something on the form, you are asked "Replace what is on the form with the memorized transaction?". The form opens with the names, items, accounts, amounts, site, class and memo that were memorized, under the note "Loaded from the memorized transaction ...". The date and the document number are today's and the next ones. Change what differs and save. Memorizing records nothing in the books, and no supervisor approval is asked for it; the approval is asked when the transaction is saved. The memorized transactions are on Memorized Transactions , where they can also be entered, rescheduled or taken off.

t: The Class box and the "No class selected" question
x: Every transaction form has a Class box. Classes are your own way of dividing the books: branches, departments, projects or product lines. They are kept in the Class List . The class you choose is copied to every ledger line the transaction posts, so each financial report can be filtered by class, and the "by Class" statements show one column per class. Journal entries and cash vouchers can also carry a different class on each line. When classes have been set up and you save a transaction without one, the program asks first. A window headed No class selected says: "This transaction has no class. It will be saved as Unclassified and will not appear under any class on the class reports." Click Choose a class to go back; the Class box is marked so you find it quickly. Click Continue saving to save it without a class. On reports, transactions without a class are grouped as (Unclassified) . When no class has been set up yet, the Class box says No classes yet (Class List) and the question is not asked.

Some actions go beyond what your role allows on its own, so a second person must approve them. The program then shows Supervisor approval is required: followed by the reason, for example "15.00% discount on LAP-001". It happens when: a discount on a line is larger than your Max discount % without approval , a price is changed from the standard price by more than your Max price change % without approval , a check, bill payment, cash voucher, refund, inventory adjustment, count adjustment or processing order is larger than your Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval , a check, bill payment or refund above that limit is voided or deleted, at the counter: discounts and price changes beyond the cashier's limits, returns and refunds, voids of POS sales, X readings and closing the register (Z reading). The Supervisor approval section has two tabs. Supervisor is here is for a supervisor standing beside you, who types their own username and password. Approval code is for a supervisor who is somewhere else: they generate a one-time code on Approval Codes and read it out to you, and you type it instead of their password. Step by step: get an approval Save as usual. The form comes back with the reason and the Supervisor approval section open, marked required . Either ask a supervisor to type their username in Supervisor username and their password in Password (the password is hidden as it is typed), or open the Approval code tab and type the eight-letter code the supervisor gave you, for example AC7K-9MXT. The dash is put in for you, and small letters are read as capitals. Click Save again. The approver's name is recorded on the transaction ( Approved by ) and in the audit trail, whichever way the approval was given: a code stands for the supervisor who generated it. A code works once: the moment the transaction is saved with it, it is spent, and if the save fails for another reason the code is given back so you can try again with it. Message What it means Approval failed: the supervisor username or password is wrong. Try again. Failed approvals are recorded in the audit trail. You cannot approve your own transaction. Another person must approve it. (username) is not allowed to approve on this page. That supervisor's role has no Approve right on this page. The approval code is not valid. Ask the supervisor for a new code. No such code exists. Check the letters, or ask for a new one. That approval code was already used. Each code works once: ask the supervisor for a new one. The code was spent on an earlier save. That approval code has expired. / ... was cancelled. The code ran out of time, or the supervisor cancelled it. That approval code was issued for another user. The supervisor made the code for a different username. That approval code is for (page), not for this page. The supervisor limited the code to one page. You cannot approve your own transaction with a code you generated. A supervisor cannot use their own code. Note A user whose role has the Approve right on the page approves their own actions: the program does not ask them for a second person. On forms that may need approval, the Supervisor approval link under the lines can also be opened before you save, so the supervisor can type their details in advance.

Invoices and sales receipts have a tick box Pending (non-posting until marked final) . A pending sale is saved as a document but does not post to the books or take items out of stock. Use it, for example, while a customer's purchase order is being approved. A pending transaction shows the yellow note "This transaction is pending . It does not affect the books or inventory until it is marked final." Lists show it with the status Pending . To make it final, open it and click Mark as final . The form opens with Pending unticked and the note Pending is unticked — saving posts this sale. Click Save . The credit limit of the customer is checked when the invoice becomes final, not while it is pending. The Home page counts the pending sales, and the Pending Sales report lists them. Assembly builds and processing orders can also be saved as pending when components are short; see Build Assemblies and Disassemble / Process Items . Estimates, sales orders and purchase orders never post: they record a commitment only, and their page says "Non-posting document: it records a commitment and does not affect the ledger." Suspended POS sales do not post either until they are recalled and completed.
Some buttons ask before they act, in a small window of the browser, for example Close this document? Remaining quantities will no longer be expected. Click OK to go on or Cancel to stop.

Most document pages open on the list of their transactions, newest first, for example the Invoices list under Customers > Create Invoices . The transaction lists of invoices, sales receipts, estimates, orders, bills, checks, payments, deposits, transfers, journal entries, adjustments and builds all work as described here. Filter What it does From / To The dates listed. The list opens on the last 90 days and the next 30 days. Status For example Open, Partially paid, Paid, Pending or Void. All lists every status. Class Appears once classes are set up. Search Part of a number, name or memo. Set the filters and click Filter . The columns are Date , No. , Name , Reference , Memo , Class (once classes are set up), Total , Open (the amount still unpaid or unapplied, on invoices, bills and credits), Status and By (who entered it). A list that holds several kinds of transaction also has a Type column. Voided transactions are struck through. The list shows up to 500 transactions; narrow the dates to see older ones. Click the number of a transaction to open it. Click New in the title bar for a blank form. Click Export to download the list, as filtered, as a spreadsheet file (CSV) that opens in Excel.

A saved transaction opens as a page titled with its type and number, for example Invoice INV-00001 . It shows the details (date, number, status, customer or supplier, class, terms, who entered it and when, who approved it), the lines, the totals with the Open balance , the Related documents (what it was created from, what it was converted to, the payments applied), and, for users allowed to see them, the General ledger entries created automatically . The buttons in the title bar depend on the transaction and on your rights: Button What it does Edit Opens the form to change it. Mark as final Posts a pending invoice or sales receipt. Print Opens the printout. Email Opens your e-mail program with a new message to the customer or supplier. Memorize Saves it as a memorized transaction to enter again later. Void / Delete See "Voiding and deleting" below. History Opens its Transaction History : every change, by whom and when. Back to list Returns to the list. Other buttons carry the document to its next step, such as Create Invoice on a sales order, Receive Payment on an invoice, Pay Bill on a bill, or Close and Reopen on estimates and orders. They are explained in the chapter for each page. Note The message that Email prepares holds a link to the printout. Only someone who can log in to GSMaRT Construction System can open that link. To send a document to a customer, print it to PDF (see below) and attach the file to the message.

Print on a saved transaction opens its printout on a plain page, without the menus, with two buttons at the top: Print and Back . Click Print on the saved transaction. Click Print at the top of the printout. The browser's print window opens. Choose your printer, or choose Save as PDF (the name differs slightly between browsers) to make a PDF file. Click Back to return to the transaction. The buttons at the top do not appear on paper. Opening the printout of a check, bill payment or refund marks it as printed, and every printout is recorded in the audit trail. Reports print the same way; see Working with reports .

A saved transaction that is wrong can be corrected with Edit . When it should not exist at all, you void it or delete it. Void keeps the document, with its number, but removes its effect on the ledger and on inventory. It stays in the lists, struck through, with the status Void , and its page shows VOID with the reason and the time. A voided transaction cannot be edited. Use it when the document was issued, for example a spoiled check. Delete removes the document completely. Its full content is kept in the audit trail. Use it for an entry made by mistake that was never issued. Estimates, sales orders and purchase orders do not post, so they cannot be voided; delete them or close them. POS sales cannot be deleted, only voided. Step by step: void or delete a transaction Open the transaction. Click Void (or Delete ). Type the reason in Reason (required, recorded in the audit trail) . If the action needs approval, let a supervisor type their username and password under Supervisor approval , or type the one-time approval code they gave you. Click Void transaction (or Delete transaction ). The program says, for example, Invoice INV-00005 was voided. or Invoice INV-00005 was deleted. A full copy is kept in the audit trail. When voiding or deleting is refused Message What to do Payments or credits have been applied to it. Remove them first (edit the payment or credit). Take the invoice or bill off the payment or credit first. It is included in deposit DEP-00001. Remove it from the deposit first. Edit the deposit and take the payment out of it. It has been refunded (…). Void the refund first. Void the refund check, then the credit. It has already been converted or received in part. Close it instead. Use Close on the order or estimate. This transaction is already void. Nothing to do. The Void and Delete buttons appear only if your role has the Delete/Void right on the page. The Voided and Deleted Transactions Summary report lists every void and deletion, so they can be reviewed.

When a period's books are final, the administrator sets a closing date in Company, Security & Closing Date . The Home page then says, for example, Books closed through 07/09/2026. From then on, transactions dated on or before the closing date can no longer be entered, edited, voided or deleted, except by users whose role has the special permission Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled . The same protection covers transactions already cleared in a bank reconciliation. Message What it means The books are closed through 07/09/2026. You do not have permission to record transactions dated on or before the closing date. Use a date after the closing date, or ask an authorised user. This transaction is dated on or before the closing date (07/09/2026) and cannot be changed. The transaction belongs to a closed period. This transaction has been cleared in a bank reconciliation. You do not have permission to change it. It was ticked as cleared in Reconcile . Tip A mistake found in a closed period is usually corrected with an entry dated in the open period, for example a journal entry, so that the figures already reported for the closed period stay as they were.

t: Access: what you can open and do
x: Every user has one or more roles, and the roles decide what the user may do. The administrator manages them in User Role Configuration and Page Access Configuration . Opening a page (View). A page appears in your menu, and can be opened, only if one of your roles allows it. A user override set by the administrator can allow or deny a single page for you alone; an override always wins over the roles. Actions on a page. For each page a role allows Create , Edit , Delete/Void , Print/Export and Approve separately. A button whose action you may not take does not appear: without Print/Export you see no Print or Export buttons, without Delete/Void no Void or Delete buttons. Special permissions. Some rights are set per role, apart from the pages: Special permission What it controls View costs and margins Cost and margin columns on forms and reports. View bank balances outside Banking Bank balances on the Home page, the Chart of Accounts and Transfer Funds. Max discount % without approval Larger discounts need supervisor approval. Max price change % without approval Larger price changes need supervisor approval. Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval Larger amounts need supervisor approval. Blank means no limit. Can exceed customer credit limits Saving an invoice over the credit limit, with a reason. Can change the Chart of Accounts and default accounts Changes to accounts and module default accounts. Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled Work in closed periods and on reconciled lines. Can design report layouts (fonts, headings and footers, columns and rows) and save or share them The Modify Report button on reports. Sites and POS terminals. A user or a role can be limited to some inventory sites and POS terminals. Such users can only record transactions for their sites, and lists, site choices and site-based reports show only their sites. Administrators can open everything. In a company with a Company Owner, the owner can always open every page of the company, whatever the roles say. When you try to open a page you may not use, the Access denied page says "You do not have permission to open" followed by the page's name. The attempt is recorded in the audit trail. Click Go to Home or Go back , and ask your administrator if you need the access. Administrators can check exactly what a user may do, and why, in Effective Access (View as User) .

The program comes with standard roles. Your administrator can change them or add roles of their own, so your company's roles may differ. Role What it is for Demo user Administrator Everything, including users, roles, page access, the closing date and the audit trail. admin Accountant Financial Set-up & Reports, Fixed Assets, Banking, all reports; designs report layouts. accountant A/R Clerk Customer transactions and the receivables reports. arclerk A/P Clerk Supplier transactions, Pay Bills and the payables reports. apclerk Inventory Clerk Items, sites, receiving, adjustments, builds, processing and counts. invclerk Sales Representative Estimates, sales orders, invoices and the Sales reports. salesrep Cashier POS sales, returns and cash drops at the assigned terminal. cashier1 POS Supervisor A cashier's work, plus approvals and X and Z readings. supervisor Auditor Views all transactions, reports and the audit trail; changes nothing. auditor The POS Supervisor approves voids, refunds, price overrides and large discounts at the counter. The Auditor cannot open the set-up pages of System Administration, the Company pages, the POS Register or the shifts page. The Cashier and the POS Supervisor of the demo company work at Makati Counter 1. The limits the standard roles start with (see the special permissions above): Role Discount % Price change % Amount Accountant 0 0 no limit A/R Clerk 10 5 ₱50,000.00 A/P Clerk 0 0 ₱100,000.00 Inventory Clerk 0 0 ₱20,000.00 Sales Representative 5 0 0 Cashier 5 0 0 POS Supervisor 30 20 ₱20,000.00 A limit of 0 means that every discount, price change or amount of that kind needs a supervisor's approval. The Administrator has no limits. Of the other special permissions, the Accountant may view costs and bank balances, change the Chart of Accounts and design report layouts; the A/P Clerk and the Auditor may view costs; the Auditor may view bank balances. Two more roles exist when the program runs several companies: The Company Owner of each company manages its users: approving employees who join with the Company Code, giving them roles, resetting passwords. See Your Company: Company Owner and Employees . The Super Admin belongs to no company. They create and manage the companies and can open any of them to work inside it. See Super Admin: Managing Several Companies . Important The demo users of the sample database are for training. Before real use, the administrator changes their passwords or switches them off in User Accounts .

t: Using GSMaRT Construction System on a phone or tablet
x: Every page is laid out for small screens as well. On a phone the top bar holds the menu button (three lines) at the left, the program's name, the Find button (funnel icon), the bell and your name. The search box is left out for lack of room; use Find , whose page has a Search names and items button. The title bar of the page stacks its buttons full width, and cards such as the Home figures sit one under the other. Tap the menu button to open the menu. It slides in as a panel headed Menu , with the same modules as on a computer. Tap a page to open it, or tap the cross at the top right to close the panel. Forms put their boxes one under the other, and the Save , Save & New and Cancel buttons stay at the foot of the screen. Good to know on small screens: A table wider than the screen scrolls sideways inside its own box: swipe the table, not the page. A soft shadow on the right edge shows that more columns are out of sight. Report lines stay on one line so they can be followed across; only long memos and descriptions wrap. Boxes and buttons are large enough to tap, and text boxes are sized so the phone does not zoom in when you tap one. The list of a type-to-search box is drawn in the part of the screen the keyboard leaves free, with the phone held upright or on its side. On the Find page, each transaction found is shown as a small block, and a drop-down replaces the sortable column headings. The POS Register has its own phone layout; see Point of Sale .

What you see What to do Access denied Your role does not allow the page or the action. Ask your administrator. Your session expired or the form was already submitted. Go back, refresh the page and try again. The form was sent twice, or your session changed (for example you logged in again in another tab). Go back, reload the page, enter the data again and save. Page not found The address is wrong. Use the menu. Database update needed The program was updated and the database needs the matching update. Nothing is lost. Ask your administrator (with several companies, the Super Admin) to run it, then click Reload . A red box above a form The form was not saved. Correct what the box says and save again. You were logged out after a period of inactivity. Log in again. Save long forms before the time-out. For anything else, click the Help button of the page you are on, or ask your administrator.

The Home Dashboard is the page that opens after you log in. It shows the key figures of the business, a button for every transaction you may enter, and the reminders that need your attention. Where to find it: Home > Home Dashboard. It also opens when you log in, and when you click GSMaRT Construction System at the top left of any page. The whole page, from the figures at the top to the open POS shifts at the bottom: What the page shows Part What it shows Welcome line Your name, today's date and, when a closing date is set, Books closed through that date. Accounts Receivable What customers owe: the balance of the accounts receivable account(s) in the general ledger. overdue document(s) Invoices, statement charges and finance charges past their due date and not paid in full. Accounts Payable What you owe suppliers: the balance of the accounts payable account(s). bill(s) due within 7 days Unpaid bills due within the next seven days, including those already overdue. Sales this month (net of VAT) Invoices, sales receipts and POS sales from the first of the month to today, before VAT. pending sale(s) Invoices and sales receipts saved as pending. Items at or below reorder point Active inventory parts and assemblies whose total quantity on hand is at or below their reorder point. negative stock record(s) Item and site combinations whose quantity on hand is below zero. Quick actions A button for every transaction page on which you may create, grouped by module. Cash and bank accounts Each active bank account and its balance. Open POS shifts The cashier shifts not yet closed: Terminal , Cashier , Opened , Float . Memorized transactions due Memorized transactions set to remind you, with their due date. Asset maintenance due Preventive maintenance tasks that are due or overdue. To-do reminders Notes marked as to-dos on customers and suppliers that are not done yet. My recent activity Your last ten actions from the audit trail, with the date and time. Not everyone sees every part. Each one appears only for the users it concerns: The four figures at the top appear for users who may open the pages behind them: the receivables figure for users of the A/R Aging Summary or the Customer Center, the payables figure for users of the A/P Aging Summary or the Vendor Center, the sales figure for users of Sales by Item Summary, POS Daily Sales Summary or Create Invoices, and the reorder figure for users of the Inventory Center or Inventory Stock Status by Item. Cash and bank accounts appears only with the special permission View bank balances outside Banking . Open POS shifts appears for users who may open Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings, and only while a shift is open. Memorized transactions due appears for users who may open Memorized Transactions, and only when something is due. Asset maintenance due appears for users who may open Preventive Maintenance, and only when a task is due. The Report Center button in the title bar appears for users who may open the Report Center. Step by step: start a transaction from the Home page Find the module in Quick actions , for example Customers . Click the button of the transaction, for example Create Invoices . For estimates, sales orders, invoices, sales receipts, statement charges, credit memos, bills, purchase orders, checks and journal entries, a blank form opens at once. The other buttons open the page itself. Step by step: see the detail behind a figure Click the blue line under the figure. The page behind it opens: - under Accounts Receivable : the A/R Aging Summary , - under Accounts Payable : Pay Bills , - under Sales this month (net of VAT) : Sales by Item Summary for this month, - under Items at or below reorder point : Inventory Stock Status by Item . If you may not open that page, the line is plain text instead of a link. Step by step: deal with a reminder Memorized transactions due: click Open on the card. The Memorized Transactions list opens, where you enter each one. The card shows Due or Overdue beside each date. Asset maintenance due: click Open . Preventive Maintenance opens on the tasks that are due. A task shows, for example, 3 days overdue or Due in 20 days , and stays on the card until someone acknowledges that it is complete. Cash and bank accounts: click an account to open its register in Use Register . Good to know The figures are worked out when the page opens. To bring them up to date, open the Home page again. The receivables and payables figures are ledger balances. They include opening balances, journal entries to those accounts, and transactions of every date, future-dated ones too. The sales figure leaves out voided, pending and suspended sales. Credit memos and POS returns are not taken off it; the sales reports show the net figure. To-do reminders are added as notes, with the To-do box ticked, in the Customer Center and the Vendor Center . The card shows up to ten, the earliest due first; a due date that has passed is shown in red. When nothing is open it says No open reminders. The bell in the top bar and the pop-up after log-in show the same maintenance tasks as the Asset maintenance due card.

Search finds a customer, a supplier, an item or a document from any word or number you remember: part of a name, a document number, a reference or a barcode. Where to find it: the search box in the top bar (type and press Enter). Also Home > Find > Search names and items . Search is not listed in the menu. The results are grouped by kind. Each line is a link. What Search looks in Group Looks in Opens Customers Name, company name, e-mail, phone The customer in the Customer Center Vendors Name, company name, e-mail The supplier in the Vendor Center Items Item code, item name, or the whole barcode The item's form in the Item List Transactions Number, reference, memo, receipt number, payee The transaction Beside each result is a short description: the company name and phone of a customer or supplier, the type of an item, and the date, name and total of a transaction. Step by step: search Click the search box in the top bar. Type what you remember, for example ABC , INV-00003 or a barcode. Press Enter. The Search page lists what matches. Click a result to open it. To search again, type in the box on the Search page and click Search . Good to know A word matches anywhere in the text: ABC finds ABC Trading Corp. and any document whose number, reference or memo contains ABC. A barcode must be typed in full. Each group shows up to 20 matches, and Transactions shows the 50 most recent. When nothing matches, the page says Nothing found for followed by your words. A group appears only if you may open the page it leads to, and only the kinds of transaction you may open are listed. A transaction is found by its own number, reference, memo or payee, not by the customer's or supplier's name. To list every transaction of a customer, use Find with the customer's name.

Find looks for transactions in every module at once: estimates, orders, invoices, sales receipts, payments, credit memos, bills, supplier debit memos, bill payments, checks, cash vouchers, deposits, transfers, journal entries, inventory adjustments and transfers, builds, processing orders, POS sales and returns, depreciation and disposals. You describe what you know about the transaction, and Find lists every transaction that fits. Use it when you know "something about" a document but not where it is: an amount, a date range, a supplier, an item, the person who entered it. Where to find it: Home > Find, or the Find button (funnel icon) in the top bar. Find has two tabs. Simple asks for the usual few things. Advanced offers more than forty filters that can be combined in any way. The Search names and items button in the title bar opens the Search page.

The Simple tab looks for one kind of transaction by its name, dates, number and amount. Fields Field What to enter Transaction type The kind of transaction, for example Invoice or Bill . Only the kinds whose page you may open are listed. Name box The customer, supplier or other name, or Any name . Its label follows the type: Customer:Job , Supplier , Payee , Paid to , Customer or Name . Date from / To The dates to look between. Either one may be left empty. Number box Part of the document number. Its label follows the type, for example Invoice # , Bill # , Check # , P.O. # or Voucher # . Amount The exact total of the transaction, or empty for Any amount . The name box offers only the names that fit the type: customers for sales documents, suppliers for purchase documents, and every kind of name for checks, journal entries and the rest. A customer also finds the transactions of its jobs. Step by step: find a transaction on the Simple tab Choose the Transaction type . Fill in what you know; leave the rest empty. Click Find . The results appear under the tab. Reset clears the tab. The Advanced link beside the buttons, like the Advanced tab itself, opens the Advanced tab with the choices of your last search, so you can add more filters to them. Example To find the invoice of ₱89,577.60 for ABC Trading Corp., choose Invoice , type abc in Customer:Job and pick the customer, type 89577.60 in Amount and click Find .

The Advanced tab combines any number of filters. A transaction is found only when it matches every filter you set. The tab has three parts: Choose filter on the left lists every filter in alphabetical order. Type in Type to find a filter to shorten the list. A filter that is set is shown in bold with a green tick. The middle shows the filter you clicked, with a line saying what it finds, and the boxes to set it. Current choices on the right lists every filter that is set, with what it is set to. Click a line to open that filter again; click the cross at its end to remove it. With nothing set, it says that Find lists every transaction you are allowed to open, newest first. How the filters are set Lists to tick (accounts, names, items, types and so on): tick any number of entries. A transaction is found if it matches any one of them. Type in Type to narrow the list to find an entry. The count under the list says how many are ticked, or None ticked: all of them . Clear unticks them all. Short choices (for example Voided or Paid status ): pick one. Either (no filter) leaves the filter off. Dates : pick a period in Dates ( Today , This week , This month , Last month , This quarter , This fiscal year , Fiscal year to date , Last fiscal year ), or type From and To dates, which makes the period Custom . Any date leaves the filter off. Figures (amount, days past due, quantity): pick = , at most , at least or between and type the figure (two figures for between ). Any leaves the filter off. The sign of an amount does not matter. Words (memo, number, reference, address and so on): pick contains , is exactly or starts with , and type the words. Number also offers from ... to , for a range of document numbers such as INV-00005 to INV-00010. The filters Filter What it finds Account Transactions that post to, or are entered against, any of the accounts ticked. The list starts with whole groups such as All bank accounts and All expense accounts . Aging (days past due) Open invoices, statement charges, finance charges and bills this many days past their due date. Amount The total of the transaction (a journal entry, adjustment or transfer counts its debits). Approved by Transactions a supervisor approved: discounts, price changes, amounts over a limit. Billing status Costs marked billable to a customer, and whether they were billed yet. Class Transactions, or lines, carrying these classes. No class (unclassified) finds the unclassified. Cleared (bank) Whether the bank or credit-card lines were cleared in a reconciliation. Customer type Transactions of customers of these types. Date The date of the transaction. Detail level One line for each transaction, or every line of each transaction. Due date When an invoice, charge or bill falls due. Entered / modified When the transaction was first entered, or last changed (choose First entered or Last modified ). Entered by The user who entered the transaction (at the POS, the cashier). Fixed asset Depreciation, disposals and maintenance of these assets, and the purchases that brought them in. Import batch Transactions brought in by Import from CSV, by their batch reference. Item Transactions with a line for any of these items (inactive items included). Memo Words in the memo, the customer message, or the description of any line. Module Transactions entered in these parts of the system. Name The customer, supplier, employee or other name on the transaction or on any of its lines. The list starts with All customers , All suppliers , All employees and All other names . Name account no. / notes The supplier account number, or words in the notes, of the name on the transaction. Name address The street, city or province of the name (billing and shipping addresses too). Name contact person / company The contact person or company name of the customer or supplier. Name e-mail The e-mail address of the name on the transaction. Name phone / mobile / fax Any phone, mobile or fax number of the name. Name TIN The tax identification number of the name. Number The document number (or the POS receipt number). Paid status Invoices, charges and bills still open, or paid in full. Payment method Payments, receipts and POS sales paid by these methods. POS terminal Sales, returns and payments taken at these counters. Posting status Transactions that post to the books, or those that do not (estimates, orders, suspended sales). Preferred supplier Transactions with items whose preferred supplier is one of these. Printed status Documents printed, marked to be printed, or not printed. Quantity Transactions with a line of this quantity. Received (purchase orders) Purchase orders received in full, or still waiting for goods. Reference / P.O. no. The customer's P.O. number, the supplier's invoice number, the check reference. Sales rep Sales documents of these sales reps. Ship date The ship date of an invoice or order. Site Transactions at these sites (a transfer counts at both ends). Status The status the document stands at: open, partly paid, paid, pending, accepted, closed, completed, suspended. Tax code Transactions with a line under any of these tax codes. Terms Invoices, bills and orders on these terms. Transaction type Any number of kinds of transaction at once. Voided Leave voided transactions out, or find only those. Step by step: find transactions on the Advanced tab Click Advanced . Click a filter in Choose filter , for example Name . Set it in the middle, for example tick Supplier: TechDistributors Inc. It appears under Current choices at once. Click the next filter, for example Date , and set it. Repeat for every filter you need. Click Find . Reset clears every filter. Example To list every check and bill payment above ₱50,000.00 made this quarter, set Transaction type to Check and Bill Payment , Amount to at least 50000, and Date to This quarter , then click Find .

The results appear under the tabs, newest first. The header says how many transactions were found and what their amounts total, for example 13 transactions found, amounts totalling 536,512.95 . Column What it shows Date The date of the transaction. Type The kind of transaction. A voided one is greyed out and marked Void . Num The document number, or the POS receipt number. Name The customer (with the job after a colon), supplier, other name or payee. Account The transaction's main account, for example 1100 - Accounts Receivable for an invoice or the bank account of a check. Memo The memo of the transaction. Amount The total, or the debits of an entry that has no total. With Detail level set to Every line of each transaction , each line of each transaction gets a row of its own: the header then counts lines, the Account / Item column shows the line's account or item, Memo its description, and Amount its amount. Step by step: open a transaction found Click its line. The transaction opens. Or hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) and click, to open it in a new browser tab and keep the results. Or press Tab until a line is highlighted, move through the lines with the Up and Down arrow keys, and press Enter or click Go To . Go To opens the line that is picked (highlighted), which is the first line until you pick another. Buttons Button What it does Go To Opens the picked transaction. Report Opens the same results as the Find Results report, to print, memorize or design (see below). Export Downloads the results as a spreadsheet file (CSV) with the columns Date, Type, Num, Name, Account, Memo, Status and Amount. Good to know Click a column heading to sort by it; click it again to reverse the order. The arrow beside the heading shows the order. On a phone the headings are folded away and a drop-down ( Newest first , Oldest first , Largest amount first and so on) takes their place. The page shows 200 transactions at a time. Under the list, Showing 1 to 200 of the total and the buttons Newer and Older move between pages. Find only ever finds the kinds of transaction whose page you may open, at the sites you may see. Voided transactions are included unless you set the Voided filter. When nothing fits, the list says Nothing matches every one of these choices. Remove a filter, or widen the dates. Your choices are kept in the page's address, so a search can be bookmarked in the browser and run again later. Report needs access to the Find Results report, and Export needs the Print/Export right on it. Export takes up to 5,000 transactions and is recorded in the audit trail.

Find Results shows what the Find page found as a report, so the list can be printed, saved as PDF, exported, designed and memorized like any other report. A memorized Find Results report runs the same search again each time it is opened. Where to find it: the Report button above the results on the Find page. It is also listed under Home in the Report Center; opened from there, with no choices, it lists every transaction you are allowed to open. The report has no filters of its own: the choices come from the Find page, and the line under the title spells them out, for example "Transaction type: Invoice; Date: This month (09/01/2026 to 09/30/2026)". To change the search, go back to Find. Column What it shows Date The date of the transaction. Type The kind of transaction, with (void) after a voided one. Num The document number, as a link to the transaction. Name The customer, supplier, other name or payee. Account The main account, or Account / Item when every line is listed. Memo The memo, or the line description. Status An extra column, left out until it is ticked on the Modify Report panel's Columns tab. Amount The total, or the line amount. The total line counts the transactions (or lines) found in the Name column and totals the Amount column. The rows are in date order, oldest first; click a heading to sort them otherwise. Note The report lists up to 5,000 transactions. When more were found, a note under the title says Only the first 5,000 of the total are listed here. Narrow the search on the Find page to see the rest. The tools of the report are explained in Working with reports .

The Report Center lists every report you may open, grouped by module, and your memorized reports. It is the quickest way to find a report when you are not sure which module it belongs to. Where to find it: Home > Report Center, or the Report Center button on the Home page and on the Memorized Reports page. Its Memorized Reports button opens the list of memorized reports. What the page shows A line reminding you that every report can be filtered, customized, drilled into, memorized, printed or saved as PDF, exported and e-mailed. Find a report by name : type part of a name, for example "comparative" or "aging", and the cards keep only the reports whose names have every word you typed. The count under the box says how many are shown ("8 of 119 reports"). Clear the box to see them all again. Memorized reports : each report you memorized and each report other users shared, under its group (for example Month-end ), with the report it is based on under its name ("Income Statement, shared"). The card appears once there is at least one. A card for each module, listing its reports: Home , Financial Reports (the reports of the Financial Set-up & Reports menu: the trial balances, balance sheets, income statements, the comparative statements, cash flow, ledgers and journal), Fixed Assets , Customers , Vendors , Inventory , Point of Sale , Banking , BIR Reports and System Administration . Large modules divide them under headings such as CUSTOMER AND RECEIVABLES REPORTS and SALES REPORTS . Step by step: open a report Open Home > Report Center . Click the name of the report. It opens with its usual dates and filters. To open a memorized report, click its button under Memorized reports . It opens with the dates, filters and layout that were memorized. Good to know Only the reports your role allows are listed, so a module card may be short or missing. The same reports are listed in the menu, under REPORTS in each module. A shared memorized report is listed only if you may open the report it is based on.
Every report in GSMaRT Construction System works the same way. This section explains the tools once; the report sections of the other chapters describe only what is special to each report.

t: The parts of a report page
x: Part What it is Title bar The report's name and its buttons: Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report (or Layouts ), Memorize and Help . Filter bar The dates and the other choices of the report, and the Refresh button. Heading The company name, the report title and the line with the dates and filters, for example 01/01/2026 through 09/27/2026. Table The columns and rows, with group headings, subtotals and the grand total. Blue words are links. Foot The Printed line with the date, time and your name, and any footer text or signature lines of the layout. The buttons appear according to your rights: Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet and Email link need the Print/Export right on the report, Modify Report needs the special permission Can design report layouts , and Memorize needs access to the Memorized Reports page.

From the Report Center: Home > Report Center, then click the report. From the menu: open the module, unfold REPORTS , and click the report. From a memorized report: Home > Memorized Reports, or the Memorized reports buttons of the Report Center. From other pages: many pages link to their reports, for example the figures on the Home page, and blue names and numbers inside other reports.

The filter bar shows only the choices that make sense for the report. Each report opens on the dates that suit it; for example the Income Statement opens on Fiscal year to date and the aging reports on today's date. Filter What it does As of The single date a balance or aging report is worked out on. Dates A ready-made period (see the table below). Choosing one runs the report at once. From / To The first and last day of the period. From date and time / To date and time On the inventory movement reports, the sales report through inventory movement and Ending Inventory - POS Cashier: a time after each date, to see one shift of a day (see Dates with times, cashier and shift ). Empty times mean the whole days. Drop-downs such as Customer , Vendor , Item , Site , Account , Sales rep Limit the report to one of them. All means no limit. Category , Item type , Preferred supplier , Customer type Limit the report by a field of the item or the customer it is about (see Filters on related records ). Class One class, or (Unclassified) for transactions without a class. Columns On the Income Statement and some sales summaries: Total only , or a column for each Month , Quarter or Year of the period. Tick boxes Report-specific choices, for example Include estimates and sales orders , Exclude zero sales or Exclude inventory with zero balance . Ticking one runs the report at once. Search Words to look for, on the reports that have it. Dates choice Period Today Today only. This week Monday to Sunday of the current week. This month The first to the last day of the current month. Last month The whole of the previous month. This quarter The calendar quarter that contains today. Last quarter The whole of the calendar quarter before this one (the quarter of the BIR returns being prepared). This fiscal year The whole fiscal year that contains today. Fiscal year to date The first day of the fiscal year to today. Last fiscal year The whole previous fiscal year. All dates Everything, from 01/01/2000 to one year from today. Custom Starts from this month's dates; type your own in From and To and click Refresh . The fiscal year starts in the month set in Fiscal year starts (month 1-12) on Company, Security & Closing Date . Step by step: run a report for dates of your own Type the first day in From and the last day in To , or pick them with the calendar button. Set the other filters. Click Refresh . The dates in From and To are the ones used, even if the Dates list still shows an earlier choice. The line under the report's title always shows the dates actually used. Step by step: change the other filters Choose the customer, account, class or other filter. Click Refresh . Tip When the report shows nothing, it says No data for these settings. Widen the dates, or set a filter back to All .

Besides its own filters, a report can be narrowed by the fields of the records it is made from: the items it lists or sold, and the customers it is about. Every report where they apply has them in its filter bar: Filter On the reports about What it keeps Category items: inventory, sales by item, POS sales by item and category, processing The items of one category of the Category List . Item type items One kind of item: Inventory part , Inventory assembly , Non-inventory part , Service , Other charge and so on. Only the kinds that are in use are offered. Preferred supplier items The items whose preferred supplier (on the item's form) is the one chosen. Only suppliers that are the preferred supplier of an item are offered. Customer type customers: receivables, collections, sales, income by customer, open sales orders The customers of one customer type, with their jobs. Site inventory and sales One inventory site. On Quantity on Hand by Site it keeps that site's column only. The filters work together: Category Accessories with Preferred supplier TechDistributors Inc. keeps the accessories bought from that supplier. The totals, subtotals and percentages are those of what is shown. The line under the report's title names every filter chosen, for example "As of 10/04/2026, Makati Store, Category Accessories", so a printout says what it covers. A report narrowed by customer type leaves out its agreement with the ledger (the ledger is the total of every customer).

On most reports the column headings are links. Click a heading to sort by it; a small triangle shows the order (up for ascending, down for descending). Click the same heading again to reverse the order. Reports divided into groups with subtotals, such as the financial statements, and a few others whose order matters (the check register and the audit reports, for example) keep their own order, and their headings are plain text. Sort by (with Increasing or Decreasing beside it) is in the filter bar of the sales and income reports: Income by Customer Summary (Qty sold, Sales, Cost of sales, Income / (loss), Margin %), Sales by Item Summary (Qty, Amount, % of sales, COGS, Gross margin, Margin %), Inventory Sales by Site (Qty sold, Sales, Cost of sales), Sales by Item Group and POS Sales by Item Group (Qty, Total). Choosing a column or an order refreshes the report at once, and the heading line says "Sorted by Amount, decreasing". On a report divided into groups, the groups and their totals keep their places and the lines are sorted inside each group; lines without a figure (no cost on a service item, for example) come last whichever the order. Default order puts the report back in its own order. The sort is kept when the report is memorized, and the column headings of these reports sort the same way. Cost columns are offered in Sort by only to users who may view costs.

Words and numbers in blue are links to the detail behind them: a document number opens the transaction, an account on a financial statement opens the General Ledger of that account for the same period, a customer, supplier or item name opens a more detailed report or record, on some charts, a figure opens the report behind it. A link appears only when you may open the page it leads to; otherwise the text is plain.

A few reports draw charts above their table: the Accounts Receivable Graph (receivables by aging period and each customer's share), POS Sales by Hour (net sales by hour) and the Co-product & By-product Cost Allocation (allocated cost by output item, for users who may view costs). The charts print with the report.

Set the dates and filters, and click Refresh . Click Print / PDF . The report opens on a plain page, without menus or filters, with the buttons Print / Save as PDF and Back at the top. Click Print / Save as PDF . The browser's print window opens. Choose a printer, or choose to save as PDF. Click Back to return to the report. The printed page follows the Page settings of the report's layout: paper size, upright or sideways, margins, page numbers and the title at the top of each page (see "Modifying a report" below). Every printout is recorded in the audit trail. Tip Page numbers ("Page 1 of 3") and the title repeated on every page are printed by the browser in the page margins. Chrome and Edge do this; other browsers leave them off.

Set the dates and filters, and click Refresh . Click Export to spreadsheet . The browser downloads a CSV file named after the report, for example income_statement.csv . Open it in Excel or any spreadsheet program. The file holds the columns shown on the screen, in their order and with their headings, the rows shown on the screen, and the grand total. Amounts are plain numbers with two decimals, without commas, so they can be added up in the spreadsheet; dates are written year-month-day. Every export is recorded in the audit trail.

Email link opens your e-mail program with a new message. The subject is the report's title and the body is the address of the report, exactly as it is on your screen: the same dates, filters and layout. The person who receives it needs their own log-in and access to the report. If they are not logged in, the address takes them to the log-in page and then to the Home page; once logged in, they click the address again and see the report run afresh with the latest figures. Nothing is attached: to send the figures themselves, save the report as PDF or export it, and attach the file.

Users who may design reports see a Columns button beside Refresh on reports with more than two columns. It is a quick way to leave columns out: Click Columns . Tick Hide beside each column to leave out, or untick it to show it again. Click Refresh . The Columns tab of the Modify Report panel does the same and more (order, headings, widths, and fields from the related records).

t: Layouts (for users who do not design reports)
x: Users without the design permission see the report the way its default layout sets it. When other users have shared layouts for the report, a Layouts button appears in the title bar. Click it and choose a layout, or Standard for the report without any layout. While a layout is in use, the button shows its name.

Memorizing saves a report exactly as it is on the screen (the dates choice, the filters, the sort order, the columns and the layout) under a name of your own, so you can open it again with one click, share it, and have it e-mailed on a schedule. Fields Field What to enter Name The name of the memorized report. It starts as the report's title. Group A group to file it under, for example Month-end or Weekly. Groups sort the list. Share with other users Tick it to list the report for everyone. Each user can open it only if they may open the report itself. Send automatically No , Daily , Weekly or Monthly . Email to The e-mail address the scheduled report goes to. Step by step: memorize a report Set the report up: filters, sorting, columns and layout. Choose the period in Dates as the last step (see the tip below). Click Memorize . Change the Name if you wish and type a Group . Tick Share with other users if others should have it. To have it e-mailed, choose Daily , Weekly or Monthly in Send automatically and type the address in Email to . Click Save . The program says Report memorized. and shows the report again. It is now in Memorized Reports and in the Report Center. Tip A period chosen from the Dates list moves with the calendar: a report memorized on This month always shows the current month. Dates in From and To are remembered as they are. After you press Refresh , the From and To dates on the screen are sent with the report and stay fixed. To memorize a moving period, choose it from Dates after setting the other filters, and click Memorize without pressing Refresh again. Scheduled e-mail A memorized report with Send automatically set is e-mailed as a spreadsheet file (CSV) attached to a message whose subject is its name and the company name. The e-mails are sent by a program on the server, tools/send_scheduled_reports.php , which your administrator runs once a day (for example with Windows Task Scheduler). On each run: a daily report goes out once a day, a weekly report when a week has passed since the last sending, and a monthly report when a month has passed; a new scheduled report goes out at the next run; the report runs with the access of the user who memorized it, and is skipped if that user's account is no longer active or has lost access to the report; the time of the last sending is shown in the Schedule column of Memorized Reports, and each sending (or failure) is recorded in the audit trail. Note Nothing is sent when Email to is empty, or when the administrator has not set the sender up on the server. The attached file has the report's standard columns and all its rows, whatever layout was used on the screen.

The Modify Report panel, which works like the Modify Report window of QuickBooks, changes how a report looks and what it prints: which columns (the report's own and fields from the records behind each row), which rows, the heading and the foot, the fonts, how the figures are written, and the printed page. It is on every report. It needs the special permission Can design report layouts (Administrators always have it). A modified report can be used just for now, or saved as a layout, shared with the other users and made the one the report opens with. Click Modify Report in the title bar of any report. The panel opens between the filter bar and the report. Click Modify Report again to close it. While a saved layout is in use, the button reads Modify Report: followed by the layout's name. The panel has eight tabs: Columns , Rows , Heading , Fonts & look , Figures , Footer , Page and Layouts .
