Two kinds of change work differently: Fonts, sizes, colours, shading, lines, the words of the heading and the foot, and which heading lines show, change on the report as you pick them. So do showing or hiding a column, its width, its alignment and its heading, for the columns already on the report. Changes to what is printed (moving columns, the rows, the figures, the page) wait. The note Some changes show once you press "Show it this way". appears; click Show it this way to see them. The buttons at the foot of the panel: Show it this way redraws the report with every choice on the panel. Nothing is saved yet, but the report as shown can be printed, exported, e-mailed and memorized. Back to the plain report opens the report without any layout, keeping its dates and filters. The Columns tab The tab lists every column the report can print: first the report's own columns, then the related fields , the fields of the records its rows come from. A row of the Sales by Customer Detail report, for example, comes from a transaction and from a customer, so the memo, the class, the site or the status of the transaction, and the phone, the e-mail, the terms or the credit limit of the customer, can all be added to the report with a tick. The field says which record it comes from: Memo from the transaction , Phone from the customer . Column What it does Handle Drag the dotted handle at the start of a row to move the column. Print Tick to print the column, untick to leave it out. Column The column's standard name. (extra) marks a column the report offers but prints only when ticked; from the transaction , from the customer , from the supplier , from the item , from the account or from the fixed asset marks a related field. Heading printed Type the words to print over the column. Empty keeps the standard heading. Width Auto (fits the text), Narrow , Medium or Wide . Lines up Auto , Left , Middle or Right . Move To the start, up one, down one, to the end. Above the list, Find a column or field narrows the list as you type (for example "phone"), and a link per kind of record, such as Transaction fields (16) or Customer fields (14) , scrolls to that group. Under the list, Print all its own columns ticks every column of the report itself, Back to the standard columns undoes every change on this tab, and Take out the added fields unticks every related field at once. The line beside the buttons counts the columns that print and how many of them are added fields. Any column can be moved, the Date or the Name column included, and an added field can be dragged among the report's own columns, renamed, widened and lined up like any other. The related fields on offer: Record Fields Transaction Transaction type, date and number, Name (customer, supplier or payee), Reference number, Memo, Class, Site, Terms, Due date, Ship date, Status, Transaction total, Entered by, Entered on, Approved by. Customer Customer name, Company name, Contact person, Phone, Mobile, Email, Billing address, TIN, Terms, Customer type, Sales rep, Price level, Credit limit, Balance owed today. Supplier Supplier name, Company name, Contact person, Phone, Fax, Email, Address, TIN, Terms, Our account number with them, Credit limit, Balance owed today. Item Item code, Item name, Barcode, Sales description, Purchase description, Category, Item type, Unit, Tax code, Item status, Cost, Average cost, Sales price, Reorder point, Maximum stock, Preferred supplier, On hand today (all sites), Asset value today, Retail value today, Gross profit per unit (price less average cost), Gross profit % per unit, Markup % on average cost. The cost and profit fields are offered only to users who may view costs. A report that everybody can shape column by column is the Customized Inventory Report . Account Account number, Account name, Account type, Category, Parent account, Description, Bank account number. Fixed asset Asset number, Asset, Category, Location, Serial number, Date acquired, Cost, Status. Which records a report offers depends on what its rows point at: a report whose numbers open a transaction offers the transaction's fields and those of its customer or supplier; a report whose names open a customer, a supplier, an item or an account offers that record's fields; the asset reports offer the asset's. Group headings, subtotals and totals have no record behind them, so their cells in an added column stay empty. Note The fields are looked up only when they print, and only for the rows on the report, so a report without added fields is as fast as it was. Cost and Average cost appear only for users with View costs and margins , and Bank account number only for users who may see bank balances. Added fields go into the spreadsheet export, into the scheduled e-mail of a memorized report, and into a saved layout, and the report can be sorted by them like by any column. Tip: To make a collections list from the Open Invoices report, add Phone and Email from the customer and Memo from the transaction , drag them next to the customer's name, and save the result as a layout called "Collections list". The Rows tab Field What it does Which rows Every row , or Only the group headings, subtotals and totals for a summary. A report without groups says so under the box. Rows whose figures are all zero Show them or Leave them out . Only rows containing Prints only the detail rows that contain the text typed, in any column. Capitals do not matter. At most this many rows (0 = all of them) Stops after that many detail rows. Subtotal rows Untick to leave the subtotals out. Grand total row Untick to leave the grand total out. Rows taken out one by one: while the panel is open, a small button with a crossed-out eye appears at the start of each row of the report. Click it to take that row out; the row is greyed out until you click Show it this way . The taken-out rows are listed on the right, each with Put back ; Put them all back returns them all. When none is taken out, the list says None taken out. A row is recognised by the words in its first columns, so it stays out whenever the report is run. Note Leaving rows out changes what prints, not the figures: every total is still the total of the whole report. A line above the report (not printed) says how many rows are taken out or left out. The Heading tab Field What it does Report title A title of your own. Empty keeps the report's name. Line under the title One line under the title, for example "For the board meeting". More lines under the title Extra lines, one per line of the box, up to eight. The heading sits On the left , In the middle or On the right . Title in capital letters Prints the title in capitals. Company name Shows the company name. Company address Shows the address from the company settings. Company TIN Shows the TIN from the company settings. Company logo Shows the company logo. Dates and filters line The line with the dates and filters under the title. "Prepared on ..." line under the heading A line with the date, the time and the name of the person running the report, under the dates line. Off as delivered. A line under the heading A rule between the heading and the table. A note under a box says when it cannot show anything yet: No address in the company settings yet , No TIN in the company settings yet , No logo uploaded yet , or Not ticked for this report under Company, Security & Closing Date . The company details and the logo, and the reports the logo prints on, are set in Company, Security & Closing Date . The Fonts & look tab THE HEADING Font : one of Standard (Segoe UI), Arial, Calibri, Tahoma, Verdana, Century Gothic, Times New Roman, Georgia, Cambria, Garamond, Bookman Old Style, Courier New or Consolas. Nothing is downloaded: if a computer does not have the font, the browser uses a similar one. Title size : Small , Normal , Large or Extra large . Company name size : Small , Normal or Large . Colour : Black , Dark grey , Blue or Green . THE COLUMN HEADINGS Font and Size ( Small , Normal , Large ). Shading : None , Light grey , Dark, white letters or Blue, white letters . Line up : Over their figures (text left, amounts right) , All on the left or All in the middle . In bold , In capital letters , and Long headings may take two lines . THE ROWS Font and Size ( Small , Normal , Large ). Row height : Normal , Tight (more rows to a page) or Roomy . The grand total : Line above, double line below , A line above , In bold only or Shaded band . Shade every other row , Lines between the columns , A border round the table and Shade the group headings . The Figures tab Field Choices Negative figures With a minus sign -1,234.00 , In brackets (1,234.00) , In red -1,234.00 or In red brackets (1,234.00) . Zero figures Show 0.00 , Leave the cell empty or Show a dash . Decimal places on money Two (1,234.56) or None (1,235) . Show the money figures As they are (1,234,567.00) , In thousands (1,235) or In millions (1.2) . The heading then says "amounts in thousands" or "amounts in millions". Currency sign None , On the totals or On every amount . The sign is ₱, from the system settings. Thousands separator (1,234) Untick to print 1234 instead of 1,234. The Footer tab Field What it does Text at the foot of the report Your own text, for example "Confidential: for internal use only". Up to eight lines. The foot text sits On the left , In the middle or On the right . A line above the foot A rule between the table (or the signature lines) and the foot text. "Printed on ... by ..." line The line with the date, time and name of the person who printed the report. Page numbers on the printed pages "Page 1 of 3" at the foot of each page (Chrome and Edge). Signature lines at the foot Prints signature lines under the report. Caption under each signature line One caption per line, up to four. As delivered: Prepared by, Checked by, Approved by. Names printed above the captions The names to print above the lines, in the same order as the captions. Example For a trial balance to be signed, tick Signature lines at the foot , keep the three captions, and type the names of the bookkeeper, the chief accountant and the owner, one per line, in Names printed above the captions . The Page tab Field Choices Paper The printer's own , A4 (210 x 297 mm) , Letter (8.5 x 11 in) , Long / Folio (8.5 x 13 in) or Legal (8.5 x 14 in) . Printed page Upright (portrait) or Sideways (landscape) . Margins Narrow (6 mm) , Normal (12 mm) or Wide (20 mm) . Report title at the top of every printed page From the second printed page on, in the top margin (Chrome and Edge). These settings are for the printed page only. Click Print / PDF above the report to see them. The Layouts tab Open a saved layout lists Standard (no layout) and every layout of this report that is yours or shared, marked (opens by default) and shared where they apply. Choosing one opens the report in it. When there is none, the tab says No layout saved for this report yet. Save this layout opens the window described below. Delete followed by the layout's name deletes the layout that is open. It appears for the layout's owner and for administrators. Every saved layout opens Saved Report Layouts .

t: Saving, sharing and deleting a layout
x: A layout keeps everything set on the Modify Report panel's tabs, the added fields included, so the report can be opened the same way again, by you or by everyone. Field What it does Name The layout's name, for example "Trial Balance for the bank". Replace "..." instead of adding another Shown when the layout that is open is yours, and ticked: saving updates it. Untick to save a new layout. Open this report with this layout from now on Makes it the layout the report opens with. Let the other users use it too Shares it. Users who cannot design reports can then choose it from their Layouts button. Step by step: save a layout Open the report and click Modify Report . Make your changes on the tabs. There is no need to click Show it this way first: everything on the panel is saved, including changes not shown yet. Open the Layouts tab and click Save this layout . Type a Name . Tick Open this report with this layout from now on and Let the other users use it too as needed. Click Save the layout . The report opens in the new layout, with the message Layout "Trial Balance for the bank" saved. It is on the Modify Report panel of that report. Default and shared layouts A layout marked as the default opens whenever the report is opened by someone who can see it: only you for a private layout, everyone for a shared one. A report has one default at a time. Making a layout the default takes the mark off the report's other layouts that you can see. To see the report without its default layout, click Back to the plain report on the Modify Report panel, choose Standard under Layouts , or choose Standard (no layout) on the Layouts tab. A layout can be changed only by its owner, and deleted by its owner or an administrator. To adapt someone else's layout, open it, change it and save it under a new name. Important Making one of your private layouts the default also takes the mark off a shared layout that was the default for everyone, and nobody else sees your private layout. Everyone else then gets the plain report. Keep the default on a shared layout when others rely on it. Step by step: delete a layout Open the report in the layout (Layouts tab > Open a saved layout ). Click Delete followed by the layout's name. Click Delete it to confirm. The report itself is not changed. The program says Layout deleted. Layouts can also be deleted on the Saved Report Layouts page. Message What it means Give the layout a name. The Name box is empty. That layout belongs to another user, so it cannot be changed here. Save it under a new name instead. Untick Replace and save a new layout. Saving a report layout needs the "Can design report layouts" permission. An administrator can give it to your role. Your role lacks the permission.

Columns with costs and margins appear only for users with the special permission View costs and margins . Reports based on sites show only the sites you may see. Some reports print a note under the title, for example the Accounts Receivable Graph's "A few customers owing a large share of the total indicates concentration risk." Saving a layout also needs access to the Saved Report Layouts page, and memorizing needs access to the Memorized Reports page. Ask your administrator if the buttons are missing.

Memorized Reports lists the reports you memorized and those other users shared, with their schedules. Use it to open them, check when a scheduled report was last sent, and remove the ones no longer needed. Where to find it: Home > Memorized Reports. The columns Column What it shows Group The group given when memorizing. The list is sorted by group, then name. Name The memorized report's name. Click it to open the report. If you may not open the report, the name is not a link and no access is shown beside it. Report The report it is based on, for example Income Statement. Shared Yes when it is shared with the other users. Schedule For a scheduled report: how often, the address and the time it was last sent. Owner The username of the person who memorized it. Remove Deletes the memorized report. Shown to its owner and to administrators. Step by step: open a memorized report Open Home > Memorized Reports . Click the report's Name . It opens with its memorized dates, filters and layout. Step by step: remove a memorized report Click Remove on its line. Click OK to confirm Remove this memorized report? The program says Memorized report removed. The removal is recorded in the audit trail. Step by step: change a memorized report A memorized report cannot be edited in place. To change it: Open it from the list. Change the dates, filters or layout. Memorize it again, under the same name if you wish. Remove the old one. Good to know To memorize a report, open the report and click Memorize (see Working with reports ). Scheduled reports are e-mailed by tools/send_scheduled_reports.php , which your administrator runs daily; the page says so above the list. When the list is empty it says No memorized reports yet.

Saved Report Layouts lists every report layout that is yours or shared with you, for all reports at once, so they can be kept tidy: opened, made the default, or deleted. Layouts are made on the report itself, with the Modify Report button. Where to find it: Home > Saved Report Layouts, or Every saved layout on the Layouts tab of the Modify Report panel. The columns Column What it shows Report The report the layout belongs to. Click it to open the report in this layout. Layout The layout's name, with its own report title under it when it has one. Columns How many of the report's columns it prints, for example 4 of 4 shown , or standard . Owner Who saved it, marked shared when others may use it. (default) opens by default when the report opens with this layout. Buttons Button What it does Make default Makes this layout the one its report opens with. Shown to users who may design reports, on layouts that are not the default yet. Delete (bin icon) Deletes the layout after you confirm. Shown to its owner and to administrators. Step by step: make a layout the default Click Make default on its line. The program says, for example, "Trial Balance for the bank" now opens by default. Any other default layout of that report that you can see loses its mark. Step by step: delete a layout Click the bin button on its line. Click OK to confirm Delete the layout followed by its name. The program says Layout deleted. The report itself is not changed. When no layout is saved, the list says No layouts saved yet. Open a report and press Modify Report. Good to know To change a layout, open it from the Report column, click Modify Report , make the changes and save it with Replace ticked (see Working with reports ). There is no button to take the default mark off without choosing another default; to stop a layout opening by default, make another layout the default, or delete it.

Win the work. Record the lead or tender in Leads & Tenders , decide to bid, prepare the estimate . Sign the contract. Enter it in Contracts with its amount, advance, retention, liquidated damages and bonds, and send it for approval. Set up the project. Project Set-up creates the project, its class and its stockyard. Add the BOQ , turn the approved estimate into the budget , build the schedule and its milestones . Build. Every day: timesheets , daily site reports and equipment logs . As needed: material requests , canvass , purchase orders, deliveries and issues ; subcontracts and their billings ; change orders ; inspections and safety records. Bill and collect. Each month a progress billing on the schedule of values, certified by the client and invoiced; payments received in accounting; revenue recognized at month end; shared costs allocated . Close. Close-out : punch list, final billing, retention release, warranty, and financial closure once nothing is left open. Documents that need someone's decision go through approvals . The route decides who approves at each step; nobody approves a document they submitted, and each step is kept with the name, date, time and comment.

t: Project Center and the project workspace
x: Where to find it: Projects > Project Center. The list shows the projects you may see (your own projects, or all of them if your role or your account allows it) with their progress, contract value, cost and status. The project picker at the top of every screen remembers the project you work on, so the lists of the other pages open on it. Click a project to open its workspace ( Project Workspace). The tabs show everything about it in one place: Overview: contract value with variations, work completed, cost to date and committed, estimated final cost, projected profit and margin, collections and receivables, the project in figures, its status and what waits for approval. Budget & cost: budget against actual and committed by cost code, estimate at completion. Schedule & milestones , Billing & collections , Materials, labor & equipment , Quality & safety and Documents & records . The Record button opens the forms of the project (site report, timesheet, material request, billing and so on) with the project filled in.

Creates and edits projects: code (the next number is offered), name, client, contract, location, project manager, site engineer and quantity surveyor, division, contract value, start and target finish dates, floor area, and how progress is measured (from the schedule, or a figure kept on the project). What the program records: saving a new project creates its class in Financial Set-up > Class List and, when asked, an inventory site for its stockyard, and adds the standard close-out checklist. The project's team (manager, engineer, QS and the members added) are the users who see it when Construction Settings limits each user to their own projects. The status follows the work: Planning, Mobilization, Active (set when the first site report is approved), On hold, Substantially completed, Completed, Under warranty and Closed. Closing goes through Close-out .

The clients are the customers of accounting: the same record, with its terms, TIN, the taxes it withholds (for example 2% for contractors, and 5% VAT for a government office) and a client class (government, private, corporate, institutional). A client's page shows its contracts, projects, billings and receivables.

A contract holds the client, title and client reference, scope, type (lump sum, unit price, cost-plus, time and materials, hybrid), the original amount net of VAT, the tax code and withholding taxes, payment terms, the advance and its recoupment percentage, the retention percentage and its cap, liquidated damages, warranty and defects liability periods, the key dates (signing, notice to proceed, commencement, completion) and its bonds and insurance. Submit contract for approval sends it along its route (in the sample: Project Director, then General Manager). Once approved it is Active : its client, amount, type, advance and retention are locked, and its value changes only through change orders . A project can be billed only when its contract is active.

The pipeline of work: each lead or tender with the client or prospect, source (PhilGEPS, referral, invitation to bid), estimated value and cost, probability, bid due date, status (lead, qualifying, bidding, submitted, won, lost, no bid), the bid or no-bid decision with its reasons, the bid security, and the tender document checklist. A won tender is turned into a project.

An estimate lists the cost of the work by category (materials, labor, equipment, subcontract, hauling, site preparation, utilities, permits, temporary facilities, site administration, project and corporate overhead, contingency) and cost code, with quantity, unit and unit cost. The contingency and markup percentages give the total price. Each estimate of a project or tender is a new version; an approved one is never edited. From an approved estimate, budget from estimate prepares the project's first budget, summed by cost code and cost type.

The bill of quantities as priced in the contract: item number, description, unit, quantity and unit rate, and the cost code each line belongs to. It is the schedule of values the progress billings are made on. A line that carries the work of one activity can be linked to it, so a billing ahead of that activity's verified progress is flagged. Lines of client-approved change orders are added by the program, marked as variations. A line that has been billed cannot be removed or lowered below what was billed.

The budget of a project by cost code and cost type. It goes through its approval route (in the sample: project manager, project director, finance manager). The first approved budget is the baseline ; later changes are revisions (a revision copies the budget in force; a client-approved change order prepares one for its cost impact). An approved budget is never edited, so the original and the current budget are always both available. Material requests, purchases and subcontracts are checked against the remaining budget of their cost code (Construction Settings decides whether going over warns or blocks).

The activities of a project, written as a work breakdown: WBS code (1.2 sits under 1), name, cost code, planned start and finish, weight, planned quantity and unit, budget man-hours, predecessors and milestones. Predecessors are written with the WBS code and, when needed, the type and lag: 2.1 , 2.1SS+10 , 2.3FF-5 . Loops are refused. The tabs: Gantt chart by day, week or month, with the baseline under each bar and today's line. Activities and logic: the grid of activities. Work out the critical path runs the forward and backward pass, sets the early dates, the total float and the critical activities. Set baseline keeps the planned dates for comparison. Update progress: quantity done or percent, actual start and finish. Approved daily site reports update the progress by themselves. Three-week look-ahead and Earned value (planned value, earned value, actual cost, CPI, SPI, estimate at completion). The physical progress of a project is the weighted progress of its activities.

Each milestone has its scope, scheduled date, billable value, measurement method, the person responsible and a different reviewer, whether the client must certify it, and its deliverables (accomplishment report, photos, inspection report, test results, engineer certification, signed acceptance, as-built drawings), each required or not. The steps: deliverables marked submitted, the milestone submitted by the person responsible, put under review , then accepted with the approved completion or rejected with the reason, and the client's certification recorded. A milestone becomes billable only when it is accepted, every required deliverable is accepted, its completion is 100% (or certified by the client) and the client's certification is in when the contract needs it. The program decides this; nobody ticks it by hand.

Requests for more time with the cause (weather, client delay, variation, force majeure and others), the days requested and the decision: granted, partially granted or rejected. Days granted move the project's revised finish date.

The work items every cost is charged to (01 General Requirements, 03-300 Structural Concrete and so on), each with its usual cost type and, when wanted, the ledger account it is charged to. Cost codes are shared by all projects and are copied to a new company.

A change order records a change to the work: type (client request, additional work, scope reduction, claim and others), who asked for it, the reason, its lines with price and cost by cost code, and its effect on time, labor, equipment and billing. Submit for internal approval. The route depends on the amount (in the sample, from P1M the General Manager approves too). Record the client's approval with its date and reference (or the settlement amount of a claim). From that moment the change is part of the revised contract value, its lines join the schedule of values so they can be billed, the completion date moves by its days, and a budget revision is prepared for its cost. Pending change orders are shown beside the contract value but are not billable.

One report per project per day: weather in the morning and afternoon, site conditions, manpower and man-hours (offered from the day's timesheets), equipment used, materials used, the accomplishment of each activity (quantity, or percentage points for activities measured in percent), delays and their hours, safety observations, inspections, instructions received, issues, and photos. The report is written by the foreman or engineer and approved by the project manager. Approving it adds its accomplishment to the schedule. The form keeps a draft on the phone when the site has no signal and sends it later. The list warns about working days without a report.

Inspection and test plans, quality checklists (from the checklist templates), material tests, equipment safety checks, pre-pour and final inspections, each with the location, inspector, checklist, findings and result: passed, passed with conditions, failed. A failed inspection leads to a nonconformance report .

A defect or deviation with the activity and cost code, the party responsible, the root cause, the corrective and preventive actions, the rework cost and the due date. Status: open, corrective action in progress, verified, closed. Open NCRs keep a project from being closed.

Incidents (with the persons involved, severity and lost-time hours), near misses, toolbox meetings and trainings (with attendees), PPE issuance, permits to work (with their validity), hazard observations and equipment safety checks. The Quality and Safety report gives the incident rate per 200,000 man-hours.

Each worker's trade, classification (direct labor, indirect labor, site staff, labor-only subcontractor, agency), daily or hourly rate, overtime and holiday multipliers, burden percentage (employer contributions and benefits), daily allowance, shift and break, assigned project, skills, certifications and safety documents. A worker from a labor-only contractor or agency names that supplier: their hours are recorded but their cost comes through the supplier's bill. Every worker is also an employee name in accounting, so payroll and cash advances show by name in the ledger.
The trades (carpenter, mason, steelman, operator and others) with their usual daily rate, offered when a worker is added.

One timesheet per project, day and shift: each worker's time in and out (or hours), break, activity and cost code, absent or holiday, remarks. The program works out regular and overtime hours, minutes late and undertime, and the cost at the worker's rate with burden and allowance. Checks: a worker cannot be on two timesheets at overlapping times (on any project), nor over the maximum hours a day; attendance is not recorded for future days. What the program records when the project manager approves it: a journal entry by project and cost code, Dr Direct Labor (or Site Supervision for indirect labor and site staff) and Labor Burden, Cr Accrued Payroll and the statutory contributions payable. An approved timesheet is corrected by reopening it with the reason.

A run gathers the approved timesheets of a pay period not yet paid: days, regular and overtime hours, gross pay, allowances, the cash advances to deduct and the other deductions (the employees' share of SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG, loans). It is approved (in the sample, chief accountant then finance manager) and posted: Dr Accrued Payroll by project, Cr Salaries and Wages Payable, Employee Advances and the contributions payable. The net pay is then paid in Banking (a check or a transfer to the payroll account). Payslips print from the run.

A worker's request with the amount and purpose goes for approval (the request notes any amount still owed). Once approved it is released from a cash or bank account (a cash voucher, Dr Advances to Employees) and deducted in the next payroll run.

Every unit: type, make and model, plate or serial number, ownership (owned, rented, leased, with the lessor), the fixed asset record of an owned unit, how it is costed (a standard rate per operating hour and per idle hour, the rental bills, or actual costs), the meter (hours or km), fuel, the usual operator, insurance, inspection and registration dates, and the meter reading of the next service. Status: available, deployed, idle, under repair, off-hired, disposed.

Books a unit for a project from one date to another, then records it going out and coming back with the meter readings. A unit is never booked on two projects at the same time, and a unit whose insurance expires before the dispatch starts cannot go out. The booking board shows the next two weeks of every unit.

The daily log of a unit on a project: operating, idle and breakdown hours, meter at the start and end of the day, fuel, operator, activity and cost code. The unit must be dispatched to that project that day, works on one project a day and not more than 24 hours. The charge is the operating hours at the hourly rate plus the idle hours at the idle rate. What the program records when the project manager approves it: Dr Equipment Costs Charged (project and cost code), Cr Equipment Cost Recovery (the company's), so each project carries the cost of the fleet it used while the fleet's own costs (fuel, repairs, depreciation) stay with the company.

The engineer or foreman requests materials for a project: items, quantities, cost codes and activity, the date needed, and whether they are delivered to the site (the project's stockyard) or to the warehouse. On submission the request is checked against the remaining budget of each cost code; a request over budget is flagged as high risk on its approval (or refused, if Construction Settings blocks it). The route depends on the amount (in the sample, the project manager, and from P100,000 also the purchasing manager). An approved request is canvassed, ordered, delivered and issued; its status follows: approved, partially ordered, ordered, issued, closed.

A canvass starts from an approved material request. Each supplier's quotation is entered with its reference, delivery days, terms, validity and its price for each line. The comparison shows the total of each quotation, whether it is complete, the lowest price of each line and the lowest complete quotation. Award chooses the supplier. Choosing anything but the lowest complete quotation, or buying on a single quotation, needs the reason. The award goes for approval by amount; once approved the program writes the purchase order in accounting, charged to the project and its cost codes and delivered where the request said.

The purchase orders of the projects still to be received (late ones are marked), received in accounting's Receive Items or entered as the supplier's bill against the order, so stock and payables are recorded once. The deliveries of the last 60 days are listed for the quality check: the quantity accepted and rejected with the reason. A rejected quantity goes back to the supplier on a supplier debit memo.

Issue to project: materials taken from the warehouse or the stockyard for the work, by cost code and activity. The stock on hand is checked. Return from project: unused materials back to stock; the project's cost is credited. Use on site (consumption): when Construction Settings costs materials when used, the quantities used and wasted reported from site. Transfer to another project: approved by the project manager of the giving project and the operations manager; the cost moves from one project to the other. What the program records: with materials costed when issued, an issue is an inventory adjustment Dr Direct Materials (project, cost code), Cr Inventory. With materials costed when used, an issue moves the stock to the project's stockyard and the consumption charges the project.

For each project and material: bought, issued, returned, used, wasted and transferred, and what is left at the stockyard (the material reconciliation), with the warehouse items at or below their reorder point.

The subcontractors are suppliers of kind subcontractor: their trades, accreditation (PCAB licence) and its expiry, qualifications, rating, tax code and the withholding tax deducted from their payments. A subcontract cannot be submitted while the accreditation is expired.

The work package, scope, items (quantity, unit, rate, cost code and the activity whose progress verifies it), retention, advance and its recoupment, tax code, dates and terms. On submission the items are checked against the budget. Once approved the agreement is active; it is changed only through a variation. The agreement's page shows what was billed, retained, recouped and paid. An advance is paid in Vendors > Advances to Suppliers and recouped from the billings.

The subcontractor's progress claim (entered here or sent through the subcontractor portal with their invoice attached): quantities accomplished this period per item, back charges and penalties. The program works out the gross, retention, recoupment of the advance actually paid, VAT and the net. Checks: the same invoice number is never recorded twice for a subcontractor (here or as a bill in accounting); no item past its contract quantity; no item billed more than 5 points ahead of the progress verified on site. What the program records when it is approved (in the sample: QS, project manager, finance manager, and from P500,000 the General Manager): a bill, Dr Subcontract Costs + Input VAT, less Retention Payable, less back charges, Cr Accounts Payable, with the advance applied for the recoupment. The bill is paid in Pay Bills with the withholding tax. A completed subcontract's retention is released with a retention release billing.

The kinds of billing: progress on the schedule of values (percent or quantity per line), quantity-based for unit-price contracts, milestone (only billable milestones), time and materials, change order, final, advance (mobilization), and retention release. The billing shows each line's scheduled value, previous, this period and to date; the gross accomplishment; materials stored on site; the retention (up to its cap), the recoupment of the advance, other deductions, VAT, the tax the client is expected to withhold, and the amount due. Checks: no line past 100% and no billing past the revised contract unless an authorized adjustment is recorded by someone with Approve on billings; a billing ahead of the verified physical progress is flagged. The steps: Submit billing for approval (in the sample: project manager, QS, chief accountant, finance manager, General Manager). Send out to the client. Record the client's certificate with its date and reference. If the client certifies less than was applied for, the lines are scaled down and retention, recoupment and VAT worked out again. The program then makes the invoice in accounting. The client's payment is received in Customers > Receive Payments, with the taxes the client withheld. What the program records on the invoice of a progress billing: Dr Accounts Receivable for the amount due, Dr Retention Receivable, Dr Advances from Clients for the recoupment, Cr Progress Billings on Contracts (a contract liability) and Output VAT. An advance billing credits Advances from Clients; a retention release credits Retention Receivable. When revenue follows the billings (Construction Settings), the accomplishment is credited to Contract Revenue instead. The client representative can also certify billings in the client portal .

At each period end the revenue earned is worked out by the method in Construction Settings: percentage of completion by cost (cost to date over estimated total cost), by physical progress, at completion of the contract, or as billed. The recognition shows the contract value, estimated total cost, cost to date, percent complete, revenue earned to date, recognized before, this period, and the provision for a loss when the estimated cost is higher than the contract. Approved (in the sample by the chief accountant), it posts Dr Contract Assets, Cr Contract Revenue, and the loss provision when needed. Only the latest recognition of a project can be reversed. The Work-in-Progress report compares the revenue earned with the billings: under-billings and over-billings. When a project is completed, the progress billings are settled against the contract assets.
The invoices of each project with what is collected, open and overdue, and the payments received with the taxes withheld. Payments themselves are entered in Customers > Receive Payments.
Retention held by clients (receivable) and retention held from subcontractors (payable) by project, the advances not yet recouped, and when each retention falls due for release.

Costs shared by several projects (the yard and warehouse, a crane serving two sites, the safety officer) are entered in accounting without a project, then allocated here: the source (a transaction or an amount of an expense account), the period, the basis (equal shares, man-hours, equipment hours, direct cost, materials, contract value, revenue, floor area, fixed shares or custom units from an allocation rule) and the projects. The program shows each project's share before it is approved. Approved (in the sample: chief accountant and finance manager), it posts a reclassification: Cr the expense account without a project, Dr the same account for each project. The same cost is never allocated twice. A posted allocation is reversed or reallocated (the new one replaces it when it is approved), never edited.
Named bases for allocations, and for fixed shares or custom units, the share of each project.

Project costs entered in accounting without a cost code (for example a check charged to a project's class), listed so each can be given its cost code. The shared expenses waiting to be allocated are listed too.

The documents waiting for you: the document, project, amount, the step and how long it has waited (overdue ones are marked). Open one to see it in full, then Approve , Return for correction, Reject (both need the reason, which is sent to the person who submitted it), Delegate the step to another user, or Escalate it to the General Manager and the owner. The count beside Approvals in the menu shows how many wait for you. Approval History lists every request with each step taken, by whom and when, and can be exported.

A route is chosen by the kind of document, the amount (from and below), the project (or every project) and the risk (high-risk documents, such as a request over budget, can follow a stricter route). Each step is for a role, for one user, or for the project's own manager, engineer or quantity surveyor, with the hours before it is overdue. A document with no matching route needs one approval by a user with Approve on its page.

The document register of a project: drawings, specifications, BOQ, method statements, permits and others by discipline, each with its revisions (the file, notes, status and who approved it). The current revision is shown; superseded ones are kept.

Requests for information, submittals, shop drawings, material submittals, transmittals and technical approvals: who sent them to whom, the date due, the response and its date, and the status (open, answered, approved, approved as noted, revise and resubmit, rejected, closed).
The project's registers: risks (probability, impact, cost and days at stake, response), issues, decisions, site instructions, correspondence, meeting minutes, delays and the diary.

Close-out checklist: the standard items (final accomplishment, punch list cleared, certificate of completion, as-built drawings, manuals and warranties, final billing and collection, retention release, subcontractors closed out, warranty registered, final cost reviewed), each pending, in progress, completed or waived. Punch list and defects: location, description, party responsible, severity, due date, cost, and whether the warranty covers it. An item is closed only after it is rectified and verified. Warranty: starts the defects liability period from the completion date. Financial closure: the program lists what is still open: purchase orders, client and supplier balances, retention both ways, advances, pending approvals, unposted documents, punch items, checklist items, NCRs, active subcontracts and revenue not yet recognized. A project with open items is closed only as a documented exception approved along the closure route.

A client representative (a user linked to the client) sees only the client's own projects: progress and schedule, milestones, billings and statements, change orders, documents and site photos. They can certify a billing, approve or decline a change order, and send a message to the project manager.

A subcontractor's user sees their agreements with the progress verified on site, their billings and payments, and the retention held. They submit a progress billing with their invoice attached; the quantity surveyor and the project manager are notified to check it.

Where to find them: Reports > Report Center, group Project Reports. Each report shows only the projects you may see and can be narrowed to one project, client, project manager or status; it prints, exports to a spreadsheet, can be memorized and e-mailed like every other report, and its Columns box shows the optional columns. Project financials: Project Portfolio Summary, Project Income Statement, Project Cost Breakdown, Budget versus Actual Cost, Committed Costs and Open Purchase Orders, Estimate at Completion, Estimated Cost to Complete, Project Cash Flow Statement, Project Profitability Forecast, Work-in-Progress / Contract Position, Earned Revenue versus Billing, Client Profitability. Billing and collections: Project Billing Statement, Project Collections Statement, Accounts Receivable Aging by Project, Retention Receivables. Costs and resources: Project Accounts Payable, Material Consumption and Wastage, Worker Man-hours and Labor Cost, Labor Productivity, Equipment Utilization, Subcontractor Statement, Cost Allocations, Supplier Spend by Project. Contracts and progress: Change Order Register, Contract Summary, Earned Value, Milestones and Deliverables, Quality and Safety. The Executive Dashboard shows the portfolio: contract value, estimated cost and profit, billings and collections, receivables, cash needed in the next 30 days, projects over budget or behind schedule, equipment and manpower, and the large approvals waiting. The Project Manager Dashboard shows your approvals, deliverables pending, cost against budget, work ready to bill, manpower on site today, equipment, site issues and material requests in progress. The Finance Dashboard shows bank and cash balances, receivables and payables with their aging, collections expected in the next 30 days, retention both ways, the margins and receivables of each project, and the finance approvals waiting.

Where to find it: System Administration > Construction Settings. Revenue recognition: percentage of completion by cost or by physical progress, at completion, or as the billings are certified. Changing it after revenue was recognized needs the reason. When materials become project cost: when issued to the project, or when the site reports them used. Billing past a line of the schedule of values: refuse (unless an authorized adjustment is recorded) or warn. Requests and commitments past the budget: refuse until a revision is approved, or warn and flag the approval as high risk. VAT on progress billings: on the accomplishment less the advance recouped, or on the gross accomplishment. Who sees which project: only the project's team (and the users or roles marked all projects), or every user with access to the page. Maker-checker: nobody approves what they submitted, or (small companies) allowed. The usual retention, regular hours a day, the most hours a worker can log in a day, when an approval step is overdue, and the project code prefix.

The Chart of Accounts is the list of every account the books use: cash and bank accounts, receivables, inventory, payables, equity, income and expenses. Here you add accounts, group them under parent accounts, mark the ones that keep a subsidiary ledger, and open the ledger or the register of any account. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Chart of Accounts The accounts are shown in five cards, Assets , Liabilities , Equity , Incomes and Expenses , each sorted by code. A sub-account is indented under its parent with an arrow, for example 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking under 1000 Cash. Accounts that the modules need, such as 1100 Accounts Receivable, 1200 Inventory and 2000 Accounts Payable, carry a grey system tag. Tick Include inactive accounts above the list to show the accounts you have made inactive; they appear greyed out. The columns Column What it shows Code The account code. The list is sorted by it. Name The account name. Click it to open the General Ledger of this account. Type The account type (see the table below). Normal Debit or Credit : the side that increases the account. With SL Yes when the account keeps a subsidiary ledger. Balance The balance of the account on its normal side, for all dates. A negative balance is shown in brackets. Links Edit , Register and Delete , for the users allowed to use them. The balance of a parent account is only what was posted to the parent itself; the balances of its sub-accounts are not added to it. In the demo company, 1000 Cash shows 0.00 while its sub-account 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking shows 815,734.14. Bank balances show as ••• to a user who has neither the special permission View bank balances outside Banking nor access to Use Register . Account types The account type decides where the account appears on the statements and which forms offer it. The category and the normal balance follow from the type. Account type Category Normal balance Section on the statements Bank Asset Debit Current Assets; counts as cash on the Statement of Cash Flows Accounts Receivable Asset Debit Current Assets Other Current Asset Asset Debit Current Assets Fixed Asset Asset Debit Fixed Assets Other Asset Asset Debit Other Assets Accounts Payable Liability Credit Current Liabilities Credit Card Liability Credit Current Liabilities Other Current Liability Liability Credit Current Liabilities Long Term Liability Liability Credit Long-term Liabilities Equity Equity Credit Equity Income Income Credit Income Other Income Income Credit Other Income Cost of Goods Sold Expense Debit Cost of Goods Sold Expense Expense Debit Expenses Other Expense Expense Debit Other Expenses Some types also change what the forms allow: Bank accounts are the ones offered on Write Checks , Make Deposits , the cash account of a Cash Voucher and Reconcile . Create cash funds such as a petty cash fund or a revolving fund as Bank accounts too, so they can be paid out of and reconciled. Credit Card accounts can be chosen on Write Checks and Transfer Funds. Other Current Asset accounts can be chosen in Transfer Funds and as the Deposit to account of a sales receipt. A journal entry line to an Accounts Receivable account needs a customer, and a line to an Accounts Payable account needs a vendor. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Account type The type from the table above. A new account starts as Expense . Code Up to 20 characters. Every account needs its own code. Name Up to 120 characters. Sub-account of Leave blank for a main account, or choose the parent. Only main accounts are listed, and the parent must be of the same category (an asset under an asset, an expense under an expense). Type part of the code or name to search. Normal balance From type takes the normal balance of the type. Choose Debit or Credit only for a contra account (see below). Active Untick to stop offering the account on forms. It keeps its history and still shows on reports. With SL (keeps a subsidiary ledger) Tick when you want a listing of the names (customers, suppliers, employees, other names) that transacted this account. See "With SL" below. Bank account no. (bank accounts) The bank's account number, for your reference. Description A note about what the account is for. The form reminds you: "Contra accounts (accumulated depreciation, sales returns, drawings) use the opposite normal balance of their type." For example, 1525 Accumulated Depreciation - Machinery is a Fixed Asset account with a Credit normal balance, so it reduces the fixed assets on the Balance Sheet. Step by step To add an account: Open Financial Set-up & Reports > Chart of Accounts . Click New account . Choose the Account type . Type the Code and the Name . If the account belongs under another one, choose it in Sub-account of . Leave Normal balance at From type unless this is a contra account. Tick With SL if you want the account to keep a subsidiary ledger. For a bank account, type the Bank account no. Click Save account , or Save account & New to save it and start another one straight away. To change an account: Click Edit on the account's line. Change what you need. The title of the form shows the code, for example "Edit account 1000". Click Save account . To make an account inactive: Click Edit on the account's line. Untick Active . Click Save account . To delete an account: Find the account. A Delete link appears only on an account that is not a system account and whose balance is zero. Click Delete and confirm "Delete this account?". To open an account's register: click Register on its line. The link appears for Bank, Credit Card, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Other Current Asset and Other Current Liability accounts. See Use Register . To export the list: click Export . The file chart_of_accounts.csv holds the code, name, type, category, normal balance, parent, With SL, balance and active flag of every account shown. Export needs the print/export permission on this page. Buttons New account: opens a blank account form. Shown only to users with the special permission to change the Chart of Accounts. Export: downloads the list as a spreadsheet file. Module default accounts: opens Module Default Accounts . With SL: keeping a subsidiary ledger An account marked With SL keeps a listing of the names that transacted it, like a subsidiary ledger of advances to employees, deposits from customers or loans from officers. While the box is ticked: every journal entry, cash voucher and check that posts to the account must name a customer, supplier, employee or other name. On a journal entry or cash voucher the name is chosen on the line; on a check, the payee of the check counts for every line. saving without a name is refused with a message that names the account, for example "The account 1400 - Prepaid Expenses is marked "With SL", so the line posting to it needs a name: choose a customer, supplier, employee or other name." the Subsidiary Ledger and the Schedule of Accounts list the account and its names. The rule applies to entries saved after the box is ticked. Entries made earlier keep whatever name they had. What it records Adding or changing an account posts nothing. Every change is written to the audit trail. Good to know "Enter the account code and name." Both are required. "Another account uses this code." Choose a different code. "A sub-account must be under a parent account of the same category." Choose a parent of the same category, or change the type. "System accounts used by the modules cannot be made inactive." Accounts with the system tag must stay active. "This account has transactions; it cannot be moved to a different category." You can change the type within the same category (for example from Expense to Other Expense), but not from an expense to an asset once entries have been posted. "This account is in use. Make it inactive instead of deleting it." An account cannot be deleted while it has ledger entries or transaction lines, is a module default account, has sub-accounts, or is used on an item. Make it inactive instead. Without the special permission to change the Chart of Accounts, the list is read-only and the New account , Edit and Delete links do not appear.

Classes split the books your own way: by branch, department, project or product line. Every transaction form has a Class box, the class is copied to every ledger line the transaction posts, and the financial reports can be filtered by class or shown with one column per class. You name the classes yourself and can rename them at any time. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Class List The columns Column What it shows Class name The name shown on forms and reports. Description Your note about the class. Order The position of the class in drop-down lists (lowest first). Entries How many transactions carry this class. Net income (FY) Income less expenses posted with this class in the current fiscal year. Shown only to users who may open Income Statement by Class . Active Yes or No . Fields Field What to enter / what it means Class name Up to 80 characters, for example Main Branch, Piggery or Meat Shop. Two classes cannot share a name. Order in lists A whole number. Classes are listed from the lowest number up, then by name. Description An optional note, up to 255 characters. Active (offered on transaction forms) Untick to stop offering the class on new transactions. It stays on the transactions that already have it and in the report filters. Step by step To add a class: Open Financial Set-up & Reports > Class List . In the New class panel, type the Class name . Type the Order in lists and a Description if you want them. Click Save class , or Save class & New to add another one straight away. To rename or change a class: Click Edit on the class's line. The panel becomes Edit class . Change the name, order, description or Active box. Click Save class . Click Cancel to go back to a blank form without saving. To delete a class: click Delete on its line and confirm. The link appears only on a class that no transaction carries. Buttons Income Statement by Class and Balance Sheet by Class open the two reports that show one column per class. What it records Nothing is posted. The class you choose on a transaction is copied to its ledger lines when the transaction is saved. Good to know "Renaming a class changes its name everywhere, including past transactions and reports." Reports always show the current name. "Another class already has this name." Choose a different name. "Cebu Store is already used on transactions, so it cannot be deleted. Make it inactive instead." Any use counts, including a line of a journal entry or a POS terminal's default class. When you save a transaction with the Class box empty, the program asks first: No class selected , "This transaction has no class. It will be saved as Unclassified and will not appear under any class on the class reports." Click Choose a class to go back to the box, or Continue saving . The question is not asked while no class exists yet. On journal entries and cash vouchers each line can carry its own class. The class at the top of the form fills the class of every line that has an account.

This list holds the people and bodies that are paid or tracked without being a customer or a supplier: employees (cash advances, reimbursements), owners, government offices and the like. The names appear in the Paid to and SL lists of cash vouchers, in the Name list of journal entries and in the Pay to the order of list of checks, next to the customers and suppliers. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Employees & Other Names Three tabs filter the list: All , Employees and Other names . The columns Column What it shows Name The name as it appears in the pickers. Type Employee or Other name . Employee no. The employee number, if any. Position The position, or the relationship for other names. Phone The phone number. Active Yes or No . Fields Field What to enter / what it means Type Employee or Other name . On the Employees or Other names tab it starts with that type. Name Required, up to 120 characters. The same name cannot be entered twice with the same type. Employee no. Optional, for employees. Position / relationship For example Cashier, or "Permits and clearances". Phone Optional. TIN The tax identification number, if any. Address Optional. Notes Optional. Active Untick to leave the name out of the pickers. It stays on the documents that already have it. Step by step To add a name: Open Financial Set-up & Reports > Employees & Other Names . In the New name panel, choose the Type . Type the Name and the other details you have. Click Save name , or Save name & New to add another one. To change a name: click Edit on its line, change the details in the Edit name panel, and click Save name . To delete a name: click Delete on its line and confirm. The link appears only on names that no transaction carries. Buttons Cash Voucher opens the Cash Voucher page. Good to know "This name is already on the list." A name of the same type already exists. "Ella Ramos is already used on transactions, so it cannot be deleted. Make it inactive instead." In the pickers, employees are listed as "Ella Ramos (Employee)" and other names as "Barangay Treasurer (Other name)", so you can tell them from a customer or supplier with the same name. Adding a name here does not give that person a login. Users are managed in User Accounts .

A memorized transaction is a saved copy of a transaction you enter again and again: the monthly rent check, a standing invoice, the payroll journal entry. It keeps the names, accounts, items and amounts; the date and the document number are given each time it is entered. You can enter it from the list whenever you need it, get a reminder when it is due, or let the program enter it on its due date. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Memorized Transactions. The Home page also shows Memorized transactions due with an Open button when a reminder is due (see Home Dashboard ). The columns Column What it shows Name and type The name you gave it, with its type (Invoice, Bill, Check, Journal Entry, Inventory Adjustment and so on) and its notes underneath. Name on the transaction The customer, supplier or payee of the saved copy. Amount The total of the saved copy. Schedule How it is entered: Automatically , Reminder , When needed or, for an adjustment or a batch of invoices, Loaded when needed (the full wording shows when you point at it), with the frequency under it, for example "Every month" or "Every 2 weeks". Next due The next due date, with Due or Overdue under it when a reminder is due. Entered How many times it was entered, for example "3 of 12 times" when a number is set, with the date of the last entry under it. Lines with a reminder due are marked with a coloured edge. Inactive ones are greyed out. When you use groups, each group has its own heading line. Memorizing a transaction You add to this list in two ways, for users who may create memorized transactions: From the form, before saving: Memorize Transaction beside the save buttons of every transaction form (see Memorize Transaction and Load Memorized Transaction ), and Memorize Adjustment on Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand . Item receipts, batches of invoices and inventory adjustments are memorized this way. From a saved transaction: the Memorize button on the saved (not voided) invoices, sales receipts, estimates, sales orders, statement charges, credit memos, bills, supplier debit memos, purchase orders, checks, journal entries and cash vouchers. Load Memorized Transaction on a new form fills the form from one of them. On this list, the Open button (open on the form) does the same: it opens a new form of its kind filled from it. Field What to enter / what it means Name it Starts as the name on the transaction and its type, for example "Accounting Partners & Co. Bill". Required. Group (optional) A heading to group related entries, for example "Month-end". How it is entered Enter it automatically , Remind me when it is due or Don't remind me (I enter it from the list) . Every A number and a unit: Day(s) , Week(s) , Month(s) , Quarter(s) or Year(s) . Next due The date of the next entry. It starts one month after the transaction's date. Remind (days before) How many days before the due date the reminder starts (0 to 90). Number remaining (blank = no limit) How many more times it should be entered, for example 11 for the rest of a one-year lease. Notes Shown under the name on the list. The three ways of entering: Enter it automatically: the program records the entry on its due date, the first time anyone opens the system that day, and shows "Memorized transaction "..." was entered automatically for 09/03/2026." If several due dates were missed, it catches up one date at a time, each entry with its own date. Remind me when it is due: from the set number of days before the due date, the line shows Due (or Overdue once the date has passed) and the Home page lists it. You enter it with Enter now . Don't remind me (I enter it from the list): it waits on the list until you enter it. Step by step To memorize a transaction: Open the saved transaction, for example a bill from Accounting Partners & Co. Click Memorize . Check Name it and choose a Group if you use groups. Choose How it is entered . Set Every , for example 1 Month(s) , and the Next due date. Set Remind (days before) and Number remaining if needed. Click Memorize . The message "Memorized as "...". It is on the Memorized Transactions list." confirms it. To enter a memorized transaction now: Open Financial Set-up & Reports > Memorized Transactions . Click Enter now on its line. The dialog Enter a memorized transaction opens. Check the Date of the entry . It starts at the next due date. Leave Move the schedule on to the next due date ticked if this entry is the one that was due. Untick it for an extra entry that should not move the schedule. Click Enter it . The document is recorded straight away and opens so you can check it. To change the schedule: Click the pencil button on the line. In the Edit form at the top, change the Name , Group (optional) , How it is entered , Every , Next due , Remind (days before) , Number remaining (blank = no limit) , Stop after , Active or Notes . Click Save . To take one off the list: click the trash button and confirm "Take "..." off the memorized list? The transactions already entered from it are not touched." Buttons New journal entry opens a blank Make Journal Entries form. Enter now is shown on active lines to users who may create memorized transactions. It is green when the line is due. Open opens a new form filled from the line, to change and save. A batch of invoices and an inventory adjustment are always used this way (their figures are revised each time), so they have no Enter now ; their button is green when they are due. What it records Entering a memorized transaction saves an ordinary transaction of its type, with a new number and the date you chose, and posts it exactly as if you had typed it. An invoice or bill gets its due date from its terms. After the entry, Last entered , Entered and Number remaining are updated and Next due moves on by the frequency. Each entry is noted in the audit trail. Good to know The saved copy does not change when you edit the original transaction later. To change the amounts, memorize the corrected transaction again and delete the old line. When Number remaining reaches zero, or the next due date falls after Stop after , the memorized transaction becomes inactive and is no longer entered or reminded. An automatic entry that cannot be recorded (for example because its date is on or before the closing date, or a default account is missing) is switched to Remind me when it is due and the reason is written to the audit trail. Enter it by hand once the problem is fixed. Opening balance entries and voided transactions cannot be memorized. The transactions entered from the list are ordinary transactions: change, void or delete them on their own pages.

A budget holds the amounts you plan for each account, month by month, for one fiscal year. A budget is for the income statement or for the balance sheet, and can be limited to one class. The Income Statement vs Budget and Balance Sheet vs Budget reports put the actual figures beside it and show the difference. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Set Up Budgets. The same page, for sales forecasts per customer, is Customers > Set Up Forecast (see Set Up Forecast ). The columns Column What it shows Name The budget's name. Click it to enter the amounts. What it budgets Income statement (profit and loss) or Balance sheet . Fiscal year The year, or the months it covers when the fiscal year does not start in January. Class The class the budget is for, if any. Yearly total The sum of all its monthly amounts. Notes Your notes. Each line has an Amounts button and a delete (trash) button. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Name For example "Budget 2027". Required. What it budgets Income statement (profit and loss) lists the Income, Other Income, Cost of Goods Sold, Expense and Other Expense accounts. Balance sheet lists the asset, liability and equity accounts. Fiscal year The year the budget is for. The months follow the fiscal year set in Company, Security & Closing Date ; the form says in which month it starts. Class (optional) Leave blank for the whole company, or choose a class to budget one branch or department. The actual figures are then only those of that class. Notes Optional. Start from last year's actual figures Fills the grid with the actual figures of the year before, so you adjust them instead of typing everything. The amounts grid After Create , the budget opens in its amounts grid. Each active account of the budget's kind has a row, grouped by account type, with a box for each of the twelve months and a Year total. The Total row at the bottom adds up each month. Fill a row: type an amount, click in any box of a row, then click Across . Every month of that row gets the amount. Yearly total: type a yearly amount, click in a row, then click Spread . The amount is divided evenly over the twelve months; the last month takes the centavos left over. Notes: change the budget's notes. Enter income and expense amounts as positive figures. For a balance sheet budget, enter the balance you expect at the end of each month, also as positive figures for assets, liabilities and equity. Step by step To create a budget: Open Financial Set-up & Reports > Set Up Budgets . Click New budget . Type the Name , choose What it budgets and type the Fiscal year . Choose a Class if the budget is for one class. Tick Start from last year's actual figures if you want the grid filled for you. Click Create . The grid opens with the message "Budget 2027 created. Enter the monthly amounts below." Type or change the monthly amounts. Click Save the amounts . The message says how many monthly amounts were saved. To change the amounts later: click the budget's name or Amounts , change the figures and click Save the amounts . To compare with the actual figures: on the grid click Compare with actual , or open the report from Income statement vs budget on the list. To delete a budget: click the trash button on its line and confirm "Delete "..." and its amounts?". What it records A budget posts nothing to the books. It is only compared with the ledger by the budget reports. Good to know "There is already a budget called "Budget 2027" for 2027." Two budgets of the same kind and year cannot share a name. "Enter the fiscal year." The year must be between 2000 and 2100. When Start from last year's actual figures is ticked, the copied figures are only shown on the grid ("Last year's actual figures were copied in. Change what you need and press Save."). They are kept only after you click Save the amounts . Empty boxes and zeros are not saved. The Compare with actual button opens the report on the newest budget of that kind. If you have several budgets, choose the one you want in the report's Budget box.

A journal entry posts debits and credits directly to the accounts you choose. Routine activity posts automatically from invoices, bills, payments and the POS, so you use journal entries for what no other form records: opening balances, accruals, reclassifications, corrections and closing entries. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Make Journal Entries opens the list of journal entries. The Home page quick action Make Journal Entries opens a blank entry. The list shows the journal entries and opening balance entries of a date range (from 90 days back to 30 days ahead when it opens). Use From , To , Status ( Posted or Void ), Class and Search (number, name or memo), then click Filter . Click a number to open the entry. Export downloads the list. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Date The date the entry posts on. Entry no. Leave blank to get the next number (the grey text shows it, for example JE-00005). Type your own number only if you need one. Reference An outside reference, for example a document number. Memo What the entry is for. It is used as the memo of every line that has none. Class The class of the whole entry. It fills the class of every line. Opening balance entry Tick for the entry that brings in your opening balances. It is then labelled Opening Balance instead of Journal Entry. Reason for change Shown only when you edit a saved entry. Recorded in the audit trail. The lines: Column What to enter / what it means Account Type part of the account name to find it, for example "rent" for 6010 Rent Expense. Debit The debit amount of the line. Credit The credit amount of the line. A line has a debit or a credit, not both. Memo The description of the line. Name A customer, supplier, employee or other name. Required on Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable and With SL accounts. Class The class of the line. Change it only when this line belongs to another class. Under the lines, Totals shows the debits and the credits, and Difference shows what is still out of balance. Add line adds a row; the red X removes one. Step by step To make a journal entry: Open Financial Set-up & Reports > Make Journal Entries and click New journal entry . Check the Date . Type a Reference and a Memo . Choose the Class if you use classes. On the first line, choose the Account and type the Debit . On the next line, choose the account and type the Credit . Add more lines if needed, until Difference shows 0.00. Choose a Name on every line that needs one. Click Save entry , or Save entry & New to start another one. Example To accrue September rent of ₱85,000.00 that will be billed in October, debit 6010 Rent Expense ₱85,000.00 and credit 2200 Accrued Expenses ₱85,000.00, with the memo "Accrued rent, September". To enter opening balances: Start a new journal entry dated the day before you begin using the system. Tick Opening balance entry . Debit each asset account with its balance and credit each liability and equity account with its balance. Save when Difference is 0.00. In the demo company, OB-0001 debits 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking ₱2,500,000.00 and the other cash accounts, and credits 3000 Owner's Capital ₱3,320,000.00. To change a journal entry: Open the entry from the list. Click Edit . Change the lines or the header. Type a Reason for change . Click Save entry . To print a journal entry: open it and click Print , then click Print above the page. See the print format below. To void or delete a journal entry: open it, click Void or Delete , type the reason and confirm. Voiding keeps the entry with no effect on the ledger; deleting removes it, and a full copy stays in the audit trail. To memorize a journal entry: open it and click Memorize (see Memorized Transactions ). The saved entry shows the date, number, status, memo, class and who entered it, the lines as you entered them, and General ledger entries created automatically with the total debits and credits. A ledger line that was cleared in a bank reconciliation is marked cleared . Buttons Edit , Print , Memorize , Void , Delete : see the procedures above. Each appears only when you have the permission. History opens the Transaction History of the entry. Back to list returns to the Journal Entries list. Journal list (on the form) goes back to the list without saving. The print format The printed journal entry has the company name, address and TIN (and the logo, when the administrator has switched it on for this document), the title JOURNAL ENTRY or OPENING BALANCE , the number and the date. Under it are the memo, reference, site and class, then a table with Account , Description , Name , Class , Debit and Credit , the two totals, and the signature lines Prepared by (the user who entered it), Checked by and Approved by . A line without its own class prints the class of the entry. What it records Each line posts to its account exactly as entered: a debit line debits the account, a credit line credits it. The name and the class of the line go with it to the ledger, so a line to 1100 Accounts Receivable with the name ABC Trading Corp. changes that customer's balance. An opening balance entry posts the same way; only its label differs. Good to know "A journal entry needs at least two lines." "Debits (85,000.00) must equal credits (80,000.00)." The totals must agree to the centavo. "Choose an account for every journal line." A line with an amount needs an account. "A journal line cannot have both a debit and a credit." Split it into two lines. "Lines posted to Accounts Receivable need a customer name." and "Lines posted to Accounts Payable need a vendor name." Choose the name on that line. A journal entry to Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable changes the customer's or supplier's balance, but it is not an invoice or a bill: it does not appear in Receive Payments or Pay Bills . Use those modules for sales and purchases. A journal entry never changes item quantities, even when it posts to 1200 Inventory. Use Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand for stock. "The books are closed through 06/28/2026. You do not have permission to record transactions dated on or before the closing date." Only users with the special permission Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled can post on or before the closing date, or change an entry that was cleared in a bank reconciliation. A voided entry cannot be edited. When the Class at the top is empty but every line that has an account carries its own class, the program saves without asking about the class. Journal entry numbers (JE-) are shared with other entries the program makes itself, such as bank service charges, interest earned and cash over and short, so the numbers on this list may skip.

Each module posts to a set of default accounts: the receivable, the payable, the tax accounts, the inventory and cost of sales, the clearing accounts of the POS and so on. They are set up before any transaction is recorded. Items, tax codes, payment methods and fixed asset categories can carry their own accounts; the defaults are used when they do not. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Module Default Accounts, or the Module default accounts button on the Chart of Accounts. Fields Default What it is used for Accounts Receivable Debited by invoices, statement charges and finance charges; credited by payments and credit memos. Creditable Withholding Tax Debited with the income tax (1% / 2%) a customer withholds on a payment. Creditable VAT Withheld Debited with the VAT (5%) a government customer withholds on a payment: a VAT credit (2550Q Item 16). Default Sales Income Credited by sales lines whose item has no income account. Finance Charge Income Credited by assessed finance charges. Output Tax Credited with VAT on sales when the tax code has no output tax account. Reimbursable Expense Income Credited when billable costs are added to an invoice. Sales Discounts Debited with early-payment discounts given on customer payments. Sales Returns and Allowances Debited by credit memo lines. Undeposited Funds Debited by payments and sales receipts waiting to be deposited; credited by Make Deposits. Accounts Payable Credited by bills; debited by bill payments and supplier debit memos. Default Purchases / Expense Debited by purchase lines whose non-stock item has no expense account. Input Tax Debited with VAT on purchases when the tax code has no input tax account.
