Purchase Discounts Credited with early-payment discounts taken in Pay Bills. Withholding Tax Payable (Expanded) Credited with the income tax (1% / 2%) withheld from suppliers in Pay Bills, until it is remitted (0619-E, 1601-EQ). VAT Withheld Payable Credited with the VAT (5%) withheld from suppliers in Pay Bills, until it is remitted (1600-VT). Advances to Suppliers Debited by advances paid to suppliers; credited when they are applied to bills. Cost of Goods Sold Debited with the cost of stock sold, when the item has no cost of sales account. Inventory Adjustment (Shrinkage) The other side of inventory adjustments and physical counts. Inventory Asset The stock account of items that have no asset account of their own. Processing / Disassembly Variance The variance of processing orders. Item Group Price Variance The group price of the item groups sold less the prices of their items, for the groups without a price variance account of their own. Processing Labor & Overhead Absorbed Credited with labor and overhead added to processing orders. Card Clearing POS card and other non-cash tenders whose payment method has no clearing account. Cash on Hand (Register) POS cash sales of a terminal that has no cash account of its own. Cash Over and Short The difference found when a POS shift is closed. E-wallet Clearing POS e-wallet tenders whose payment method has no clearing account. Bank / Merchant Charges Merchant fees on card settlements in Make Deposits, and the suggested service charge account in Reconcile. Interest Income The suggested interest account in Reconcile. Gain / Loss on Disposal of Assets The gain or loss when a fixed asset is disposed of. Opening Balance Equity The other side of opening balances brought in with items and fixed assets. Retained Earnings Holds the net income of earlier fiscal years on the Trial Balance and the Balance Sheet. Step by step To change a default account: Open Financial Set-up & Reports > Module Default Accounts . In the card of the module, choose the new account in the drop-down beside the label. Change any other defaults you need. Click Save default accounts . The message says how many defaults were changed. Good to know Changing a default affects only transactions saved from then on. Saved transactions keep what they posted, until they are edited and saved again. Only active accounts are offered. A default cannot be cleared back to — not set — once it is set. The boxes are greyed out, with the note "You need the "Chart of Accounts changes" permission to edit these.", for users who lack the edit permission on this page or the special permission Can change the Chart of Accounts and default accounts . If a default the program needs is missing, saving a transaction stops with "The default account "Undeposited Funds" is not set. Set it under Financial Set-up & Reports > Module Default Accounts." Every change is written to the audit trail with the old and the new account.

This page keeps the short lists the other modules use: payment terms, tax codes, payment methods, price levels, sales representatives, customer types, item categories and billing groups. Each list has its own tab. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists Every tab works the same way: the list is on the left, and the Add panel on the right adds a new entry. Click Edit on a line to change it in the Edit panel. Step by step To add an entry: Click the tab of the list. Fill in the Add panel. Click Save , or Save & New to add another one. To change an entry: Click Edit on its line. Change the fields. Click Save . Cancel returns to a blank Add panel. Entries cannot be deleted from this page. Untick Active to stop offering one on forms (the last three lists have no Active box). Payment terms Field What to enter / what it means Name For example "Net 30" or "2% 10 Net 30". Net days Days from the document date to the due date. "Due on receipt" is 0. Early-payment discount % The discount for paying early, for example 2. Discount if paid within (days) The number of days the discount is allowed, for example 10. Active Untick to stop offering the terms. Invoices and bills work out the due date from the terms. Receive Payments and Pay Bills offer the early-payment discount while it is still allowed. Tax codes Field What to enter / what it means Code The short code shown on forms, for example VAT12. Name For example "VAT 12%". Rate % The tax rate. Non-taxable, VAT-exempt and zero-rated codes have 0. Output tax account The account credited with this tax on sales. Blank uses the default Output Tax account. Input tax account The account debited with this tax on purchases. Blank uses the default Input Tax account. Active Untick to stop offering the code. Prices on sales and purchase forms are VAT-exclusive: the tax of each line is the line amount times the rate. Payment methods Field What to enter / what it means Name For example Cash, GCash or Credit/Debit Card. Type Cash , Check , Card , E-wallet , Bank transfer , Gift voucher or Other . POS clearing account The account a POS tender of this method is debited to, for example 1060 Card Clearing. When it is blank, a POS sale uses the default Card Clearing or E-wallet Clearing account, and a customer payment taken at the counter uses Undeposited Funds. Cash tenders always go to the terminal's cash account. POS payment option Ticked methods are offered as tenders on the POS Register. Active Untick to stop offering the method. Card and e-wallet balances waiting in their clearing accounts are settled to the bank in Make Deposits . Price levels Field What to enter / what it means Name For example Wholesale or VIP. Adjust standard price by % The change from the item's standard price: -5 for 5% less, 5 for 5% more. Active Untick to stop offering the level. Every company has ten levels, Wholesale , VIP , Retail Plus and Price Level 4 to Price Level 10 as delivered; give them your own names here, or all at once with Rename price levels on Set Item Prices and Levels . A customer with a price level gets these prices on sales forms and at the POS. Prices of single items can be set per level in Set Item Prices and Levels. Sales representatives Field What to enter / what it means Name The representative's name. Initials Short initials, for example MS. Linked user The user account of the representative, if any. Commission % The rate the Sales by Rep Summary report uses to work out each representative's commission. Active Untick to stop offering the representative. Customer types Only a Name , for example Corporate, Government, Retail or School. You choose a customer's type in the Customer Center and can find transactions by customer type in Find . Item categories Only a Name , for example Accessories or Computers. You choose an item's category on the item form of the Item List , which also shows it in a Category column, and the POS reports can total the sales by category. A note above the tab points to the Category List of the Inventory menu, which also deletes categories (moving their items to another one) and shows how many items each holds. Billing groups Only a Name , for example "Monthly Service Contracts". A customer put in a billing group is picked together with the rest of the group in Create Batch Invoices . Good to know "Enter a name." Every entry needs a name. Text fields hold up to 80 characters. Two entries can have the same name; check the list before adding. Every addition and change is written to the audit trail.

The reports of this module are listed under Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports in the sidebar, and in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . They all read the general ledger, so they always agree with each other and with the transactions. Every report has the common report tools: Refresh , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report and Memorize , and a click on an account or a number opens the detail behind it. These are explained once in Working with reports . This section describes what is special to each report. Most financial reports have a Class filter. All shows everything; a class shows only the ledger lines of that class; (Unclassified) shows only the lines that have no class.

The Trial Balance lists every account with a balance on a date, in a Debit or a Credit column, and checks that the two totals agree. Use it at month-end before you prepare the statements. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Trial Balance Filters: As of (the date of the balances) and Class . The columns: Account (code and name; click it to open its General Ledger), Type , Debit and Credit . The TOTAL row adds each column. How to read it: balance sheet accounts show their balance at the date. Income and expense accounts show only the activity of the current fiscal year, from the first day of the fiscal year to the As of date, as the note above the table says. The net income of earlier years is included in Retained Earnings. If the two totals differ, the note ends with Out of balance! in red. Tip Accounts with a zero balance are left out, so the list stays short.

The Balance Sheet shows what the company owns, owes and is worth on a date. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Balance Sheet Filters: As of and Class . How to read it: the report has three parts. ASSETS has Current Assets (Bank, Accounts Receivable and Other Current Asset accounts), Fixed Assets and Other Assets. LIABILITIES has Current Liabilities (Accounts Payable, Credit Card and Other Current Liability accounts) and Long-term Liabilities. EQUITY lists the equity accounts and the line Net Income (fiscal year to date) ; Retained Earnings includes the net income of earlier years. Each group has its total, and the last line is TOTAL LIABILITIES AND EQUITY . Contra accounts show as negative figures: 1525 Accumulated Depreciation - Machinery shows -28,950.00 under Fixed Assets. The note above the table says "Assets = Liabilities + Equity." when the two sides agree. Note Filtered by class, the two sides may not agree, because a journal entry or cash voucher can carry a different class on each line. The note then explains this instead of showing an error.

The same balance sheet with one column per class, an Unclassified column for entries without a class, and a Total column. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Balance Sheet by Class, or the Balance Sheet by Class button on the Class List . Filters: As of only. How to read it: every active class has a column, and an inactive class has one when it has entries. Click an amount in a class column to open the General Ledger of that account for that class. The note says "Assets = Liabilities + Equity in total." A single column rarely balances on its own, because a payment received by one branch may settle the invoice of another, or a journal line may carry its own class. The note names the columns that do not balance.

This trial balance shows only the movement of each account between two dates, not the balance carried from before. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Trial Balance by Date Range Filters: Dates (a preset such as This month ), From , To and Class . The columns: Account , Type , and the net movement in Debit or Credit , with a TOTAL row. How to read it: in the picture, 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking has a debit of 203,828.98: the account went up by that much in September. Use it to review one month's activity or to check a period before you close it.

For each account, the total of all debits and the total of all credits posted between two dates, and their difference. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Trial Balance of Totals Filters: Dates , From , To and Class . The columns: Account , Type , Total debit , Total credit and Net movement (debits less credits). The TOTAL row shows the grand totals; when the books balance, the total debits equal the total credits and the net movement is 0.00. Example In September, 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking received 288,828.98 and paid out 85,000.00, a net movement of 203,828.98. The Trial Balance by Date Range shows only the 203,828.98.

A balance sheet built only from the transactions dated between two dates. Every figure is the change during the period, not the balance at the end of it. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Balance Sheet by Date Range Filters: Dates , From , To and Class . The columns: Account and Change in the period . How to read it: assets are shown debit-positive, and liabilities and equity credit-positive, so both sides agree. The Equity section includes Net income of the period . A negative asset figure means the asset went down; in the picture, 1200 Inventory fell by 129,128.33 during September.

Puts the actual income and expenses beside an income statement budget and shows the difference. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Income Statement vs Budget, the Income statement vs budget button on Set Up Budgets , or Compare with actual on a budget. Filters: Budget: the budget to compare with. With none chosen, the newest income statement budget is used. Show: Year to date (from the first month of the budget to the month the fiscal year has reached today), The whole fiscal year , or One month at a time . Month: the month of the fiscal year (Month 1 is the first month of the fiscal year), used with One month at a time . Class: shown above the report, but the figures always follow the class of the budget itself. The columns: Account , Actual , Budget , Difference (actual less budget) and % of budget (how much of the budget was reached). Accounts are grouped under INCOME, COST OF GOODS SOLD, EXPENSES, OTHER INCOME and OTHER EXPENSES, each with a total, and a NET INCOME line closes the report: income and other income, less cost of goods sold, expenses and other expenses. It matches the net income of the Income Statement for the same months. The note names the budget and the months shown. How to read it: for income, a positive difference is good news; for an expense, a positive difference means you spent more than planned. Click an account to see its entries in the General Ledger. When no budget exists, the report says "No budget has been set up yet. Financial Set-up & Reports > Set Up Budgets makes one."

Puts the actual balances of the asset, liability and equity accounts beside a balance sheet budget. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Balance Sheet vs Budget, or Compare with actual on a balance sheet budget. Filters: Budget ; Show ( As at the latest month , The whole fiscal year or One month at a time ); Month ; Class (shown, but the figures follow the class of the budget). The columns: Account , Actual , Budget , Difference and % of budget , grouped under ASSETS, LIABILITIES and EQUITY with totals. How to read it: a balance is a figure at a point in time, so the report compares the balances at the end of the last month shown, not a sum of months. With As at the latest month , that is the month the fiscal year has reached today. The equity accounts show only what was posted to them; the profit of the current year is not added to them on this report.

The Income Statement (profit and loss) shows the income, costs and expenses of a period and the resulting net income. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Income Statement Filters: Dates (starts at Fiscal year to date ), From , To , Class , and Columns : Total only , or one column per Month , Quarter or Year followed by a Total column. How to read it: the report runs Income , Cost of Goods Sold , GROSS PROFIT , Expenses , NET OPERATING INCOME , Other Income , Other Expenses and NET INCOME . Contra-income accounts such as 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances and 4060 Sales Discounts show as negative figures inside Income. Click an account to see its entries. Tip Choose Columns: Month with Dates: This fiscal year to see the months side by side and spot an expense that jumped.

The Income Statement with one column per class, an Unclassified column and a Total column. Use it to compare the profit of your branches, departments or projects. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Income Statement by Class, or the Income Statement by Class button on the Class List . Filters: Dates , From and To . How to read it: the lines are the same as on the Income Statement. Click an amount in a class column to see the entries of that account for that class. In the picture, Makati Store had sales of 56,773.50 and a gross profit of 13,930.17 in the fiscal year to date. Large Unclassified figures mean transactions were saved without a class.

The Income Statement with one column per month, side by side, a Total column and the change from the month before. Use it to follow sales, costs and profit month after month. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Comparative Income Statement by Month. Also in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . It is given to the roles that may open the Income Statement. Filters: Dates (starts at Fiscal year to date ), From , To and Class . Every calendar month the range touches has a column; the first and the last are cut at the From and To dates, so a range ending on October 22 shows October 1 to 22. How to read it: the lines are those of the Income Statement : Income, Cost of Goods Sold, GROSS PROFIT , Expenses, NET OPERATING INCOME , Other Income, Other Expenses and NET INCOME . Each month's column equals the Income Statement run for that month, and Total equals the Income Statement for the whole range. The last two columns compare the last period with the one before it: Change (for example "Change (Oct 2026 vs Sep 2026)") is the last less the one before, and % change is that change over the one before (blank when the one before is zero). Click an account's figure to open the General Ledger of that account for that column's period; the account name opens it for the whole range.

The same comparison by calendar quarter (Q1 January to March, Q2 April to June, Q3 July to September, Q4 October to December), with a Total column and the change from the quarter before. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Comparative Income Statement by Quarter. Also in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . It is given to the roles that may open the Income Statement. Filters: Dates (starts at Fiscal year to date ), From , To and Class . A quarter that has only begun shows the part of it inside the range. The last two columns compare the last period with the one before it: Change (for example "Change (Oct 2026 vs Sep 2026)") is the last less the one before, and % change is that change over the one before (blank when the one before is zero). Click an account's figure to open the General Ledger of that account for that column's period; the account name opens it for the whole range.

The Income Statement of each fiscal year side by side, with a Total column and the change from the year before. Fiscal years start in the month set in Company, Security & Closing Date ( Fiscal year starts ); a year that starts in January is headed with its number ("2026"), another one with both years ("FY 2026-27"). Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Comparative Income Statement by Year. Also in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . It is given to the roles that may open the Income Statement. Filters: Dates (starts at Custom : the last three fiscal years up to today), From , To and Class . The current year shows the fiscal year to date, so compare it with care against full years. The last two columns compare the last period with the one before it: Change (for example "Change (Oct 2026 vs Sep 2026)") is the last less the one before, and % change is that change over the one before (blank when the one before is zero). Click an account's figure to open the General Ledger of that account for that column's period; the account name opens it for the whole range.

t: Comparative Income Statement by Custom Range
x: Up to four date ranges of your own, side by side, with the change between the first two: this month against the same month last year, a promotion week against the week before, two seasons, and so on. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Comparative Income Statement by Custom Range. Also in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . It is given to the roles that may open the Income Statement. Filters: Range 1 from and Range 1 to up to Range 4 from and Range 4 to , and Class . The report opens with this month in range 1 and the same month a year earlier in range 2; ranges 3 and 4 are empty. Type the dates and click Refresh . A range with a missing date, or with From after To , is left out and named in the note. How to read it: one column per range, in the order typed, headed "Range 1: 10/01/2026 - 10/31/2026". The ranges may overlap, so there is no total column. Change (range 1 less range 2) and % change compare the first two. Click an account's figure for its General Ledger in that range.

The Balance Sheet at the end of each month side by side, with the change from the month before. Use it to see how cash, receivables, inventory, payables and equity moved through the year. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Comparative Balance Sheet by Month. Also in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . It is given to the roles that may open the Balance Sheet. Filters: Dates (starts at Fiscal year to date ), From , To and Class . There is a column for the end of each month of the range, headed with the month and the date ("Sep 2026 (09/30/2026)"); the last one is as of the To date. How to read it: the lines are those of the Balance Sheet : ASSETS , LIABILITIES and EQUITY with their groups, Retained Earnings with the earlier years' profit, and Net Income (fiscal year to date) of each column's own fiscal year. Each column equals the Balance Sheet as of its date. The last two columns compare the last column with the one before it: Change and % change . Click an account's figure to open its General Ledger up to that column's date. The note under the title says whether assets equal liabilities and equity in every column.

The Balance Sheet at the end of each calendar quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31) side by side, with the change from the quarter before. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Comparative Balance Sheet by Quarter. Also in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . It is given to the roles that may open the Balance Sheet. Filters: Dates (starts at Fiscal year to date ), From , To and Class . The quarter in progress is shown as of the To date. The last two columns compare the last column with the one before it: Change and % change . Click an account's figure to open its General Ledger up to that column's date. The note under the title says whether assets equal liabilities and equity in every column.

The Balance Sheet at the end of each fiscal year side by side, with the change from the year before. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Comparative Balance Sheet by Year. Also in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . It is given to the roles that may open the Balance Sheet. Filters: Dates (starts at Custom : the last three fiscal years up to today), From , To and Class . The current year is shown as of today. The last two columns compare the last column with the one before it: Change and % change . Click an account's figure to open its General Ledger up to that column's date. The note under the title says whether assets equal liabilities and equity in every column.

t: Comparative Balance Sheet by Custom Date
x: The Balance Sheet as of up to four dates of your own, side by side, with the change between the first two: today against the end of last year, the end of two months, the day before and after a big purchase, and so on. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Comparative Balance Sheet by Custom Date. Also in the Financial Reports card of the Report Center . It is given to the roles that may open the Balance Sheet. Filters: Date 1 to Date 4 , and Class . The report opens with today in date 1 and the last day of the previous fiscal year in date 2; dates 3 and 4 are empty. Type the dates and click Refresh . How to read it: one column per date, in the order typed, headed "Date 1: 10/22/2026". Change (date 1 less date 2) and % change compare the first two. Click an account's figure for its General Ledger up to that date. Tip All eight comparative reports print on one page width more easily in landscape: in Modify Report choose the landscape orientation and save it as the report's standard layout. Their long column headings already take two lines.

The Statement of Cash Flows explains how the cash went up or down in a period, by the indirect method. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Statement of Cash Flows Filters: Dates (starts at Fiscal year to date ), From , To and Class . How to read it: OPERATING ACTIVITIES starts from the Net Income of the period and adds the change in each Accounts Receivable, Other Current Asset, Accounts Payable, Credit Card and Other Current Liability account. The change in the accumulated depreciation accounts is added back as "(depreciation)", because depreciation uses no cash. INVESTING ACTIVITIES shows the change in the Fixed Asset and Other Asset accounts. FINANCING ACTIVITIES shows the change in the Long Term Liability and Equity accounts. NET CASH INCREASE (DECREASE) FOR THE PERIOD , Cash at beginning of period and CASH AT END OF PERIOD close the report. An increase in an asset uses cash and shows as a negative figure; an increase in a liability or equity provides cash and shows as a positive figure. Only Bank accounts count as cash, as the note "Indirect method. Cash = bank and cash accounts." says. Money still in Undeposited Funds or in the card and e-wallet clearing accounts is treated as an operating asset until it is deposited. If the ending cash does not agree with the bank balances, the note says "Does not tie to the bank balances" in red with the balance it expected.

The General Ledger lists every entry posted to each account, with a running balance. It is where you land when you click an account on any other report. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > General Ledger, or click an account name on the Chart of Accounts or on a financial report. Filters: Dates (starts at This month ), From , To , Account (blank for all accounts), Class and Search (a word in the memo, the number or the name). The columns: Date , Type , Num (click it to open the transaction), Name , Memo , Class , Debit , Credit and Balance (debit +) . How to read it: each account starts with its Beginning balance at the From date and ends with a Total line showing the total debits, total credits and the ending balance. The balance is always shown debit-positive, so an account with a credit balance, such as 2000 Accounts Payable, shows a negative balance. For income and expense accounts, the beginning balance counts only from the start of the fiscal year. Accounts with no entries and no beginning balance are left out.

The Subsidiary Ledger lists the entries of one name (or of every name) on the accounts that keep a subsidiary ledger: a customer, a supplier, an employee or an other name, with a running balance per account. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Subsidiary Ledger, or click a name on the Schedule of Accounts . Filters: Dates , From and To (starts at This fiscal year ). Account: one account, or blank for every account marked With SL . While no account is marked With SL, a blank Account lists every account the names transacted. Class. Subsidiary ledger (name): one customer, supplier, employee or other name, or — every name — . Which entries: From and to: the entries between the two dates , or To: every entry up to the To date . The columns: Date , Ref ID (the transaction number; click it to open the transaction), Account , Description (the memo, or the transaction type), Class , Debit , Credit and Balance . How to read it: the report is grouped by name, then by account, with a total line for each account and a Total row for the whole report. The Balance is debits less credits, running down each account. With From and to , the balance starts at zero on the From date, so it shows the movement of the period; choose To: every entry up to the To date to see what the name stands at on the To date. When you choose one name and leave Account blank, every account marked With SL is listed for that name, including those it has no entries on, so you see its whole subsidiary ledger at once. Example To see what an employee still owes on cash advances, choose the advances account in Account , the employee in Subsidiary ledger (name) and To: every entry up to the To date .

The Schedule of Accounts lists, for each account, the names that transacted it and the amount each one stands at. Use it to support an account balance with its list of names, for example a schedule of accounts receivable or of employee advances. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Schedule of Accounts Filters: Dates , From , To , Account (blank for every account marked With SL), Class (blank includes every class and the entries without one) and Which entries (as on the Subsidiary Ledger). The columns: Column What it shows SL Code A short code for the name: c for a customer, v for a supplier, o for an employee or other name, followed by its number. Subsidiary Ledger Name The name. Click it to open its Subsidiary Ledger for that account. Kind Customer, Supplier, Employee or Other name. Current Amount What the name stands at, on the account's normal side. How to read it: each account is a group with a Total line; names that net to zero are left out. The amounts follow the account's normal balance, so on 1100 Accounts Receivable a positive amount is what the customer owes. For a true balance rather than a period's movement, choose To: every entry up to the To date . While no account is marked With SL and no account is chosen, the note asks you to choose an account or tick With SL on the accounts you want a schedule of.

The Journal lists every posted transaction with all its ledger lines, in date order: the book of original entry. Where to find it: Financial Set-up & Reports > Reports > Journal Filters: Dates (starts at This month ), From , To , Class and Type (one kind of transaction, for example Check or Deposit). The columns: Date , Type and Num (on the first line of each transaction; click the number to open it), Account , Memo , Class , Debit and Credit . The TOTAL row adds the debits and the credits. How to read it: each transaction starts on a new line with a rule above it. Use the Type filter to review, for example, all the deposits of the month. With a Class chosen, only the lines of that class are shown. The report shows at most 2,000 transactions; narrow the dates if you need more.

t: How the Fixed Assets module works
x: Before you enter the first asset, set up these lists once, in this order: Chart of Accounts. Every category needs three accounts: the asset account (for example 1530 Transportation Equipment), its accumulated depreciation account (1535 Accumulated Depreciation - Transportation) and a depreciation expense account (6090 Depreciation Expense). See Chart of Accounts . Module Default Accounts. The account Gain / Loss on Disposal of Assets (4300 Gain (Loss) on Disposal of Assets in the demo) must be set, or disposals stop with a message. See Module Default Accounts . Asset Categories . A category groups similar assets and decides the three accounts they post to, plus the method and useful life that new assets start with. Asset Locations . Where the assets are kept. Locations let you list, report and depreciate one branch or building at a time. Then the day-to-day work is: Add each asset in the Fixed Asset Register . The same form can record the purchase (a check, a bill, or an opening balance). At each month end, post depreciation in Run Depreciation . Record repairs and servicing in Asset Maintenance , and schedule recurring work (change oil, registration renewal, cleaning) in Preventive Maintenance . When an asset is sold, scrapped or donated, record it in Dispose of Assets .

Each asset uses one of four methods. Depreciation is always charged by month. For the three time-based methods, the program works out the charge for each asset year (the twelve months starting with the month the asset was acquired) and charges one-twelfth of it every month; an asset acquired on any day of July is depreciated for the whole of July. Units of production charges each month for the units used in it. Net book value (cost less accumulated depreciation) never goes below the salvage value. Method How the charge is worked out Demo example Straight-line (Cost less salvage) spread evenly over the useful life in months FA-00001, ₱7,500.00 a month Declining balance Net book value times (multiplier ÷ life); switches to straight-line when that gives more FA-00002, ₱40,000.00 a month in year 1 Sum-of-the-years'-digits (Cost less salvage) times remaining years ÷ sum of the years FA-00003, ₱2,500.00 a month in year 1 Units of production (Cost less salvage) ÷ estimated total output, times the units used in the month FA-00004, ₱1.50 per unit Example The Packaging Machine PM-500 cost ₱500,000.00, has a salvage value of ₱50,000.00 and a useful life of 5 years, straight-line. It depreciates ₱450,000.00 over 60 months: ₱90,000.00 a year, ₱7,500.00 a month. The Delivery Van (L300) cost ₱1,200,000.00 with a salvage value of ₱200,000.00 over 5 years, declining balance with a multiplier of 2: the rate is 2 ÷ 5 = 40%, so year 1 is ₱480,000.00, or ₱40,000.00 a month. For declining balance and sum-of-the-years'-digits the life is counted in whole years. In the last month of a time-based life the program charges whatever is left down to the salvage value, so rounding never leaves a few centavos behind.

Active : in service and still depreciating. Fully Depreciated : the net book value has reached the salvage value. The asset stays in service (it still appears under In service ) but no more depreciation is charged. Disposed : sold, scrapped or donated. It no longer depreciates and is left out of the lists of assets in service.

The Fixed Asset Register is the list of all fixed assets with their cost, accumulated depreciation and net book value. You also add new assets here, open an asset to see its depreciation schedule, correct it, and record the usage of units-of-production assets. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Fixed Asset Register. The Asset register button on Run Depreciation and Asset Locations also opens it, and the number of assets on Asset Locations opens it filtered to that location. The filters Filter What it does Status In service (the default: active and fully depreciated assets), Fully depreciated , Disposed or All Category Shows only the assets of one asset category Location All locations , one location, or (No location) for assets without one The list refreshes as soon as you change a filter. When one location is chosen and you may open Run Depreciation, a Run depreciation for this location button appears beside the filters. The columns Column What it shows Asset no. The number given by the program (FA-00001, FA-00002 ...). Click it to open the asset. Description , Category , Location As entered on the asset Class The asset's default class. Shown only when classes are set up. Acquired The acquisition date Method , Life The depreciation method and the useful life in years Cost The acquisition cost Accum. dep. Opening accumulated depreciation plus all depreciation posted (voided runs are left out) Net book value Cost less accumulated depreciation Status Active , Fully Depreciated or Disposed The Total row adds up the cost, accumulated depreciation and net book value of the assets listed. Buttons New asset opens a blank asset form (needs the create permission on this page). Run depreciation opens Run Depreciation .

The new asset form has four parts: the asset itself, its depreciation settings, how it was acquired, and notes. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Description The name of the asset, for example Delivery Van (L300). Required. Category The asset category. Required. On a new asset, choosing a category fills in its default Method and Useful life (years) . Serial / plate no. Serial number, plate number or property tag Location Where the asset is kept, from the Asset Locations list. Manage locations opens that list in a new tab. Site The inventory site (branch) the asset belongs to. Its disposal entry and its maintenance bills and checks are recorded under this site. Default class The class this asset's depreciation is recorded under when Run Depreciation is posted with no class chosen. Shown only when classes are set up. Vendor The supplier. Required when the purchase is recorded as a bill; used as the payee of the check. Acquired date The date the asset was bought or put in service. Depreciation starts with this month. Cost The acquisition cost, net of VAT. Must be more than zero. Method Straight-line , Declining balance , Units of production or Sum-of-the-years'-digits Useful life (years) Must be more than zero. Decimals are allowed. Salvage (residual) value The value expected at the end of the life. Depreciation stops there. Rate multiplier (2 = double) Declining balance only. 2 gives double-declining balance, 1.5 gives 150%. Estimated total output and Unit Units of production only: the total the asset is expected to produce in its life (units, hours, kilometers) and the name of the unit Record the purchase How the purchase is recorded in the books (see below) Bank account Paid now only: the bank or credit card account the check is drawn on Payee (if no vendor) Paid now only: the name printed on the check when no vendor is chosen Vendor's invoice no. On account only: the supplier's invoice number, kept as the bill's reference Accumulated depreciation to date Existing asset only: depreciation already recorded before you started using GSMaRT Depreciation recorded through Existing asset only: the date that accumulated depreciation runs to. Required when the accumulated depreciation is more than zero. Cost is net of 12% input VAT (VAT added) Paid now or on account: tick it to add 12% input VAT on top of the cost Class The class of the purchase transaction (check, bill or opening balance) Notes Anything worth keeping about the asset The Record the purchase box has four choices: Paid now (Write Checks) : the program writes a check from the chosen bank account. On account (Enter Bills) : the program enters a bill for the vendor, with the vendor's terms and due date. You pay it later in Pay Bills . Existing asset (opening balance) : for an asset the company already owned before it started using GSMaRT. The program writes an opening balance entry. Already recorded elsewhere : no entry is made. Use it when the purchase was already recorded, for example in a check written in Write Checks. Step by step: add an asset bought by check Go to Fixed Assets > Fixed Asset Register and click New asset . Type the Description , for example Packaging Machine PM-500. Choose the Category , for example Machinery and Equipment. The method and life fill in from the category. Type the Serial / plate no. and choose the Location , Site , Default class and Vendor . Enter the Acquired date and the Cost . Check the Method , Useful life (years) and Salvage (residual) value , and change them if this asset is different. Under How was the asset acquired? , leave Record the purchase on Paid now (Write Checks) and choose the Bank account . Tick Cost is net of 12% input VAT (VAT added) if the supplier charged VAT. Click Save asset (or Save asset & New to enter the next asset). The program gives the asset its number and opens it. Step by step: add an asset bought on account Follow steps 1 to 6 above, and make sure the Vendor is chosen. Set Record the purchase to On account (Enter Bills) . Type the Vendor's invoice no. and tick the VAT box if it applies. Click Save asset . The bill appears in Vendors > Enter Bills and in Pay Bills, due according to the vendor's payment terms. Step by step: add an asset the company already owned Follow steps 1 to 6 above. Enter the original Acquired date and the original Cost . Set Record the purchase to Existing asset (opening balance) . Enter the Accumulated depreciation to date and the Depreciation recorded through date, for example the last day of the month before you started using the program. Click Save asset . The months up to the Depreciation recorded through date are treated as already depreciated; Run Depreciation continues from the month after. Tip To load many assets at once, use Import from CSV . Imported assets are added without an accounting entry unless you ask for an opening balance entry for them. What it records Paid now (Write Checks) writes a check (numbered in the check series): Account Debit Credit The category's asset account, for example 1520 Machinery and Equipment Cost 1300 Input Tax (only when the VAT box is ticked) 12% of cost The chosen bank account, for example 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking Cost plus VAT On account (Enter Bills) enters a bill with the same debits and a credit to 2000 Accounts Payable for the vendor. Existing asset (opening balance) writes an opening balance journal entry: Account Debit Credit The category's asset account Cost The category's accumulated depreciation account Accumulated depreciation to date 3900 Opening Balance Equity Cost less accumulated depreciation Already recorded elsewhere records nothing in the ledger. In every case the asset is added to the register with status Active .

Click an asset number to open it. The left card shows the asset's details, the accumulated depreciation, the net book value and the status. (source) beside the acquisition date opens the check, bill or opening balance that recorded the purchase. On the right, the Annual schedule shows how much each asset year will depreciate (for time-based methods), and Depreciation posted lists every depreciation entry with its period, entry number, units and amount. An opening balance row appears first when the asset was entered with accumulated depreciation. The buttons at the top: Edit opens the asset form. Dispose opens Dispose of Assets with this asset chosen. Hidden for disposed assets. Compare methods opens the Depreciation Schedule by Asset report for this asset. Back returns to the register. For a declining balance asset the Method line also shows the rate, for example "2× straight-line rate = 40.00%". For a units-of-production asset it shows the estimated total output and the rate per unit. When the estimates were changed after depreciation started, a Change in estimate line shows from when, the net book value and the number of months the new basis uses. Step by step: record the usage of a units-of-production asset A units-of-production asset is depreciated only for months with a usage figure. You can enter it on the asset or directly on Run Depreciation. Open the asset from the register. In the Record usage (meter reading / production count) card, enter the Year , the Month and the Units used in that month (not the meter reading itself). Click Save . The last 24 months entered are listed under the button. Entering a month again replaces its figure. Note The usage for depreciation is separate from the odometer or running hours kept for maintenance. The meter reading on a maintenance record or a preventive maintenance task does not feed depreciation.

Open the asset and click Edit . What you may change depends on whether depreciation has already been posted. Before any depreciation is posted you may change everything, including the Acquired date and the Cost . When the purchase was recorded by this form (a check, a bill or an opening balance), the program corrects that transaction too, so the ledger stays in step with the asset. A note under the fields links to that transaction. After depreciation is posted (or when the asset has opening accumulated depreciation): The Acquired date and the Cost are locked. To correct them, void the depreciation entries first in Run Depreciation, then edit the asset. The Category cannot change. A change to the method, the useful life, the salvage value, the multiplier or the estimated total output is a change in estimate . A Changes apply from (change in estimate) date appears. The program leaves past depreciation as it is and spreads the remaining net book value over the rest of the new useful life, starting with the later of the month you enter and the month after the last depreciation posted. Example The Delivery Van was depreciated for July and August 2026 (₱80,000.00). In September you decide its life is 8 years, not 5. Edit the asset, change Useful life (years) to 8 and leave Changes apply from on today's date. From September 2026, the net book value of ₱1,120,000.00 less the ₱200,000.00 salvage value is depreciated, still by declining balance, over the remaining 94 months (96 months less the 2 already passed). Good to know Asset numbers come from the asset number series (FA-00001, FA-00002 ...). You cannot type your own number on the form. Changing the location of an asset is a normal edit; there is no transfer entry, because the location does not change the accounts. Messages you may see: "Enter the description and a useful life greater than zero.", "Choose the asset category.", "Enter the acquisition date and cost.", "Enter the estimated total units for units-of-production depreciation.", "Choose the bank account for the check.", "Choose the vendor for the bill.", "Enter the date depreciation was recorded through.", "The new salvage value is higher than the remaining net book value.", "The category cannot change after depreciation has been posted.", "The cost cannot be lower than the salvage value." When you correct the cost of an asset whose purchase check or bill was changed by hand in the meantime, the program cannot find the asset line and says: "The purchase was recorded on ..., and its asset line no longer matches the old cost. Correct that transaction first, then the asset." Paying by check is subject to your amount limit ( Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval in User Role Configuration ). This form has no supervisor approval box. If the cost is above your limit and you do not have the Approve permission on Write Checks, the program stops with "Supervisor approval is required ...". Ask a user who may approve checks to add the asset, or write the check in Write Checks and add the asset with Already recorded elsewhere . Voiding or deleting the purchase check or bill does not remove the asset; it only removes the (source) link. The register has no delete button, so an asset entered by mistake stays in the register: correct it instead, while no depreciation is posted. Every addition and change is written to the audit trail, including changes in estimate with their effective date.

Run Depreciation posts the monthly depreciation of all assets in one journal entry. Do it once a month, after the month has ended and before you print the month's financial statements. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Run Depreciation. The Run depreciation button on the Fixed Asset Register and the Run Depreciation quick action on the Home page open it too. The page opens on the previous month. In the demo, today is 09/27/2026, so it opens on August 2026, which has already been posted: every asset shows posted and the Total to post is 0.00. Choose another month in Period to see what can be posted for it. Each asset shows the depreciation the program has worked out, ticked and ready to post. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Period The month to depreciate. The entry is dated the last day of that month, as the note beside the filters says ("Entries are dated 08/31/2026."). Location All locations , one location, or (No location) . Only the assets of the chosen location are listed and posted. Tick box Tick the assets to post. The box in the header ticks or clears all of them. Assets already posted for the period have no box, nor do time-based assets with nothing to post. Asset , Category , Location , Default class , Method , Cost The asset's details. Default class is shown only when classes are in use. Accumulated The accumulated depreciation before this run Usage this month Units-of-production assets only: the units used in the period. Type it here or on the asset. Depreciation The amount to post, or posted when the period was already done for this asset Notes Warnings: "N earlier month(s) not yet depreciated", "enter usage first", "fully depreciated" Memo (optional) The memo of the entry. Left blank, it reads "Depreciation for August 2026" (with " - location" when one location is chosen). Class Choose a class to record the whole entry under it, or leave Class: each asset's own default class to record every asset under its default class. Shown when classes are set up. Step by step: post the month's depreciation Go to Fixed Assets > Run Depreciation . Check the Period . Change it if you are not posting last month. For each units-of-production asset, type the units used in Usage this month . Click Save usage only if you want to keep the figures and post later. Read the Notes column. If an asset has earlier months not yet depreciated, post those months first (choose the earlier Period and post it). Untick any asset you do not want to depreciate this time. Type a Memo and choose a Class if needed. Click Post depreciation . The program posts one journal entry and shows "Depreciation of 57,650.00 posted for 4 asset(s): debit Depreciation Expense, credit Accumulated Depreciation." Step by step: depreciate one location at a time Choose the Location at the top of the page, or click Run depreciation for this location in the Fixed Asset Register. Post as above. Only that location's assets are listed and posted, and the memo names the location. Choose the next location and post again. Step by step: undo a depreciation run In Posted depreciation , click the entry number (for example JE-00002). Click Void (the entry stays, marked VOID, with no effect on the ledger) or Delete (the entry is removed; a full copy stays in the audit trail). Type the reason and confirm. The assets in that run can then be depreciated again for that period. An asset that had become Fully Depreciated through that run goes back to Active . The posted entry Open a run from Posted depreciation to see it. The view shows the lines as they were posted and the General ledger entries created automatically . The buttons are Print , Void , Delete , History and Back to list . A depreciation entry cannot be edited; void it and post again instead. Print shows the entry as a journal voucher titled DEPRECIATION, with Prepared by, Checked by and Approved by lines. Click Print on that page to send it to the printer. What it records The program adds up the depreciation of the selected assets by category (and by class) and writes one pair of lines for each: a debit to the category's depreciation expense account and a credit to its accumulated depreciation account. The August 2026 run of the demo: Account Debit Credit 6090 Depreciation Expense ₱57,650.00 1555 Accumulated Depreciation - Computer and POS ₱2,500.00 1525 Accumulated Depreciation - Machinery ₱15,150.00 1535 Accumulated Depreciation - Transportation ₱40,000.00 The entry takes its number from the journal entry series (JE-00001, JE-00002 ...). For each asset the program also records the period, the units used and the amount, which appear on the asset under Depreciation posted . An asset whose net book value reaches its salvage value becomes Fully Depreciated . Note Categories that share the same expense and accumulated depreciation accounts are posted on one pair of lines. In the demo, Machinery and Equipment (₱7,500.00) and Production Machinery (usage-based) (₱7,650.00) both use 6090 and 1525, so the entry shows one pair of ₱15,150.00. The line description names only one of the two categories. Good to know A period can be posted only once per asset. To post it again, void or delete the run first. The program never catches up skipped months by itself. If you skip a month, the Notes column warns you; choose the skipped month and post it. A units-of-production asset without a usage figure for the period is skipped, with the warning "Skipped FA-00004 (enter the meter reading / production count first)". A disposed asset is depreciated up to its disposal month and not after. Messages: "Select the assets to depreciate." (nothing ticked), "Nothing to post for this period." (every ticked asset had nothing to charge). The entry is dated the last day of the period. If that date is on or before the closing date, only users with the special permission to change closed periods can post it. See Company, Security & Closing Date . Posting needs the create permission on this page; voiding and deleting need the delete permission; printing needs the print permission.

Use Dispose of Assets when an asset leaves the company: it is sold, traded in, scrapped, donated or lost. The program brings the depreciation up to date, removes the asset's cost and accumulated depreciation from the books, records the money received, and posts the gain or loss. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Dispose of Assets. The Dispose button on an asset opens it with that asset chosen. The page opens with an empty Asset box and today as the Disposal date . Below is the list of Disposed assets with their cost, proceeds and disposal entry. When you choose an asset, its cost, accumulated depreciation, net book value and method appear, with the disposal form. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Asset The asset to dispose of. Only assets in service are listed. Disposal date The date of the sale or disposal. It cannot be before the acquisition date. Warning and Post them first (prorated to the disposal month) Shown when months up to the disposal month are not yet depreciated, with an estimate of the amount. Leave it ticked to post those months before the disposal. How / why (sold, scrapped, donated…) Required. It becomes part of the entry's memo and the audit trail, for example "Sold to ABC Trading Corp." Proceeds received The money received. Leave 0 for an asset scrapped or donated. Received into The account the money went into: a bank account or an Other Current Asset account. The default is 1050 Undeposited Funds. Class The class of the disposal entry. It starts with the asset's default class. Step by step: dispose of an asset Go to Fixed Assets > Dispose of Assets (or open the asset and click Dispose ). Choose the Asset and set the Disposal date . The page reloads with the asset's figures. If the yellow warning appears, leave Post them first (prorated to the disposal month) ticked so the depreciation is complete up to the disposal month. Type How / why , the Proceeds received and choose Received into . Click Record disposal and confirm "Dispose of this asset?". The program shows the Asset Disposal entry. The asset's status becomes Disposed . What it records If the catch-up box was ticked, the program first posts one depreciation entry for each month not yet depreciated, up to and including the disposal month (memo "Depreciation to disposal date - FA-00002"). Then it posts the Asset Disposal entry: Account Debit Credit The category's accumulated depreciation account Accumulated depreciation The Received into account Proceeds 4300 Gain (Loss) on Disposal of Assets Loss, if any Gain, if any The category's asset account Cost Example The Delivery Van (cost ₱1,200,000.00) is sold on 09/30/2026 for ₱1,050,000.00. With September depreciated, its accumulated depreciation is ₱120,000.00 and its net book value ₱1,080,000.00. The entry debits 1535 Accumulated Depreciation - Transportation ₱120,000.00, 1050 Undeposited Funds ₱1,050,000.00 and 4300 Gain (Loss) on Disposal of Assets ₱30,000.00 (the loss), and credits 1530 Transportation Equipment ₱1,200,000.00. The disposal entry is recorded under the asset's site and numbered in the journal entry series. When the buyer paid straight into the bank, choose the bank account in Received into . When you leave 1050 Undeposited Funds, the proceeds are not listed among the payments to deposit in Make Deposits ; deposit them there as a line of Other receipts with From account 1050 Undeposited Funds. Step by step: undo a disposal In Disposed assets , click the entry in the Entry column (or open it from the asset's status line). Click Void or Delete , type the reason and confirm. The asset goes back to Active and its disposal date and proceeds are cleared. The catch-up depreciation entries are separate entries and stay posted; void them in Run Depreciation if they should go too. Good to know Messages: "Choose an asset in service.", "The disposal date is before the acquisition date.", "Enter how and why the asset was disposed of.", "Choose the account that received the proceeds." (proceeds entered without an account). The gain or loss uses the default account Gain / Loss on Disposal of Assets . If it is not set, the program says so; set it in Module Default Accounts . For a units-of-production asset, the catch-up only posts months that have a usage figure, and the estimate in the warning shows 0.00. Enter the usage for the missing months first (on the asset or in Run Depreciation). Recording a disposal needs the create permission on this page.

Asset Maintenance keeps the history of every repair, servicing, inspection and upgrade of an asset: the supplier, the spare parts (with part, serial and model numbers for warranty claims), the labor, pictures of the parts, and the cost. When you save a record, the program also records the payment in the books as a bill, a check or a cash voucher, so maintenance is entered only once. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Asset Maintenance. It is also a Home page quick action, and Maintenance records on Preventive Maintenance opens it. The list shows the records of the last twelve months (and the next 30 days), void records left out. The filters Filter What it does From , To The maintenance dates to list Asset , Location One asset, or the assets of one location Type Repair , Preventive maintenance , Inspection / testing or Upgrade / overhaul Supplier Records of one supplier Status Completed and in progress (the default), Completed , In progress or Void Search (record, asset, part no., serial, model) Finds records by record number, description, problem, reference, asset, or any part's number, description, serial or model Click Show to apply the filters. The columns Date , Record (a picture icon shows when pictures are attached), Asset , Type , Work done , Supplier , Parts , Labor , Total , Paid through (the bill, check or cash voucher, marked "(void)" when voided) and Status . The last row counts the records and totals the parts, labor and cost (void records are not counted). Buttons New maintenance record opens a blank record. Preventive maintenance opens Preventive Maintenance . It turns red and shows the number of tasks due, for example Preventive maintenance (2 due) . Export downloads the list as a CSV file that opens in a spreadsheet (needs the print permission).

Fields Field What to enter / what it means Fixed asset The asset repaired or serviced. Type part of its name or number. The location and last meter reading appear under the box. Required. Date The date of the work. Required. Type Repair , Preventive maintenance , Inspection / testing or Upgrade / overhaul Status Completed , or In progress (post the cost later) for work not yet finished Supplier of the parts / service The supplier. Required when the cost is entered as a bill. Performed by (mechanic, technician, shop) Who did the work Supplier's invoice / job order no. The supplier's document number, kept as the reference of the bill or check Meter reading The odometer or running hours at the time of the work. It updates the asset's current meter reading (the reading only moves forward). Problem reported / reason Why the work was needed Downtime (days) How long the asset was out of use Next service date For your reference; shown on the record. To be reminded, set up a task in Preventive Maintenance. Maintenance description (work done, including what the labor was for) What was done. Required when labor is entered. Preventive maintenance task this completes One of the asset's preventive maintenance tasks. Saving the record as Completed acknowledges the task and moves it to its next due date. Spare parts and materials grid (one line per part; click Add part , Add 5 parts or Add 10 parts for more lines, and the square plus button at the end of a line to insert one above it): Column What to enter Part no. , Description , Brand The part. The description is required on a line that has a part number or cost. Serial no. , Model no. , Size Details that identify the part for warranty claims and re-ordering Qty , Unit , Unit cost Quantity (blank counts as 1), unit (for example pc) and cost per unit, net of VAT Amount , Warranty until Qty times unit cost (worked out for you) and the end of the part's warranty Labor grid (click Add labor line , Add 5 lines or Add 10 lines for more lines): Column What to enter Work done The job, for example Remove and install radiator and water pump. Required on every labor line. Worker / mechanic Who did it Charge By the hour (man-hours times rate) or Bulk charge (one agreed amount) Man-hours , Rate per hour , Amount For By the hour , the amount is worked out. For Bulk charge , type the amount. Disbursement (linked to accounting) : Field What to enter / what it means How is it paid? On account: enter a Bill (pay later in Pay Bills) , Paid by check: write a Check Voucher , Paid in cash: petty cash / revolving fund Cash Voucher , or No entry: already recorded elsewhere, or no cost Bank account Check only: the account the check is drawn on Cash account (petty cash, revolving fund) Cash voucher only: the cash fund that paid Parts charged to , Labor charged to The expense accounts. They start with the first active expense account whose name contains "Repair" (6030 Repairs and Maintenance in the demo). Class The class of the payment. On a new record it takes the asset's default class. Costs are net of 12% VAT (add input VAT) Tick it when the supplier charged VAT: 12% is added to the parts and the labor Supervisor approval For a check or cash voucher above your amount limit Pictures of the materials and parts : choose one or more JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP files, up to 8 MB each, and type a caption under each preview. Notes holds anything else. The box on the right totals Parts , Labor , Input VAT 12% and Total cost . Step by step: record a repair paid on account Go to Fixed Assets > Asset Maintenance and click New maintenance record . Choose the Fixed asset , for example Delivery Van (L300) (FA-00002), and set the Date , Type and Status . Choose the Supplier of the parts / service and fill in Performed by , the job order number and the Meter reading . Describe the Problem reported / reason and the Maintenance description . Enter each spare part in Spare parts and materials . Enter each labor line in Labor , choosing By the hour or Bulk charge . Under How is it paid? , leave On account: enter a Bill (pay later in Pay Bills) . Check the expense accounts and the VAT box. Add pictures if you have them. Click Save record . The message tells you which document was created, for example "Maintenance record MNT-00001 saved: Bill BILL-00003 for 12,500.00 was created." Step by step: record work that is still in progress Enter the record as above, with Status set to In progress (post the cost later) . Save it. No bill, check or cash voucher is made yet. When the work is done, open the record, click Edit , change Status to Completed , complete the parts and labor, and save. The payment is recorded now. Viewing a record Click the record number to open it. The top card shows the asset, date, type, status, supplier, performer, reference, location, meter reading, downtime, next service date, the preventive task done, the class and who entered it. Below are the spare parts (a Warranty until date still in the future shows in green), the labor, the pictures (click one to open it full size), the Cost box, and the Accounting box with the document that paid the cost and its ledger lines. When the cost is an unpaid bill, Pay this bill opens Pay Bills for the supplier. The buttons are Edit (not for void records), Print , Void , Delete and Back to list . Print gives the ASSET MAINTENANCE RECORD: the asset and its serial or plate number, the supplier and reference, the problem and the work done, the parts and labor tables, the total cost, and signature lines. Step by step: change or cancel a record To change it , click Edit , make the changes and save. The bill, check or cash voucher is updated to match. If you choose another How is it paid? , the old document is voided and a new one is created. Pictures are removed with the Remove link under each one on the edit form. To void it , click Void , type the reason and click Void maintenance record . The record and its details stay, marked void, and its bill, check or cash voucher is voided. To delete it , click Delete , type the reason and click Delete maintenance record . The record, its pictures and its accounting document are removed. A full copy is kept in the audit trail. What it records On a record with parts of ₱11,000.00 and labor of ₱1,500.00, paid on account with no VAT, the program enters a bill for the supplier: Account Debit Credit 6030 Repairs and Maintenance (parts) ₱11,000.00 6030 Repairs and Maintenance (labor) ₱1,500.00 2000 Accounts Payable ₱12,500.00 With the VAT box ticked, 12% of the parts and labor is also debited to 1300 Input Tax. A check credits the bank account instead of Accounts Payable; a cash voucher credits the cash fund. The bill uses the supplier's terms, is dated the maintenance date and is recorded under the asset's site. It is a normal bill: it appears in Enter Bills, Pay Bills and the payables reports. Good to know Recording the payment needs permission on the page of the document: create (or edit) on Enter Bills for a bill, on Write Checks for a check, on Cash Voucher for a cash voucher. Without it the program says "Your role cannot create a Bill. Ask someone who can, or save the record with "No entry" and have accounting record the payment." A check or cash voucher above your amount limit needs supervisor approval (the Supervisor approval box). Messages: "Choose the fixed asset that was repaired or maintained.", "Describe the maintenance that was done, or enter the parts and labor.", "Enter the maintenance description: what the labor was for.", "Enter the parts or the labor cost, or choose "No entry" when there is nothing to pay.", "Choose the supplier: a bill is owed to a supplier.", "Choose the bank account the check is drawn on.", "Choose the cash account the voucher is paid from.", "The preventive maintenance task belongs to another asset.", "... is not a picture. Upload JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP files." A paid bill or a reconciled check blocks voiding or deleting the record until the payment is dealt with. The Parts charged to and Labor charged to lists also offer Fixed Asset accounts. Charging a cost to an asset account does not change the asset's cost in the register, so the register and the ledger would no longer agree.

Preventive Maintenance keeps the recurring tasks that fall due by date, by meter reading, or both: vehicle registration renewal, insurance renewal, change oil, tune-up, cleaning of air-conditioning units, computers and solar panels, calibration, permits. A task that is due keeps reminding everyone who may open this page until someone acknowledges that it is complete. A repeating task then moves to its next due date. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Preventive Maintenance. It also opens from the bell in the top bar, from the Asset maintenance due card on the Home page, from the reminder pop-up, and from the Preventive maintenance button on Asset Maintenance. The three cards at the top count the active tasks: Overdue (past their due date or meter), Due soon (inside their reminder period) and Upcoming (scheduled, not reminding yet). Click a card to see those tasks. How a task becomes due By date : a task starts reminding the chosen number of days before its due date ( Due in 20 days ) and becomes overdue the day after ( 3 days overdue ). By meter : a task starts reminding when the asset's current meter reading is within 10% of the meter interval of the due reading, and becomes overdue when the reading reaches it. For a change oil every 5,000 km due at 50,000 km, it reminds from 49,500 km. A task with both a date and a meter takes whichever is more urgent. The tabs Every tab can be narrowed with the Asset , Location and Kind of task filters. Reminding now lists the overdue and due tasks, the most urgent first. Overdue rows have a red edge and due rows an orange edge. Upcoming lists the active tasks that are not reminding yet. All tasks lists every task, including stopped and finished ones. Completed is the log of every task acknowledged as complete: Completed (date), Asset , Task , Was due (in red when done late), Meter , Remarks , Acknowledged by and Record (the maintenance record, when the task was done through one). The Kind of task filter does not apply to this tab. The task lists show Asset (with its description and location), Task (with its notes), Due (the date, and the due meter with the current reading), State , Repeats , Last done and Responsible , followed by the Completed button, the edit button (pencil) and the delete button (trash).

Click New task . The form opens above the tabs. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Fixed asset The asset. Required. Kind of task Vehicle registration renewal , Insurance renewal , Change oil , Tune-up / servicing , Cleaning (air-con, computers, solar panels ...) , Inspection / calibration / testing , Permit / license renewal or Other maintenance . Choosing one fills in the task name if you have not typed one. Task (what has to be done) For example LTO registration renewal, or Change oil and filter. Left blank, the kind of task is used. Next due date When the task is next due Remind (days before) How many days before the due date it starts reminding (0 to 365; 14 by default) Repeats Tick it for a recurring task. Untick it for a one-time task, which is finished once acknowledged. Every The date interval, for example 3 month(s) or 1 year(s). Units: day(s), week(s), month(s), year(s). or every (meter: km, hours) The meter interval, for example 5000 Next due at meter reading The meter reading at which the task is next due. Leave blank for a task by date only. Required when a meter interval is entered. Meter reading of the asset now The asset's current odometer or running hours, and the unit (km, hours). It updates the asset's reading. The last reading is shown in grey. Person responsible Who takes care of it Notes (office to go to, requirements, supplier ...) For example Bring the OR/CR and the emission test result Active (keeps reminding) On the edit form only. Untick it to stop the task without deleting it. Step by step: add a recurring task Click New task . Choose the Fixed asset and the Kind of task , and check the Task name. Enter the Next due date and Remind (days before) . Leave Repeats ticked and enter Every (for example 12 month(s)), or a meter interval with the Next due at meter reading , or both. Enter the current meter reading if the task goes by meter, the Person responsible and any Notes . Click Save task (or Save task & New ). The message tells you when it starts reminding, for example "Task saved. It starts reminding 14 day(s) before 10/17/2026." To change a task, click its pencil button. The form opens as Edit task . Step by step: acknowledge a task as complete Click Completed on the task's row. The dialog Acknowledge the task as complete opens. Enter the Date completed (it cannot be in the future). Enter the Meter reading . It is required when the task repeats by meter. Type the Remarks (official receipt number, who did it, findings). Tick Then record the parts, labor and payment in Asset Maintenance if there is a cost to record. Click Task is complete . The task is written to the Completed log and its reminder stops. A repeating task moves to its next due date: counted from the due date when the work was done on time or early, from the completion date when it was late. The next due meter is the reading entered plus the meter interval. A one-time task is finished. If you ticked the last box, a new maintenance record opens for the asset. Tip When the work has a cost, you can instead create the maintenance record first and choose the task in Preventive maintenance task this completes . Saving the record as Completed acknowledges the task in one step and links the record in the log. The reminders The bell in the top bar shows the number of tasks due or overdue. Click it to open this page on Reminding now . With nothing due, the bell is quiet. The pop-up "Maintenance due: N tasks" appears after you log in, once a day, and again whenever the list of due tasks changes. Later closes it; Open Preventive Maintenance opens this page. It does not appear on this page itself. The Home page card "Asset maintenance due" lists up to 12 due tasks with their state and date, and an Open button. The reminders are shown to every user who may open Preventive Maintenance, and they stay until the task is acknowledged as complete. Disposed assets never remind. Good to know Delete (trash button) removes a task that was never completed. A task with completed entries is stopped instead, and its log stays: "The task was stopped. Its 1 completed entries stay in the log." Messages: "Choose the fixed asset.", "Enter when the task is next due: a date, a meter reading, or both.", "Enter the meter reading at which the task is next due.", "Enter the meter reading: this task repeats by km.", "The completion date cannot be in the future." If a task should no longer repeat by meter, clear or every (meter: km, hours) before unticking Repeats ; the meter interval is kept otherwise. Adding tasks needs the create permission, editing and acknowledging need the edit permission, deleting needs the delete permission. The Upcoming Preventive Maintenance and Completed Preventive Maintenance reports print these lists.

Asset categories group similar assets and decide which accounts they post to. The category also gives new assets their default depreciation method and useful life. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Asset Categories. The list on the left shows each category with its three account codes ( Asset / Accum. / Expense ), Default method , default Life and the number of Assets in it. Inactive categories are shown in grey. The form on the right adds a new category. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Name The category name, for example Transportation Equipment. Required. Asset account The Fixed Asset account the cost is debited to, for example 1530 Transportation Equipment Accumulated depreciation account The Fixed Asset account credited by depreciation, for example 1535 Accumulated Depreciation - Transportation Depreciation expense account The expense account debited by depreciation, for example 6090 Depreciation Expense. Expense, Other Expense and Cost of Goods Sold accounts are offered. Default method The method a new asset in this category starts with Default life (years) The useful life a new asset starts with (at least 0.5) Active Untick it to stop offering the category on the asset form. Its assets are not affected. Step by step: add or change a category Go to Fixed Assets > Asset Categories . To add one, fill in the New category form. To change one, click Edit on its row; the form becomes Edit category . Enter the Name and choose the three accounts. Choose the Default method and Default life (years) . Click Save category (or Save category & New ). Cancel leaves the edit form. Good to know All three accounts are required: "Enter the name and all three accounts." Create the accounts first in the Chart of Accounts . Asset and accumulated depreciation accounts must be of the type Fixed Asset to appear in the lists. The accounts are read from the category each time depreciation is run or an asset is disposed of. Changing the accounts of a category that already has assets sends their later depreciation and disposals to the new accounts, while their cost and past depreciation stay in the old ones. Prefer a new category, or move the balances with a journal entry. The default method and life only fill in the form of a new asset; changing them does not change existing assets. Categories cannot be deleted. Make an unused one inactive.

Asset Locations is the list behind the Location box of every asset: a branch, a building, a room, a vehicle yard. The Fixed Asset Register, the asset reports, Asset Maintenance, Preventive Maintenance and Run Depreciation can all be filtered by location. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Asset Locations. The Manage locations link on the asset form opens it in a new tab. The list shows each location with the number of Assets in service (click it to open the register filtered to that location), their total Cost , and whether it is Active . Fields Field What to enter / what it means Location name For example Head Office, Cordova Plant, Motor Pool. Required, and it must be unique. Active (offered on the asset form) Untick it to stop offering the location on new assets. Assets already there keep it. Step by step: add, rename or delete a location Go to Fixed Assets > Asset Locations . To add a location, type the Location name and click Save location (or Save location & New ). To rename one, click Edit , change the name and click Save location . The new name is written on every asset at that location. To delete one, click Delete on its row and confirm. The link appears only when the location has no assets in service. Good to know A location that still has assets, including disposed ones, cannot be deleted: "Main Warehouse still has assets. Move them to another location first, or make the location inactive." Messages: "Enter the name of the location.", "There is already a location named ...".

The fixed asset reports are under Fixed Assets > Reports in the sidebar and in the Report Center. Their common tools (Refresh, Columns, Print / PDF, Export to spreadsheet, Email link, Modify Report, Memorize, and clicking a figure to see the detail) are explained in Working with reports . Most of them have a Location filter with (No location) for assets without one.

The register of assets as of a date, with their cost, salvage value, accumulated depreciation and net book value. Use it at month end or year end to support the fixed asset accounts on the balance sheet. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Fixed Asset Register Report. The filters: As of , Asset category and Location . The columns: Asset no. (click to open the asset), Description , Category , Location , Acquired , Method , Life (yrs) , Cost , Salvage , Accum. dep. and Net book value , with a TOTAL row. The report lists the assets acquired on or before the date and not disposed of by then.
