Accumulated depreciation includes opening accumulated depreciation and the depreciation posted for months up to the as-of month. Tip Run it as of the last day of a month after posting that month's depreciation. The Cost total should equal the balance of the asset accounts and the Accum. dep. total the balance of the accumulated depreciation accounts on the balance sheet.

Compares straight-line, double-declining balance and sum-of-the-years'-digits year by year for one asset, or for any figures you type in. Use it to choose a method before adding an asset, or to explain an asset's depreciation. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Depreciation Schedule by Asset, or Compare methods on an asset. The filters: Asset , or with Asset on All , the Cost , Salvage and Life (years) of an example asset. Left blank, the example uses a cost of ₱500,000.00, a salvage value of ₱50,000.00 and 5 years. The columns: Year , the yearly depreciation by Straight-line , Double-declining balance and Sum-of-the-years'-digits , and the net book value at the end of each year under each method ( NBV (SL) , NBV (DDB) , NBV (SYD) ). The note above the table gives the depreciable cost, the double-declining rate and, for a units-of-production asset, the rate per unit. Note The comparison always uses a multiplier of 2 for declining balance and whole years for the life, whatever the asset's own settings. All three methods depreciate the same total; only the timing differs.

The depreciation posted in a period, by category and asset. Use it to check the depreciation expense of the month or year and to see which assets it came from. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Depreciation by Category. The filters: Dates (this fiscal year by default), From , To , Asset category and Location . The columns: Category / asset (grouped by category with a total for each), Method , Units used (units-of-production assets) and Depreciation . Only depreciation entries dated in the period and not voided are counted; opening accumulated depreciation is not.

The assets acquired and the assets disposed of in a period. Use it for the fixed asset movement schedule of the financial statements. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Additions and Disposals. The filters: Dates , From , To and Location . The report can also be narrowed by Asset category (see Filters on related records ). The columns: Two sections. Additions lists each asset acquired in the period with its Category , Date and Cost , and Total additions . Disposals lists each asset disposed of in the period with its Cost , Accum. dep. , Proceeds and Gain / (loss) , and Total disposals .

Every maintenance record in a period with its cost and the document that paid it. Use it to review what was spent on repairs and servicing. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Maintenance History. The filters: Dates , From , To , Vendor , Class , Asset , Location and Type (repair, preventive maintenance, inspection, upgrade). The columns: Date , Record (click to open it), Asset , Location , Type , Work done , Supplier , Reference , Parts , Labor , VAT , Total and Paid through . Void records are left out.

The maintenance cost of each asset in a period, most expensive first, compared with what the asset cost. An asset whose maintenance keeps climbing is a candidate for replacement. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Maintenance Cost by Asset. The filters: Dates , From , To , Class , Asset category , Location and Type . The columns: Asset (click to open its maintenance records), Category , Location , Jobs (number of records), Repairs (records of the type Repair), Parts , Labor , Total cost (before VAT), % of cost (the period's maintenance as a percentage of the asset's cost), Downtime (days) and Last job .

Every spare part recorded on maintenance records in a period, with its identifying numbers, supplier and warranty. Use it to follow up warranty claims and to see which parts are replaced often. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Spare Parts Used. The filters: Dates , From , To , Vendor , Asset and Location . The columns: Date , Record , Asset , Part no. , Description , Brand , Serial no. , Model no. , Size , Qty , Unit , Unit cost , Amount , Supplier and Warranty until . Tip To find one part across all records, use the Search box of the Asset Maintenance list: it searches part numbers, descriptions, serials and models.

Every labor line of the maintenance records in a period: the work, who did it, the man-hours and the charge. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Maintenance Labor. The filters: Dates , From , To , Vendor , Asset and Location . The columns: Date , Record , Asset , Work done , Worker / mechanic (the record's Performed by when no worker was typed on the line), Charge ( By the hour or Bulk charge ), Man-hours , Rate , Amount and Supplier . The total row adds up the man-hours (bulk charges have none) and the amounts.

The preventive maintenance tasks that are overdue, due now, or coming up. Print it for the person responsible, or to plan the month's servicing. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Upcoming Preventive Maintenance, or Upcoming report on Preventive Maintenance. The filters: Asset , Location , Kind of task , and Show : Overdue and due now , Due within 30 days , Due within 90 days , Due within a year or Every active task . Overdue and due tasks are always included. The columns: Asset , Location , Task (click it to open the asset's tasks), Kind , Due date , Due at meter , State , Repeats , Last done , Responsible and Notes . Overdue tasks are shown in red. The note above the table counts the overdue, due and upcoming tasks. Note When the report first opens, the Show box displays Overdue and due now , but the report lists the tasks due within 90 days. Choose the option you want and click Refresh .

The tasks acknowledged as complete in a period, and whether they were done on time. Where to find it: Fixed Assets > Reports > Completed Preventive Maintenance. The filters: Dates , From , To , Asset and Location . The columns: Completed , Asset , Location , Task , Was due , Timing ("5 day(s) late", "2 day(s) early" or "on the due date"), Meter , Remarks , Acknowledged by , Maintenance record (click to open it) and Cost (the total of that record). The note above the table counts the tasks completed and how many were late.

t: How a sale moves through the program
x: A sale can start as a quotation and end as money in the bank. You do not have to use every step: a walk-in sale goes straight to a sales receipt, and a regular account customer can be invoiced without an estimate or an order. Step Page Effect on the books Quote a price Create Estimates None Take an order Create Sales Orders None Bill on account Create Invoices Debits Accounts Receivable Bill many customers at once Create Batch Invoices Debits Accounts Receivable Sell for cash Enter Sales Receipts Debits Undeposited Funds Add a charge to an account Enter Statement Charges Debits Accounts Receivable Charge interest on late accounts Assess Finance Charges Debits Accounts Receivable Collect Receive Payments Credits Accounts Receivable Take goods back or give a credit Create Credit Memos/Refunds Credits Accounts Receivable Bank the collections Banking > Make Deposits Moves Undeposited Funds to the bank Remind the customer Create Statements None Estimates and sales orders are non-posting documents: they record a commitment but never touch the ledger or the stock on hand. Everything else in the table posts to the general ledger the moment you save it (unless you save an invoice or sales receipt as pending, explained under Create Invoices ). Collections are recorded in 1050 Undeposited Funds by default. They stay there until you group them into a bank deposit with Make Deposits , exactly as the cashier brings the checks and cash to the bank. Customers and jobs A job is a record kept under a customer, for a project or a branch you bill separately. It is shown as Customer:Job , for example ABC Trading Corp.:Office Renovation Project . A job has its own address, terms, price level and transactions, and it rolls up into its customer: The customer's open balance includes the balances of its jobs. Receive Payments is done for the customer; the invoices of its jobs are listed with it. Statements are made per customer and include the jobs. Finance charges are assessed on the customer, for the overdue documents of the customer and its jobs. The credit limit that counts is the customer's own, compared with the balance of the customer and all its jobs. A job cannot have jobs of its own.

Before you enter customers, make sure these lists hold what you need. They are kept under Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists in the Financial Set-up & Reports module: Payment terms : name, net days and an optional early-payment discount (for example "2% 10 Net 30": 2% off if paid within 10 days, due in 30). Tax codes : for example VAT12 (12%), ZR, EX and NT, each with its output tax account. Payment methods : Cash, Check, GCash, Bank Transfer and so on. Price levels : the demo company has Wholesale (-5%), VIP (-10%), Retail Plus (+5%), Price Level 4 to Price Level 10 (0%, ready to be renamed). Fixed prices per item and level are set on the item or in Set Item Prices and Levels (see Inventory ). Sales representatives : with their commission %, used by the Sales by Rep reports. Customer types and Billing groups (billing groups are used by Create Batch Invoices ). The accounts every customer transaction uses (Accounts Receivable, Undeposited Funds, Default Sales Income, Sales Returns and Allowances, Sales Discounts, Finance Charge Income, Reimbursable Expense Income, Creditable Withholding Tax, Creditable VAT Withheld and Output Tax) are set in Module Default Accounts . If one is missing, saving stops with a message such as "The default account "Accounts Receivable" is not set. Set it under Financial Set-up & Reports > Module Default Accounts." The finance charge rate, minimum charge and grace period are set in Company, Security & Closing Date . The discount and price limits of each role, and whether a role may exceed credit limits, are set in User Role Configuration .

The Customer Center is where you keep customer and job records and where you see everything about one customer: balance, credit limit, transactions, notes and reminders. It is also the quickest place to start any sale for a customer, because every form opens with the customer already filled in. Where to find it: Customers > Customer Center The customer list The left side lists your customers in alphabetical order, each job indented under its customer with an arrow. The figure beside each name is that record's own Accounts Receivable balance. Type to find a customer or job : the list narrows as you type, letter by letter, to the customers and jobs whose name, company name, contact person, phone or mobile contains what you typed. The count under the box says how many are shown ("3 of 24 customer(s) and job(s)"). When nothing matches, the list says No customer matches. Press Enter to search the whole list on the server. Press Enter to open the first match, or, when the list on screen is filtered to active customers, to search the whole list, inactive ones included. The drop-down beside it shows Active customers (the default), All customers including inactive ones (marked "inactive"), or only those With balance . Click a name to show its details on the right. At the top of the page, New customer / job opens a blank customer form and Export list downloads the list shown as a spreadsheet file (CSV) with the name, parent customer, company, contact, phone, email, billing address, terms, credit limit, balance and active flag. Exporting needs the print permission. A customer's details The top card shows the name (as Customer:Job for a job), the company name and TIN, the contact person, phone, mobile and email, and the billing address. On the right are: Open balance : what the customer owes today. For a customer, it includes the balances of its jobs. Credit limit : the limit, or "none". Available credits : shown in green when the customer has unapplied payments or credit memos. Below are the Terms , Price level (Standard when none is set), Tax , Rep , Type and Pays by (preferred payment method). Example In the list, ABC Trading Corp. shows ₱171,410.40, its own balance. The details show an open balance of ₱178,354.40, because its job Office Renovation Project owes another ₱6,944.00. The buttons under the details work on the selected customer: Button What it does Edit Opens the customer record for changes Add job Starts a new job under this customer (customers only) Estimate , Sales order , Invoice Opens a new form for this customer Sales receipt , Statement charge , Credit memo Opens a new form for this customer Receive payment Opens Receive Payments for this customer Apply credits to invoices Shown when credits are available; applies them in Receive Payments Balance detail Runs Customer Balance Detail for this customer Transaction list Runs Transaction List by Customer for this customer Statement Makes last month's statement for this customer The Transactions card lists the customer's documents, newest first (up to 300), including those of its jobs. Use the type drop-down to show one kind only (Estimates, Sales orders, Invoices, Sales receipts, Payments, Credit memos, Statement charges, Finance charges or Refunds) and the date box to change the starting date, which is 1 January of last year by default. The columns are Type , No. , Date , Job (filled for a job's document), Amount , Open (the unpaid part of an invoice or charge, or the unused part of a payment or credit memo) and Status . Click a number to open the document. The Notes and to-do reminders card shows the Notes field of the customer record first, then every note added here, with who added it and when. A to-do has a checkbox icon and a Done link; a done to-do is struck through. Open to-dos also appear under To-do reminders on the Home dashboard, overdue dates in red, so collection calls are not forgotten. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Customer / job name The name used on every list and form. Required. Job of (leave blank for a customer) For a job, the customer it belongs to. Leave blank for a customer. Company name The registered name. Printed on documents and statements instead of the name when filled. Contact person The person you deal with. Shown on the Collections Report. Phone , Mobile Contact numbers. Email Used by the Email buttons of documents and statements. TIN Printed under the Bill to address. Billing address Printed on invoices and statements, copied into Bill to on forms. Shipping address Copied into Ship to on forms. Payment terms Copied into Terms on invoices; decides the due date. Credit limit (0 = none) The most the customer may owe. 0 means no limit. Price level Standard, or a price level that changes the prices on sales forms. Tax code Used by Create Batch Invoices on taxable lines. Preferred payment method Suggested on Receive Payments and on sales receipts started from here. Customer type A grouping of your own, for example Corporate or School. Sales representative Copied into Sales rep on forms. Billing group (batch invoicing) Puts the customer in a group for Create Batch Invoices. Taxes this customer withholds The taxes of the Withholding Tax Table the customer usually withholds from what it pays you, for example a government office: WT on VAT 5% and WT on Goods 1%. Receive Payments ticks them when one of its invoices is ticked. Approved account customer at the POS Allows charge sales to this customer at the POS register. Active Untick to hide the customer from the drop-downs of forms. Reason for change (required for credit limit changes) Shown when editing. Explain any credit limit change. Notes Free text shown at the top of the notes card. Step by step To add a customer: Click New customer / job . Type the Customer / job name and leave Job of blank. Fill in the company, contact, addresses, TIN and the terms, credit limit, price level and other settings. Click Save customer , or Save customer & New to go on with the next one. To add a job: Select the customer in the list. Click Add job . The form opens with the customer in Job of . Type the job name and its own address, terms and settings. Click Save customer . To change a customer or its credit limit: Select the customer and click Edit . Change what you need. If you changed Credit limit (0 = none) , type the reason in Reason for change (required for credit limit changes) . Click Save customer . To add a note or a to-do reminder: Select the customer. In the Notes and to-do reminders card, type the note in Add a note or reminder . Optionally pick a date, and tick To-do if it is something to follow up. Click Add . When the task is done, click Done beside it. Good to know Customers are never deleted. Untick Active instead; the history stays and the customer disappears from the drop-downs of new forms. Two customers cannot have the same name, and two jobs of one customer cannot either: "Another customer or job already has this name." A credit limit change without a reason stops with "Enter a reason for changing the credit limit." Users with the Approve permission on the Customer Center, and administrators, may leave the reason blank. Every change is kept in the audit trail with the values before and after. Adding notes needs the edit permission on the Customer Center. The price level and sales representative of the record chosen on a form are used, so a job can have its own price level.

Six pages share the same form, list and document view: Create Estimates , Create Sales Orders , Create Invoices , Enter Sales Receipts , Enter Statement Charges and Create Credit Memos/Refunds . This section explains what they have in common; each page's own section explains only what is different. The list of documents Clicking one of these pages in the sidebar opens its list. At the top are New (to start a document) and Export (to download the list shown as a spreadsheet file; needs the print permission). Filter What it does From , To The date range. It starts 90 days back and ends 30 days ahead. Status Shows one status only. The choices depend on the page. Class Shown when classes are in use; shows one class. Search Finds a number, reference, memo or customer name. Click Filter to apply them. The list shows up to 500 documents: Date , No. , Name , Reference , Memo , Class , Total , Open (on pages where something can remain unpaid or unused), Status and By (the user who entered it). Voided documents are struck through. Click a number to open the document. The header of the form These fields appear at the top of every sales form. Fields that only some forms have are explained in their page's section. Field What to enter / what it means Customer:Job The customer or job. Type part of the name to find it. Required. Date The document date. Today by default. Number Leave blank to get the next number shown in grey, such as INV-00014 (auto). You may type your own. Sales rep Filled from the customer. Used by the Sales by Rep reports. Bill to Filled from the customer's billing address. Ship to Filled from the customer's shipping address. Printed on the document. Class Shown when classes are set up. The class the whole document belongs to. Memo An internal note. It is also the memo of the ledger lines and prints in small grey text. Customer message Printed at the bottom of the document. "Thank you for your business." by default. When you choose the customer, the program fills in Bill to , Ship to , Sales rep and (on invoices) Terms from the customer record. On a new invoice or credit memo with no lines yet, the page reloads for that customer, so the billable costs or the customer's open invoices can be shown. Note The printed "Bill to" block is always taken from the customer record (company name, billing address and TIN), not from the Bill to box of the form. To change the address on the printout, correct the customer record in the Customer Center . Item lines The lines grid holds what you sell. Three blank lines are ready (one on a statement charge); click Add line , Add 5 lines or Add 10 lines for more, the square plus button at the end of a line to insert an empty line above it, and the red X to remove a line. The Inventory site chosen at the top is copied onto every line. Column What to enter / what it means Item The item. Type part of its code or name to find it. Description Filled with the item's sales description. You may change it. Qty The quantity, in the unit shown in U/M. Set to 1 when you pick an item. U/M The unit of measure. Shown only when an item on the form has more than one unit. Rate The price for one unit. Filled from the item and the customer's price level. Discount A figure, and % (percent of the line) or Amt (an amount off the line). Amount Quantity times rate, less the discount. Worked out for you. Tax The tax code, taken from the item. The tax is worked out from the amount. How the item list shows each item (code first or name first) is set under "Searching for items" in Company, Security & Closing Date , for all forms or for each form separately. Whichever way it is shown, typing any part of the code or the name finds the item. Only active items are offered. If you type an Amount yourself on a line that has a quantity and no discount, the program works the Rate back from it. On a line with no quantity and no rate, the amount you type is used as it is. Every line with a description or an amount needs an item: "Choose an item for every line that has a description or amount." A form with no lines stops with "Add at least one line." Prices and price levels When you pick an item, the rate is the item's sales price for the customer chosen on the form: A customer with no price level (Standard) gets the item's sales price. A customer with a price level gets the fixed price set for that item and level, if there is one. Otherwise the sales price is changed by the level's percentage. With VIP (-10%), an item selling at ₱899.00 is offered at ₱809.10. Choose the customer before the items. Lines already on the form keep their rates if you change the customer afterwards. See the Item Price List for the price of every item at every level. Units of measure Items that belong to a U/M set can be sold in any unit of the set (see Inventory ). The U/M column starts on the item's default sales unit. Changing the unit re-prices the line for the new unit. Stock always moves in the base unit. Example Metro School Supplies buys 3 dz (dozen) Keyboard USB at ₱11,000.00 a dozen, with ₱1,500.00 off ( Amt ). The line amount is 3 × ₱11,000.00 less ₱1,500.00 = ₱31,500.00, and 36 pc leave the warehouse. Discounts on a line Type the discount in the Discount column and choose % or Amt beside it. A percent cannot be more than 100, and an amount off can never be more than the line itself. The printout shows the discount in the description, for example "(less 1,500.00)". Special items Besides service, inventory, non-inventory, assembly and other charge items, four kinds of items behave differently on a sales form: Discount item : with a percentage, it takes that percent off the line just above it; without one, it takes off the amount in its Rate (or its sales price). Its amount is negative. Subtotal item : adds up the lines above it, back to the previous subtotal, and shows the total under its description. Put a discount item right after a subtotal to discount a group of lines. Group item : a set of items sold together at its own Group price (see Item groups on sales documents ). Payment item : money received on the document itself. Type the amount in Rate ; it reduces the total due and is recorded in Undeposited Funds. Item groups on sales documents An item group (for example GRP-WFH Work-from-Home Bundle: a laptop, a mouse and a backpack) is sold on one line of an estimate, sales order, invoice, sales receipt, statement charge or credit memo, and at the POS. Pick the group: Qty is the number of groups and Rate is the price of one group, its Group price (with the customer's price level), or the sum of the prices of its items when Adopt the Group Price in the Item Group is cleared or the group has no group price (see Item groups: group price and price variance ). A discount on the line is taken off the group. When the document is saved, the group line is recorded as the items in it, each at its own price, so stock, cost of sales and the sales of each item are kept as always, plus one line Price variance: Work-from-Home Bundle for the group price less the prices of its items, posted to the group's Price variance GL account . The document total is the group price times the quantity. A group sold for less than its price, or at another price, needs the same supervisor approval as an item. A document with item groups has two buttons above its lines, on its page and on its edit form: Button What it shows View by item group One line per group: the group, how many, its price and amount, and under the description the items it holds. Editing in this view changes the group as a whole: a new quantity or price re-prices all of its items and its variance, and the saved lines keep their place (what was invoiced from a sales order stays linked). View item details Every item of each group on a line of its own, at its own price, with the price variance line and "In item group ..." under the description. Each line can be edited on its own. Print prints the document the way it is shown. A sales order or estimate with groups comes across to its invoice by group, with the groups still to be invoiced; invoicing one group of four leaves three on the sales order. When Track Item Group Sales transactions is ticked (System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date > Inventory and POS), each group sold is also kept apart as a group, for Sales by Item Group and POS Sales by Item Group . Tax and totals The box at the bottom right shows Subtotal , Tax and Total , and changes as you type. Tax is worked out per line: the line amount times the rate of its tax code. The printed document shows "Subtotal (net of VAT)", "VAT" and "Total". Supervisor approval Estimates, sales orders, invoices, sales receipts and batch invoices check every line against the limits of your role (set in User Role Configuration ): Max discount % without approval : applies to a line discount (a percent, or an amount off counted as a percent of the line) and to the percentage of a discount item. Max price change % without approval : a rate that differs from the customer's price by more than this percent. A blank limit on the role means no limit. If a line goes over, saving stops with a message such as "Supervisor approval is required: 15.00% discount on LAP-001. Ask a supervisor to enter their username and password below." and the Supervisor approval box opens, marked "required". The supervisor types their Supervisor username and Password there, and you save again. The supervisor must have the Approve permission on the page and cannot approve their own document. Their name is recorded as Approved by on the document and on the printout. A user who has the Approve permission on the page does not need anyone else. Other messages you may see: "Approval failed: the supervisor username or password is wrong." (the failed attempt is logged) and "(name) is not allowed to approve on this page." Example In the demo company the A/R Clerk role may give up to 10% discount and change prices by up to 5% without approval. Class When classes are set up, the Class box appears on every form. If you save without choosing one, the program asks: "This transaction has no class. It will be saved as Unclassified and will not appear under any class on the class reports." Click Choose a class to go back, or Continue saving . Saving Save saves and opens the saved document. Save & New saves and opens a blank form for the next one. Cancel leaves without saving. If something is wrong, the form comes back with the message in red at the top and nothing is saved. Correct it and save again. A saved document is posted at once; editing it later removes the old ledger entries and stock movements and records the new ones, so the books always match the document. The saved document A saved document shows its details (date, number, status, customer, class, reference, due date, terms, sales rep, account, payment method, site, memo, who entered it and when, and who approved it), its lines, and the totals with the Open balance (invoices and charges) or Unapplied credit (credit memos). Users with the "View costs and margins" permission also see the Cost of each stocked line and a General ledger entries created automatically card with the journal lines. Related documents lists the documents it was created from, converted to, paid by, applied to, refunded by or deposited in, each one clickable. Button What it does Edit Opens the form to change the document Print Opens the printable copy Email Starts an e-mail to the customer in your mail program Memorize Saves the document as a memorized transaction Close / Reopen Estimates and sales orders: stop or resume expecting the rest Void Cancels the document's effect but keeps it (posting documents) Delete Removes the document History Opens its change history in Transaction History Back to list Returns to the list Other buttons appear when they apply, such as Create Invoice , Receive Payment , Mark as final , Apply credit to invoices and Refund ; they are explained on each page. Printing and emailing Print opens the document on a clean page with Print and Back buttons on top. Click Print to send it to a printer or save it as PDF from your browser. The printout carries the company name, address, TIN and phone (with the logo when the administrator switched it on), the document title and number, the date, the due date or "Valid until", the customer's name, billing address and TIN, the ship-to address, reference, terms, site and class, the lines, the customer message and memo, the totals ("Balance due" on invoices and charges), and signature lines for Prepared by , Checked by , Approved by and Received by . A voided document prints with "VOID". Email opens a new message in your own e-mail program, addressed to the customer's email, with a subject such as "Invoice INV-00002 from Sample Trading Company" and a link to the printable copy. The program does not send the e-mail itself; you check and send it. Printing and emailing both need the print permission and are recorded in the audit trail. Memorizing Memorize keeps a copy of the document to enter again later, for example a monthly service invoice. The dialog asks for Name it , Group (optional) , How it is entered (Enter it automatically, Remind me when it is due, or Don't remind me), Every (a number and Day(s), Week(s), Month(s), Quarter(s) or Year(s)), Next due , Remind (days before) , Number remaining (blank = no limit) and Notes . The names, items and amounts are kept; the date and number are given each time. See Memorized Transactions . Voiding and deleting Both ask for a Reason (required, recorded in the audit trail) . Void keeps the document, marked VOID with the reason and time, and removes its effect on the ledger and the inventory. Its status becomes Void. Delete removes the document. A full copy stays in the audit trail. Estimates and sales orders never post, so they have only Delete . The program refuses to void or delete a document when: payments or credits were applied to it: "Payments or credits have been applied to it. Remove them first (edit the payment or credit)." it was included in a bank deposit: "It is included in deposit DEP-00001. Remove it from the deposit first." a credit memo or payment was refunded: "It has been refunded (…). Void the refund first." an estimate or sales order was already converted in part: "It has already been converted or received in part. Close it instead." Rules for every form The closing date: without the permission "Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled", you cannot enter, change, void or delete a document dated on or before the closing date: "The books are closed through 08/31/2026. You do not have permission to record transactions dated on or before the closing date." A document cleared in a bank reconciliation cannot be changed by users without that permission. Users limited to certain inventory sites only see and use those sites: "You are not allowed to record transactions for that site." Inactive customers and items are not offered on new forms. Every save, edit, void, delete, print and e-mail is recorded in the audit trail.

An estimate is a price quotation. Use it when a customer asks how much something will cost before ordering. It does not affect the books or the stock, and when the customer accepts, you turn it into a sales order or an invoice with one click, without typing the lines again. Where to find it: Customers > Create Estimates. Also Estimate in the Customer Center, and Create Estimates under Quick actions on the Home dashboard (opens a new form). The list's Status filter offers Pending, Accepted and Closed. Fields The common fields are explained under Working with sales forms, earlier in this chapter. The estimate adds: Field What to enter / what it means Reference Any reference, for example the customer's inquiry number. Valid until How long the quoted prices hold. 30 days from today by default. Printed on the estimate. Status Pending (waiting for the customer), Accepted or Closed . The lines grid has the Discount column. The Supervisor approval box is below the lines. Step by step To prepare an estimate: Click New . Choose the Customer:Job . Bill to, Ship to and Sales rep fill in. Check the Date and Valid until . Add the lines: choose each item, then correct the quantity, rate or discount if needed. Type a Memo if useful, for example "Office equipment for 5 workstations". Click Save . To send it, open the estimate and click Print or Email . To turn an accepted estimate into a sales order or an invoice: Open the estimate. Click Create Sales Order or Create Invoice . The new form opens with a blue note "Creating from Estimate EST-00001." and with the customer, addresses, sales rep, class and lines of the estimate, including their tax. The memo reads "From Estimate EST-00001". Change what is different, for example the quantity the customer really ordered. Click Save . To bill an estimate in stages (progress billing), create the invoice from the estimate and lower the quantities or amounts to the part you are billing now. The estimate remembers how much of each line has been invoiced. The next invoice made from it leaves out the lines already invoiced in full, but brings any other line at its full estimate quantity, so lower it again to the part being billed. To close an estimate the customer declined, open it and click Close , then confirm "Close this document? Remaining quantities will no longer be expected." Reopen puts it back to Pending. What it records Nothing. An estimate is a non-posting document ("Non-posting document: it records a commitment and does not affect the ledger."). It does not move stock. The status changes by itself: Creating a sales order from a Pending estimate makes it Accepted . Invoicing part of it makes it Accepted ; invoicing every line in full makes it Closed . Close makes it Closed; Reopen makes it Pending. Good to know Estimates cannot be voided, only deleted, and only while nothing has been created from them. After that, use Close . Discounts and price changes above your limits need supervisor approval, even on an estimate, so a quotation cannot promise a price the company would not approve. The Related documents card lists every sales order and invoice made from the estimate.

A sales order records what the customer ordered and you have promised to deliver. Use it when goods are delivered or billed later, or in parts. The order tracks how much of each line has been invoiced, so back orders are never forgotten. Where to find it: Customers > Create Sales Orders. Also Sales order in the Customer Center, Create Sales Order on an estimate, and Create Sales Orders under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. The list's Status filter offers Open, Partially filled, Closed and Void. Fields The common fields are explained under Working with sales forms, earlier in this chapter. The sales order adds: Field What to enter / what it means Customer P.O. No. The customer's purchase order number. Carried to the invoice. Expected ship date When you expect to deliver. Shown on the Open Sales Orders reports. Inventory site The warehouse or store the goods will come from. When you edit a saved order, the grid has two more columns: Invoiced (the quantity already invoiced) and Closed (tick to stop expecting the rest of that line). A line that has been invoiced in part has no X : it cannot be removed, only closed. Step by step To enter a sales order: Click New , or click Create Sales Order on the estimate. Choose the Customer:Job and type the Customer P.O. No. Set the Expected ship date and the Inventory site . Enter or check the lines. Click Save . To invoice what you deliver: Open the sales order and click Create Invoice (shown while the order is Open or Partial). The invoice opens with every line not yet fully invoiced, at the quantity still open. Closed lines are left out. Lower the quantities to what you are delivering now, or remove the lines you are not delivering. Click Save . The order's Invoiced column goes up and its status becomes Partial, or Closed when everything is invoiced. To stop expecting the rest of an order, open it and click Close (all lines), or edit it and tick Closed on single lines. Reopen opens all lines again. What it records Nothing in the ledger ("Non-posting document"). The quantities not yet invoiced count as "on sales order" in the inventory reports and in Open Sales Orders by Item , which helps purchasing see what is needed. The status is set by the program: Open (nothing invoiced), Partial (some lines invoiced) and Closed (every line invoiced or closed). Good to know A line already used on an invoice cannot be removed: "A line that was already used on another document cannot be removed. Close the line instead." A sales order cannot be voided, and cannot be deleted once invoiced in part; use Close . If you delete or void an invoice made from the order, the invoiced quantities go back on the order. The expected ship date is not printed on the sales order itself; it appears in the Open Sales Orders reports.

An invoice bills a customer who pays later. It records the sale, the output VAT and the amount the customer owes, and takes stocked items out of inventory. Use it for every credit sale; use a sales receipt instead when the customer pays on the spot. Where to find it: Customers > Create Invoices. Also Invoice in the Customer Center, Create Invoice on an estimate or sales order, and Create Invoices under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. The list's Status filter offers Unpaid (open or partly paid, not pending), Open (nothing paid yet), Partially paid , Paid , Pending and Void . The Open column shows what is still owed on each invoice. Fields The common fields are explained under Working with sales forms, earlier in this chapter. The invoice adds: Field What to enter / what it means Customer P.O. No. The customer's purchase order number. Printed as "Reference". Terms Filled from the customer. Decides the due date and any early-payment discount. Due date (blank = from terms) Leave blank to use the date plus the terms' net days. Inventory site The warehouse or store the goods leave from. Pending (non-posting until marked final) Tick to save the invoice without posting it yet. If the customer has billable costs, a Billable time and costs for this customer card appears below the lines, with a Markup % box. Step by step To enter an invoice: Click New . Choose the Customer:Job . Terms, Sales rep, Bill to and Ship to fill in, and the page reloads for that customer. Type the Customer P.O. No. if there is one. Leave Due date blank to use the terms. Check the Inventory site . Enter the lines. Click Save . To bill costs you paid for a customer's job (billable time and costs): Make sure the costs were entered in Enter Bills or Write Checks with the customer or job in Customer:Job and Billable ticked (see Vendors and Payables ). Start the invoice for the customer. Costs of the customer and of all its jobs are listed with their date, source, vendor, description and amount. Tick Add on each cost to bill. Type a Markup % if you add a margin (it applies to every ticked cost). Click Save . Each cost becomes a line "Reimbursable: …" credited to Reimbursable Expense Income, and it leaves the list of unbilled costs. To hold an invoice until it is approved (pending): Tick Pending (non-posting until marked final) before saving. Save. The invoice shows "This transaction is pending. It does not affect the books or inventory until it is marked final." When it is approved, open it and click Mark as final . The form opens with Pending unticked and the note "Pending is unticked — saving posts this sale." Click Save . The invoice now posts. To collect on an invoice, open it and click Receive Payment . See Receive Payments . What it records For every line: a credit to the item's income account (4000 Sales if the item has none) and a credit to the output tax account of its tax code (2100 Output Tax by default). For an inventory or assembly item, also a debit to Cost of Goods Sold and a credit to Inventory at the item's average cost, and the quantity leaves the inventory site. The total is debited to 1100 Accounts Receivable for the customer. Example Invoice INV-00002 bills Office Renovation Project for 2 hr installation (₱3,000.00) and 4 hr repair (₱3,200.00), both VAT12. Account Debit Credit 1100 Accounts Receivable ₱6,944.00 4010 Service Income ₱3,000.00 2100 Output Tax ₱360.00 4010 Service Income ₱3,200.00 2100 Output Tax ₱384.00 For a laptop sold from stock, two more lines appear, for example debit 5000 Cost of Goods Sold ₱32,000.00 and credit 1200 Inventory ₱32,000.00. Special lines post as follows: a discount item debits its own income account (it is a negative amount), a payment item debits 1050 Undeposited Funds, and billable costs credit 4110 Reimbursable Expense Income. The status is Open until a payment or credit is applied, then Partial , then Paid . A pending invoice has the status Pending , posts nothing, has no open balance and is left out of the aging reports. Good to know Credit limit: when you save an invoice that is not pending, the program adds it to the balance of the customer (with all its jobs) and compares the result with the customer's credit limit. Over the limit, saving stops with a message such as "Credit limit exceeded: balance 178,354.40 + this invoice 80,000.00 > limit 250,000.00." Users without the permission "Can exceed customer credit limits" see "You are not allowed to exceed customer credit limits." and cannot save it. Users with it get a Credit limit override reason box: type the reason and save again; the override is recorded in the audit trail. A pending invoice skips the credit limit check until it is marked final. Items with no unit cost: an inventory part (or assembly) that has neither a Unit cost on its item form nor an average unit cost cannot be sold on an invoice, sales receipt, statement charge or POS sale, because its cost of goods sold would be zero. Saving stops with "This item has no unit cost and no average unit cost, so the sale would record no cost of goods sold: 0224 - Chicken Feet WN. Enter the unit cost on the item (Inventory > Item List), or receive it at its cost first, then save again." For an item group, each item of the group is checked and the message adds "(in item group GRP-WFH)". An item with a unit cost but no stock received yet goes out at that unit cost. The check can be switched off with Block sales of items with no unit cost in Company, Security & Closing Date ; estimates and sales orders are not checked. Selling more than the quantity on hand follows the setting Allow selling or moving stock below zero (with warning) . Switched on (the standard), the program first asks "Saving the transaction will lead the inventory to a negative balance. Do you want to continue?" (see Stock below zero: the Yes / No question ); Yes saves the invoice and a yellow message names the items now below zero, for example "Stock is now below zero: LAP-001 at Main Warehouse (-2.00).", No goes back to the invoice. Switched off, the invoice is not saved: "Not enough stock: LAP-001 at Main Warehouse has 3.00 on hand, and this would leave -2.00. …" The same applies to sales receipts. See "Stock below zero" in Inventory . An invoice with payments or credits applied cannot be voided or deleted until they are removed from the payment or credit. The printed "Balance due" is the open balance; a pending invoice prints ₱0.00 there because it is not yet owed. To bill many customers the same items at once, use Create Batch Invoices . Charge sales at the POS register also create invoices (see Point of Sale ).

Create Batch Invoices bills the same items to many customers in one step, for example a monthly service fee to all your maintenance contract customers. Each customer gets a separate invoice with their own terms and prices. Where to find it: Customers > Create Batch Invoices, or Create Batch Invoices under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Select a billing group… Picks a billing group and ticks its customers. Select all Ticks or unticks every customer. Customer checkboxes The customers to invoice. The billing group shows after the name. Invoice date The date of every invoice. Today by default. Inventory site The site the goods leave from. Memo "Monthly billing" and the month by default. Customer message Printed on each invoice. Class Shown when classes are set up. Use each customer's price level Ticked by default: each invoice uses the customer's price level. Item lines The items, quantities, rates and discounts billed to every customer. The totals under the lines are for one invoice, "before customer-specific prices". Step by step Choose a group in the Select a billing group… box. The page reloads with that group's customers ticked, so choose the group before typing anything else. Tick or untick customers as needed. Check the Invoice date , Inventory site , Memo and Customer message . Enter the lines to bill. Leave Use each customer's price level ticked to price each invoice for the customer, or untick it to bill everyone the rates you typed. Click Create invoices . The page shows "N invoices created (batch B…)" and a card with every invoice, its customer and total, and an Email link for each. Click Print all to print every invoice of the batch, each on its own page. What it records Each invoice posts exactly like one entered in Create Invoices : debit Accounts Receivable, credit income and output tax, and cost of goods sold for stocked items. Each invoice gets the customer's own terms, due date, sales rep, billing and shipping address. On lines that have a tax code, the tax code of the customer record is used instead when the customer has one, so a zero-rated customer is billed ZR. Good to know Messages: "Enter the invoice date.", "Select at least one customer." and "Enter the items to bill." Discounts and price changes above your limits need supervisor approval, as on single invoices. The rates are compared with the items' standard prices. Batch invoices are not checked against credit limits and are never pending. Jobs are listed by their own name (for example "Office Renovation Project"), and can be ticked like customers. Billing groups are made in Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists ; a customer joins a group in its record in the Customer Center .

A sales receipt records a sale paid in full on the spot: cash, check, card or e-wallet. It records the sale and the money received in one step, so there is nothing to collect later. Where to find it: Customers > Enter Sales Receipts. Also Sales receipt in the Customer Center, and Enter Sales Receipts under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. The list's Status filter offers Open, Closed, Paid, Pending and Void. A posted sales receipt shows Open, because there is nothing left to pay on it. Fields The common fields are explained under Working with sales forms, earlier in this chapter. The sales receipt adds: Field What to enter / what it means Check / reference no. The check number or payment reference. Inventory site The site the goods leave from. Payment method How the customer paid. Filled from the customer when started from the Customer Center. Deposit to Where the money goes. 1050 Undeposited Funds by default. Pending (non-posting until marked final) Tick to save it without posting yet. A customer is required. Use a customer such as "Walk-in Customer" for anonymous counter sales. Step by step Click New . Choose the Customer:Job . Type the Check / reference no. and choose the Payment method . Leave Deposit to on 1050 Undeposited Funds if the money will be deposited later with other collections, or choose the bank account if it went straight to the bank. Enter the lines. Click Save . The printout is titled "OFFICIAL RECEIPT" unless the administrator set another "Receipt title for sales" in Company, Security & Closing Date . What it records The same income, tax and cost of goods sold lines as an invoice, but the total is debited to the Deposit to account instead of Accounts Receivable. Example SR-00001 sells Juan Dela Cruz a laptop, a backpack and a mouse for ₱46,466.56. Account Debit Credit 1050 Undeposited Funds ₱46,466.56 4000 Sales ₱41,488.00 2100 Output Tax ₱4,978.56 5000 Cost of Goods Sold ₱32,850.00 1200 Inventory ₱32,850.00 The view lists the cost lines item by item (₱32,000.00, ₱500.00 and ₱350.00); they are added up here. The money stays in Undeposited Funds until you include it in a deposit with Make Deposits . The Related documents card then shows "Deposited in: Deposit DEP-00001". Good to know A pending sales receipt works like a pending invoice: nothing posts until you click Mark as final and save. A sales receipt included in a deposit cannot be voided or deleted until it is removed from the deposit. Discounts and price changes above your limits need supervisor approval.

A statement charge adds an amount to a customer's account without a full invoice, for example a late payment fee or a small service charge. It appears on the customer's next statement and can be paid in Receive Payments like an invoice. Where to find it: Customers > Enter Statement Charges. Also Statement charge in the Customer Center, and Enter Statement Charges under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. Fields The form is shorter than an invoice: there is no sales rep, inventory site, Bill to or Ship to, and the lines grid has no Discount column and starts with one line. Field What to enter / what it means Customer:Job The customer charged. Required. Date The date of the charge. Number Blank for the next number (SC-…). Reference Any reference. Due date (blank = from terms) When the charge is due. The form has no Terms field, so a blank due date becomes the charge date. Class , Memo , Customer message As on other sales forms. Step by step Click New . Choose the Customer:Job . Type a Due date if the charge is not due at once. Choose the item, for example LATE-FEE, and check the amount. Type a Memo such as "Late payment fee". Click Save . What it records Like an invoice: debit 1100 Accounts Receivable, credit the item's income account and output tax. SC-00001 for Green Valley Clinic debits Accounts Receivable ₱200.00 and credits 4100 Finance Charge Income ₱200.00, the income account of the LATE-FEE item. The status is Open, Partial or Paid, as for invoices. Open statement charges appear in the aging reports, on statements and in Receive Payments. Good to know Statement charges are not checked against the credit limit or the discount limits. To charge interest on overdue balances for all customers at once, use Assess Finance Charges .

A statement of account shows a customer what they owe: the balance, the transactions of the period and how old the unpaid amounts are. Send statements at the end of the month or before a collection call. Where to find it: Customers > Create Statements, Statement in the Customer Center, or Create Statements under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. Fields Field What to enter / what it means From The first day of the period. First day of last month by default. To (statement date) The last day of the period and the date of the statement. Format Balance forward , Open item or Transaction statement . Customers (none selected = all) Pick one or more customers (hold Ctrl to pick several). None picked means all active customers. Skip zero balances Ticked by default: customers owing nothing get no statement. Skip customers with no activity Leaves out customers with no transactions in the period. Include aging summary Ticked by default: adds the aging row at the bottom. Only customers are listed, not jobs; a customer's statement includes its jobs. The three formats: Balance forward : starts with the balance at the From date ("Balance forward"), then each transaction of the period with its Charges , Payments / credits and running Balance . Open item : lists only what is still open at the statement date: each unpaid invoice or charge with its Due date, Amount and Open balance , and each unapplied payment or credit as a negative amount. A job's document shows the job name. Transaction statement : the transactions of the period with Charges and Payments / credits, without the balance forward row or running balance. Step by step Set From and To (statement date) . Choose the Format . Pick the customers, or none for all. Tick or untick the options. Click Preview statements . The statements appear below the settings. Click Print all (N) to open the printable statements in a new tab, each on its own page, and print them. To e-mail a statement, click the button with the customer's name (shown for customers with an email). It opens a message in your e-mail program with the subject "Statement of account as of 09/30/2026" and the balance in the text. Each statement shows the company name, address and TIN, "STATEMENT", the statement date and format, the customer's company name and billing address, the table, the aging row ( Current , 1 - 30 , 31 - 60 , 61 - 90 , > 90 and Amount due , or just "Amount due" without aging) and the line "Please disregard this statement if payment has already been made. Thank you." Example ABC Trading Corp.'s September statement starts with a balance forward of ₱183,332.80, shows payment PMT-00001 of ₱101,500.00 (₱100,000.00 received and ₱1,500.00 withholding tax) and invoices INV-00002 and INV-00003, and ends with ₱178,354.40 due, of which ₱81,832.80 is 1 - 30 days past due. Good to know Statements record nothing in the books. They read Accounts Receivable, so they always agree with the Customer Balance reports. The aging row counts days past the due date as at the statement date. Unapplied credits count as Current. Printing statements needs the print permission. Previewing and printing are recorded in the audit trail.

Assess Finance Charges works out interest on overdue balances for every customer and posts it as finance charges. Run it at the end of a month if your terms allow you to charge interest on late payments. Where to find it: Customers > Assess Finance Charges, or Assess Finance Charges under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. The box at the top shows the settings in use, for example "Annual interest rate 12.00%, minimum charge 50.00, grace period 0 days, earlier finance charges are not charged interest. Interest runs from the due date (or the last assessment) to the assessment date. A customer already charged on or after the assessment date is not charged again." They are changed with Finance charge settings , which opens Company, Security & Closing Date (Annual interest rate %, Minimum finance charge, Grace period (days) and Charge interest on earlier finance charges). The columns Column What it means Checkbox Ticked customers are charged. All are ticked at first. Customer The customer. Jobs are included in their customer. Overdue documents Each overdue document and the days of interest counted. Last charged The date of the customer's last finance charge. Overdue balance The open amount of those documents. Finance charge The interest worked out. You may change it. How the charge is worked out For each open invoice, statement charge (and earlier finance charge, if that setting is on) whose due date plus the grace period is before the assessment date: interest = open amount × annual rate ÷ 100 × days ÷ 365 the days run from the due date, or from the last finance charge if that is later, to the assessment date. a customer who already has a finance charge dated on or after the assessment date is left out: that period has been charged. The interest of all the customer's documents is added up, and a customer's charge is never less than the minimum charge. Example On 09/27/2026, INV-00001 of ABC Trading Corp. has ₱81,832.80 open and has been due for 20 days. At 12% a year: ₱81,832.80 × 12% × 20 ÷ 365 = ₱538.08. Green Valley Clinic was last charged on 09/26/2026, so only 1 day counts; its interest is below the minimum, so it is charged ₱50.00. Step by step Type the Assessment date and click Recalculate . Untick the customers you will not charge. Change a Finance charge amount if you agreed on another figure. Choose a Class if you use classes. Click Assess charges . The program shows "N finance charge(s) posted." and opens the list of finance charges. Posted finance charges opens this list at any time. Click a number to open a finance charge; from there you can print, email, void or delete it. What it records One finance charge per ticked customer, numbered FC-…, dated and due on the assessment date, with the memo "Finance charge on overdue balance as of …" and a line naming the documents charged: Account Debit Credit 1100 Accounts Receivable ₱538.08 4100 Finance Charge Income ₱538.08 Finance charges appear on the next statement, in the aging reports and in Receive Payments. Good to know If nobody is overdue, the page shows "No customers have overdue balances as of …". "Select at least one customer to charge." appears if you click Assess charges with every customer unticked or every amount at zero. A customer is never charged twice for the same period. After an assessment, the customers charged no longer appear for that date or any earlier one, and if the page is sent again (a double click, or a second user assessing at the same time) the program posts nothing more for them and says "Not charged again, already charged on or after …" with their names. To undo a charge, void it; the customer then appears again. A saved finance charge cannot be changed, so it has no Edit button. To correct a charge, void it and assess again, or enter a statement charge for the difference.

A forecast holds the sales you expect from each customer, month by month, for one fiscal year. Compare it with what was really sold using the Forecast vs Actual by Customer report. Where to find it: Customers > Set Up Forecast The list shows Name , What it budgets , Fiscal year , Customer , Class , Yearly total and Notes , with an Amounts button to enter the figures and a trash button to delete the forecast. Forecast vs actual opens the report. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Name For example "Forecast 2026". Required. What it budgets Always "Sales forecast by customer". Fiscal year The year the forecast covers. Customer (blank = one sheet for all customers) One customer, or All customers in one sheet. Class (optional) Limits the actual figures to one class. Notes Any note. Start from last year's actual figures Fills the months with last year's income for the customer. The months follow the fiscal year start set in Company, Security & Closing Date ; the form says, for example, "The fiscal year starts in January". Step by step Click New forecast . Type the Name and Fiscal year , and choose the customer or leave it blank for all customers. Tick Start from last year's actual figures to begin from last year's sales. Click Create . The amounts page opens. For each customer (one sheet per customer when you chose all customers), type the expected sales in the income account rows, one box per month. The row, column and grand totals update as you type. To fill a row quickly, click in the row, type an amount in Fill a row and click Across (the same amount every month), or type a yearly amount in Yearly total and click Spread (divided evenly over the twelve months). Click Save the amounts . The page shows "N monthly amount(s) saved." To change the figures later, click Amounts on the list. Good to know Only active income and other income accounts are offered as rows. The same name cannot be used twice for the same year: "There is already a forecast called "…" for 2026." Deleting asks "Delete "…" and its amounts?" and cannot be undone. Forecasts do not record anything in the books. Budgets for accounts are made in Set Up Budgets .

Receive Payments records money a customer pays on their account and applies it to their invoices and charges. It also handles early-payment discounts, tax withheld by the customer, available credits and overpayments. Where to find it: Customers > Receive Payments. Also Receive payment in the Customer Center, Receive Payment on an open invoice, and Receive Payments under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Received from The customer. Choosing one reloads the page with their open invoices. Date The date the payment was received. Amount received The money received. If you leave it blank, it adds up the payments you apply. Payment method How it was paid. Filled from the customer. Check / reference no. The check number or transfer reference. Deposit to Where the money goes. 1050 Undeposited Funds by default. Class Shown when classes are set up. Memo Any note. Under the fields, the program shows the Customer balance and, if any, the Available credits . Only customers are listed in Received from . The invoices of a customer's jobs are listed with the customer, with a Job column. The Outstanding invoices and charges table lists every open invoice, statement charge and finance charge, the ones due first at the top: Column What it means Checkbox Tick to pay the invoice. Date , Type / No. The document. Click the number to open it. Job The job, when the document belongs to one. Due The due date, in red when overdue. Original , Open The document total and what is still owed. Disc. avail. The early-payment discount the terms allow on this date. Discount The discount you give. Posted to Sales Discounts. Withholding The taxes the customer withheld, by type (see below). Ask the customer for its BIR Form 2307. Credits Available credit used on this invoice (shown when there are credits). Payment The part of the money received applied to this invoice. Totals applied adds up the Payment column (and the Credits column). The bar at the bottom shows Received , Applied , Unapplied and, when used, Credits applied . Step by step To record a payment: Choose the customer in Received from . Check the Date , choose the Payment method and type the Check / reference no. Type the Amount received , or leave it blank for now. Tick the invoices being paid. With no amount typed, each ticked invoice is paid in full and the amount received adds itself up. With an amount typed, each ticked invoice gets what is left of it, and the program tells you when an invoice can only be paid in part. Or, after typing the amount received, click Auto-apply amount : the amount is spread over the invoices, oldest due first. Anything left over stays as a credit for the customer. Type any Discount , and tick the taxes the customer withheld in the Withholding box of the invoices they belong to. Check Deposit to . Click Save payment (or Save payment & New for the next customer). The program shows "Payment saved." and opens the payment. Example ABC Trading Corp. pays INV-00001 with a check of ₱100,000.00 and a BIR Form 2307 for ₱1,500.00 withheld. Tick the tax in the Withholding box of INV-00001 and type 1,500.00 over its amount, and type 100,000.00 in Payment : the invoice is reduced by ₱101,500.00. The taxes the customer withheld The Withholding box of an invoice opens the taxes of the Withholding Tax Table that apply to payments from customers. Tick the ones the customer withheld (one or more): each amount is worked out from the open balance net of VAT and can be typed over, and the Payment on the invoice drops by the same figure. A customer's usual taxes ( Taxes this customer withholds on its record) are ticked when its invoice is ticked. The box works even before the invoice is ticked: its tax base already shows the open balance net of VAT, and ticking a tax ticks the invoice. Example (a government buyer): the City Government of Makati pays an invoice of ₱100,688.00 (₱89,900.00 plus ₱10,788.00 VAT) and withholds 5% VAT (₱4,495.00) and 1% income tax (₱899.00) on the ₱89,900.00. Tick WT on VAT and WT on Goods on the invoice: Payment becomes ₱95,294.00, the check received. The two kinds are kept apart, as the BIR requires: the 1% / 2% income tax withheld is debited to 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax (a credit against the company's income tax), the 5% VAT withheld to 1315 Creditable VAT Withheld (a VAT credit, 2550Q Item 16, listed in the Creditable VAT Withheld Schedule ). Neither is input VAT. A payment saved before the taxes were kept by type keeps its withholding as it was. To give the early-payment discount: Enter the payment date. If it is within the discount days of the invoice's terms (for example "2% 10 Net 30"), the Disc. avail. column shows the discount and the Discount box shows it in grey. Type the discount in Discount . It is not filled in for you. Apply the rest as the payment. Example Cebu Tech Hub pays INV-00006 of ₱96,718.72 within 10 days on terms 2% 10 Net 30. The discount is ₱1,934.37, and the payment ₱94,784.35. To apply available credits (unapplied payments or credit memos): Choose the customer. The Available credits card lists each credit with its date, memo and available amount. Click Apply available credits to spread all the credits over the open invoices, the ticked ones first, then the oldest; or type an amount in Apply now on a credit; or type an amount in the Credits column of an invoice. Add a payment if money was also received, or leave Amount received blank to apply only the credits. Click Save payment . The message says how much credit was applied ("Credits applied." when no money was received). To refund an overpayment: Record the payment with the full amount received. The part not applied stays as a credit: "Overpayment of … is kept as a credit for this customer." Tick Refund any overpayment before saving to go straight to the refund form, or later click Refund on the payment. See Create Credit Memos/Refunds . To change a payment, open it from the Payments list and click Edit . The customer cannot be changed. Payments taken at the POS are changed from the POS module. Payments list opens the list of customer payments. Its Status filter offers Has unapplied credit , Fully applied and Void , and the Open column shows the unused part of each payment. What it records Account Debit Credit Deposit to (1050 Undeposited Funds) Amount received 4060 Sales Discounts Discounts 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax Income tax withheld (1% / 2%) 1315 Creditable VAT Withheld VAT withheld (5%) 1100 Accounts Receivable Total of the above For the ABC Trading Corp. example: debit Undeposited Funds ₱100,000.00 and Creditable Withholding Tax ₱1,500.00, credit Accounts Receivable ₱101,500.00. The invoices paid become Partial or Paid. Applying a credit moves no money and records no ledger entry: the credit memo or earlier payment already reduced Accounts Receivable. It only links the credit to the invoice, so both show as settled. Good to know The payments applied can never be more than the amount received. The Unapplied figure turns red, a message explains, and the save buttons are disabled until you correct it or click Auto-apply amount . Messages you may see: "Choose a customer.", "The amount received cannot be negative.", "The amount applied to INV-… is more than its open balance (…).", "You applied … but received only …. Lower the payments on the invoices, or correct the amount received.", "Credit … has only … available.", "Enter the amount received or choose credits to apply." and "The credits chosen (…) are more than the open invoices can take. Lower the credit amounts by …". Pending invoices are not listed; mark them final first. Credits recorded on a job are not listed when you receive a payment from the customer. Open the job's credit memo and click Apply credit to invoices instead. A payment included in a bank deposit cannot be voided or deleted until it is removed from the deposit. Voiding a payment removes its applications, so its invoices are open again. Money in Undeposited Funds reaches the bank account with Make Deposits .

A credit memo reduces what a customer owes: for goods returned, a price correction or an allowance. The credit can be kept for later, applied to an invoice at once, or paid back as a refund. This page also records refunds of overpayments. Where to find it: Customers > Create Credit Memos/Refunds. Also Credit memo in the Customer Center, and Create Credit Memos/Refunds under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. The list shows credit memos and customer refunds together, with a Type column. The Open column shows the credit still available. A refund queued for printing shows "to print" beside its status until it is printed. Fields The common fields are explained under Working with sales forms, earlier in this chapter. The credit memo adds: Field What to enter / what it means Reference For example the invoice the goods were sold on. Inventory site The site of the sale. Return goods to stock Ticked by default: stocked items come back into inventory. Return to site Where returned goods go. Same as inventory site by default. On a new credit memo, the What to do with this credit card asks: Field What to enter / what it means Credit Keep as available credit , Apply to an invoice now or Give a refund . Invoice With Apply: the open invoice to reduce. Choose the customer first so the list fills. Step by step To record returned goods: Click New . Choose the Customer:Job . The page reloads for the customer. Leave Return goods to stock ticked if the goods can be sold again, and choose Return to site if they go to another site. Untick it for defective goods that will not return to stock. Enter the items, quantities and rates returned, with the same tax code as the sale. Type a Memo such as "Returned 2 defective keyboards". In Credit , choose what to do with it: Keep as available credit : the customer uses it on a later payment. Apply to an invoice now : choose the Invoice ; the credit reduces it by up to its open balance. Give a refund : after saving, the refund form opens ("Now record how the refund was paid."). Click Save . To apply a kept credit later, open the credit memo and click Apply credit to invoices . Receive Payments opens with all the customer's available credits spread over the open invoices; change the amounts if needed and click Save payment . See Receive Payments . To refund a credit memo or an overpayment: Open the credit memo or payment and click Refund (shown while it has unapplied credit). The page "Refund Credit Memo CM-00001" shows the customer and the available credit. Fill in: Date . Pay from account : the bank account the refund is paid from. Required. Refund method : cash, check and so on. Amount : the available credit by default; you may refund less. Memo : "Refund of Credit Memo CM-00001" by default. Class , when classes are set up. Queue a refund check for printing : tick if a check will be printed. Click Record refund . The program shows "Refund recorded." and opens the refund. The refund takes the next check number and prints as a REFUND VOUCHER with the payee, address, TIN, amount in words, the account paid from, the ledger lines and signature lines including Received by . What it records A credit memo is the reverse of a sale. Each line is debited to 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances (whatever item it is), its tax is debited to the output tax account, and the total is credited to 1100 Accounts Receivable. With Return goods to stock ticked, stocked items come back into the site at the current average cost: debit Inventory, credit Cost of Goods Sold. Example CM-00001 credits Metro School Supplies for 2 keyboards returned to stock. Account Debit Credit 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances ₱1,898.10 2100 Output Tax ₱227.77 1200 Inventory ₱1,233.33 5000 Cost of Goods Sold ₱1,233.33 1100 Accounts Receivable ₱2,125.87 A refund pays the credit back: Account Debit Credit 1100 Accounts Receivable Refund amount Pay from account (bank) Refund amount The credit memo's status is Open while it has unapplied credit and Closed when it is fully applied or refunded. Good to know Refund messages: "The refund must be more than zero and no more than the available credit (…)." and "Choose the account the refund is paid from." A refund above your role's "Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval" needs supervisor approval ("refund above your amount limit"). Voiding or deleting a refund above that amount needs approval too. Refunds cannot be edited: "Refunds cannot be edited. Void it and record a new one." A credit memo that was refunded cannot be voided until the refund is voided: "It has been refunded (…). Void the refund first." Voiding a credit memo that was applied removes the application and reopens the invoice. The What to do with this credit card only appears on a new credit memo. Discount and price limits are not checked on credit memos.

These reports show who owes what, how old the amounts are and how customers pay. They share the report tools explained in Working with reports : Refresh , Columns , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize , and clicking a figure or number to open what is behind it. All of them are in the sidebar under Customers > Reports , in the group "Customer and Receivables Reports", and in Home > Report Center . Where a report has a Customer filter, choosing a customer also includes its jobs. The aging reports sort each open amount by the number of days past its due date at the As of date: Current (not yet due, and all unapplied credits), 1 - 30 , 31 - 60 , 61 - 90 and > 90 days past due. Pending invoices are never included.

Shows, for each customer and job, how much is owed and how long it has been overdue. Use it to see at a glance who to call first. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > A/R Aging Summary. Also the "overdue document(s)" link under Accounts Receivable on the Home dashboard. Filters: As of and Customer . Each row is a customer or job with its open amounts in the five aging columns and the Total . Unapplied payments and credits are included as negative Current amounts, so Metro School Supplies shows -₱2,625.87 in Current. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type (see Filters on related records ). Above the table the report checks itself against the ledger: "Accounts Receivable per ledger: 253,913.11 — agrees with the aging total." If it says the ledger "differs from the aging total", something was posted to Accounts Receivable without a customer document, usually a journal entry; look for it in the General Ledger. Click a customer to open the A/R Aging Detail for that customer.

Lists every open document grouped by aging period, so you can see exactly which invoices are late. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > A/R Aging Detail Filters: As of and Customer . The groups are Current, 1 - 30 days past due, 31 - 60, 61 - 90 and > 90, each with its total. The columns are Type , Date , Num (click to open), Customer , Terms , Due date , Days past due and Open balance . The report keeps its own order and cannot be re-sorted. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type (see Filters on related records ).

Shows the Accounts Receivable balance of every customer and job at a date, straight from the ledger. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Customer Balance Summary The report can also be narrowed by Customer and Customer type (see Filters on related records ). Filter: As of . Columns: Customer:Job and Balance . Only customers with a balance are listed. When every entry to Accounts Receivable names a customer, the total equals the Accounts Receivable account on the Balance Sheet at the same date. Click a name for its Customer Balance Detail.

Lists every transaction that changed each customer's balance, with a running balance. Use it to answer "how did we arrive at this balance?". Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Customer Balance Detail, or Balance detail in the Customer Center. Filters: As of and Customer . For each customer and job: Type , Date , Num , Memo , Amount (charges positive, payments and credits negative) and the running Balance , then a total. A payment shows the full amount taken off the balance, including any discount and withholding: PMT-00001 shows -₱101,500.00. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type (see Filters on related records ).

Lists every unpaid invoice, statement charge and finance charge, and every unapplied payment or credit memo, grouped by customer. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Open Invoices Filters: As of and Customer . Columns: Type , Date , Num , Terms , Due date , Days past due and Open balance , with a total per customer. Unapplied credits appear as "Unapplied Customer Payment" or "Unapplied Credit Memo" with a negative amount. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type (see Filters on related records ). Tip Unapplied credits next to open invoices of the same customer can be applied to them in Receive Payments , with or without new money.

Lists only the overdue documents, with the customer's contact person, phone and email, ready for collection calls. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Collections Report Filters: As of and Customer . Each customer heading shows the Contact , Phone (phone and mobile) and the email in the Num / email column. Under it: Type , Date , Num / email (the document number), Due date , Days overdue and Amount due , with a total per customer. Documents not yet due and unapplied credits are left out. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type (see Filters on related records ).

Shows how many days, on average, each customer takes to pay an invoice in full. Use it to review credit terms and credit limits. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Average Days to Pay Summary Filters: Dates (this fiscal year by default), From , To and Customer . Columns: Customer , Invoices paid and Average days to pay , and an OVERALL AVERAGE row. Only invoices fully paid during the period count; the days run from the invoice date to the date of the payment or credit that finished paying it. Statement and finance charges are not included. Click a customer for the detail. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type (see Filters on related records ).
