Date the order on or after the bill that brought the stock in. Click Save as pending . The order is saved, does not affect inventory or the books, and shows its amounts as estimates. When the inputs are in, open the order. In the box "When the inputs are available at the processing site, complete the order here.", check the Processing date and click Complete and post . The saved order The page shows the order's details (date, number, status, type, method, formula × batches, sites, reference, memo, who entered and approved it), the Inputs (consumed) , the Additional processing costs , and the Outputs (produced) and cost allocation with the Yield of each output (actual against planned, red when below 100%). The inputs grid ends with a Total inputs line (quantity and cost), the outputs grid with a Total outputs line (quantity, the allocation percentages, which add up to 100%, and the cost allocated), then a Variance qty line, the input quantity less the output quantity, and a Variance line: the inputs and additional costs less the outputs. The variance is 0.00 when the whole cost was allocated, and is highlighted when it is not, for example with the Current average cost or Manual amounts method, where the difference is posted to the variance account. A completed order also shows the General ledger entries created automatically . The Quantity summary box gives the Input quantity , the Output quantity and the Variance qty (inputs less outputs) ; when the lines use different units of measure (boxes in, pieces out) it says so, since the quantities are added as entered. The Cost summary box gives input materials, additional costs, total cost, by-products and scrap, co-products and variance. Each input shows its Unit cost and Cost . Example A meat shop cuts 5.02 kg of pork into 2.3 kg of Pork Humba and 2.7 kg of Pork Menudo. Total inputs 5.02, total outputs 5, so the Variance qty (inputs less outputs) is 0.02 kg: the trimmings lost in cutting. The cost of the 5.02 kg is still spread over the two outputs. Its buttons: Edit: changes the order (not on a voided one). Saving a posted order posts it again. Run again: a new order with the same formula, batches and site. Print: the PROCESSING ORDER printout. The inputs table gives each input's Qty , Unit cost and Cost ; the Total inputs and Total outputs lines close the grids, and a small table at the right gives Inputs , Outputs , Variance (inputs less outputs) and Variance qty (inputs less outputs) , followed by the Prepared by, Processed by and Checked / approved by lines. Users who may not view costs get the quantities only, with the variance qty. Void: keeps the document but takes the outputs back out of stock and returns the inputs. Delete: removes it; its full content stays in the audit trail. History , Back to list . What it records The inputs and additional costs are credited; the outputs are debited with their allocated cost. When PRC-00005 is completed (2 TRD-PC at ₱3,000.00 and ₱300.00 of labor, shared by relative sales value after the scrap): Account Debit Credit 1200 Inventory (4 RAM-8GB) ₱3,131.69 1200 Inventory (2 SSD-512) ₱3,048.31 1200 Inventory (8 SCRAP-KG by-product) ₱120.00 1200 Inventory (2 TRD-PC) ₱6,000.00 5200 Direct Labor Absorbed ₱300.00 With Current average cost or Manual amounts , a difference between the cost and the outputs' values is posted to the variance account: a debit when the outputs are worth less (a loss), a credit when they are worth more (a gain). Good to know A supervisor must approve an order whose total cost is more than your Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval . "Every input needs an item and a quantity greater than zero." and "Outputs must be inventory or assembly items." An order is not posted while an input has no unit cost or average unit cost, or a co-product or by-product would be received at no cost: "The processing order cannot be posted with no unit cost: the input PORK-LOIN has no unit cost or average unit cost, and the outputs PORK-CHOP, PORK-WASTE would be received at no cost. ..." The input shows no unit cost in red in Est. unit cost , and the output's Unit cost box is outlined in red. Enter the unit cost of the input on its item form or receive it at its cost first, and give every co-product and by-product a share of the cost (scrap may stay at zero). Save as pending still works, and Complete and post is checked the same way. The check can be switched off with Block posting processing orders with no unit cost in Company, Security & Closing Date . "This order cannot be voided: its outputs were already used, and stock would go below zero for ..." appears when the outputs were sold or used and negative stock is not allowed. When it is allowed, the void goes ahead with the warning "Its outputs were already used; stock is now negative for .... Record the missing receipt or adjustment." "A voided processing order cannot be edited." The costs of a pending order are estimates at today's average costs. How processing orders move the average cost A processing order is often where an item's average cost changes most, because it does two things at once: it takes the inputs out at their average cost, and it puts the outputs in at their share of that cost. Five things decide what it does to the averages. The inputs go out at the average of all sites. Whatever the input's average is when the order is saved passes into the outputs. If the input's average is wrong, every output inherits it: a carcass at an overstated ₱462.69 instead of ₱225.00 makes every cut about twice as dear. Each output takes its share of the cost. The share follows the Allocation method of the order or its formula: with Physical units or Weight / measure every kilo gets the same unit cost, trimmings as much as the chops; with Relative sales value the dearer cuts take more; with Fixed percentages the shares never change. When the input cost, the shares or the yields change from one order to the next, the unit cost of an output changes with them, and so does its average. A formula with relative sales value or fixed percentages keeps the unit costs steadier. With Current average cost (difference to variance) the outputs come in at their own average, which then does not move at all; the difference goes to the processing variance account. Outputs received while they are below zero. When the counter sells cuts before the processing order is entered, the cuts go below zero at their last average. The order then settles that shortfall at its own unit cost and charges the difference to cost of goods sold (see Stock below zero ). Before version 31 the difference stayed on the few units left and could multiply the average. Inputs used before the bill is entered. The same happens to the input: processed before the supplier's bill is in, it goes below zero, and the bill settles the shortfall. Entering the bill first, or on the same date (the stock received is counted first on each date), keeps the cuts at the bill's cost. Back-dated and edited orders. A saved order is costed at the averages of the moment it is saved, not of its date, and saving an old order again issues its inputs at today's average. Utilities: Verify & Rebuild Data works every cost out again in date order. The Average Cost Changes report lists each of these as it happened, with the average before and after; tick Processing, disassembly and builds only to see the processing orders alone. Note Version 31 fixes a fault that made averages jump after processing orders. A processing order that uses all of a bill leaves the site at zero, and Rebuild Data removed such zero rows from the quantities table. When the order or the bill was saved again later, the quantity at that site was not taken down, so the table held less than the movements (the Inventory Center showed "The quantity on hand (-4.81) differs from the total of its movements (91.86) by -96.67"), and every receipt after that divided the value by too small a quantity: bills at ₱225.00 showed averages of ₱625.64 and ₱462.69. The average is now always worked out on the quantity of the movements, and the upgrade script puts the quantities table right. Run Rebuild Data once after the upgrade so the orders and sales costed at the overstated averages are costed again.

After you count the goods at a site, type the counted quantities here. The program compares them with the system quantities and posts the differences as one inventory adjustment with the reason "Count difference". Where to find it: Inventory > Physical Inventory Count. Also the Enter counts button of the Physical Inventory Worksheet and the Home dashboard Quick actions . Fields Field What to enter Site The site you counted. Changing it reloads the page. Hide system quantities (blind count) Tick it so the counter does not see the system quantities; the System qty and Difference columns are hidden. Count date The date of the count. Counted by The counter's name. It goes into the memo: "Physical count by ...". Count sheet no. The number of the count sheet. Class The class, if you use classes. Counted For each item, the quantity counted. Leave it blank to skip the item. The grid lists every active inventory part and assembly with its Unit , Pref. vendor , System qty and, as you type, the Difference (negative in red). Step by step: count a site Click Print blank worksheet . The Physical Inventory Worksheet opens for the site with the system quantities hidden; print it and count. Open Inventory > Physical Inventory Count and choose the Site . Type the Count date , Counted by and Count sheet no. Type each counted quantity in Counted . Leave items you did not count blank. If the Supervisor approval box opens, ask a supervisor to type their username and password. Click Post count differences . The message "n count difference(s) posted." appears and the adjustment opens. What it records One inventory adjustment for the site, with a line for each item whose count differs ("Count difference (counted x, system y)"). Missing goods are debited to 5100 Inventory Adjustments and Shrinkage and credited to 1200 Inventory at average cost; extra goods the reverse. The adjustment appears in the adjustments list . Good to know "No differences to post. Counted quantities match the system." The difference is worked out against the system quantity when you post, not when the page was opened. Stop sales and receipts at the site while you count, or post the count right after. A supervisor must approve when the differences are worth more than your amount limit. Users without the Create permission see blank lines in the Counted column instead of boxes.

Change Item Prices raises or lowers the sales price of many items at once, by a percentage or an amount, or sets it from cost with a markup. Where to find it: Inventory > Change Item Prices. Also Change prices by percentage on Set Item Prices and Levels. Fields Field What to enter Item type All types , Inventory parts , Assemblies , Non-inventory parts , Services or Other charges . Category All categories or one category. Change Adjust the current price , or Set new price from cost (markup) (users who may view costs). By With Adjust the current price : Percent or Fixed amount . Percent / amount (negative to lower) The percentage or amount. Type a minus sign to lower prices. For a markup, the markup percentage on cost. Round to nearest No rounding , 0.05 , 1.00 , 10.00 or 100.00 . The table shows, for each active item of the chosen type and category, a tick box, the item name/code, display name, Category , Cost (average cost for stocked items; users who may view costs), Current price and New price (in blue when it changes). Step by step: raise prices by a percentage Open Inventory > Change Item Prices . Choose the Item type and Category . The page reloads with those items. Choose Adjust the current price , Percent , type 5 and choose Round to nearest 1.00 . Click Preview . Check the New price column. Untick the items that should keep their price (the box in the heading ticks or unticks all). Click Apply to selected and confirm "Update the selected prices?". The message "n price(s) updated. New prices apply immediately on invoices, sales receipts, the POS and the Item Price List." appears. Step by step: price from cost Choose Set new price from cost (markup) . Type the markup, for example 40 for cost plus 40%. Click Preview , check, then Apply to selected . Good to know "Select at least one item." Prices never go below 0.00. Changing a price does not change the value of stock already on hand, or documents already saved. Price levels that follow a percentage follow the new price; fixed level prices do not change. Each change is recorded in the audit trail with the old and new price. The Item Price List button opens the Item Price List report.

This page shows one grid with the default selling price and every price level of many items, so you can set a whole price list in one pass and save it once. Where to find it: Inventory > Set Item Prices and Levels. Every company has ten price levels. As delivered they are Wholesale (−5%), VIP (−10%), Retail Plus (+5%) and Price Level 4 to Price Level 10 (0%, the same as the default price); the Rename price levels button at the top of the page gives them your own names (see below). The filters Filter What it does Item type All types, or inventory parts, assemblies, non-inventory parts, services or other charges. Category All categories or one. Find (code, name or barcode) Part of a code, name or barcode. Items per page 50, 100, 250, 500 or All of them . Include inactive items Lists inactive items too, marked inactive . Show Applies the filters. The grid The first columns are the item name/code, display name, Category and Cost (users who may view costs). Then: Default price: the item's sales price. Type the new figure. One column per active price level, in the order of the levels, with its percentage under the name ( same as default for 0%). An empty box follows the level's percentage of the default price; the figure it would use is shown in grey. Type a figure to fix that item's price on that level; clear it to go back to the percentage. With all ten levels active the grid is wide: it scrolls sideways inside its card, and the item columns stay in view. The note above the grid reminds you: "Prices exclude tax unless your items are set up tax-inclusive." Fill a column The box Fill a column writes figures into a whole column of the page in one go: Field What to enter Fill a column Default price or a price level. With The level's own percentage of the default price (price level columns only), The default price, changed by a percentage , Cost plus a markup percentage , One figure for every row or Nothing (empty the column) (price level columns only). Percent / figure The percentage or figure. Round to nearest No rounding, 0.05, 1.00, 10.00 or 100.00. Click Fill the column . "Filling a column only writes the figures into the boxes below. Nothing is saved until you press Save prices." Note The level's own percentage and Nothing (empty the column) are for the price level columns: an emptied level follows its own percentage of the default price again. Every item keeps a default price, so both choices are greyed out while Default price is chosen, and a default price box left empty keeps the price the item already has. Rename price levels Rename price levels at the top of the page opens a panel with one box per level, Level 1 to Level 10 , each with its name, its percentage and an Active tick. It is for users with the Edit right on Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists , where the same levels can also be changed one at a time. Field What to enter Name The level's name as it will read everywhere: on this page, on the item form, on the customer's record, on the Item Price List and in the Modify Report fields. Up to 40 characters; two levels cannot have the same name. Percentage The level's percentage of the default price, between −100 and 1000. A negative figure is a discount (−5 = 5% below the default price), a positive one a mark-up, 0 the default price itself. Active Untick to hide a level everywhere (the grid, the item form, the customer form, the price list). An inactive level keeps its prices and comes back when ticked again. Click Save the price levels . The message Price levels saved: lists what changed, for example "Price Level 6 renamed Contractor, Contractor now -8%"; Nothing was changed: the price levels are already as shown. says so otherwise. The change is in the audit trail. Renaming a level does not change any price: the figures typed for the items stay, and customers assigned to the level keep it. Example A hardware store names level 6 Contractor at −8% and level 7 Senior citizen at −20%, keeps Price Level 8 to Price Level 10 inactive until they are needed, and assigns each contractor customer the Contractor level on the customer's record. Step by step: set a VIP price list Open Inventory > Set Item Prices and Levels and choose the Item type or Category . To give VIP customers cost plus 30% on these items, choose Fill a column VIP , With Cost plus a markup percentage , type 30 , choose Round to nearest 10.00 and click Fill the column . Change single boxes by hand where needed, for example a VIP price of ₱36,500.00 for LAP-001. Type a Reason (recorded in the audit trail) , for example New price list, effective this month . Click Save prices and confirm. The message "n default price(s) and n price level figure(s) saved. New prices apply immediately on invoices, sales receipts, the POS and the Item Price List." appears. If the items run over several pages, move to the next page and repeat. "Only the items on this page are saved." Start again throws away what you typed and reloads the page. Good to know "A price cannot be less than nothing (...)." "Nothing was changed: the prices on this page are already what is shown." A figure equal to the level's percentage price is not kept as a fixed price, unless the item already had a fixed price there. Saving needs the Create or Edit permission on this page. Price levels themselves (names, percentages, active) are set with Rename price levels on this page or under Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists ; a customer's level is chosen on the customer (see Customer Center ).

The inventory reports are under Inventory > Reports . They use the common report tools ( Refresh , Columns , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize , and clicking a figure to see its detail), explained in Working with reports . Cost and value columns are shown only to users who may view costs. Most of them list only active items and active sites, and a user limited to some sites sees only those.

One line per stocked item with the quantity at each site in its own column and the Total . Use it to see at a glance where your stock is. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Quantity on Hand by Site. Also the Quantity on Hand by Site button of the Inventory Site List. Filters: As of , Item , Site , Category , Item type and Preferred supplier . As of is today when the report opens, showing the quantities on hand now; choose an earlier date to see what each site held at the end of that day, worked out from every receipt, sale, transfer, adjustment and build up to and including it. Item limits the report to one item. Site shows that site's column only (and its total), for example Gabi KMF without the other sites. Category , Item type and Preferred supplier keep the items of one category, one kind or one supplier (see Filters on related records ). Click an item code to open it in the Inventory Center. Exclude zero qty leaves out the items with nothing on hand at the sites shown: with a Site chosen, the items that site does not hold; with all sites, the items no site holds. The totals are not changed by it.

The quantity and value of every stocked item as of a date, with its share of the total and its value at selling price. Use it at month end to support the inventory balance in the balance sheet. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Inventory Valuation Summary. Filters: As of , Inventory site and Item . Leave Inventory site on All for the whole company, or choose a site to value only its stock. The columns: The report can also be narrowed by Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ). Column Meaning On hand Quantity at all sites on the date, or at the chosen site. Avg cost Asset value ÷ on hand. Asset value The book value of the item on the date. % of tot asset Its share of the total asset value. Sales price Today's sales price. Retail value On hand × sales price. % of tot retail Its share of the total retail value. Users who may design reports can add the item's own fields as columns with Modify Report (see Modifying a report ), among them Gross profit per unit (price less average cost) , Gross profit % per unit , Markup % on average cost , Category , Preferred supplier , Reorder point and Maximum stock . For a report that anybody can shape, use the Customized Inventory Report . The line above the table gives the balance of the inventory asset account(s) in the ledger on the date and says whether it "agrees with the total asset value". If it "differs", look for journal entries posted directly to the inventory account. Click an item to open its valuation detail up to the date. With a site chosen, the note names the site instead: the quantities are that site's, and each is valued at the item's weighted average cost of all sites, because the cost of an item is averaged across the sites (the same rule as Inventory Valuation Summary by Site ). The ledger comparison is for the whole company only.

The same valuation, grouped by site, with a total for each site. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Inventory Valuation Summary by Site. Filters: As of and Site . Columns: Site / item , Description , On hand , Avg cost , Asset value and Retail value . As the note says, "Site values use each item's weighted average cost (costs are averaged across all sites)." The report can also be narrowed by Item , Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ).

Every movement of each item in a period, with the running quantity, average cost and value. Use it to trace how an item's cost changed or to find a transaction. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Inventory Valuation Detail. Also the Valuation detail button of the Inventory Center, and clicking an item on the Inventory Valuation Summary. Filters: Dates (default This month ), From , To , Item and Site . For each item the report shows an Opening line, one line per movement ( Type , Date , Num (click to open), Name of the customer or vendor, Site code, Qty , Cost , On hand , Avg cost , Asset value ) and a Total line. The report can also be narrowed by Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ). Example For BAG-001 in September 2026: opening 19 at ₱500.00 (₱9,500.00), the damage adjustment ADJ-00001 −2 (−₱1,000.00), the POS sale POS-000002 −1 (−₱500.00), closing 16 worth ₱8,000.00.

Every transaction that changed an item's average cost, with the average before and after, the change and what caused it. Use it to find out why an average jumped: a processing order, a bill at another price, stock received while it was below zero, a back-dated entry, a value adjustment. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Average Cost Changes. Also the Average cost changes button of the Inventory Center, which opens it for the item and all dates. Filters: Dates (default This month ), From , To , Item , Category , Item type , Preferred supplier , Change of at least (any change, or 1% to 100% of the average before) and Processing, disassembly and builds only . For each item the report lists, in the order the costs were worked out (the order the transactions were entered): Type , Date , Num (click to open), Site , Qty , Unit cost , On hand before (all sites), Avg before , Avg after , Change , Change % and What moved it , then Average now . A change of 25% or more is shown in red. The cost columns are shown only to users who may view costs. What moved it Means Received at a cost different from the average A bill, item receipt or return at another price. Processing output at its share of the cost An output of a processing order or disassembly; its unit cost is its share of the inputs and additional costs. Built at the cost of its components An assembly built from its parts. Received while 3.00 short (below zero); the shortfall was settled at this cost The item was below zero; the receipt settled the shortfall (see Stock below zero ). Value adjustment A value-only line of Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand . The last of the stock went out with the value left The issue that brought the item to zero took out all the value left. Entered after later-dated movements; ... A back-dated entry: it was costed at the average of the day it was entered. Rebuild Data costs it again in date order. The report can be opened by the roles that may open the Inventory Valuation Detail.

What you have, what is committed, what is coming, and what to order. Use it every week to plan purchases and builds. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Inventory Stock Status by Item. The line under Items at or below reorder point on the Home dashboard opens it too. Filters: Dates (default This quarter ; used only for Sales / week ) and Item . The columns: The report can also be narrowed by Site , Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ). Column Meaning Reorder pt The reorder point; for an assembly, the larger of the reorder and build points. On hand Quantity at all sites now. On sales order Still to deliver on open sales orders. Available On hand less on sales order. Order / build Reorder or Build when Available plus On PO is at or below the reorder point. Suggested qty Maximum stock less Available less On PO. On PO , Next delivery Still to receive on open purchase orders, and the earliest expected date. Sales / week Net quantity sold per week over the chosen dates. Rows to reorder or build are highlighted. The Create purchase order button at the bottom starts a purchase order ( Create Purchase Orders ).

The same figures grouped by preferred vendor, so you can order from each supplier in one purchase order. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Inventory Stock Status by Vendor. Filters: Dates and Vendor . Items without a preferred vendor come first under (no preferred vendor) . Beside each vendor's name, create PO starts a purchase order to that vendor. The report can also be narrowed by Site , Category and Item type (see Filters on related records ).

The stock status of each item at each site, to see where a store is short while another has stock. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Inventory Stock Status by Site. Filters: Dates , Item and Site . Each item is a group with one line per site that has stock, sales orders or purchase orders. A site where Available is below zero is highlighted and marked Short : cover it with a transfer from another site or order more. Reorder points and suggested quantities are not shown per site. The report can also be narrowed by Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ).

A count sheet listing every stocked item with a blank line to write the count on. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Physical Inventory Worksheet. Also Print blank worksheet on the Physical Inventory Count page. Filters: As of , Site (blank for all sites) and Hide system quantities (blind count) . As of is today when the report opens, and On hand (system) is then the quantity on hand now. Choose an earlier date to print the system quantities of that day: every receipt, sale, transfer and adjustment up to the end of that date is counted, so a count taken on that day can be compared with what the books said then. The note under the title says which date the quantities are of. Columns: Item , Description , Pref. vendor , Unit , On hand (system) (blank on a blind count) and Physical count . The heading line has spaces for "Counted by" and "Date". Print it with Print / PDF ; after the count, the Enter counts button opens Physical Inventory Count for the site. The report can also be narrowed by Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ).

The builds saved as pending because components were short, with what is still missing. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Pending Builds. Also the Pending Builds button on Build Assemblies. The report can also be narrowed by Item and Category (see Filters on related records ). Filter: Site . Columns: Date , Build ref. (click to open the build and complete it), Assembly , Site , Qty to build , Missing components (for example "MON-024 (short 7)", or Ready to build when nothing is short any more) and Memo .
The same list grouped by site. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Pending Builds by Site. The report can also be narrowed by Item and Category (see Filters on related records ).

Every processing order of a period with its inputs, outputs and costs. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Processing & Disassembly Register. Also the Register button of the Processing Orders list. Filters: Dates (default This month ), Site , Process type , Formula and Status . Columns: Date , Num , Type , Formula (with the number of batches), Site , Inputs , Outputs , Variance qty (input quantity less output quantity; Input qty and Output qty can be added in Modify Report ), Input materials , Added costs , Total cost , By-products & scrap , Co-products , Variance , Allocation and Status . Pending orders show estimated amounts in grey and are left out of the totals; voided orders are listed for reference.

How the cost of each completed processing order was shared among its outputs, item by item. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Co-product & By-product Cost Allocation. Filters: Dates (default This fiscal year ), Item , Site , Process type and Output role . A pie chart shows the allocated cost by output item (with more than six items, the five largest and Other ) to users who may view costs. The table is grouped by output item: Date , Num , Type , Role , Qty , U/M , Method , Basis ( auto when the item's own price or cost was used), Share of order cost , Allocated cost and Unit cost , with a total for each item. Use it to explain the cost of refurbished or processed goods. The report can also be narrowed by Category and Item type (see Filters on related records ).

Planned against actual quantities of completed processing orders, to see whether a process yields what the formula expects. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Processing Yield Analysis. Also the Yield analysis button of a used formula. Filters: Dates (default This fiscal year ), Item , Site , Formula and Show ( Summary by formula and item or Every order ). Lines are grouped by formula; orders loaded from an assembly's bill of materials come under Assembly bills of materials / other . Lines typed in by hand have no planned quantity and are left out. Columns: Item , Line ( Input or the output role), Orders , Date , Num , Planned qty , Actual qty , Difference and Actual vs planned . Planned quantities come from the formula or bill of materials times the batches run. Rows more than 2% off plan are highlighted. The report can also be narrowed by Category and Item type (see Filters on related records ).

The items whose quantity at a site is below zero. Negative quantities distort average cost and cost of goods sold, so clear this report regularly. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Negative Inventory Listing. The report can also be narrowed by Item , Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ). Filters: As of and Site . As of is today when the report opens: the list shows the quantities on hand now. Choose an earlier date to see which items were below zero on that day, from every movement up to the end of that date; Last issue is then the last document up to that date that took the item out. Columns: Item (click for the Inventory Center), Description , Site , On hand and Last issue , the last document that took the item out at that site (click to open it). For each line, record the missing item receipt, transfer or adjustment. "No data for these settings." means there is no negative stock.

t: No. of Days Inventory Has No Movement
x: How long each stocked item has gone without being sold to a customer: the date of its last sale and the number of days since, with its last movement of any kind. Use it to find slow and dead stock before it spoils or loses its value, and to plan promotions and returns to suppliers. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > No. of Days Inventory Has No Movement. Filters: As of (today as delivered), Inventory site , Category , Not sold for at least ( Any number of days , 30, 60, 90, 180 days or 1 year) and Items ( Only items in stock , as delivered, or All items, in stock or not ). With a site chosen, only the sales and movements at that site count. The report can also be narrowed by Item , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ). Column Meaning On hand The quantity on the date (at the site, if one is chosen). Value That quantity at average cost; shown to users who may view costs. Last sold The date of the last invoice, sales receipt or POS sale of the item, or Never sold . Days not sold Days from the last sale to the As of date. An item never sold counts from the day it first came in. Age An extra column (tick it on the Columns tab of Modify Report ): the band, under 30 days, 30-89 days, 90-179 days, 180-364 days or over a year. Last movement (any) The last change of quantity of any kind: a receipt, a transfer, an adjustment, a build or a sale. Days since any movement An extra column too: days from that movement to the date. The items longest without a sale come first, and items 90 days or more without a sale are marked with an amber edge. Click an item to open it in the Inventory Center.

One line per inventory part or assembly, with the columns you choose: the item's own details, its stock and value, its prices and the profit per unit, and what was sold and bought in a period, among them the gross profit amount and the gross profit percentage of each item. Add a column, take one out, and memorize the report as you shaped it. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Customized Inventory Report. It is given to the roles that may open the Inventory Valuation Summary. Filters: Dates (this month as delivered; the sales and purchases are those of the period, the stock and value those at its end), Item , Inventory site , Category , Item type , Preferred supplier , and Items : Active items , Active items in stock , Items sold in the period or Active and inactive items . Choosing the columns Click the Columns box. The columns are in groups; tick the ones to print and untick the ones to leave out, then click Show (or just close the list). Tick all and Clear work on the whole list, and the search box at the top finds a column by name. With nothing ticked, the box reads Standard columns . Every user who may open the report can choose its columns; columns that show costs are offered only to users who may view costs. Group Columns Item Item , Description , Sales description , Purchase description , Barcode , Category , Item type , Unit , Preferred supplier , Tax code , Status , Reorder point , Maximum stock Stock and value at the end of the period On hand , Below reorder point by , Average cost , Asset value , % of total asset value , Sales price , Retail value , % of total retail value , Gross profit in stock (retail less asset value) Profit per unit Purchase cost , Gross profit per unit (sales price less average cost), Gross profit % per unit (of the sales price), Markup % on cost (of the average cost) Sales in the period Qty sold , Sales amount , Average selling price , Cost of sales , Gross profit (sales amount less cost of sales), Gross profit % (of the sales amount), % of total sales , Last sold Purchases in the period Qty bought , Purchase amount , Last bought (what came into stock from suppliers; a bill made from an item receipt is counted once) The standard columns are Item , Description , Category , Unit , On hand , Average cost , Asset value , Sales price , Gross profit per unit , Gross profit % per unit , Qty sold , Sales amount , Gross profit and Gross profit % . The TOTAL line adds up the quantities and amounts; its Gross profit % is the total gross profit over the total sales. Click an item for the Inventory Center, a sales amount for Sales by Item Detail , and an asset value for the Inventory Valuation Detail . Example To see which frozen products earn the most this year, choose Dates This fiscal year , Category Frozen Products and Items Items sold in the period . In Columns , keep Item , Description , Qty sold , Sales amount , Gross profit and Gross profit % , untick the others, and click Show . Click the Gross profit heading to sort the items by it. Changing the design and keeping it Memorize keeps the report with its filters and columns, for you or shared with others (see Memorized Reports ); Export to spreadsheet and Print / PDF take the columns on the screen. Users who may design reports also have Modify Report : the order and headings of the columns, their widths, fonts, the heading and the footer, the page, and saved layouts (see Modifying a report ). The Columns box keeps the order a layout gives the columns.

How the stock of each item moved over a period: what it had at the start, what came in, what went out and what it had at the end. Use it to explain the change in stock from one date to another, site by site, and to trace any figure to the transactions behind it. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Inventory Movement Summary Report. It is given to the roles that may open No. of Days Inventory Has No Movement. Filters: Dates with a From date and time and a To date and time (this month as delivered), Item , Site , Class , Category , Cashier and Shift . The site, class and item filters narrow the beginning balance and the movements alike. With Class , the movements of the transactions (or the lines) of that class count; (Unclassified) keeps those without a class. The times, the cashier and the shift are explained in Dates with times, cashier and shift . Column Meaning Item code , Item description The inventory part or assembly. Click the code to open it in the Inventory Center. Beg. balance The ending inventory of the day before the From date: every movement up to the end of that day. In What came into stock in the period: Write Checks and Cash Vouchers with inventory (whether the quantity is positive or negative), Receive Items, Receive Items and Enter Bills, Transfer Inventory to the site, Adjust Quantity (the quantity added), Build Assemblies (the assembled items) and Disassemble / Process Items (the outputs). Out What went out of stock in the period: Create Invoices, Create Batch Invoices, Enter Sales Receipts, POS sales (and statement charges), less credit memos and POS returns that restock, Transfer Inventory from the site, Adjust Quantity (the quantity taken off), Build Assemblies (the component items), Disassemble / Process Items (the inputs consumed) and Supplier Debit Memos. Ending balance The ending inventory of the To date: Beg. balance + In - Out . Only transactions dated within the range count in In and Out , and voided transactions are left out. The TOTAL line adds up the four columns. With every site, a transfer counts as In at the site it went to and as Out at the site it left, so it does not change the total; with one site chosen, only that site's side counts. Only the items with a figure are listed, inactive items that moved included. Every figure, the TOTAL line included, can be drilled down: click it to open Inventory Movement Transactions with the source transactions of that figure. Dates with times, cashier and shift A business open 24 hours with three shifts (for example 12:01 AM - 8:00 AM, 8:01 AM - 2:00 PM and 2:01 PM - 12:00 AM) can see the beginning inventory, the movements and the ending inventory of each shift. Each date has a time box beside it: Box What it does From date and time The time the period starts, from the beginning of that minute. Empty means the start of the day. To date and time The time the period ends, to the end of that minute. Empty means the end of the day. For 2:01 PM - 12:00 AM, type the To date as the next day at 12:00 AM, or leave the To time empty. Cashier A cashier: the site becomes the outlet the cashier worked at in the period (the site of the terminal of the cashier's shifts, or the cashier's default POS site), so the report shows the stock the cashier is answerable for. Shift One POS shift (the list shows the cashier, the terminal, its site, and the time it was opened and closed): the dates and times are set to the moment the shift was opened and the moment it was closed (now, for a shift still open), with its cashier and site. Change the dates afterwards if needed; they are kept. How a transaction is placed in time: on its own date, at the time of day it was recorded. A POS sale is recorded as it is rung up, so it falls in the shift that made it. A delivery entered later and dated an earlier day counts on that day, at the time of day it was entered. The ending inventory of one shift is always the beginning inventory of the next, and the IN and OUT of the three shifts add up to those of the whole day. The heading shows the dates with their times ( 10/09/2026 08:01 AM through 10/09/2026 02:00 PM ), and a drill-down keeps the times and shows the Time recorded of each transaction. Example Hotdogs started September with 15 packs. 100 came in (purchases, a transfer and an adjustment) and 87 went out (sales, a transfer out and a build). The report shows Beg. balance 15, In 100, Out 87 and Ending balance 28. Click 100 to see the purchases, the transfer and the adjustment that make it up.

The same movements as the summary, with In and Out split by the kind of transaction, so you can see how much of the change came from purchases, transfers, adjustments, builds, processing, sales and returns to suppliers. Where to find it: Inventory > Reports > Inventory Movement Detailed Report. It is given to the same roles as the summary. Filters: as the summary, Dates with their times, Item , Site , Class , Category , Cashier and Shift (see Dates with times, cashier and shift ). Group Column What it counts Beg. balance The ending inventory of the day before the From date IN Purchases Write Checks and Cash Vouchers with inventory, positive or negative; Receive Items; Receive Items and Enter Bills IN Transfer inventory Transfer Inventory into the site IN Adjust quantity Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand, the positive differences (physical counts and opening quantities included) IN Build assemblies Build Assemblies: the assembled items IN Disassemble / process items Disassemble / Process Items: the outputs OUT Sales Create Invoices, Create Batch Invoices, Enter Sales Receipts and POS sales, less credit memos and POS returns that restock OUT Transfer inventory Transfer Inventory out of the site OUT Adjust quantity Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand, the negative differences OUT Build assemblies Build Assemblies: the component items used OUT Disassemble / process items Disassemble / Process Items: the inputs consumed OUT Supplier debit memo Supplier Debit Memos that return items Ending balance The sum of Beg. balance and every IN and OUT column The IN and OUT headings stand over their columns. The OUT columns are negative, as the quantities left the stock, so Ending balance is the plain sum of the line. A check that takes items back (a negative quantity) reads negative under Purchases . The TOTAL line adds up every column, and an empty cell means no movement of that kind. Export to spreadsheet names the columns with their group ( IN - Transfer inventory , OUT - Transfer inventory ). Click any figure to open its source transactions in Inventory Movement Transactions .

The source transactions behind a figure of the Inventory Movement Summary Report , the Inventory Movement Detailed Report or the Sales Report Through Inventory Movement . It is not in the menu: it opens when you click a figure, with that figure's item, dates, site, class and kind of movement already chosen. Filters: Dates with their times, Item , Site , Class , Category , Movement and Cashier . Movement says which movements are listed: Beginning balance and Ending balance (every movement up to the date), All IN , All OUT , Delivery and Withdrawals (IN and OUT without the sales documents), or one kind (for example IN: Purchases or OUT: Supplier debit memo ). Columns: Type , Date , Time recorded (when the report has times), Num (click it to open the transaction), Name , Site , Movement and Qty (in positive, out negative), item by item with a total per item and a TOTAL line that equals the figure you clicked. Class , Entered by and Cost (for users who may view costs) can be added with Modify Report .

t: How the Point of Sale works
x: A few ideas explain the whole module. A terminal is a counter. Each POS terminal (for example POS-01 Makati Counter 1) sells from one inventory site, keeps its cash in one cash account, and numbers its own receipts (MK1-00000001, MK1-00000002 ...). Terminals are set up in POS Terminals . A shift belongs to a terminal. Nothing can be sold until someone opens a shift on the terminal with the opening cash float. Every sale, return and payment taken at the terminal is counted in that shift until the register is closed with the Z-reading. Anyone allowed to use the terminal sells on its open shift. Every sale posts at once. When the cashier completes a sale, it is recorded as a POS Sale dated that day, posted to the ledger and taken out of the site's stock. There is no end-of-day posting to wait for. The payment decides the account. Cash goes to the terminal's cash account. Every other payment goes to the account of its payment method: for cards and e-wallets a clearing account, which is emptied when the provider's settlement is recorded in Make Deposits . Sensitive actions need a supervisor. Voids, returns and refunds, X- and Z-readings, and discounts or price changes beyond the cashier's limits need a second person: a supervisor types their own username and password on the same screen. A user who has the Approve permission on the page approves their own action.

The cashier opens a shift on the terminal with the opening cash float ( Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings ). The cashier sells on the POS Register and prints the receipts. When the drawer holds too much cash, the cashier records a cash drop. A supervisor may run an X-reading at any time to see the sales so far. Returns, refunds, reprints and voids are done in POS Receipts, Returns & Voids . At the end of the day the cashier counts the drawer and closes the register with the Z-reading. Any difference is posted to Cash Over and Short. The bookkeeper deposits the day's cash and records the card and e-wallet settlements in Make Deposits .

Set these up once, in this order: Sites and items. The store's site in the Inventory Site List , and the items with their sales price, tax code and barcode in the Item List . Prices are entered before VAT; the register adds the VAT of each item's tax code. Payment methods. Under Financial Set-up & Reports > Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists , tab Payment methods (see Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists ), each method has a Type , a POS clearing account , and the tick POS payment option , which puts it on the register. The demo methods are in the table after this list. Terminals. One per counter in POS Terminals , with the users who work it. Access. Give cashiers page access to POS Register (Create), Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings (Create) and POS Receipts, Returns & Voids (Create and Print/Export). Give supervisors the Approve permission on those pages. Voiding a sale needs Delete/Void on POS Receipts for the user who clicks Void , and a supervisor's approval as well. See Page Access Configuration . Limits. In User Role Configuration , the special permissions Max discount % without approval and Max price change % without approval set how far a cashier may go alone, and Can exceed customer credit limits allows charges beyond a customer's limit. Company settings. In Company, Security & Closing Date : the POS receipt wording , the Bluetooth receipt printer , and Default site & class for POS transactions , which lets a cashier's register open on their own store's counter with their class already chosen. Account customers. A customer who may buy on credit at the counter needs the tick Approved account customer at the POS and a Credit limit (0 = none) in the Customer Center . A customer's Price level gives them their prices at the register too. The payment methods of the demo company, and the account each one debits when a sale is paid with it: Payment method Type Account debited on a sale Cash Cash The terminal's cash account (1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers) Credit/Debit Card Card 1060 Card Clearing GCash, Maya E-wallet 1065 E-wallet Clearing Gift Voucher Gift voucher 2120 Gift Vouchers Outstanding P.O. Card Card 1070 P.O. Card Clearing Bank Bank transfer 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking A method without a POS clearing account uses a module default: E-wallet Clearing for e-wallets, Card Clearing for the others. Module Default Accounts also holds Cash on Hand (Register) , the account a new terminal starts with, and Cash Over and Short . Check and Bank Transfer are not POS payment options in the demo. Note Selling at the POS and depositing the cash are duties that should be kept apart. When a role or user gets both POS Register and Make Deposits with create or edit rights, the program warns and asks you to tick a box to save anyway. The sidebar menu Point of Sale has Transactions (POS Register; Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings; POS Receipts, Returns & Voids), Setup (POS Terminals) and Reports . The transaction pages you may create are also on the Quick actions box of the Home dashboard.

The POS Register is the selling screen. The cashier puts the items in the cart, chooses the customer, takes the payment and completes the sale; the receipt opens at once. From the same screen the cashier can suspend a sale and recall it, charge an approved account customer, and take a payment on a customer's account balance. Where to find it: Point of Sale > POS Register. Also the Go to register button of the shifts page, the Register button of POS Receipts, and the Home dashboard Quick actions . If no terminal is available to you, the page says "No POS terminal is assigned to you. Ask an administrator to set up a terminal and assign it to your account." If the terminal has no open shift, it says "No shift is open on ..." with an Open a shift button (see Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings ). The top bar Site: the site the counter sells from. When you may use counters at several sites, it is a drop-down: choosing a site moves you to the first counter you may use there. The terminal drop-down, for example POS-01 - Makati Counter 1 : choose another counter you may use. Shift & readings opens the shifts page; Receipts / returns opens POS Receipts, Returns & Voids. The register opens on the counter you chose last. When you have not chosen one since you logged in, it opens on a counter at your default site (set by the administrator), or else on the first counter you may use. Fields: entering items Field What to enter Quantity How many of the next item. It starts at 1 and is selected, so typing replaces it. Item code / name Scan the barcode, or type any part of the item name or code. The line under the boxes names the terminal, the site, when the shift was opened and by whom, and your discount limit (for example "your discount limit 5.00%"). When you tap or click in Item code / name , a list of items drops down under it: the name, the code, the stock at this site and the price for the customer on the sale. It narrows with every letter; words can be typed in any order ("usb 32" finds USB Flash Drive 32GB). Tap a line to put that item in the cart with the quantity you typed. With a keyboard, the arrow keys move along the list, Enter takes the highlighted line and Escape closes the list. After each item, the cursor goes back to Quantity , set to 1 again. A barcode scanned while the cursor is still in Quantity sells one of that item. The register sells services, inventory parts, non-inventory parts, assemblies and other charges. Groups, discount, subtotal and payment items are not offered. The cart Column What it shows or takes Item The name, the code and the stock at this site. Qty The quantity. Type another; 0 removes the line. U/M For an item with several units of measure: the unit sold. The price follows the unit. Price The unit price before VAT. You may type another price. Discount A discount on the line: type a figure and choose % (a percentage of the line) or Amt (an amount off the line). Amount Quantity × price, less the discount. The red cross removes a line. Scanning the same item again at the same price, with no discount, adds to its quantity instead of making a new line. Fields: the sale panel Field What to enter Customer Leave it empty for a walk-in customer, or pick the customer. A customer with a price level shows "Price level: ..." under the box, and the items still at list price are re-priced at once; prices you typed stay. Customer name on the receipt Shown for walk-in customers only: a name to print on the receipt (optional). Class Shown when classes are set up: the class of the sale. It starts on your default class, else the class of the last sale on this terminal, else the terminal's default class. Subtotal (net of VAT) , Discounts , VAT , TOTAL Worked out as the cart changes. Payment boxes One box for each POS payment option ( Cash , Credit/Debit Card , GCash , Maya , Gift Voucher , P.O. Card , Bank in the demo). Type the amount paid with each. Ref / approval no. Beside each non-cash box: the card approval code, e-wallet reference or voucher number. It is printed on the receipt. Change Cash handed over less the cash needed. Balance due What is still to be paid. Note (optional) A note kept on the sale. Supervisor approval Opens when a supervisor must approve; see below. Tapping an empty Cash box fills in the total, selected, so you can type the amount the customer hands over straight away. Buttons Button What it does Complete sale Records the sale with its payments and opens the receipt. When the cart holds more of an item than the site has, it asks first (see below). Suspend Puts the sale aside unpaid, to recall later. Charge to account Records the sale as a charge invoice to an approved account customer. Shown only when such customers exist. Clear Empties the cart after "Clear the cart?". Cancel suspended sale On a recalled sale: deletes it. Recall In the Suspended sales list under the cart: brings a suspended sale back. Receive In Customer paying an account balance : records a payment on account. Step by step: sell to a walk-in customer for cash Check that the top bar shows your counter and that the shift is open. Type the quantity, press Enter (or tap Item code / name ), then scan or type the item and press Enter (or tap it in the list). Repeat for each item. Correct a quantity, price or discount on its cart line if needed. Leave Customer empty. Type the customer's name in the box under it if it should be on the receipt. Tap the Cash box: the total is filled in. Type the amount handed over, for example 50000 for ₱50,000.00. Change shows what to give back. Tap Complete sale . The message "Sale completed. Change: ₱..." appears and the receipt opens. Tap Print (or Bluetooth printer ), give the receipt and the change, then tap New sale . If the cart holds more of an item than the site has in stock (for example 11 when the cart line says "stock 9"), tapping Complete sale first shows Stock will go below zero : "Saving the transaction will lead the inventory to a negative balance." with the item, the stock and what would be left, and "Do you want to continue?". Tap Yes to complete the sale, or No to go back to the cart and change or cancel the sale. Nothing is recorded until you tap Yes. Step by step: take a card, e-wallet or split payment Put the items in the cart. Type the amount paid by card, GCash, Maya, voucher, P.O. card or bank in its box, and the reference or approval number beside it. If the customer pays the rest in cash, type the cash handed over in Cash . Check that Balance due is 0.00 and tap Complete sale . The non-cash amounts may not be more than the total; any change is given from the cash. Step by step: sell at a customer's price level Pick the customer in Customer , before or after scanning the items. For example Metro School Supplies has the Wholesale level (−5%). The line "Price level: Wholesale (-5% on items without a custom price)" appears and the list-priced lines are re-priced: an item's fixed price for the level if it has one, otherwise the level's percentage. Complete the sale as usual. The next sale starts with the same customer and class; change Customer back to empty for the next walk-in buyer. Step by step: give a discount On the cart line, type the discount in Discount and choose % or Amt . Tap Complete sale . If the discount is more than your limit, the sale is not recorded and the message "Supervisor approval is required: ... Ask a supervisor to enter their username and password below, or type a one-time approval code." appears. The Supervisor approval box opens, marked required . On the Supervisor is here tab, the supervisor types their username and password in the two boxes. If the supervisor is not at the counter, tap the Approval code tab instead and type the one-time code they generated on Approval Codes and read out to you. Tap Complete sale again. The same approval is asked when a typed price differs from the customer's price by more than your Max price change % without approval . The supervisor must have the Approve permission on the POS Register ("... is not allowed to approve on this page." otherwise) and cannot be the cashier ("You cannot approve your own transaction."); a wrong password gives "Approval failed: the supervisor username or password is wrong." A code is refused with "The approval code is not valid", "That approval code was already used", "... has expired", "... was cancelled" or "... was issued for another user" (see Supervisor approval ). Every approval is kept in the audit trail, and every discounted line appears in the POS Discount Log . Step by step: suspend a sale and recall it With the items in the cart, tap Suspend . The message "Sale suspended. Recall it from the list when the customer is ready." appears and the cart is empty for the next customer. The sale waits in the Suspended sales list under the cart (time, user, customer, total). It posts nothing and does not move stock. When the customer is back, tap Recall . The cart is filled again and "Recalled suspended sale #..." is shown. Take the payment and tap Complete sale , or tap Cancel suspended sale to drop it. Suspended sales are kept per terminal. Step by step: charge an account customer Put the items in the cart and pick the customer in Customer . Tap Charge to account . The message "Charged to ..." appears. The sale is recorded as an invoice to the customer, due by the customer's terms, and the receipt opens with the title CHARGE INVOICE . The invoice appears in the customer's balance and is paid later through Receive Payments or at the counter. The program refuses with "Choose the account customer to charge." when no customer is chosen, "... is not an approved account customer for charges at the counter." when the customer is not ticked Approved account customer at the POS , and "This charge would exceed the customer's credit limit of ₱...." unless you have Can exceed customer credit limits . Step by step: take a payment on an account balance In the box Customer paying an account balance , pick the customer. Type the Amount , choose the payment method and type the Reference . Tap Receive . The message "Payment of ₱... recorded." appears and a receipt titled ACKNOWLEDGEMENT RECEIPT opens. The payment is applied to the customer's open invoices, earliest due date first. Any amount left over stays on the customer's account as an unapplied credit. Cash taken this way counts in the shift's expected cash. Selling an item group Item groups (for example GRP-WFH Work-from-Home Bundle) are offered on the register like any item: type part of the group's code or name and pick it. The group goes into the cart on one line at its Group price (the customer's price level applies), or at the sum of the prices of its items when Adopt the Group Price in the Item Group is cleared or the group has no group price. Change the quantity or give a discount on the line as usual. When the sale is completed, the group's items leave the store's stock and are recorded at their own prices, and the difference from the group price goes to the group's price variance account, as on an invoice (see Item groups on sales documents ). A suspended sale with a group comes back with the group on one line. Using the register on a phone On a phone the register stacks the parts one under the other: the top bar, the entry boxes, the cart, then the customer, totals and payment boxes. The U/M column appears only when an item in the cart is sold by the unit. When the phone's keyboard opens, the list of items is placed in the part of the screen the keyboard leaves free; with the phone on its side, the entry row moves to the top so the list has the whole space. One tap on a line sells the item.

After a sale, charge, payment or return, the receipt opens. It shows the company name, address, VAT REG TIN and terminal name; the title; the receipt number, date and time, the customer (or "Walk-in customer") and the cashier; each line with its quantity, price, discount and amount; VATable sales , VAT and TOTAL ; each payment with its reference; Amount tendered and Change ; and the footer text. A voided sale prints " VOID ". The company logo is printed when it is switched on for POS receipts. Button What it does Print Prints the receipt on the computer's printer. Bluetooth printer Sends the receipt to a Bluetooth roll printer. Shown when Bluetooth printing is switched on. New sale Goes back to an empty register. View by item group / View item details On a sale with item groups: the group on one line (as the receipt is printed by default), or the items in it with the price variance. The wording is set in System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date > POS receipt wording : the titles for sales ( OFFICIAL RECEIPT by default), returns ( RETURN / REFUND ), charges ( CHARGE INVOICE ) and payments on account ( ACKNOWLEDGEMENT RECEIPT ), the footer lines, and whether "Walk-in customer" is printed when the sale has no name. Printing on a Bluetooth roll printer A receipt can go straight from the browser to a 58 mm or 80 mm Bluetooth thermal printer (such as the Officom OC-PT210), with nothing installed on the phone or till. The administrator ticks Offer a Bluetooth printer on every receipt under Bluetooth receipt printer in Company, Security & Closing Date and chooses the Paper width ( 58 mm roll (32 characters per line) , 80 mm roll, small type (42 characters per line) or 80 mm roll (48 characters per line) ). The Test print button there prints a short sample. On the first receipt, tap Bluetooth printer , pick the printer in the list the browser shows, and allow it. The printer is remembered for the next sales. On the next receipts, tap Bluetooth printer . The message "Sent to ..." confirms it. Other settings: Only offer printers whose name starts with (to hide other devices), Blank lines fed after each receipt , Cut the paper at the end (printers with a cutter), and Print as soon as a receipt opens, when the printer is already connected . Important Bluetooth printing works only in Chrome, Edge, Opera or Samsung Internet on Android, or Chrome or Edge on a computer, and only when the program is opened on an https:// address (or http://localhost/ on the computer running it). Firefox, iPhones and iPads, and the browsers inside Facebook and Messenger cannot do it. When the browser cannot, the receipt says so and explains why. If "No printer was picked, so nothing was printed." appears, tap the button again and choose the printer. "The printer could not be reached: ..." means the printer is off, out of range or connected to another phone. What it records A completed sale is a POS Sale , numbered POS-000001 and so on, with the terminal's receipt number. It posts: Account Debit Credit Payment accounts (cash, clearing) Sale total, by payment 4000 Sales (item's income account) Amount net of VAT 2100 Output Tax VAT 5000 Cost of Goods Sold Cost of stocked items 1200 Inventory Cost of stocked items Example POS-000008, one SET-OFFICE Office Monitor Set paid with Maya: debit 1065 E-wallet Clearing ₱14,548.80; credit 4000 Sales ₱12,990.00 and 2100 Output Tax ₱1,558.80; debit 5000 Cost of Goods Sold and credit 1200 Inventory ₱7,706.66, the average cost of the set. Line discounts reduce the sales amount; they are not posted to a separate discount account. The stock goes out of the terminal's site at average cost. When the site has less than is sold, the setting Allow selling or moving stock below zero (with warning) decides: switched on, Complete sale (and Charge to account ) first shows the window Stock will go below zero : "Saving the transaction will lead the inventory to a negative balance.", the items with the stock at the site and what would be left, and "Do you want to continue?". Yes completes the sale and a yellow message names the items now below zero; No closes the window and leaves the sale on the screen, to change the quantity, take the item off or cancel the sale; switched off, the sale is not completed and the register shows "Not enough stock: …" so the cashier can take the item off the cart (see "Stock below zero" in Inventory ). An item (or an item of a group) with no unit cost and no average unit cost cannot be sold: Complete sale shows "This item has no unit cost and no average unit cost, …" and the sale stays on the screen (see Items with no unit cost ). A charge sale is an Invoice that debits 1100 Accounts Receivable instead of the payment accounts. A payment on account is a Customer Payment that debits the terminal's cash account (cash), the clearing account of the method (a card or e-wallet method without one uses 1060 Card Clearing or 1065 E-wallet Clearing, like a sale paid that way), or 1050 Undeposited Funds for the other methods, and credits 1100 Accounts Receivable. A suspended sale posts nothing. Good to know "Open a shift for this terminal first." "The cart is empty." "Payment is short by ₱...." Enter more cash or another payment. "Card, bank, e-wallet and voucher amounts are more than the total." Non-cash payments cannot give change. "Choose the customer, amount and payment method." (payment on account). Selling needs the Create permission on the POS Register. The date of a sale is the day it is completed, not the business date of the shift. The stock shown in the item list and cart is the site's stock when the page was opened.

This page opens and closes the cashier's shift on the current terminal, records cash taken out of the drawer, and prints the X- and Z-readings. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings. Also the Shift & readings button of the register, and the Home dashboard Quick actions . The Home dashboard also lists the shifts that are open. Fields: Open a shift Shown when the current terminal has no open shift. Field What to enter Terminal The counter you are opening. Only the terminals you may use are listed. Business date The trading day the shift belongs to. Today by default. Opening cash float The change fund placed in the drawer. 2000.00 by default. The current shift The card Current shift shows who opened it, when, and the opening cash float the cashier entered, then the running figures: Line Meaning Sales The number of sales and the first and last receipt numbers. Gross sales The sales before discounts, net of VAT. Discounts The line discounts given. Returns Refunds given, VAT included. Voids Sales voided in the shift, with their number, VAT included. Net sales + VAT Sales less returns, VAT included. Opening cash float The change fund the cashier put in the drawer when the shift was opened. It is part of the cash expected in the drawer. Payment lines The amount taken by each payment method (returns deducted); also Cash (account payments) and Charged to accounts when there are any. Cash drops Cash taken out of the drawer. Expected cash in drawer Opening float + cash sales − cash refunds + cash account payments − cash drops. Step by step: open a shift Open Point of Sale > Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings . Choose the Terminal , check the Business date and type the Opening cash float . Click Open shift . The message "Shift opened. You can start selling." appears and the register opens. Step by step: record a cash drop Take the cash out of the drawer and count it. In the Cash drop box, type the Amount removed and the reason, for example Excess cash to safe . Click Record drop . The message "Cash drop of ₱... recorded." appears and the drop is listed under the box. A cash drop posts nothing: the money is still the store's cash. It lowers the expected cash in the drawer, and it is added back to the cash to deposit when the shift is deposited. Step by step: run an X-reading In the X-reading (mid-shift) box, a supervisor types their username and password (the boxes are not shown to a user who may approve on this page). Click Run X-reading . The reading opens, ready to print. It "Prints a sales summary without closing the register." Earlier X-readings of the shift are listed under the button; click one to print it again. Step by step: close the register Count the cash in the drawer, including the float. Type the total in Cash counted in drawer . A supervisor types their username and password under it. Click Close register and print Z-reading and confirm "Close the register now?". The message "Register closed. Over/(short): ₱..." appears and the Z-reading opens. Print it and keep it with the cash. The reading An X-reading or Z-reading shows the company, TIN and terminal; X-READING or Z-READING #n (Z numbers run per terminal); the Business date , when it was Printed and By whom; First receipt , Last receipt , Sales count , Gross sales , Discounts , Returns , Voids , Net sales (net of VAT) and VAT ; Opening cash float , the amount of each payment method, Cash drops and Expected cash in drawer . A Z-reading adds Counted cash and Over / (short) , and ends with "End of day - counters reset"; an X-reading ends with "Mid-shift reading - register not closed". Print prints it and Back returns to the shifts page. All readings are listed in the X- and Z-Reading Summary . Recent shifts, and earlier ones The table on the right lists the latest 30 shifts: Date , Terminal , Cashier (who opened it), Status (with "corrected" under it when the closing entries were corrected), Float (the opening cash float), Expected , Counted and Over/short . Correct (or Details ) opens the shift, Z opens its Z-reading, and deposited opens the deposit that took its cash to the bank. To see the shifts of earlier days, use the boxes above the table: Box What it does Business dates Latest shifts (the 30 most recent), Today , Yesterday , This week , Last week , This month , Last month or Custom dates . Choosing one fills From and To . From , To The first and last business date. Typing a date makes the choice Custom dates . Status Open , Closed , Closed, not deposited , Deposited or Corrected . Terminal , Cashier One counter, or one cashier. Click Show . The heading says how many shifts were found for the dates, and a line under the table totals their floats, expected and counted cash and over/short. With more than 100 shifts, Earlier and Newer under the table move between the pages. Clear goes back to the latest shifts. A shift and its figures Details on a line of the recent shifts opens the shift: its Terminal , Cashier , Business date , Opening cash float , when it was Opened and Closed and by whom, when it was Last corrected , the Cash to deposit (counted cash less the float plus the drops), and links to its Cash over/short entry and the deposit. The figures of the shift are the same lines as the current shift's, with the Cash counted and the Over / (short) of a closed shift, and the list of its cash drops. Z-reading at the top prints the reading again. Correcting the closing entries When the cashier entered a wrong figure (a float of 1,000 typed as 2,000, a cash drop not recorded or recorded twice, a count of 5,717 typed instead of 5,771), the closing entries of the shift can be corrected afterwards, and the journal entry follows them. It needs the Edit right on this page: administrators and POS supervisors have it, cashiers do not, and they see Details instead of Correct . In Recent shifts , click Correct on the shift. Change what was wrong: Opening cash float , the amount of a Cash drop (0 takes it out), A cash drop not recorded with Its reason , or Cash counted . Expected cash , Over / (short) and Cash to deposit under the boxes change as you type. Type Why the entries are corrected (required) , for example cashier typed 5,717 instead of 5,771 . If you may not approve on this page, a supervisor approves in the Supervisor approval box (or with a one-time approval code). Click Save the correction and confirm. The message gives the new expected cash and over/short, says what happened to the journal entry, and gives the cash Make Deposits now takes from the shift (or how the deposit was changed). What the correction does: The expected cash and the over/short are worked out again from the sales of the shift, the float and the drops. The Cash Over/Short entry is changed to the new difference; it is made when there was none and now there is a difference, and it is voided when the drawer now agrees ("The Cash Over/Short entry was voided: the drawer now agrees."). The Z-reading keeps its number and prints the corrected figures, with the line "Closing entries corrected ... by ...". The shift shows Last corrected , and every correction is listed under Corrections on the shift page (when, who, why, and each figure before and after) and kept in the audit trail. The cash to deposit follows: Make Deposits takes the shift at the corrected figures (counted cash less the float plus the drops). When the cash of the shift is already on a deposit, the deposit follows too: its line for the shift becomes the new cash to deposit, its total and its ledger entry change with it, and the change is in the deposit's audit trail ("POS shift #... corrected: its cash to deposit is now ..."). The message names the deposit and the amount before and after, and the correction appears under Corrections as "Cash deposited". Example POB1 Counter 2 closed with a float of ₱3,000.00, ₱12,170.48 expected and ₱9,170.48 counted: short ₱3,000.00, because the cashier counted the drawer without the float. Correct Cash counted to 12,170.48: the over/short becomes 0.00, the Cash Over/Short entry is voided, and the cash to deposit becomes ₱9,170.48 (12,170.48 less the 3,000.00 float that stays in the drawer). If the shift was already on deposit DEP-00004 for ₱6,170.48, that deposit becomes ₱9,170.48 at the same time. Important: A correction that would leave nothing to deposit from a shift that is on a deposit is refused: take the shift off the deposit first ( Edit on the deposit), then correct it. A shift dated on or before the closing date cannot be corrected, like any other entry in a closed period, and neither can a deposit cleared in a bank reconciliation be changed without the permission for it. What it records Opening a shift, cash drops and X-readings post nothing; they are recorded in the audit trail. Closing the register posts the difference between the counted and expected cash as a Cash Over/Short entry dated the business date. For the shortage of ₱20.00 above: Account Debit Credit 6200 Cash Over and Short ₱20.00 1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers ₱20.00 When the drawer has more than expected, the entry is reversed: a debit to the cash account and a credit to Cash Over and Short. No entry is made when the count agrees. The cash of a closed shift is then taken to the bank with Make Deposits , which lists the closed shifts not yet deposited, each for the counted cash less the opening float (which stays in the drawer) plus the cash drops. Good to know "A shift is already open on this terminal." Only one shift at a time per terminal. "Choose a terminal assigned to you." "There is no open shift on this terminal." "Enter the amount removed from the drawer." and "Count the drawer and enter the cash counted." "Supervisor approval is required: X-reading." and "... closing the register (Z-reading)." Every X- and Z-reading needs a supervisor. "Nothing was changed: the figures are already the ones entered at closing." and "Say why the closing entries are corrected (it is kept in the audit trail)." when correcting a shift. "After this correction nothing is left to deposit from the shift (counted cash less the float plus the drops), but deposit DEP-... holds ... for it. Take the shift off the deposit first (Edit on the deposit), then correct the shift." The page works on the terminal chosen on the register. To work on another counter, choose it in the register's terminal drop-down first.

This page lists the POS sales and returns. From it you reprint a receipt, take goods back and refund the customer, or open a sale to void it. Where to find it: Point of Sale > POS Receipts, Returns & Voids. Also the Receipts / returns button of the register, and the Home dashboard Quick actions . The list Part What it does From , To The dates to list. Both start on today. Terminal All or one terminal. Time , Receipt When it was recorded, and the receipt number; click it to open the sale. Type POS Sale or POS Return . Terminal , Cashier , Customer Where, by whom (user name) and for which customer. Total The total, negative for returns. Status Completed or Void . Voided lines are struck through. Reprint Prints the receipt again. Return Takes goods back from the sale (sales only). Suspended sales are not listed; they are on the register. The sale Click a receipt number to open the sale: its date, number, status, class, site and receipt number; the items with quantity, rate, discount, amount, tax and cost; the Tenders with their references and the amount tendered and change; and, for users who may view costs, the General ledger entries created automatically . The buttons are Print (the receipt again), Void , History and Back to list . POS sales cannot be edited or deleted. Step by step: reprint a receipt Find the sale on the list (change From and To for an older one). Click Reprint . The receipt opens; click Print or Bluetooth printer . Reprinting needs the Print/Export permission on this page, and every reprint is recorded in the audit trail. Step by step: take goods back and refund Make sure a shift is open on your terminal.
