A non-VAT supplier's invoice has no claimable input VAT. Identify noncreditable, exempt, import, capital-goods, unpaid-payable and adjustment amounts separately.

Form D of the guide: the 5% VAT government customers withheld from the company, the VAT credit of 2550Q Part V Schedule 3 and Item 16. The filters: Dates , From , To and Customer . The columns: Payment date , Government withholding agent , TIN , VAT invoice reference , Withholding tax , VAT-exclusive tax base , VAT WHT rate and VAT amount withheld . Quarter and Payment no. can be added. Match each line to the government purchaser, the invoice, the proof of payment and the BIR Form 2307 received, and tick it off once the certificate is in hand. Government VAT withheld is not input VAT.

Form A of the guide, the quarterly VAT reconciliation, with the item numbers of BIR Form 2550Q (April 2024 edition). The filters: Dates (this quarter as delivered), From and To . Run it for one quarter. Item What it is Where it comes from 31A, 31B VATable sales net of VAT, and their output VAT The Output VAT / Sales Register 32, 33, 34A Zero-rated sales, exempt sales, total sales The same register 37B Total adjusted output VAT 31B, with no adjustments 38 Input VAT carried over from the previous quarter The excess input VAT of the quarter before (when its allowable input VAT was more than its output VAT) 44A, 44B Domestic purchases net of VAT, and their input tax The Input VAT / Purchases Register 48A Domestic purchases with no input tax Zero-rated, exempt and non-VAT purchases 50B, 51B, 60B Current, total available and total allowable input tax 44B, plus 38 61 Net VAT payable before payment credits 37B less 60B 15 Net VAT payable carried to the tax payable section 61 when it is positive 16 Creditable VAT withheld (Schedule 3) The Creditable VAT Withheld Schedule 17, 20 Advance VAT payments / other credits, total credits 16 (no other credits are kept) 21 Tax still payable, or the excess input VAT carried to the next quarter 15 less 20 The last line, under NOT VAT , gives the 1% / 2% income tax withheld by customers: an income-tax credit, kept apart because it never reduces the VAT due. Example (the guide's sample quarter): VATable sales of ₱350,000.00 with output VAT ₱42,000.00 (Items 31A, 31B, 37B); purchases of ₱100,000.00 with input VAT ₱12,000.00 (44A, 44B, 50B, 51B, 60B); net VAT before credits ₱30,000.00 (61, 15); creditable VAT withheld by government buyers ₱10,000.00 (16, 20); VAT still payable ₱20,000.00 (21). The ₱5,000.00 of income tax withheld on the sales is shown apart and does not reduce the ₱20,000.00. 2550Q is filed quarterly, generally within 25 days after the quarter closes. The official form has more items (uncollected receivables, capital goods, importations, special adjustments) than this worksheet: use the actual amounts and the latest BIR instructions.

From the guide's filing workflow: Return / document Purpose General filing cycle BIR Form 2550Q VAT-registered seller: output less allowable input VAT, less the qualifying VAT credits Quarterly; generally within 25 days after the quarter closes BIR Form 1600-VT The withholding agent remits the VAT withheld Monthly; generally by the 10th of the following month BIR Form 0619-E The withholding agent remits the expanded income tax withheld in months 1 and 2 of the quarter Monthly for the first two months; generally by the 10th of the following month BIR Form 1601-EQ Quarterly expanded withholding return (including the quarter-end month) Quarterly; generally by the last day of the month after the quarter closes BIR Form 2307 Certificate of the creditable income tax and business tax withheld Issued and reconciled under the BIR's timing rules BIR Form 1604-E and alphalists Annual reconciliation of the expanded withholding Annual; check the updated tax calendar A company's monthly-to-quarterly routine Keep each supplier's and customer's tax profile current: VAT status, TIN, whether it is a government or top withholding agent, its usual withholding taxes. Enter the VAT invoices with the VATable, zero-rated and exempt amounts and the tax codes. Withhold the taxes as separate taxes in Pay Bills (and record what customers withheld in Receive Payments). Never net the 5% VAT withheld and the 1% / 2% against the same VAT account. Each month: run the Withholding Tax Remittances for 0619-E and 1600-VT. Each quarter: print the BIR Form 2307 certificates, run the Summary of Taxes Withheld for 1601-EQ, and the 2550Q worksheet with its registers for the VAT return. Reconcile the registers with the general ledger: 2100 Output Tax, 1300 Input Tax, 2110, 2115, 1310 and 1315, and keep the acknowledgments of the returns filed.

Every page of the program is protected. Before you create users, it helps to know the pieces that decide what a user can do. Roles. A role is a named set of permissions that matches a job, such as A/R Clerk or Cashier. You set the permissions once on the role, then give the role to users. Changing a role changes the access of every user who has it. A user can have several roles: their permissions add together. Page access. The View right decides whether a page appears in the menu and can be opened at all. A denied page is hidden from the menu, the Home screen, the search box and report drill-downs. If someone opens it another way (an old bookmark, a link in an e-mail), the program shows Access denied and records the attempt in the audit trail. Action rights. On each page a role may open, it may also be given Create , Edit , Delete/Void , Print/Export and Approve . Sensitive permissions. Limits and yes/no rights that are not tied to one page, such as the largest discount a user may give without a supervisor. Sites and POS terminals. Which inventory sites a user may record transactions for, and at which POS counters the user may sell. User overrides. An exception for one user on one page, which always wins over the user's roles. The Administrator role. A role marked Administrator (full access to everything) opens every page with every right and every sensitive permission. Company Owner and Super Admin. When several companies run on the platform, the Company Owner and the Super Admin working inside a company have full authority in it, and no role or override can lock them out. See Company Owner and Super Admin . The rights on a page Right What it allows View Open the page. It appears in the menu. Without View, the other rights on that page do nothing. Create Add new records or transactions on the page, including Save & New and copying. Edit Change saved records. On some setup pages it also runs the page's main action, such as saving settings or rebuilding data. Delete/Void Delete or void records and transactions. Print/Export Print, save as PDF, export to a spreadsheet, and download files such as import templates and backups. Approve Approve actions that need a supervisor on this page: voids, refunds, price overrides, large discounts and amounts over a user's limit. A user who has Approve on a page approves their own action there. Anyone else is stopped with a message that begins "Supervisor approval is required", and a supervisor who has Approve on that page types their own username and password in the Supervisor approval box of the same form. Nobody can approve their own transaction by typing their own name there. Sensitive permissions These are set on the role, in the Sensitive permissions (set separately from the grid) box. Permission What it does View costs and margins Shows item costs, cost of sales and margins. Without it, costs are hidden from the user, and the item import refuses cost columns. View bank balances outside Banking Shows bank balances on the Home dashboard, the Chart of Accounts, reports and fund transfers. Max discount % without approval The largest discount the user may give on sales forms and at the POS before a supervisor must approve. Max price change % without approval The largest change from an item's price the user may make on a sales form before approval is needed. Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval Checks, bill payments, refunds, cash vouchers, inventory adjustments and similar amounts above this need approval. Can exceed customer credit limits Lets the user save an invoice that takes a customer over the credit limit, after typing a reason. Without it, such an invoice is refused. Can change the Chart of Accounts and default accounts Needed to add or change accounts and to change Module Default Accounts. Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled Lets the user record, change, void or delete transactions dated on or before the closing date, and change transactions already cleared in a bank reconciliation. Can design report layouts (fonts, headings and footers, columns and rows) and save or share them Lets the user change how a report looks and which columns and fields it prints with Modify Report , and save or share the layout. For the three number limits, a blank box means no limit, and 0 means that every discount, price change or amount needs approval. When a user has several roles, a yes/no permission is yes if any role says yes, and a limit is the highest of the roles (a blank on any role means no limit). A role that does not set a limit at all counts as 0. The standard roles A new company comes with nine standard roles. You can change them, and you can copy one to make a custom role. Role What the role can do Main limits Administrator Everything in every module, including users, roles, page access, the closing date and the audit trail. None A/P Clerk Vendors module transactions, Pay Bills, and the Vendors and Payables reports. Views costs; amounts up to ₱100,000.00 A/R Clerk Customers module transactions and the Customer and Receivables reports. Discount 10%, price change 5%, amounts up to ₱50,000.00 Accountant Chart of Accounts, Fixed Assets, Banking and reconciliation, all module reports and the financial statements. Views costs and bank balances; may change the Chart of Accounts; no amount limit Auditor View-only access to all transactions, reports and the audit trail. Cannot create or change anything. Views costs and bank balances Cashier POS sales, returns and cash drops at the assigned terminal only. Discount 5%, no price change, every approval amount needs a supervisor Inventory Clerk Items, sites, receiving, adjustments, builds, processing orders, stock counts and quantity reports. Amounts up to ₱20,000.00 POS Supervisor Everything a cashier can do, plus approving voids, refunds, price overrides and large discounts, and X- and Z-readings. Discount 30%, price change 20%, amounts up to ₱20,000.00 Sales Representative Estimates, sales orders, invoices and the Sales reports. Discount 5%, no price change Duties that should be kept apart The program warns when one person would be able to handle both sides of a task that is normally split between two people. The pairs it checks are: creating vendors and paying bills ( Vendor Center and Pay Bills ); receiving customer payments and reconciling the bank account ( Receive Payments and Reconcile ); adjusting inventory and counting it ( Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand and Physical Inventory Count ); entering bills and writing checks ( Enter Bills and Write Checks ); selling at the POS and depositing the cash ( POS Register and Make Deposits ). A pair counts only when both pages are allowed with Create or Edit . When you save a role or a user that combines such duties, the save stops with a segregation of duties warning. You may still save by ticking the box under the warning; the decision is recorded in the audit trail as a Sod Override entry.

This page lists everyone who can log in to the company, and it is where you add a new employee, change their roles, reset a forgotten password, unlock a locked account and deactivate someone who has left. Where to find it: System Administration > User Accounts The list Column What it shows Name The user's full name. Click it to open the user. Username The name the user logs in with. Employee no. Your own employee number, if entered. Roles The roles the user has. Sites The inventory sites the user is limited to (codes such as ST1), or "all". Status Active , Inactive or Locked . A user who joined with the Company Code shows Waiting for approval or Rejected instead. Company Owner and temp password may also appear here. Last login Date and time of the last successful log-in. Overrides How many page overrides the user has (see Page Access Configuration ). The drop-down above the list ( All statuses ) shows only Active , Inactive or Locked users. The list is sorted by name. Fields Click New user to open a blank form, or click a name to edit that user. Field What to enter Username 3 to 50 characters: letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore. It is saved in lower case and must be unique. When several companies share the platform, it must be unique across all of them. Full name Required. This name appears on the records and audit entries the user creates. Email Optional. Employee no. Optional, for your own reference. Temporary password (new user) Required. It must follow the password rules shown under the fields. New password (optional) (existing user) Leave blank to keep the current password. Type one to replace it. Roles Tick at least one. Administrator shows "(full access)". Permissions from several roles add together. Inventory sites the user may work at Tick sites to limit the user to them. None ticked means all the sites the user's roles allow. POS terminals Tick the counters the user may sell at. None ticked means any active terminal at the sites the user may work at. The line under the password fields repeats the company's password rules, for example "Password rules: at least 8 characters, upper- and lower-case, a number, a symbol. The user must replace it at first login." A password may also not contain the username. When a user's roles limit them to some sites and you also tick sites on the user, the user may work only at sites that are in both lists. In the demo company, the Cashier role allows the Makati Store and the Cebu Store, and Ella Ramos is ticked for the Makati Store only, so she works at the Makati Store. Step by step: add a user Click New user . Type the Username , Full name and, if you keep them, the Email and Employee no. Type a Temporary password that follows the rules shown. Tick the user's Roles . If the user should work only at certain sites or counters, tick them under Inventory sites the user may work at and POS terminals . Click Save user , or Save user & New to start the next user at once. Give the username and temporary password to the employee. At the first log-in the program makes them choose their own password (see Getting Started ). If the roles combine duties that should be kept apart, the save stops with a Segregation of duties warning. Tick I understand; save anyway (the decision is recorded in the audit trail) and click Save user again, or change the roles. The user's page When you open an existing user, the page shows the same form plus two boxes on the right. The first box shows Status , Last login (with the computer's IP address), Failed attempts (wrong passwords since the last good log-in), Password changed (with ", must change at next login" when a temporary password is waiting) and Created . The second box holds the account actions. It appears only if you have Edit on this page. Button What it does Unlock account Shown only when the account is locked. Sets it back to active and clears the failed attempts. Type a Reason first if you want one recorded. Deactivate (employee left) The user can no longer log in. Type a reason such as "resigned" in the box above it. The program asks you to confirm. Reactivate Shown instead of Deactivate for an inactive user. Lets them log in again. Reset password Sets the Temporary password typed above it. The user must change it at the next log-in. A locked account is unlocked at the same time. Across the top, Effective access shows exactly what the user can open (see Effective Access (View as User) ), Activity opens the User Activity report for this user, and Back returns to the list. Step by step: change a user's roles Click the user's name. Tick or clear the roles, sites and terminals. Leave New password (optional) blank unless you also want to set a new password. Click Save user . The change applies from the next page the user opens. Step by step: help a user who forgot the password or is locked out Click the user's name. Type a temporary password in the Temporary password box of the right-hand panel. Click Reset password . Give the temporary password to the user. At the next log-in they must choose a new one. If the user remembers the password and was only locked out after too many wrong tries, click Unlock account instead. Step by step: an employee leaves Click the user's name. Type the reason in Reason (e.g. resigned) . Click Deactivate (employee left) and confirm. A user who works in two companies When several companies share the platform, one person can work in two (or more) of them with one log-in, without being made a Super Admin: a group accountant who keeps the books of two companies, a purchasing officer who buys for both. The person stays a user of their own company. The other company gives them access with Add user from another company on its User Accounts page (the button is also on Employees & Users ), and decides there what they may do. Field What to enter Their username The username the person logs in with at their own company. They keep that one log-in and password. Roles in this company Tick at least one. They decide what the person may do in this company only. Inventory sites , POS terminals As for any user: tick to limit the person to them. Reason (recorded in the audit trail) Why the person gets access, for example "Accountant of the group". Step by step: let a user of another company work here Log in to the company the person should also work in (with an account that may add users), and go to System Administration > User Accounts . Click Add user from another company . Type Their username , as they log in at their own company. Tick their Roles in this company , and sites or POS terminals if they should be limited. Type the reason and click Give access to this company . The person's page opens. The person now sees the company name at the top of the screen as a switch with both companies, and moves between them without logging in again (see Working in two companies ). Example Ana Cruz ( accountant ) is the accountant of Sample Trading Company and also keeps the books of ABC Distribution Corp. John Doe, the owner of ABC, opens User Accounts in ABC, clicks Add user from another company , types accountant , ticks the Accountant role and the reason "Group accountant", and clicks Give access to this company . Ana logs in at Sample Trading as always; the top bar now offers ABC Distribution Corp. too. In ABC she can do only what the Accountant role of ABC allows. What the other company sees: The person is listed in its User Accounts and Employees & Users with "User of" and their own company under the name. They have the same username and name, but no password here: there are no password fields and no Reset password for them. Their password is changed at their own company. Their page has a User of another company box with their own company, when access was given and by whom, and when they last switched here. What they do here is recorded in this company's audit trail under their username; each switch is recorded too ("Company Switch"). A supervisor approval they give here is checked against the password of their own company. What their own company sees: their user page has an Also works in box with the other companies, and the list shows "Also works in" under their name. Ending the access In the company they work in: open the user and click Remove access to this company (with a reason). The account there is switched off, so their name stays on what they entered, and Give access back turns it on again later. The same is Remove access to this company under Manage on Employees & Users. In their own company: Remove beside the other company in the Also works in box. It also ends by itself when their account in their own company is deactivated or locked. If the person is working in the other company when the access ends, the next page they open takes them back to their own company with the message "Your access to ... has ended. You are back in your own company." Messages: "No active user of another company logs in with that username. Check the spelling with the person.", "... is already a user of this company. Change their roles in User Accounts instead.", "... already has access to this company.", "Give at least one role in this company.", "You cannot remove your own access." Good to know Users are never deleted, so their names stay on the transactions and audit entries they created. Deactivate them instead. An account is locked after the number of wrong passwords set under Failed logins before lockout on Company, Security & Closing Date . The user sees "Too many failed attempts. The account is now locked." and then "This account is locked. Only an administrator can unlock it." An inactive user sees "This account is inactive. Contact your administrator." You cannot deactivate your own account, remove the Administrator role from your own account, or deactivate the last active administrator ("This is the last active administrator."). With several companies: only the Company Owner (or the Super Admin) can change the Company Owner's account, and the Company Owner cannot be deactivated. A user who registered with the Company Code and is still Waiting for approval cannot be reactivated here; approve them under Company > Join Requests (see Company Owner ). Messages you may see when saving: "That username is taken.", "That username is already used on this platform. Choose another.", "Assign at least one role.", "Enter the full name." and "The temporary password must have ..." followed by the rules it missed. Every save, reset, unlock, deactivation and reactivation is recorded in the audit trail, with the reason you typed.

Use this page to set up the roles: which pages each role may open, what it may do there, its sensitive permissions and its sites. Set up roles before you add users, and change a role instead of changing many users one by one. Where to find it: System Administration > User Role Configuration. The Role permissions button on Page Access Configuration also opens it. The list Column What it shows Role The role's name. full access marks an administrator role; standard marks the roles that came with the program. Click the name to edit the role. What the role can do The description you gave the role. Pages How many pages the role may open, out of all the pages of the program (for example 25 / 168). Users How many users have the role. Sites All , or the codes of the sites the role is limited to. (links) Copy starts a new role with the same settings. Delete appears only for a custom role that no user has. Fields Click New role to start from an empty role, or Copy beside a role to start from a copy of it. Field What to enter Role name Required, and different from every other role. A copy starts as the old name plus "(copy)". What the role can do A short description shown in the list, for example "Customers module transactions and the Customer and Receivables reports." Administrator (full access to everything) Tick only for a role that must open everything. The grid below is then ignored. Sites All sites , or Only: with the sites ticked. If you choose Only: , tick at least one site, or users of the role can work at none. Sensitive permissions (set separately from the grid) The nine permissions described in How access works . Number boxes show "blank = no limit". Permissions by page One row per page, grouped by module, with the columns View , Create , Edit , Delete/Void , Print/Export and Approve . In the grid, each page name is followed by its kind in brackets: (center), (list), (setup), (transaction), (report) or (admin). The grey row of each module has a tick box in every column: ticking it ticks that column for every page of the module, for example View for all of Customers. The rights on a row count only when View is ticked on that row. A page with Create ticked but not View is not saved. Step by step: create a role for a new job Click Copy beside the role closest to the new job (or New role to start empty). Change the Role name and What the role can do . Choose the Sites . Set the Sensitive permissions . Leave a limit blank for no limit, or type 0 to make every case go to a supervisor. In Permissions by page , tick View for every page the job needs, then the other rights on those pages. Click Save role . The bar with Save role , Save role & New and Cancel stays at the bottom of the window while you scroll. Give the role to users on User Accounts . Example The demo A/R Clerk has View , Create , Edit and Print/Export on the Customers pages other than reports, View and Print/Export on the Home pages and the Customer and Receivables reports, and View only on the Item List. It has no Delete/Void , so voids go to someone else. Its limits are a 10% discount, a 5% price change and ₱50,000.00. Step by step: change a role Click the role's name. Change the ticks and limits. Click Save role . The message "Role saved. Every user with this role is updated at once." confirms the change. At the bottom of the page, Users with this role lists the users affected. The Page access view button at the top of an existing role opens the same role on Page Access Configuration , which is quicker when you only want to allow or deny whole pages. Step by step: delete a custom role Make sure no user has the role (the Users column shows 0). Click Delete beside it and confirm. Standard roles and roles with users cannot be deleted ("Only custom roles with no users can be deleted."). Good to know At least one role must keep full administrator access. Clearing the Administrator box on the last such role is refused ("At least one role must keep full administrator access."). A number box that holds text is refused: ""Max discount % without approval" must be a number or blank." If the role combines duties that should be kept apart, a Segregation of duties warning appears. Tick Save anyway (the warning and the decision are recorded in the audit trail) and save again, or change the grid. Administrator roles are not checked. Every role change is recorded in the audit trail with the rights before and after, so an auditor can see who widened a role and when.

This page decides which pages each role or user can open, without the detail of the action rights. It is the quickest place to allow or deny a whole page or module, to give one user an exception, and to compare all roles side by side. Where to find it: System Administration > Page Access Configuration. The Page access view button on a role also opens it. The page has three tabs: By role , By user (overrides) and Matrix (all roles) . At the top, Effective access opens Effective Access (View as User) and Role permissions opens User Role Configuration . By role Choose a role in the drop-down. The pages are listed by module. The heading of each module shows how many of its pages are allowed (for example "Home 7 / 7 allowed"), and modules with at least one allowed page open by themselves. Each page shows its kind (center, list, transaction screen, setup screen or report, plus the report group) and a drop-down set to Allowed or Denied . Choose the role. Set each page to Allowed or Denied , or use Allow module and Deny module on a module's heading. Type a Reason for the change (recorded in the audit trail) . Click Save page access . The message tells you how many page settings changed, for example "2 page setting(s) changed for A/P Clerk. Changes apply the next time users open a page." Note A page you allow here gets only View , plus Print/Export if the role never had the page before. Set Create , Edit , Delete/Void , Approve (and Print/Export where it is missing) on User Role Configuration . Denying a page removes all its rights from the role. An administrator role cannot be changed here: the page shows "The Administrator role has full access to every page." and the drop-downs are greyed out. By user (overrides) An override is an exception for one user on one page. It always wins over the user's roles, including the Administrator role. Use it for a short-term need or a single exception, so you do not have to create a new role. Choose the user in the drop-down (you can type part of the name). A line shows the user's roles and how many overrides they have. For each page you see: Column What it shows Page The page name. Rows with an override are highlighted. From roles Allowed (with the roles that allow it) or Denied , as the roles alone decide. Setting for this user Inherit from role , Override: allow or Override: deny . Actions when allowed by override Tick boxes C (Create), E (Edit), D (Delete/Void), P (Print/Export) and A (Approve), used only with Override: allow . Set by Who set the override, when, and the reason. Choose the user. Open the module and find the page. Choose Override: allow and tick the actions, or Override: deny . Type a Reason for the override . Click Save overrides . Check effective access beside it shows the result. To remove an override, set the page back to Inherit from role and save. Example In the demo company, Ben Garcia (arclerk) has Override: deny on Assess Finance Charges with the reason "Finance charges are assessed by the accountant", and Maria Santos (salesrep) has Override: allow with P on Customer Balance Summary because she "Needs balances for account visits". You cannot deny yourself User Accounts , User Role Configuration or Page Access Configuration ("You cannot deny yourself access to the administration pages."), so you cannot lock yourself out by mistake. Matrix (all roles) The matrix shows every page down the side and every role across the top, with Allowed in green or Denied in red. Administrator roles show Allowed everywhere. The matrix shows page access only, not the action rights, and it cannot be changed here. The links above it are Key pages only (eleven sensitive pages such as Chart of Accounts, Receive Payments, Pay Bills, Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand, POS Register, Reconcile, Audit Trail and User Role Configuration), All pages and Print . Good to know Saving on this page needs Edit on it. Without it, you can look but the drop-downs are greyed out. Every change is recorded in the audit trail with each page's old and new setting and your reason. The User Access and Permission Changes report lists them. The Company Owner and the Super Admin are never locked out by an override.

This page shows what one user can really do once all their roles, overrides and sensitive permissions are combined. Use it to answer "why can't Ella open this page?" or to check an account before an audit. Where to find it: System Administration > Effective Access (View as User). You can also click Effective access on a user's page, Check effective access on the By user tab of Page Access Configuration, or a figure in the Pages allowed column of the User Access and Permission Changes report. Choose the user in the drop-down. Tick Show denied pages too to list every page, not only the allowed ones. Print prints the page. What the page shows The user box: the name, username and status, Roles , Sites ("all", or the site names), POS terminals ("any at allowed sites" when none is assigned) and Pages allowed (for example 4 of 168). Sensitive permissions : each of the nine permissions with Yes , No , a number or No limit . The page table: Module , Page , Access ( Allowed or Denied ), a tick under each right the user has ( Create , Edit , Delete/Void , Print/Export , Approve ), and Comes from . Comes from names the role or roles that grant the page, "User override (allowed)" or "User override (denied)", "Administrator role", "Company Owner" or "Super Admin", or "No role grants it" for a denied page. Rows with an override are highlighted. Good to know Looking up a user is itself recorded in the audit trail (action View Access ). To change what you see here, change the user's roles on User Accounts , the roles on User Role Configuration , or the overrides on Page Access Configuration .

This page holds the company-wide settings: the company's name and TIN as printed on reports and vouchers, the password and log-in rules, the closing date, finance charge rates, POS receipt wording, the Bluetooth receipt printer, how items are listed in the transaction forms, default POS sites and classes, and the company logo. Where to find it: System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date All the boxes belong to one form. Change what you need anywhere on the page, then use the bar at the bottom of the window: type a Reason for the change (recorded in the audit trail) and click Save settings . The message tells you how many settings changed. Only users with Edit on this page can save; others see the settings greyed out. Company Field What to enter Company name Printed at the top of every report and document, and shown in the top bar. With several companies, two companies cannot share a name. Address The company's address. TIN The company's Tax Identification Number, for example 000-123-456-000. Phone The company's phone number. Email The company's e-mail address. Fiscal year starts (month 1-12) The month the fiscal year begins: 1 for January, 7 for July. Report date choices such as This fiscal year and Fiscal year to date , and the budget year of Set Up Budgets, follow it. With several companies, the platform's record of the company follows the name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN saved here. Closing date Field What to enter Books closed through (blank = open) The last day of the closed period, for example 07/09/2026. Leave blank to keep every period open. Once the books are closed through a date, users without the sensitive permission Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled cannot record, change, void or delete a transaction dated on or before that date. They see "The books are closed through 07/09/2026. You do not have permission to record transactions dated on or before the closing date." or "This transaction is dated on or before the closing date (07/09/2026) and cannot be changed." The Home dashboard shows "Books closed through" with the date. There is no separate closing password: who may still work in a closed period is decided only by that sensitive permission on the user's roles. Every change of the closing date is recorded in the audit trail as a Closing Date Change , with the reason you typed. Step by step: close a month Make sure all the month's transactions are entered and the bank accounts are reconciled. Make a backup on Backup & Restore . Open Company, Security & Closing Date . Enter the month's last day in Books closed through (blank = open) . Type the reason, for example "June 2026 closed", and click Save settings . Security policy Field What to enter Minimum password length At least 6. The standard is 8. Require upper- and lower-case letters Ticked: a password needs both. Require a number Ticked: a password needs a digit. Require a symbol Ticked: a password needs a character that is not a letter or digit. Passwords expire after (days, 0 = never) After this many days since the last change, the user must choose a new password at the next page they open ("Your password has expired. Please choose a new one."). The standard is 90. Failed logins before lockout Wrong passwords in a row that lock the account. At least 1; the standard is 5. The log-in page tells the user how many attempts are left. Log out after inactivity (minutes) A user who opens no page for this long is logged out ("You were logged out after a period of inactivity."). At least 1; the standard is 30. The password rules apply whenever a password is set or changed, by the user or on User Accounts. Existing passwords are not checked again until they are changed. Audit trail Field What to enter Keep audit trail entries for at least (years) Your company's retention period, 10 by default. The note under it says what the program does: audit trail entries are read-only and cannot be switched off, edited or deleted, and database triggers block changes even outside the application. The program never removes audit entries, so this number records your policy; keep entries at least as long as tax and accounting regulations require. Finance charges Field What to enter Annual interest rate % The yearly rate for overdue customer balances, 12 by default. Minimum finance charge The smallest charge assessed, ₱50.00 by default. Grace period (days) Days after the due date before a charge is assessed. Charge interest on earlier finance charges Ticked: earlier finance charges also earn interest. These are used by Assess Finance Charges . Inventory and POS Field What it means Track Item Group Sales transactions Ticked (the standard): every item group sold is recorded in a table of its own, as a group (how many groups, at what price, for how much), for Sales by Item Group and POS Sales by Item Group . Cleared: groups sold are not recorded there (their items are still recorded as always). Adopt the Group Price in the Item Group Ticked (the standard): the Group price of an item group is its price on estimates, sales orders, sales receipts, invoices and POS sales; the difference from the prices of its items goes to its price variance account. Cleared (or a group without a group price): a group is sold at its consolidated price, the sum of the prices of its items. See Item groups: group price and price variance . Allow selling or moving stock below zero (with warning) Ticked (the standard): a document that takes an item below zero at a site is saved, with a yellow message naming the items now below zero. Cleared: such a document is refused with "Not enough stock: …", whether it is an invoice, a sales receipt, a POS sale, a transfer, an adjustment or any other document that takes stock out; and a processing order on Disassemble / Process Items whose outputs were already used cannot be voided or deleted. Block sales of items with no unit cost (inventory parts and the items of item groups) Ticked (the standard): an invoice, sales receipt, statement charge or POS sale is refused when it sells an inventory part or assembly that has neither a Unit cost on its item form nor an average unit cost, because its cost of goods sold would be zero and its profit overstated. An item group is sold as its items, so the items of the group are checked too. The message names the items and the group they are in. Cleared: such sales are saved as before. See Items with no unit cost . Block posting processing orders with no unit cost (inputs, co-products and by-products) Ticked (the standard): Save and post and Complete and post on Disassemble / Process Items are refused when an input has no unit cost or average unit cost, or a co-product or by-product would be received at no cost (scrap may be). Save as pending is still allowed. Cleared: such orders are posted as before. Only a save that lowers the quantity is checked, so older documents can still be corrected while an item is below zero. The No negative quantities on hand check on Utilities: Verify & Rebuild Data and the Negative Inventory Listing show the items below zero. POS receipt wording Field Standard wording Receipt title for sales OFFICIAL RECEIPT Receipt title for returns and refunds RETURN / REFUND Receipt title for sales charged to an account CHARGE INVOICE Receipt title for payments on account ACKNOWLEDGEMENT RECEIPT Text at the bottom of the receipt (one line of text per line) "Thank you for shopping!" and "This serves as your official receipt." (up to 600 characters) Print "Walk-in customer" when the sale has no customer name Ticked A title left blank goes back to the standard wording. The customer's name is printed under the date whenever the sale has one. Bluetooth receipt printer A POS receipt can be sent straight from the browser to a small Bluetooth roll printer, such as the Officom OC-PT210, with nothing installed on the phone or the till. Field What to enter Offer a Bluetooth printer on every receipt Ticked: every receipt shows a Bluetooth printer button. Paper width 58 mm roll (32 characters per line) , 80 mm roll, small type (42 characters per line) or 80 mm roll (48 characters per line) . Only offer printers whose name starts with (blank = offer every device found) The start of your printer's name, to keep other Bluetooth devices out of the list. Blank lines fed after each receipt Paper fed at the end so the receipt can be torn off; 4 by default. Cut the paper at the end (printers with a cutter only) Tick only if the printer has a cutter. Print as soon as a receipt opens, when the printer is already connected Ticked: no need to tap the button for each sale. Test print prints a short sample so you can check the paper width. The printer is paired once from a receipt: tap Bluetooth printer , pick it from the list the browser shows, and it is remembered for the next sale. Important Bluetooth printing works only in Chrome, Edge, Opera or Samsung Internet on Android, or Chrome or Edge on a computer. Firefox, iPhones and iPads, and the browsers inside Facebook and Messenger cannot use Bluetooth. The program must also be opened on an https:// address or on http://localhost/. On a plain address such as http://192.168.1.10/ the browser refuses Bluetooth, and the receipt says so. Searching for items This box decides how items are listed in the item drop-downs of the transaction forms: Item name/code + Display name (for example "LAP-001 - Laptop 14-inch i5 16GB") or Display name + Item name/code ("Laptop 14-inch i5 16GB - LAP-001"). Typing any part of either the code or the display name finds the item, whichever order you choose. All transactions, unless one is set differently below is the choice for every form. The two buttons Set every transaction to Item name/code + Display name and Set every transaction to Display name + Item name/code set all the forms at once. The table lists the 22 forms that have item boxes (Create Estimates, Create Invoices, Enter Bills, POS Register, Write Checks and the others), each with a choice of its own. A form set differently from the overall choice is marked. Receipt Management lists supplier documents, not items; the bill it opens follows Enter Bills. A form on the same choice as the overall box follows it when you change that box. Default site & class for POS transactions This box appears when there are users who can be given a default. It is optional and set for one user at a time. Use Find a user to find a row. Column What to choose User name The user (with username and roles). Default site The site whose counter the user's POS Register opens on, or No default . Default class The class every new sale of the user starts with, or No default . Anyone left blank works as before: the counter is the first one they may use, and the class comes from the counter or from the previous sale. The cashier can still change either one on the sale in front of them. Company logo Field What to do Upload the logo (or Replace the logo ) Choose a JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP or BMP file of up to 2 MB. A wide logo on a white or transparent background prints best. The preview shows it before you save. Remove the logo Tick and save to remove the current logo. Show the logo on Tick each report and voucher that should carry the logo. The list under Show the logo on has a group for Vouchers and documents (such as Check Voucher, Cash Voucher, Journal Voucher, Deposit Voucher, POS Receipt (register) and Customer Statement) and a group of reports for each module. Ticking a group's box ticks the whole group. Find a report or voucher narrows the list, Tick all and Clear all work on the entries shown, and the count beside the heading says how many are ticked. The logo is printed beside the company name on the reports and vouchers ticked, on screen, on Print / PDF and on paper. Good to know Messages when saving: "Passwords must be at least 6 characters.", "Allow at least one failed login.", "The session timeout must be at least one minute.", "Books closed through (blank = open): enter a valid date." and, for the logo, "The logo file is larger than 2 MB. Save a smaller copy and upload that." or "That file is not a picture the system can show. Use a JPG or PNG file." Every save is recorded in the audit trail as a Settings Change listing each setting's old and new value.

Verify Data checks that the books, the customer and vendor balances, and inventory agree with each other. Rebuild Data repairs what it can: it replays inventory transactions in date order, on each date the stock received before the stock used or sold, so costs and cost of sales match the dates, and it refreshes document balances. Run the checks at every month-end before you close the books. Where to find it: System Administration > Utilities: Verify & Rebuild Data. The Verify & Rebuild Data button on Backup & Restore also opens it. Verify data The checks run every time you open the page. Run the checks again repeats them. The heading shows No problems or the number of problems, and the number of warnings. Each check has a green tick (in order), a yellow triangle (warning) or a red cross (problem), with the Result and What to do . Check What it compares If it fails General ledger balances All debits less all credits in the ledger; it must be 0.00. Contact support: a posting did not balance. Every transaction balances The debits and credits of each transaction. The screen suggests Rebuild data. Accounts receivable matches the customer balances The A/R accounts (1100 Accounts Receivable) against the total of the customers' balances. Rebuild data refreshes document balances. Accounts payable matches the vendor balances The A/P accounts (2000 Accounts Payable) against the total of the vendors' balances. Rebuild data refreshes document balances. Inventory ledger matches the inventory movements The inventory asset accounts (1200 Inventory) against the value of all stock movements. Rebuild data recalculates inventory costs. Quantities on hand match the movements Each item's quantity at each site against the movements that make it up, including a site that has movements but no quantity row. Rebuild data recalculates quantities. Since version 31 the average cost is always worked out on the movements, and an item whose quantities differ is put right the next time it moves. Average cost matches the value on hand (warning) Each item's average cost against its value and quantity on hand. Rebuild data recalculates inventory costs. Inventory entered in date order (warning) Items with movements recorded after later-dated ones, such as a purchase entered late but dated early, or, on one date, stock used or sold before that day's receipt was entered (a processing order typed before the bill of the same day). Rebuild data replays them in date order. No negative quantities on hand (warning) Items below zero at a site. Record the missing purchase, transfer or adjustment. See Negative Inventory Listing . No orphan transaction lines Lines left without their transaction. Contact support. No document is over-applied Payments, discounts and withholding applied to a document beyond its total. Open the payment or credit memo and correct the applied amounts. Document statuses match their balances Invoices, bills, statement charges and finance charges whose Open, Partial or Paid status does not match the balance. Rebuild data refreshes document balances. Module default accounts are set Every entry of Module Default Accounts has an account. Set them under Module Default Accounts . Example In the screenshot, Inventory entered in date order warns that 9 items (BAG-001, CAB-HDMI, KEY-001, LAP-001 and others) have movements recorded out of date order. A rebuild re-costs them so the cost of sales on each sale matches its date. Rebuild data Option What it does Recalculate inventory costs Replays every inventory transaction in date order: by date; on one date, first the transactions that only bring stock in (bills, item receipts, returns, adjustments up), then those that take some out and put some in (processing orders, builds, transfers), then those that only take it out (sales, adjustments down); then in the order entered. Average costs, item values and the cost of sales on past sales are restated. The sales amounts, quantities and the rest of the ledger are untouched. Refresh document balances and statuses Recalculates the open balances of invoices, bills, statement and finance charges, credit memos, payments, supplier credits and sales receipts, and the status of estimates, sales orders and purchase orders. Step by step: rebuild data Make a backup on Backup & Restore . Ask everyone else to stop entering transactions until you finish. Tick one or both options. Type a Reason (kept in the audit trail) , for example "month-end check". Click Rebuild data and confirm ("Rebuild now? Cost of sales on past sales may change. Make a backup first."). Read the Rebuild result , then look at the checks again. The Rebuild result says how many inventory transactions were replayed over how many items, how many document balances were refreshed and how long it took. Users who may view costs also see the total cost of sales before and after, the difference, and a table of the first 100 transactions whose cost changed ( Date , Type , Number , Cost before , Cost after , Difference ). If nothing changed, it says "No cost of sales amount changed: every transaction was already costed in date order." What it changes A cost rebuild changes the amounts posted to the cost of sales account (5000 Cost of Goods Sold) and the inventory account (1200 Inventory) on transactions that move stock. Transactions dated on or before the closing date are re-costed as well; their sales totals do not change. The rebuild runs as one piece of work: if it fails part-way, nothing is changed. It is recorded in the audit trail as Rebuild Data , with the cost of sales before and after. Good to know Anyone who can open the page can run the checks. Rebuild data needs Edit on this page; without it the box says "You can run the checks above. Rebuilding data needs the edit permission on this page." The standard Accountant role can run the checks but not rebuild. A rebuild re-posts only the transactions that move inventory. If General ledger balances or Every transaction balances still fails after a rebuild, contact support. The page does not change any transaction's date, quantity or selling price.

Use this page to load records from a spreadsheet instead of typing them: the chart of accounts, inventory items with their opening stock, customers, vendors, fixed assets, and whole transactions such as invoices, bills, checks, journal entries and POS sales. It is most useful when you start using the program and bring over lists and balances from another system. Where to find it: System Administration > Import from CSV. The page has a Backup & Restore button at the top, because you should back up before every import. How an import is safe Nothing is written until every line of the file has been read and checked. A file with even one bad line changes nothing. Check the file reads the whole file and reports every problem without writing anything. The writing runs as one piece of work, so a problem found while writing also leaves the books exactly as they were. A document number that is already in the books stops a transaction import, so the same file is not posted twice by mistake (checks are recognised by their check number). What you can import The drop-down What are you importing? groups the kinds of records like this: Group What are you importing? One line of the file is An existing record Lists Chart of accounts one account same code: updated Inventory Inventory items one item same code: updated Names Customers one customer or job same name: updated Names Vendors (suppliers) one supplier same name: updated Names Fixed assets one asset always added Customer transactions Invoices , Sales receipts , Sales orders one item line same number: refused Supplier transactions Purchase orders , Receive items and enter bills one item line same number: refused Banking Write checks , Cash vouchers , Journal entries one line of the document same number: refused Point of sale POS transactions one item line same receipt no.: refused For transactions, the lines that carry the same Document no. (or Receipt no. for POS) make one document; its header details (date, customer, memo and so on) are taken from its first line. Preparing the file Save the sheet as CSV in Excel: File > Save As > CSV (Comma delimited) . The file name must end in .csv or .txt . A file that uses semicolons instead of commas is read as well. Any of the ways Excel saves a CSV is read correctly: CSV (Comma delimited) in Windows' own encoding, CSV UTF-8 and Unicode Text (UTF-16, with tabs). Curly quotes (“Mismo” brand), dashes, the peso sign and accented letters in a name or a description come through as typed; they used to stop the import with an "Incorrect string value" error. The first line holds the column names, such as code , name and opening_qty . The order does not matter, capitals do not matter, and a space may stand for the underscore ( Sales Price is read as sales_price ). A column you do not need can be left out. A column the program does not know is ignored. Blank lines are skipped. Dates may be written as 2026-09-30, 09/30/2026, Sep 30, 2026 and in other common ways. A date such as 03/04/2026 is read month first, as March 4. Numbers may have comma separators (12,500.00). Do not type a peso sign or other text in a number column. Yes/no columns accept Yes, Y, 1, True, Oo or Opo for yes. Anything else counts as no. A column that names a list entry (a term, a tax code, an account, a site, a customer) must match the list exactly. Accounts may be given by code or name (6040 or Office Supplies Expense), tax codes by code (VAT12), sites by code or name (WH or Main Warehouse), items by code, display name or barcode. The template's second line is an example. Replace it with your own data or delete it before importing. Step by step: check a file, then import it Choose the kind of record in What are you importing? The page shows a note on how that kind is read, a Download the blank template button, and on the right a table of its columns with the ones that are needed. Click Download the blank template and open it in Excel. Fill in one line per record (or per document line). Save it as CSV. Under CSV file , click Choose File and pick the file. Click Check the file . If the result says The file was not imported , correct the listed lines in the spreadsheet, save, choose the file again and check again. When the result says The file was checked and "The file is in order: nothing was written yet", look the lines over. Click Import these N item(s) (or Import these N record(s) ) and confirm. The file you checked is imported without being chosen again. Check and import in one step checks the file and, if it is in order, imports it at once. The program asks you to confirm ("Check and import this file in one step? Records are added to the books."). Use it only for files you have checked before. The result of a check When the file has problems, the result lists them by line number of the file (line 1 is the column names), up to 200 of them. Nothing was written. In this example, line 4 names the site "XX", which does not exist, so the program reports that "XX" is not in the sites list and asks for the site of the opening quantity. Changing it to WH or Main Warehouse fixes both lines of the message. When the file is in order, the result shows a preview. For Inventory items : the number of new items, items to update, items with opening stock (and its value, if you may view costs) and any new categories, then a table with Line , Item , Type , Category , Unit , Cost (only if you may view costs), Price , Opening stock and Will be ("Added", or "Updated" with the number of columns that will change). For accounts, customers, vendors and fixed assets: Line , Name and Details . For transactions: Document , Date , Lines and Total . A file that passed the check is kept on the server for one day for the Import these button. If it is gone ("The checked file is no longer here. Choose the file and check it again."), check the file again. After the import The result then shows Imported , how many records were written, and What was created , with a link to each item or transaction (updated records say "(updated)"). The Recent imports table at the bottom lists the last 15 imports: When , What , File , Records , Written (0 when the file was refused), By and Notes (the first problems). A check alone is not listed. Every record added or updated by an import is recorded in the audit trail as Import Create or Import Update . Inventory items: the columns The price level columns depend on your price levels: there is one price_level_ column for every active price level, numbered by the level. The template always has the right ones. In the demo company they are price_level_1 Wholesale, price_level_2 VIP, price_level_3 Retail Plus, price_level_4 Price Level 4 and price_level_5 Price Level 5. Column What goes in it Needed code Item name / code, unique, up to 40 characters (LAP-001). Yes name Display name, up to 120 characters. For a new item item_type Inventory part, Non-inventory part, Service, Inventory assembly, Other charge, Group, Discount, Subtotal or Payment. Blank = Inventory part. barcode Barcode, unique. description Sales description. purchase_description Purchase description. category Category. A new one is added to the Category list. unit Unit such as pc, box or kg. Blank = pc. Ignored when a U/M set is named. uom_set U/M set as named in Units of Measure. Blank = single unit. sales_unit Unit of the U/M set offered first on sales (code or name). purchase_unit Unit of the U/M set offered first on purchases. cost Purchase cost per unit. sales_price Sales price. For a discount item, the fixed discount amount. price_level_1 and the others Price for that price level. Blank = the level's own percentage. discount_pct Discount items: the discount %, or 0 for the fixed amount in sales_price . tax_code Tax code (VAT12, ZR, EX, NT). income_account Income account, code or name. Blank = the module default (4000 Sales). cogs_account Cost of goods sold account, inventory parts and assemblies only. Blank = 5000. asset_account Inventory asset account, inventory parts and assemblies only. Blank = 1200. expense_account Expense or purchase account for non-inventory parts, services and other charges. preferred_vendor Preferred supplier, as named in the vendor list. reorder_point Reorder point (minimum). max_stock Maximum stock. build_point Build point, for assemblies. components Assemblies and groups: CODE x quantity; CODE x quantity. For a new assembly or group opening_qty Opening quantity on hand, new inventory parts and assemblies only. opening_cost Opening cost per unit. Blank = the cost column. opening_site Site of the opening quantity, code or name. Blank = the only site, if there is one. With opening_qty opening_date Date of the opening quantity. Blank = today. is_active Yes for an active item. Blank counts as yes. Inventory items: how the import treats them An item whose code is already on the Item List is updated, not added again, and only the columns that are in the file change. A blank cell in a column that is in the file clears that field (for example a blank barcode removes the barcode). A blank income_account , cogs_account or asset_account keeps what the item has. The type of an existing item cannot be changed by an import. Components may be written as BOLT x 4; NUT x 4 , and also with * , = or : instead of x , or one per line. A component with no quantity counts as 1. A component must already exist or appear earlier in the file, and it must be an inventory part, assembly, service, non-inventory part or other charge. Components in the file replace the item's components. Opening quantities are only for new inventory parts and assemblies. Change the stock of an existing item with Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand . A price level column with a price sets a special price for that level; a blank cell removes the special price so the level's own percentage applies again. A U/M set cannot be changed on an item that was already entered in units of its present set. If your roles do not let you view costs, the file may not fill cost , opening_cost or opening_qty . Inventory items: what it records The items are added to the Item List . For the opening quantities, the program posts one inventory adjustment for each site and date, with the memo "Opening stock of N imported item(s)": Account Debit Credit 1200 Inventory (the item's asset account) quantity x opening cost 3900 Opening Balance Equity same amount Example The checked file above adds PRN-001 Inkjet Printer with 5 at WH - Main Warehouse at ₱4,500.00 (₱22,500.00) and CAB-USB USB Cable 2m with 10 at ₱80.00 (₱800.00), both as of 09/01/2026. Both lines share a site and date, so one adjustment of ₱23,300.00 is posted: Inventory debited and Opening Balance Equity credited. An opening date on or before the closing date is refused unless you may change closed periods. Chart of accounts: the columns Column What goes in it Needed code Account code (6075). Yes name Account name. Yes account_type Account type, exactly as the Chart of Accounts lists it (see below). Yes parent_code For a sub-account, the code of its parent. normal_balance Debit or Credit. Blank = from the account type (right for all but contra accounts). bank_account_no Bank account number, for bank accounts. with_sl Yes when the account keeps a subsidiary ledger ("With SL"). description Description. is_active Yes for an active account. Blank counts as yes. The account types are Bank, Accounts Receivable, Other Current Asset, Fixed Asset, Other Asset, Accounts Payable, Credit Card, Other Current Liability, Long Term Liability, Equity, Income, Other Income, Cost of Goods Sold, Expense and Other Expense. The parent must already exist or appear earlier in the file, and it must be of the same category (asset, liability, equity, income or expense). An account whose code already exists is updated with the file's values; it cannot move to another category if the modules post to it or it already has transactions. See Chart of Accounts . Customers: the columns Column What goes in it Needed name Customer name, or Customer:Job for a job (ABC Trading Corp.:Office Fit-out). Yes company_name , contact_person , phone , mobile , email Contact details. billing_address , shipping_address , tin Addresses and TIN. terms Payment terms as named in the Terms list (Net 30). credit_limit Credit limit. price_level , tax_code , customer_type , sales_rep Entries of those lists. allow_pos_charge Yes if the customer can charge at the POS. notes Notes. For a job, the customer must already exist or appear earlier in the file. When a customer with the same name (or the same job under the same customer) is already on the list, the import updates it, and only the cells of its line that have something in them are changed. A column the file does not have, or a blank cell, keeps what is saved, and an inactive customer stays inactive. So a file with just name and phone updates the phone numbers and nothing else. To clear a field, change it on the customer's own form. Every change is recorded in the audit trail with the value before and after. Example ABC Trading Corp. has terms Net 30 and a credit limit of ₱250,000.00. A file with the line ABC Trading Corp.,0917 555 0101,, under the columns name,mobile,terms,credit_limit changes the mobile number only: the terms and the credit limit stay as they were. Vendors (suppliers): the columns Column What goes in it Needed name Supplier name (TechDistributors Inc.). Yes company_name , contact_person , phone , fax , email , address , tin Contact details and TIN. terms Payment terms. credit_limit Credit limit. default_expense_account Account the purchases usually go to, code or name (6040). account_no Your account number with the supplier. notes Notes. A supplier with the same name that is already on the list is updated the same way as a customer: only the filled cells change, and blank cells keep what is saved. Fixed assets: the columns Column What goes in it Needed description Description of the asset. Yes category Asset category as named in Asset Categories. Yes asset_no Asset number. Blank = the next number. Must not be used already. location Location. A new one is added to the Location list. serial_no Serial or plate number. vendor , class Supplier it was bought from; default class. acquisition_date Date acquired. Yes cost Cost. Yes salvage_value Salvage (residual) value. useful_life_years Useful life in years, more than zero. Yes method straight_line, declining_balance, syd or units_of_production. Blank = straight line. opening_accum_dep , opening_through Accumulated depreciation to date, and the date it runs through. post_opening Yes to post an opening-balance entry. notes Notes. An asset is added to the Fixed Asset Register without an accounting entry, so you can load a register beside an opening trial balance that already carries the assets. Put Yes in post_opening for assets that are not on the books yet: the program then debits the category's asset account with the cost, credits its accumulated depreciation account with opening_accum_dep , and credits 3900 Opening Balance Equity with the difference. An asset with accumulated depreciation needs opening_through . Invoices, sales receipts and sales orders: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Your own reference. Lines with the same one make one document. Yes date Date. All lines of a document must carry the same date. Yes customer Customer, or Customer:Job. Yes terms Payment terms. item Item code, display name or barcode. Yes description Description. qty , rate Quantity and price per unit. Yes discount_pct Discount %. tax_code , site , class Tax code, inventory site and class of the line. memo Memo (header). deposit_to Sales receipts only: the bank or cash account. Blank = 1050 Undeposited Funds. Each invoice goes to 1100 Accounts Receivable with a due date from the terms. Each document posts exactly as one entered on Create Invoices or Enter Sales Receipts would. Sales orders are saved as open orders and do not post until invoiced (see Create Sales Orders ). The doc_no is kept as the document's reference number; the program gives the document its own next number. Purchase orders and receive items and enter bills: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Your own reference. Lines with the same one make one document. Yes date Date. Yes vendor Supplier. Yes ref_no Bills: the supplier's invoice number. Purchase orders: a reference number. item Item code, display name or barcode. Yes description Description. qty , rate Quantity and cost per unit. Yes tax_code , site , class Tax code, inventory site and class. memo Memo (header). Each Receive items and enter bills document becomes a bill with the vendor's terms: the items come into stock and 2000 Accounts Payable is credited, as on Receive Items and Enter Bills . A bill is refused as a duplicate when the supplier's invoice number (or the doc_no , if ref_no is blank) is already on a bill. Purchase orders are saved as open orders and do not post (see Create Purchase Orders ). Write checks: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Your own reference. Lines with the same one make one check. Yes date Date. Yes bank_account Bank account, code or name (1010). Yes payee A supplier's name, or any name. Yes check_no Check number. A check number already used on a check is refused. account Account charged, code or name (6020). Yes description Description of the line. amount Amount. Yes tax_code , class Tax code and class. memo Memo. Each check credits the bank account and debits the accounts charged, as on Write Checks . When the payee matches a supplier's name, the check is linked to that supplier. A check without a check_no cannot be recognised as a duplicate, so never import the same checks file twice. Cash vouchers: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Lines with the same one make one voucher. Yes date Date. Yes cash_account Cash account paid from, code or name (1005 Petty Cash Fund). Yes paid_to Employee, customer, supplier or any name. Yes account Account of the line, code or name. Yes debit , credit Amount of the line on one side. memo Memo of the line. class Class. particulars Particulars (header). ref_no Reference number. The cash account is credited with the debits less the credits, which must be more than zero. See Cash Voucher . Journal entries: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Lines with the same one make one entry. Yes date Date. Yes account Account, code or name. Yes debit , credit Amount of the line on one side. description Memo of the line. name Customer, supplier, employee or other name on the line. class Class. memo , ref_no Memo and reference number of the entry. The debits and the credits of each entry must be equal. See Make Journal Entries . POS transactions: the columns Column What goes in it Needed receipt_no Receipt number. Lines with the same one make one sale. Yes date Date. Yes terminal POS terminal, code or name (POS-01). Yes customer Customer. Blank = walk-in. item Item code, display name or barcode. Yes description Description. qty , price Quantity and price per unit. Yes discount_pct Discount %. tax_code Tax code. payment_method Cash, GCash, P.O. Card and so on. Blank = Cash. class Class. Each receipt becomes a completed POS sale at the terminal's site, paid in full with the payment method given. If the terminal has no open shift, one is opened for it. See Point of Sale . Good to know Checking and importing need Create on this page. Downloading a template needs Print/Export . Transactions are saved as if entered by hand, so the closing date applies. A transaction dated on or before it is refused unless you may change closed periods; such a problem is found while writing and shown at the top of the page, and nothing is written. Messages about the file itself: "Choose a CSV file (.csv). In Excel: File > Save As > CSV (Comma delimited).", "The file is empty.", "The file holds no data lines." and "The first line of the file must hold the column names. Download the template for "Inventory items" to see them." Typical line messages: "Line 5: "Net 45" is not in the terms list (column "terms").", "Line 7: the code LAP-001 is already on line 3 of the file.", "Document INV-IMP-001 is already in the books as INV-00012. Take it out of the file, or change its document number." and "Document JE-IMP-001: the debits (25,000.00) and the credits (24,000.00) are not equal."

A backup is one .sql file that holds every table and every row of the company's database. Make one before every month-end close, before a large price change, before every import and before a rebuild, and keep copies off the server. Restoring replaces what is in the database now with what is in the file. Where to find it: System Administration > Backup & Restore. The Backup & Restore button on Import from CSV also opens it. Make a backup The box shows the Database (in the demo, gsmart; for a company added later on a multi-company platform, the company's name), the number of Tables , the Size on disk and the Backups kept here . Field What to choose What is this backup for? (optional) A note, such as "Before the month-end close". It is kept in the backup history and the audit trail. What to save Everything: structure and data for a real backup, or Structure only (no rows) for empty tables. Backups to keep on the server Keep them all , The newest 5 , The newest 10 (the standard) or The newest 20 . After the backup, older files beyond this number are deleted from the server. Compress the file (.sql.gz, much smaller) Ticked: the file is compressed. Shown only when the server can compress. Type what the backup is for. Leave What to save on Everything: structure and data . Choose how many backups to keep. Click Make the backup now and leave the page open until it finishes. The message says "Backup written:" with the file name and size, and how many older backups were removed. The file is named after the database and the date and time, for example gsmart_20260927_141929.sql.gz . A structure-only backup ends in _structure . Backups on the server The table lists the files in the backups folder (shown beside the heading, for example storage/backups), newest first, with File , Made and Size . Download saves a copy to your computer. Do this at least weekly and keep the copy somewhere other than the server. The trash button deletes a file. In the box that opens, type the Reason (required, recorded in the audit trail) and click Delete this backup . Files whose name starts with before_restore_ are the automatic backups made before a restore. Files marked uploaded came from From a file on my computer . Backup history lists the last 20 backups, restores and deletions: When , What ( Backup , Restore or Deleted ), File , Tables , Rows , By and Note . Restore from a backup Important A restore replaces every table of the database with what the file holds. Anything entered since that backup was made is lost. Ask everyone else to log out first. Open the tab From a backup kept here (or From a file on my computer to upload a .sql or .sql.gz file). Choose the Backup to restore (or choose the file). Type the Reason (recorded in the audit trail) . Type RESTORE in Type RESTORE to confirm . Click Restore (or Upload and restore ) and confirm. The message says how many statements were run. If some could not be run, a card Statements that could not be run lists them; check them before working in the books again. The upload tab tells you the largest file this server accepts. Copy a larger file into the backups folder instead and restore it from From a backup kept here . The safeguards Before it changes anything, the restore makes a fresh backup of what is there now ( before_restore_... ), so a restore can itself be undone by restoring that file. You must type RESTORE; otherwise "Type RESTORE in the box to confirm. Nothing has been changed." Only an administrator can restore (a user with the Administrator role, the Company Owner or the Super Admin), and only with Edit on this page. Others see "Only an administrator can restore the database." After the restore, the audit trail's protection is put back in place. With several companies, the list of users on the platform is brought in line with the restored users; a username that belongs to another company is reported, and that user cannot log in until the username is changed. If more than 25 statements fail, the restore stops. What is refused A file that does not end in .sql or .sql.gz ("A backup file ends in .sql or .sql.gz."). A single statement larger than 32 MB. Restore such a file with phpMyAdmin or Navicat. With several companies, only statements that rebuild the company's own tables are run (such as CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, INSERT INTO and SET). A statement that changes server settings or passwords, creates something other than a table, reads other data or names another database is listed as "not run". Good to know Making a backup needs Create , downloading needs Print/Export , and deleting needs Delete/Void on this page. The program does not make backups on a schedule. Make them yourself at the times listed above. A restore also brings back the audit trail and the backup history as they were in the file. Entries made after that backup remain in the automatic before_restore_ file. Backups to keep on the server also counts the before_restore_ and uploaded files, so a low number may remove them. Download any file you want to keep. A backup made here can be read back with phpMyAdmin (Import) or Navicat (Execute SQL File), and a file those programs wrote can be restored here. Compressed files are read back here directly. The backup file holds the tables and rows but not the two triggers that protect the audit trail. A restore on this page puts them back by itself. If you read a backup back with phpMyAdmin or Navicat instead, also run the program's database/triggers.sql file the same way, so the audit trail is protected again. If the backups folder cannot be written to, the page says so and Make the backup now is greyed out. Ask whoever manages the server to give the web server write permission on the storage folder. Backups, restores, downloads and deletions are all recorded in the audit trail.

This one-time step turns a single-company installation into a platform that can hold several companies, each in a database of its own. The present company is kept exactly as it is and becomes Company 1 . The step creates the platform (master) database, the first Super Admin account that manages every company, and the Company Code that new employees of Company 1 use to join. Where to find it: System Administration > Multi-Company Setup. The menu entry disappears once multi-company is running. Fields Field What to enter Company name Required. Filled in from Company, Security & Closing Date. TIN , Phone , Address , E-mail Filled in from the settings; correct them if needed. Contact person Optional. Company Owner An active user of this company who will manage its employees, join requests and Company Code. Administrators are listed first. Employees who join with the Company Code wait for the Company Owner's approval Ticked by default. Clear it to let new employees in without approval. Username (Super Admin) 3 to 50 characters, different from every username of this company. Filled with superadmin. Full name (Super Admin) Filled with Platform Administrator. E-mail (Super Admin) Optional. Password and Password again At least 10 characters (or the company's minimum, if longer) with upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a symbol. A backup of this database was made (System Administration > Backup & Restore) Tick after you have made the backup. The What happens box lists the five things the step does: the platform database is created on the same MySQL server with the same user as config/config.php ; this database is registered as Company 1 without any record being moved, changed or deleted, and nobody's password changes; every user of the company is listed in the platform database so the log-in page knows where they belong; Company 1 gets its Company Code and owner; and the Super Admin account is created. Step by step: set up several companies Make a backup on Backup & Restore and download it. Read Before you start . The storage folder must be writable, and the MySQL user needs the right to create databases, tables, triggers and foreign keys. On shared hosting, create the platform database in the control panel first. Check the Company 1 details and choose the Company Owner . Fill in the Super Admin's username, full name and password twice. Tick the backup box. Click Set up and confirm. The result shows the Company Code (for example STC-B8TJC), the Super Admin username and the number of Company users registered . Everyone keeps logging in with the same username and password.
