From then on this page only says that multi-company is running, and names the company and its number. Good to know Only an administrator can run the setup, even if the page is allowed to other roles. Set up is greyed out when the storage folder cannot be written to. Messages you may see: "Tick the box to confirm that a backup of the database was made.", "The two Super Admin passwords do not match.", "The Super Admin needs a username of its own: admin is already a user of this company.", "Choose an active user of this company as its Company Owner." and "The master database gsmart_master already belongs to other companies." A company added later gets its own copy of this company's set-up (chart of accounts, tax codes, terms, roles and the other lists), never its customers, suppliers, items, users or transactions. Companies are created, switched on and off and given owners by the Super Admin; see Super Admin . The Company Code and the employees are managed under Company > Company Profile & Code ; see Company Owner .

The audit trail is a permanent log of every action that creates, changes or removes information, and of every log-in, failed log-in and denied page. The audit reports read it in different ways. What is recorded. Each entry holds the date and time, the user and their roles at the time, the computer's IP address and browser, the POS terminal and site where there is one, the module and page, the action, the record (with its number), the amount, the fields that changed (before and after), a full copy of the record where useful, the reason typed and the supervisor who approved. Among the actions recorded are: create, edit, delete and void of every transaction; print, reprint, export and e-mail of documents and reports; log-in, log-out, session timeout, failed log-ins, account locks and unlocks, password changes and resets; denied pages and failed supervisor approvals; changes to users, roles, page access, overrides, settings and the closing date; segregation of duties and credit limit overrides; imports, backups, restores and data rebuilds; POS shifts, cash drops and readings; bank reconciliations; memorized transactions entered automatically. It cannot be changed. Nobody, not even an administrator, can edit or delete an audit entry. Two database triggers refuse any change or deletion, even when someone works on the database directly with another program. The audit trail cannot be switched off. The only way older entries are replaced is by restoring a backup, which brings back the audit trail as it was in the backup file. The last five reports below (Voided and Deleted Transactions Summary and Detail, User Activity, Login History, and User Access and Permission Changes) use the common report tools (dates, Refresh , Columns , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize and drill-down), explained in Working with reports .

The Audit Trail lists every entry, newest first, and lets you filter them by date, user, module, page, action, record type and text. Use it to answer "who changed this, when, and what was it before?" Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Audit Trail, or Home > Report Center. The filters Filter What it does From and To The dates of the entries. The page opens from seven days ago to today. User One user's entries. Module One module, or Security for log-ins, lock-outs and denied pages. Page One page of the program. Action One kind of action, such as Void, Delete, Login Failed or Settings Change. Record type One kind of record, such as transaction, user, role or item. Record / text Words found in the record's name or number, the reason, the changes or the username. Click Filter to apply them. The number of entries found is shown above the table. The table shows 100 entries per page, with page numbers underneath. The columns Column What it shows Date / time When it happened, to the second. User Username, with the user's roles underneath. Where IP address, and the POS terminal and site when there is one. Module / page The module, with the page underneath. Action What was done: Create, Edit, Print, Void, Login and so on. Record The record. A transaction is a link to it (or marked deleted ); the clock icon opens its Transaction History ; [copy] opens the full copy saved with the entry. Amount The amount, when the action has one. Changes (before → after) Up to eight changed fields with old and new values, then "+N more". Reason / approval The reason typed and, if a supervisor approved, "Approved by" with their username. Rows for deletions, voids, failed log-ins, locked accounts, denied pages, failed approvals, segregation of duties overrides and credit limit overrides are highlighted. The terminal under Where is the POS counter the user last opened in the POS Register during that log-in session. It therefore also appears on entries the user made on other pages afterwards, as on the Banking prints in the screenshot. Export downloads the filtered entries (up to 50,000) as a CSV file for a spreadsheet; it needs Print/Export and is itself recorded in the audit trail. Print prints the page. Tip To see everything one clerk did yesterday, set From and To to yesterday, choose the clerk in User and click Filter . To find every change to one invoice, type its number in Record / text .

Transaction History shows every recorded version of one transaction, oldest first: who created it, each edit with the fields that changed, prints, voids and deletions, with the reasons and approvals. It works even for a transaction that was deleted, because the audit trail kept a copy. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Transaction History. You can also click History on a transaction form, the clock icon beside a transaction in the Audit Trail, or a number in the Voided and Deleted Transactions Summary . Type the document number, for example INV-00012, in the box. Click Find . The program opens the history of the latest transaction whose name contains what you typed, so type the whole number. The heading shows the transaction and its present status (such as Partial , Paid or Void ), or deleted . Open current version at the top opens the transaction itself. Each entry is a card with: the action and, for saves, the version number ("Create, version 1"), the user and their roles, the date and time and the IP address; the Reason and Approved by , when there are any; a Field / Before / After table of what changed; Content after this action (or Content before this action for a void or delete), which opens the full header and lines as they were. A card for a void or a deletion has a red border. Good to know Someone who may not open the transaction's own page, and may not open the Audit Trail either, is refused the history of that transaction.

This report lists every transaction voided or deleted in the period, with who did it, why and who approved. Voids and deletions are a common way to hide errors or theft, so review them regularly. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Voided and Deleted Transactions Summary, or Home > Report Center. The filters are Dates (the date of the void or deletion; the report opens on This month ), User and Module . Column What it shows Voided / deleted When the transaction was voided or deleted. Action Voided or Deleted . Type and Num The kind of transaction and its number. Click the number for its Transaction History . Txn date The transaction's own date. Name The customer, vendor or payee. Original amount The transaction's total before it was voided or deleted. User Who voided or deleted it. Reason The reason typed. Approved by The supervisor who approved, if any. The last line gives the number of transactions and the total of the original amounts. Example In September 2026 the demo shows check 1010 to Office Snacks Co. (₱2,500.00) voided because it was "printed with wrong payee", estimate EST-00002 for Cebu Tech Hub deleted as a "Duplicate of an existing quotation", and POS sale POS-000004 (₱10,068.80) voided by the supervisor.

The same transactions as the summary, with the full content of each as it was just before it was voided or deleted: its date, name, memo and total, every line, and the documents it had been applied to. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Voided and Deleted Transactions Detail, or Home > Report Center. The filters are the same as the summary: Dates , User and Module . Each transaction starts with a shaded line that gives VOIDED or DELETED, the type and number, when and by whom, the approver if any, and the reason (for example VOIDED Check 1010 by admin, reason: Check printed with wrong payee). It is followed by a line with the date, name, memo and total, then its lines with Transaction / item (item code or account), Description , Qty , Rate and Amount . "Was applied to" lines show payments or credits it had been applied to. The rows cannot be sorted.

User Activity counts what each user did in the period, by module and action, and flags work done outside business hours. Use it to spot unusual activity, such as voids late at night or a clerk working in a module outside their job. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > User Activity, or Home > Report Center. The Activity button on a user's page opens it for that user. The filters are Dates (the report opens on This week ), User and Module . Column What it shows User / module A shaded line per user with the number of log-ins in the period, then one line per module. Action The action, such as Create, Print, Void or Closing Date Change. Count How many times. Click it to open the Audit Trail filtered to those entries. First and Last The first and last time in the period. Outside business hours How many of them happened outside business hours. Business hours are taken as 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Monday to Saturday. Lines with activity outside these hours are highlighted. A Total line closes each user.

Login History lists log-ins, log-outs, timeouts, failed log-ins, locked and unlocked accounts, password resets and denied pages. Check it for repeated failed log-ins, which can mean someone is guessing a password. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Login History, or Home > Report Center. The filters are Dates (the report opens on This week ) and User . The user filter finds both what the user did and what was done to their account, such as an unlock. Column What it shows Date / time When it happened, newest first. User The username. Event Login, Logout, Session Timeout, Login Failed, Account Locked, Account Unlocked, Password Change, Password Reset, Access Denied, Approval Failed and so on. Detail The reason, such as "Wrong password (attempt 2 of 5)", or the page and action for a denied page, such as "User Role Configuration (open)". IP address The computer's address. Workstation The browser and system used. The note above the table counts the failed log-ins and denied page access attempts in the period. Failed log-ins, locks, denied pages and failed approvals are highlighted. The report shows up to 5,000 events.

This report is made for periodic access reviews. The first part shows each user's current access; the second lists every change to users, roles, page access and security settings in the period. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > User Access and Permission Changes, or Home > Report Center. The only filter is Dates (the report opens on This month ); it applies to the second part. Current access by user has one line per user: Column What it shows User / when Full name and username. Status / change active, inactive or locked. Roles / record The user's roles. Pages allowed / details Pages the user may open out of all pages (for example 31 / 168). Click it for Effective Access . Overrides Number of page overrides. Last login / reason Last successful log-in. Active users who have not logged in for 90 days are highlighted: confirm that departing employees were deactivated. A user who has never logged in is not highlighted, so look at blank Last login / reason cells as well. Changes to users, roles and page access lists, in order, each user created or edited, deactivated or activated, role created, edited or deleted, page access change and override, segregation of duties override, password reset, account lock and unlock, settings change and closing date change. Each line shows when and by whom, the change, the record, the details (old → new, up to six fields) and the reason. Tip Run this report every quarter, print it, and have the owner or the auditor sign it after checking that each person's access still fits their job.

A few facts explain almost everything on the Company pages: Each company has its own database. A database is the store where the program keeps its records. Every company on the platform has a separate one: its customers, suppliers, items, transactions, reports, users, audit trail, logo, uploaded receipts and backups are in it and nowhere else. When you log in, the program opens your company's database and no other. Nobody can see another company's records. There is no report, link, setting or search that reaches into another company. A Company Owner cannot even see another company's user list. Your company is decided on the server when you log in, from your username; nothing typed in the address bar, a form or a cookie can change it. Everybody logs in on the same page. There is no company to choose. You type your own username and password; the log-in page looks the username up, finds the company it belongs to, and checks the password, the lock-out and the approval in that company. Usernames are unique across all companies. Because the log-in page finds your company by your username, no two people on the platform can have the same one, whatever company they are in, and no company user can have a Super Admin's username. A username can therefore be refused as "already taken" even though nobody in your own company uses it: choose another. The Company Code is only for joining. Each company has a code, for example STC-B8TJC . A new employee types it once, on the join page, to say which company they belong to. It is not a password: it logs nobody in and opens nothing. After joining, the employee always logs in with their own username and password. A company can be switched off. The Super Admin can make a company inactive. Its users are logged out at their next click with the message "Your company's access is currently suspended. Please contact your Company Owner.", nobody can log in or join, and everything in the company (database, users, records) is kept until it is switched on again. The checks are repeated on every click. Each time you open a page, the program checks again that your company is still active and that your account still belongs to it.

Person What they do Super Admin Belongs to no company. Creates companies, gives each one its Company Owner, switches companies on and off, and can open any company to work inside it. Company Owner One per company. Has full access to every page of the company, approves the employees who join, manages the users and the Company Code. Administrators Users with a full-access role such as Administrator . They can use the Company pages but cannot change the Company Code, the joining rules or the owner's account. Employees Everyone else. They see the pages their roles and page access allow.

t: What makes the Company Owner different
x: Full authority. The owner can always open every page of the company and do everything on it, whatever the roles, Page Access Configuration and user overrides say. Nothing can lock the owner out of their own company. Effective Access (View as User) gives Company Owner as the reason. A protected account. Only the owner (or the Super Admin) can change the owner's account. On Employees & Users the owner's row shows Company Owner instead of a Manage button to everybody else, and on User Accounts an administrator who tries gets "Only the Company Owner can change the Company Owner's account." Cannot be deactivated. "The Company Owner cannot be deactivated. The Super Admin can make someone else the owner first." Chosen by the Super Admin. The owner of a new company is set when the Super Admin creates it (or later on the company's page); the owner of Company 1 is chosen on Multi-Company Setup . To hand the company over to someone else, ask the Super Admin. Shown in the user menu. Click your name at the top right: the first line reads Company Owner followed by your roles, for example Company Owner, Administrator .

When the Super Admin creates a new company with its owner's account, they give the owner a username and a temporary password , a password that must be replaced at the first log-in. In the examples of this chapter the company is ABC Distribution Corp. and its owner is John Doe , username johndoe . Step by step Open the log-in page of the program. Type your username (for example johndoe ) in Username and the temporary password in Password . Click Log in . The Change password page opens with the message "Please replace your temporary password before continuing." You cannot open any other page until the password is changed. In Current password , type the temporary password. In New password , type the password you will use from now on. The line under the boxes gives your company's password rules. Type the new password again in Confirm new password . Click Change password . The message "Your password has been changed." appears and the Home page opens. The password rules come from the company's settings ( System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date ). A new company starts with the rules of the company its set-up was copied from, for example "at least 8 characters, upper- and lower-case letters, a number, a symbol. Passwords expire every 90 days." The new password must also not contain your username and must differ from the temporary one. If something is wrong you see one of these messages: "Your current password is incorrect.", "The new passwords do not match.", "Choose a password different from your current one." or "The new password must have ..." followed by what is missing. After the change, the Home page of your company opens. The company name appears in the top bar beside the program name, and the sidebar has every module, including Company at the bottom.

t: What a new company already has
x: A company created by the Super Admin is not a blank database. It receives a copy of the set-up lists of another company (usually Company 1), so it can start work quickly: the company settings, with your company's own name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN (no logo and no closing date); the modules and pages of the menu, the user roles with their page access and special permissions; the document numbering, with every counter starting again from 1; the chart of accounts (with the bank account numbers left blank) and the module default accounts; the terms, tax codes, payment methods, price level names, customer types, billing groups, item categories, units of measure, and fixed asset categories with their accounts; one inventory site, Main . Nothing else is copied: no customers, suppliers, items, employees or other names, no users (you are the only user), no transactions, balances, budgets, fixed assets, POS records or audit trail. That is why every figure on the Home page is zero.

A good order for the first day: Check the company details, the logo, the password rules and the closing date in System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date . Enter the bank account numbers in the Chart of Accounts, and add or remove accounts to suit the company. Add the other inventory sites you use ( Inventory > Inventory Site List ) and the POS terminals ( Point of Sale > POS Terminals ) if you sell over the counter. Enter or import your customers, suppliers and items (see System Administration for Import from CSV ), then your opening balances. Bring in your people: hand out the Company Code (see Company Profile & Code ) or create their accounts with New user .

This page shows your company as the platform knows it, its Company Code, and the rules for employees who join with the code. Everybody who can open the page sees the code, so it can be handed out; only the Company Owner can change it. Where to find it: Company > Company Profile & Code. The Company Code button on Employees & Users opens it too. In the first picture the page belongs to Company 1, Sample Trading Company, whose owner is the System Administrator ( admin ). In the second it is seen by John Doe, owner of the new company ABC Distribution Corp.; two employees are waiting for his approval. What the page shows Part What it shows Company Code The code in large letters, and under it a line that says whether it can be used right now (see the next table). Copy code Copies the code, with its dash, so you can paste it into a message. The button reads Copied for a moment. Copy join link Copies the address of the join page with the code already filled in. An employee who opens the link only has to type their own details. Text under the code A reminder that the code only tells the system which company the employee is joining, and whether each registration waits for approval under Join Requests. A new code The owner's Regenerate code button. Joining The owner's switch Employees can join with the code , the Valid until (optional) date and Save . New employees Whether employees who join wait for approval, and the role they start with. Company Name , Address , Contact person , Phone , E-mail , TIN , Status , On the platform since and Company Owner . Users How many users are Active , Waiting , Inactive , Locked and Rejected . Click a number to open that tab of Employees & Users. The line under the code: Line Meaning Employees can join with this code. The code works. If an expiry date is set, the line ends with "until" and the date. Joining with the code is switched off. The owner turned the Employees can join with the code switch off. The code expired on ... The Valid until date has passed. The company is not active, so nobody can join. The Super Admin has switched the company off. Fields These fields are shown to the Company Owner (and to the Super Admin working inside the company). Other users see the code, the copy buttons, and one sentence under New employees saying whether employees who join wait for approval. Field What to enter / what it means Employees can join with the code On: new employees can use the code. Off: the code is refused on the join page until you switch it on again. The code itself stays the same. Valid until (optional) The last day the code can be used. It works until the end of that day. Leave it empty for no limit. The date cannot be in the past. Every employee who joins waits for approval (recommended) Ticked: a new account cannot log in until you approve it under Join Requests. Not ticked: employees can log in as soon as they have joined. Role to start with A role from your company's list (full-access roles are not offered). With approval, it is ticked for you when you approve someone; with the blank choice, Chosen when approving , you pick the role each time. Without approval, every employee who joins gets this role straight away, so a role is required. Step by step To hand out the code: Open Company > Company Profile & Code . Click Copy code and paste the code into a message to the new employee, or click Copy join link and send the link instead. Tell the employee to open the log-in page, click Join your company with its Company Code , and fill in the form (see "Joining your company with the Company Code" later in this chapter). To make a new code (for example when the code was shared with the wrong people): Click Regenerate code . Confirm the question "Make a new Company Code? The current code stops working immediately." The message "The new Company Code is ... The old one stopped working just now." shows the new code. Hand it out to the employees who still have to join. Employees who already joined keep their accounts and keep logging in as before: they never use the code again. To stop joining for a while, or to set an expiry date: Under Joining , turn Employees can join with the code off, or leave it on and pick a date in Valid until (optional) . Click Save . The message reads "Joining with the Company Code is switched off." or "Employees can join with the Company Code." To allow joining again, turn the switch back on (and clear or change the date), then click Save . To change whether new employees need approval, and the role they start with: Under New employees , tick or clear Every employee who joins waits for approval (recommended) . Choose a Role to start with , or leave Chosen when approving . Click Save . The message is "Joining rules saved." To change the company's name, address, phone, e-mail or TIN, click Edit company details at the top of the page. It opens System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date , and the platform's record of your company follows what you save there. The Contact person is kept by the Super Admin on the platform. Buttons Employees & Users : opens the list of the company's users. Edit company details : opens System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date . It appears only for users who can open that page. Good to know Only the Company Owner, and the Super Admin working inside the company, can regenerate the code, switch joining on or off, set the expiry date and change the approval rule. Administrators see the line "Only the Company Owner can make a new code or switch joining off." If someone else tries anyway, the answer is "Only the Company Owner can change the Company Code and the joining rules." The code's format. The code is made of the initials of the company name (up to three letters; words such as The, And, Of, Inc, Corp, Co, Ltd and LLC are skipped), a dash, and five random characters. The random part never uses characters that are easy to confuse (0 and O, 1, I and L). "Sample Trading Company" gives codes like STC-B8TJC ; "ABC Distribution Corp." gives codes like AD-UW92E . Every code is unique on the platform, and a code that was replaced is never given out again. Typing the code. It can be typed with or without the dash, with spaces, in capitals or in small letters: AD-UW92E , aduw92e and AD UW92E are the same code. One message for every unusable code. A mistyped code, an old code, a code whose joining is switched off, an expired code and the code of an inactive company all get the same answer on the join page: "Invalid or inactive Company Code. Please verify the code with your Company Owner." This is on purpose: nobody can learn which companies exist by trying codes. Too many wrong codes. After 10 wrong codes from the same computer (the Super Admin can change the number) within 15 minutes, the join page refuses that computer for 15 minutes with "Too many attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again." A full-access role is never given without approval. If you clear the approval box, the starting role must be an ordinary role. The messages are "Without approval, new employees need a role to start with: choose one." and "A full-access role cannot be given to employees who join without approval." Every change on this page is written to your company's audit trail (actions Company Code Changed and Company Join Rules ) and to the Super Admin's platform audit log.

This is the Company Owner's list of everybody who has an account in the company, with what each person can do and how the account was made. From here you approve or reject the employees who joined, change roles, reset passwords, unlock, deactivate and activate accounts. Where to find it: Company > Employees & Users. The Employees & Users button on Company Profile & Code, and the numbers under Users there, open it too. The first picture shows the nine users of Sample Trading Company. The second shows ABC Distribution Corp. seen by its owner: John Doe himself and two employees, Maria Reyes ( mreyes ) and Paolo Cruz ( pcruz ), who joined with the Company Code and are waiting for approval. When employees are waiting and you are not on the Join requests tab, a blue notice at the top says, for example, "2 employees are waiting for approval." with a Review the join requests link. The tabs and filters Tab or filter What it does All users Every user of the company. The number beside each tab is how many users it holds. Join requests Employees who joined with the Company Code and wait for approval. Active Approved accounts that can log in. Inactive Approved accounts that were deactivated. Locked Accounts locked after too many wrong passwords. Rejected Registrations that were rejected. Search Type part of a name, username, e-mail address or employee number and click Search . Role Shows only the users who have that role. The list changes as soon as you pick one. Waiting employees are always listed first; the others follow in order of name. The columns Column What it means Employee Full name. Under it: Company Owner for the owner, and No. with the employee number when there is one. Username The name the person logs in with, and their e-mail address under it. Roles The person's roles. None yet for an employee waiting for approval. Status Active , Inactive , Locked , Waiting for approval or Rejected (with the reason under it). For employees who joined with the code, it also shows who approved them ( Approved by ) or rejected them ( By ). Account made How the account came to be, and the date. Last log-in The date and time of the last log-in, or Never . Actions Approve and Reject for waiting employees, Approve for rejected ones, Manage for everybody else (see below). The Account made column reads: Created by an administrator : made on User Accounts (this includes every user who was there before the company joined the platform); Joined with the Company Code : the employee made the account on the join page; Created with the company : the owner's account, made by the Super Admin together with the company; Created by the Super Admin : an account the Super Admin made later, for example a new owner. The Manage menu Click Manage on a user's row to see what you can do with the account: Change roles : tick the roles the person should have. Reset password : give the person a temporary password. Unlock : shown only for a locked account. Activate : shown only for an inactive account. Deactivate : shown for active and locked accounts, except your own and the Company Owner's. All details, sites and POS terminals : opens the person's page on User Accounts , for the e-mail, employee number, sites, POS terminals and every other detail. It appears only if you may edit on User Accounts. For a user of another company working here ("User of ..." under Account made ), Reset password is not offered (their password is kept at their own company), and Deactivate and Activate read Remove access to this company and Give access back . Add user from another company at the top gives such access; see A user who works in two companies . A user of this company who also works elsewhere shows "Also works in" and the other company under their name. Step by step To change someone's roles: Click Manage on the person's row, then Change roles . In the Roles of ... window, tick the roles to give and clear the ones to take away. Full-access roles are marked (full access) . Click Save roles . The message lists the roles now held, for example "Roles of Ben Garcia saved: A/R Clerk." To reset a password (for someone who forgot theirs): Click Manage , then Reset password . Type a Temporary password that follows the company's password rules. Click Set temporary password . The message reads "Temporary password set. ... must change it at the next log-in." Give the temporary password to the person. At their next log-in they must replace it on the Change password page. A locked account is unlocked by the reset. To unlock an account: Open the Locked tab (or find the person on All users ). Click Manage , then Unlock . The message reads "... was unlocked." The person can log in again with their own password. To deactivate an account (for someone who has left): Click Manage , then Deactivate . Type a Reason (kept in the audit trail) if you wish. Click Deactivate . The message reads "... was deactivated and can no longer log in. Their name stays on everything they entered." If the person is working at that moment, they are sent to the log-in page at their next click. To activate an account again: Open the Inactive tab. Click Manage , then Activate . The message reads "... was activated and can log in again." To add a user yourself, without the Company Code: Click New user . The new-user form of User Accounts opens. Fill it in as described there. The username must be free on the whole platform. Approving and rejecting employees who joined with the code is described under Join Requests . Buttons New user : opens the new-user form on User Accounts . It appears only if you may create on that page. Roles : opens User Role Configuration , where the roles and what they may do are set. Company Code : opens Company Profile & Code . Good to know Users are never deleted , so their names stay on every record and audit entry they made. Deactivate a person who has left instead. The owner's row can only be changed by the owner (and the Super Admin). Other users see Company Owner in its Actions column instead of Manage . The owner's own Manage menu has no Deactivate . The Super Admin's account is never listed. When the Super Admin works inside your company, they use an account of their own that nobody can log into; it does not appear here or on User Accounts, but everything it does is in your audit trail. Permissions. Opening the page, like every page, is controlled by Page Access Configuration ; on a new installation it follows the access of User Accounts. Change roles , Reset password , Unlock , Activate and Deactivate need the edit permission on the page; Approve and Reject need the approve permission. The Company Owner and full-access roles have both. Messages you may see: "Keep at least one role." (a user must keep a role), "You cannot remove the Administrator role from your own account." (an administrator other than the owner), "You cannot deactivate your own account.", "The Company Owner cannot be deactivated. The Super Admin can make someone else the owner first.", "Approve the registration first." (activating or unlocking an account that was never approved), "That user cannot be changed here." (the owner's account, for anyone but the owner). Temporary passwords must follow the company's password rules and may not contain the username; otherwise the message says what is missing, for example "The temporary password must have at least 8 characters, a symbol." Every change is written to the company's audit trail with the old and new values (roles, status, approval) and the reason when one was typed.

t: Joining your company with the Company Code
x: New employees can make their own account instead of waiting for an administrator to create one. All they need is the Company Code from their Company Owner. This section is written for the employee. Where to find it: on the log-in page, under the Log in button: New employee? Join your company with its Company Code . A join link sent by the owner opens the same page with the code already filled in. Fields Field What to enter Full name Your name as it should appear on the records you enter. Required. E-mail Your e-mail address. Required. Employee no. (if any) Your employee number, if your company uses them. Username The name you will log in with: 3 to 50 characters, letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore. It is saved in small letters. It must not be used by anybody on the platform. Password Your own password. It must follow your company's password rules and must not contain your username. Confirm password The same password again. Company Code The code your Company Owner gave you, for example AD-UW92E . The dash, spaces and capitals do not matter. It is not your password. Step by step Open the log-in page and click Join your company with its Company Code . Fill in Full name , E-mail and, if you have one, Employee no. Choose a Username , and type your Password twice. Type the Company Code . Click Create my account . The page then confirms which company the account was made in, for example "Your account for ABC Distribution Corp. was created". If your company wants to approve new employees, it adds "Your Company Owner has to approve it before you can log in. Once it is approved, log in with the username mreyes and the password you chose." If it does not, it says you can log in now. Click Go to log in to return to the log-in page. While you wait for approval If you try to log in before the owner has approved your account, and your password is right, the log-in page answers "Your registration is waiting for approval by your Company Owner. You can log in once it is approved." Wait until the owner tells you the account is approved, then log in with your username and the password you chose. You are not asked to change the password: it is already your own. If the owner rejected the registration, the answer is "Your registration was not approved. Please contact your Company Owner." With a wrong password you only see "Invalid username or password.", so nobody else can find out whether an account is waiting. Messages on the join page Message What to do Invalid or inactive Company Code. Please verify the code with your Company Owner. The code is wrong, old, switched off or expired, or the company is inactive. Ask the owner for the current code. That username is already taken. Please choose another. Somebody on the platform, in any company, has that username. Choose another. Your password must have ... Make the password longer or add what is listed (capital and small letters, a number, a symbol), and leave the username out of it. The two passwords do not match. Type the same password in both boxes. Enter your full name. / Enter a valid e-mail address. Fill in the box named. Choose a username of 3 to 50 characters: letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore. Remove spaces and other characters from the username. Too many attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again. Too many wrong codes were typed from this computer. Wait, then try with the right code. You are logged in already. Joining is for new employees who do not have an account yet. Someone is logged in on this browser. Log out first, or use your existing account. Note The account is made in your company's database only. Joining does not give you any access by itself: the owner decides your role when approving you (or the company's starting role is given when approval is switched off).

Join Requests lists the employees who made an account with the Company Code and wait for the Company Owner's approval. Approving lets the person log in with the role you choose; rejecting keeps them out, with a reason. Where to find it: Company > Join Requests. When employees are waiting, the menu shows how many, for example Join Requests (2) . The Join requests tab of Employees & Users, and the Review the join requests link in its blue notice, show the same list. The page has the same tabs, filters, columns and buttons as Employees & Users ; it simply opens on the Join requests tab. Clicking another tab takes you to Employees & Users. The employees who wait are also listed at the top of All users , above everybody else: Before approving, check that you know the person: the full name, username, e-mail address and employee number in the row are what they typed on the join page. Step by step To approve an employee: Click Approve on the employee's row. In the Approve ... window, tick the role or roles the person should have. If the company has a Role to start with , it is already ticked. Full-access roles are marked (full access) ; give them only to people who should see and change everything. Click Approve . The message reads, for example, "Maria Reyes is approved and can log in now." Tell the employee they can log in. If they must work only at certain sites or POS terminals, set these afterwards with Manage > All details, sites and POS terminals (see User Accounts ). To reject a registration: Click Reject on the employee's row. Type the reason in Reason (kept in the audit trail) . A reason is required. Click Reject . The message reads "The registration of ... was rejected. They cannot log in." The person moves to the Rejected tab, with the reason under the status. To approve a registration that was rejected earlier: Open the Rejected tab of Employees & Users. Click Approve on the row and continue as above. (A rejected registration cannot be rejected a second time.) What it records Approving sets the account to Active , gives it the roles you ticked, and records you as the approver (shown as Approved by in the Status column). The audit trail gets a User Approved entry with the roles given. Rejecting sets the account to Rejected and inactive, keeps the reason, and records who rejected it (shown as By ). The audit trail gets a User Rejected entry with the reason. The employee's own joining is in the audit trail too, as User Registered under the employee's username. Each of these is also written to the Super Admin's platform audit log. Good to know A role is required. Approving without a role gives "Give ... at least one role before approving." Approve and Reject need the approve permission on the page. The Company Owner and full-access roles have it. Users without it see the list but no buttons. Approval can be switched off on Company Profile & Code . Employees who join then become active at once with the starting role, and this list stays empty. Nothing is deleted. A rejected registration stays on the Rejected tab; the username stays taken. The Super Admin sees the number of employees waiting in each company, but the approval belongs to the company.

t: Logging in when there are several companies
x: Everybody, owners and employees alike, logs in on the same page with their own username and password; the page subtitle reads Log in to your company . Besides the usual messages about wrong passwords and locked accounts (see Getting Started ), you may meet these: Message Meaning Your registration is waiting for approval by your Company Owner. You can log in once it is approved. You joined with the code and the owner has not approved you yet. Your registration was not approved. Please contact your Company Owner. The owner rejected your registration. Your company's access is currently suspended. Please contact your Company Owner. The Super Admin has switched your company off. Your records are kept. Your account is no longer linked to this company. Please log in again. Your account was changed while you were working. Log in again; if it keeps happening, ask your Company Owner. Your account needs to be checked by your Company Owner before you can log in. The platform's record of your username did not match your account; the program corrects it. Try again. If the message comes back, the owner asks the Super Admin to rebuild the company's user list. Too many failed log-in attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again. Many log-ins with unknown usernames were tried from this computer. Wait 15 minutes. Tip If you forget your password, ask your Company Owner (or an administrator) to reset it on Employees & Users . The Company Code cannot be used to log in.

A user who was given access to another company (see A user who works in two companies ) logs in at their own company as always. The company name at the top of the screen then becomes a switch. Click the company name at the top (on a phone, the building button beside the program name). The list Your companies shows your own company ("Your own company") and each company that gave you access ("Access given to you"). The one open now is ticked. Click the company to work in. Its Home page opens with "You are now working in ...". No password is asked. While you work in the other company, a blue strip under the top bar says so: "You are working in ABC Distribution Corp. with access given to you. Your own company is Sample Trading Company." Click Back to Sample Trading Company on the strip, or use the switch again, to go back. In the other company you see its menus, records and reports, and you can do only what its roles for you allow. You are not a Super Admin and have no rights over the platform or other companies. Your password belongs to your own company: Change password is offered there, not in the other company. Each switch is recorded in the audit trail of the company you open. When the other company removes your access, or your own account is deactivated, the switch disappears; if you were working in the other company you are taken back to your own. Message Meaning Your access to ... has ended. You are back in your own company. The other company (or yours) removed the access while you were working there. You have no access to that company. The access was removed, or the company is not open. Your access to ... is switched off there. Please ask its administrator. The other company switched your account off. The database of ... needs the latest update first. Please ask the platform administrator (Super Admin). The other company's database is waiting for an update.

Read this once before you create the first company. It explains the words used on every platform page. One database per company. A database is the store where the program keeps its records. Each company has a database of its own, holding all of its customers, suppliers, items, transactions, users and audit trail. The database the program was installed with is Company 1 ; every company you add gets a new database, made and named by the program (in the pictures, gsmart_company_002 for the second company). Nobody ever types a database name. The platform database. One more database, the platform database (in the pictures gsmart_master ), holds the list of companies, which database each one uses, the Company Codes, which company every username belongs to, the Super Admin accounts and the platform audit log. It holds no accounting records. Nobody can see another company's records. A company user only ever works in their own company's database. The company is decided on the server when they log in, from the platform database, and is checked again on every click. Nothing in the address bar, a form or a cookie can move a session to another company. Each company's logo, pictures, receipts and backups are also kept in a folder of its own. The Super Admin belongs to no company. Your account lives in the platform database only. The platform pages never open a company's records. To work inside a company, you Open it: you then work through an account of your own in that company, and everything you do there is written in that company's audit trail. One log-in page, unique usernames. Company users, Company Owners and Super Admins all log in on the same page. The page finds where a username belongs, so a username can exist only once on the whole platform, across every company and the Super Admins. The Company Code is only for joining. Each company has a code, for example AD-UW92E , that its new employees type once on the join page. It says which company they are joining; it is not a password and opens nothing. See Company Profile & Code . The Company Owner. Each company has one owner, chosen by you. The owner has full authority inside the company, approves the employees who join, and manages its users and its Company Code. Inactive companies. A company you switch off keeps its database, users and records, but its users are logged out at their next click, nobody can log in to it or join it, and its scheduled report e-mails stop. You can still open it, and switch it on again at any time.

Several companies are switched on once, by an administrator of the existing company, on Multi-Company Setup (System Administration). That page: creates the platform database; registers the existing database as Company 1 , without moving, changing or deleting any record in it; lists every existing user on the platform, so all of them keep logging in with the same username and password; gives Company 1 its Company Code and the Company Owner chosen from its users; creates the first Super Admin with the username and password typed on that page. There is no default Super Admin password. After the set-up, Multi-Company Setup leaves the menu, and the Super Admin logs in as described below.

t: Logging in as the Super Admin
x: The Super Admin logs in on the ordinary log-in page, which reads Log in to your company once several companies are running. Open the log-in page of the program. Type your Super Admin username (for example superadmin ) in Username and your password in Password . Click Log in . The Companies page of the platform opens. If your password is a temporary one, My account opens first and asks you to replace it. The platform pages have a sidebar of their own, in two groups: Companies : Companies , New company , Database updates ; Platform : Super Admins , Platform settings , Platform audit log , My account . The top bar reads Platform administration . The button at the top right shows your full name; it opens a menu with Change password and Log out . Good to know A wrong password gives "Invalid username or password." with the number of attempts left. After 5 wrong passwords in a row (see Platform settings ) the account locks: "Too many failed attempts. The account is now locked." A locked account answers "This account is locked. Another Super Admin can unlock it (or run tools/platform.php)." and an inactive one "This account is inactive." See "When something goes wrong" at the end of this chapter. Your session ends after 30 minutes without activity (see Platform settings ): "You were logged out after a period of inactivity." Working inside a company keeps it alive. After 30 failed log-ins with unknown usernames (or wrong Super Admin passwords) from one computer within 15 minutes, that computer is stopped for 15 minutes: "Too many failed log-in attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again." Every log-in, failed log-in and log-out of a Super Admin is in the Platform audit log .

The list of every company on the platform, with its Company Code, owner, status, number of users and database. It is the page you see after logging in and the place where you Open a company to work inside it. Where to find it: Companies > Companies. It opens after you log in, and the program name at the top left leads back to it. Right after multi-company is switched on, the list has one company (Sample Builders & Development Corp. in the sample data), whose owner is the System Administrator ( admin ): With a second company, ABC Distribution Corp., created: The figures at the top Figure What it counts Active companies Companies that are switched on. The line under it gives the number of companies in all. Inactive Companies that are switched off. Their users cannot log in. Company users Every user account listed on the platform, across every company, including those waiting for approval. Waiting for approval Employees who joined with a Company Code and wait for their Company Owner. Each owner approves their own. When a company's set-up failed or is still running, a yellow notice says so, for example "1 company set-up failed. Open the company to see the steps and set it up again." The columns Column What it means # The company's number on the platform. Company 1 is the original database. Company The name (click it to open the company's details page), and under it the contact person and e-mail. Company Code The current code. joining off under it means the code is switched off. Company Owner The owner's full name and username, or Not assigned . Status Active , Inactive , Being set up or Set-up failed . Users How many accounts the company has, and how many are waiting (for example 2 waiting ). Database The company's database, and under it original database for Company 1 or since and the date it was created. Last column Open for an active or inactive company; Details for a company that is being set up or whose set-up failed. Buttons New company : opens New company . Database updates : opens Database updates . Open : works inside the company as the Super Admin (see "Working inside a company" below).

Creates a company with a database of its own, copies the set-up lists of an existing company into it, and (if you wish) creates the owner's account, all in one step. Where to find it: Companies > New company, or the New company button on the Companies page. Fields The Company box: Field What to enter / what it means Company name The company's name, as it will appear on its reports and vouchers. Required. Two companies cannot have the same name. TIN The company's Tax Identification Number. Address The company's address. Contact person The person to contact about the company. Shown on the platform and on the company's profile. Phone The company's phone number. E-mail The company's e-mail address. Notes (platform only) Your own notes. Only Super Admins see them. Copy the set-up of The company whose set-up lists are copied (the active companies are listed; Company 1 is chosen at first). Employees who join wait for the owner's approval Ticked: employees who join with the Company Code wait for the owner's approval. The starting value comes from Platform settings . The Company Owner box: Field What to enter / what it means Create the owner's account now (otherwise assign one later) Ticked: the owner's account is made with the company. Cleared: the fields below are hidden and you assign an owner later on the company's page. Full name The owner's full name. Required when the box is ticked. E-mail The owner's e-mail address. Optional. Username The owner's log-in name: 3 to 50 characters, letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore, saved in small letters. It must be free across every company and the Super Admins. Temporary password A password the owner will replace at the first log-in. It must follow the password rules of the company whose set-up is copied, and must not contain the username. Password again The same temporary password. The What is set up box on the right lists the steps, the set-up lists that are copied and what is never copied. It is a summary of what happens when you press Create company ; you do not fill anything in there. Step by step Click New company . Type the Company name and the other details of the company. Check Copy the set-up of . Choose the company whose chart of accounts, tax codes, roles and other lists are closest to what the new company needs. Tick or clear Employees who join wait for the owner's approval . Leave Create the owner's account now ticked and fill in the owner's Full name , E-mail , Username , Temporary password and Password again ; or clear it to assign the owner later. Click Create company and confirm the question "Create the company and its database now?". It takes a few moments. The company's page opens with the result. Give the owner their username and temporary password, and tell them to change the password at the first log-in. What happens when you press Create company The company gets a Company Code, unique on the platform (for ABC Distribution Corp., AD-UW92E ). A database name is chosen: the prefix from Platform settings followed by the company number in three digits, for example gsmart_company_002 . A database that already exists on the server is never used or touched: the program adds a letter instead ( gsmart_company_002_b , _c ...). The database is created, with the same character set as the copied company's. Every table is created exactly as the copied company has it today, with all its columns, keys, indexes and links between tables, and every counter starting from 1. The set-up lists are copied: the company settings (with the new company's name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN; no logo and no closing date), the modules, the pages, the roles with their page access and special permissions (every role allowed on every site), the document numbering (starting again from 1), the chart of accounts (bank account numbers left blank, no balances), the module default accounts, terms, tax codes, payment methods, price level names, customer types, billing groups, item categories, units of measure, and fixed asset categories with their accounts. One inventory site, Main , is added. The audit trail protection is put in place: database triggers that stop anybody from changing or deleting audit trail entries, even directly in the database. The owner's account is created with the company's full-access role ( Administrator ), and must change the temporary password at the first log-in. The new database is checked: every table is there, its structure matches the program, and no customer, supplier, item or transaction is in it. The company, its database and its users are registered on the platform, its file folder is made ( storage/companies/c002/ for company 2), and the first line of its audit trail is written. Only then is the company switched on. Nothing else is copied: no customers, suppliers, items, employees or other names, no users, transactions, sales, payments, bills, journals, balances, budgets, fixed assets, POS records, audit trail or other history. When everything worked, the message reads, for example, "ABC Distribution Corp. is set up with a database of its own. Company Code: AD-UW92E. The owner logs in as johndoe and must change the temporary password." The company's page shows each step with a green tick under Set-up steps : Good to know If a step fails , the company is marked Set-up failed , the database that attempt made is removed again, and nobody can log in to the company or join it. The message reads "The set-up of ... did not finish:" followed by the step and the reason, and "Nothing half-made was left behind." The company's page shows where it stopped and lets you set it up again or delete the failed record (see Company Details ). Bring the copied company up to date first. If the company whose set-up is copied still needs a program update (see Database updates ), the check in step 8 fails with "The new database does not match the program: ... (bring the template company up to date first)." Audit trail protection. On some servers the triggers cannot be created. The set-up then carries on (the company works), the Triggers step shows a red cross with the reason, and the company's page shows Missing beside Audit trail protection , with a button to try again. Messages before anything is created: "Enter the company name.", "There is already a company named ...", "The company e-mail address does not look right.", "Choose the company whose set-up is copied.", "The two owner passwords do not match.", "The owner's username: 3 to 50 characters, letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore.", "The username ... is already taken on this platform.", "Enter the owner's full name.", "The owner's e-mail address does not look right." and "The owner's temporary password must have ..." followed by what is missing. Nothing is created until all of these are right. The database user needs rights. The program creates the database with the MySQL user in config/config.php , which needs the right to create and drop databases and to create tables, keys and triggers in them. XAMPP's root user has them. On shared hosting, set the Name of new company databases: prefix in Platform settings to the prefix the host requires (for example cpuser_company_ ). The MySQL user must still be allowed to create databases with that prefix, because the program never uses a database that already exists. What the new owner sees at the first log-in, and what to do first in a new company, is in Your Company: Company Owner and Employees .

Everything about one company on a single page: its details, owner, users, Company Code, joining rules, database, status, set-up steps and recent activity. From here you change the owner, regenerate the code, switch the company off or on, and repair a failed set-up. Where to find it: Companies > Companies, then click the company's name (or Details for a company whose set-up did not finish). The page opens by itself after Create company . The page's title is the company's name; under it are the status and "Company #1, created ..." (with "set-up copied from ..." for a company made on the platform). The parts of the page Part What it holds Company information Company name , TIN , Address , Contact person , Phone , E-mail , Notes (platform only) and Save . Company Owner The current owner with e-mail and last log-in (or "This company has no Company Owner yet."), and the form to set a new owner. Users Every user of the company with Name , Username , Roles , Status , Account made and Last log-in , and the Sync user list button. Company Code The code, whether joining is on, Regenerate , the switch Employees can join with the code with a date, and New employees wait for the owner's approval with a starting role. Database Database , Origin , Tables , Checked , Program updates , Audit trail protection and Files . Deactivate or Activate Switches the company off (with a reason) or on. Set-up steps Each attempt at setting the company up, step by step, with a tick or a cross and the details. Recent platform activity The last 25 entries of the platform audit log for this company. The Database box, line by line: Line What it means Database The name of the company's database. Origin The original database (Company 1) or Created by the platform . Tables and Checked How many tables the database had when it was last checked, and when. Program updates Up to date , or how many updates still have to be run (see Database updates ). Audit trail protection In place , or Missing in red with a Put the protection back button. Files The company's own folder for its logo, pictures, receipts and backups: storage/ (the original folders) for Company 1, storage/companies/c002/ for company 2, and so on. Step by step To change the company's details: Change the fields under Company information . Click Save . The message is "Company details saved." The name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN are also written to the company's own settings, so they appear on its reports and vouchers; the change is recorded in the company's audit trail. To make one of the company's users the Company Owner: Under Company Owner , leave One of its users chosen. Pick the person in the list. Only active, approved users are listed. Click Set owner and confirm "Make this person the Company Owner?". The message is "Company Owner saved." The new owner has full authority in the company from their next click, whatever their roles. The previous owner stays a user with the roles they had. To give the company an owner with a new account: Under Company Owner , choose A new account . Fill in Username , Full name , E-mail and Temporary password . The same rules apply as on New company . Click Set owner and confirm. The message is "Company Owner saved. They must change the temporary password at the first log-in." The account gets the company's full-access role. To give the company a new Company Code: Under Company Code , click Regenerate . Confirm "Make a new code? The current one stops working at once; people who already joined stay." The message gives the new code: "New Company Code: ... The old one no longer works." Send it to the Company Owner. To stop joining, or to set the last day the code can be used: Turn Employees can join with the code off, or pick a date in the date box beside Save . Click Save . The message is "Company Code saved." The date counts to the end of that day. To change whether new employees need approval, and the role they start with: Tick or clear New employees wait for the owner's approval . Pick a role in the list, or leave Role chosen when approving . Full-access roles are not offered. Click Save . The message is "Joining rules saved." Without approval a role is required: "Without approval, new employees need a role to start with." To switch a company off: Under Deactivate , type the Reason . It is required. Click Deactivate and confirm. The message reads "... is deactivated. Its users cannot log in and nobody can join it; all of its data is kept." Users who are working at that moment are logged out at their next click with "Your company's access is currently suspended. Please contact your Company Owner." You can still open the company. To switch it on again: Under Activate , type a reason if you wish. Click Activate . The message reads "... is active again. Its users can log in." The users log in with their accounts as they were. A company whose database still needs updates cannot be switched on: "Bring the company database up to date first (Database updates)." To rebuild the platform's list of the company's usernames: Click Sync user list above the Users table. The message says how many users are listed on the platform, for example "9 user(s) listed on the platform." Use it when a user of the company cannot log in although their account is there, or after the company database was restored outside the program. If a username is also used in another company, the message names it: "These usernames belong to another company and cannot log in until they are renamed: ..." Rename that user on the company's User Accounts page and sync again. To put the audit trail protection back (when it shows Missing ): Click Put the protection back in the Database box. The message is "The audit trail protection is in place.", or "The triggers could not be created:" with the reason given by the database server. A company whose set-up did not finish A company that is Set-up failed (or still Being set up after 15 minutes) shows a red box at the top: "The set-up did not finish" (or "has not finished"), with the step and the reason, and "The company is not active, nobody can log in to it or join it, and any database this attempt created was removed again." To set it up again, once the cause is fixed (for example the database rights): If the company needs an owner's account, fill in Username , Full name , E-mail and Temporary password in the red box. Passwords are never kept, so they must be typed again. You can also leave them empty and assign the owner later. Click Set it up again . The steps run again as a new attempt, listed under Set-up steps . The message is "The company is set up and active." or "The set-up failed again. The steps below say where." To delete the failed record instead: Type the company's name exactly in Or delete this failed record: type the company name . Click Delete record and confirm. The message is "The failed company record was deleted." Its Company Code is retired. Good to know Active companies are never deleted. Only the record of a company whose set-up failed can be deleted; for any other company the answer is "Only a company whose set-up failed can be deleted. Deactivate an active company instead." Changes reach the company's audit trail. Changing the details or the owner, regenerating the code, and switching the company off or on are written in the company's own audit trail under the name platform: followed by your username, with the role Super Admin , as well as in the platform audit log. The company's users see it there. Two companies cannot share a name. "Another company already has that name." The Users list here is for reading. Users are approved, changed and deactivated inside the company, by its owner or by you after Open company (see Employees & Users ). If the company's database cannot be reached, a red line says so ("The company database cannot be reached: ..."). The company information and the Company Code can still be changed on the platform; the owner, the joining rules, the status and the user list wait until the database answers again. Open company at the top of the page works as Open on the Companies page. All companies goes back to the list.

To look at a company's books, fix a setting, approve an employee or help a user, you open the company and work inside it as its Super Admin. Where to find it: Open on the Companies page, or Open company on the company's details page . While you work inside a company: A yellow strip at the top reads "Super Admin: you are working inside ABC Distribution Corp.. Everything you do here is recorded in its audit trail." with a Back to the platform link. For an inactive company it adds "(inactive: its users cannot log in)". You see the company exactly as its users do: its menu, its Home page, its records. You have full authority, like the Company Owner: every page opens and every action is allowed, including the owner's actions on Company Profile & Code and Employees & Users . You work through an account of your own in that company, named @platform- followed by your Super Admin number (for example @platform-1 ) and shown as "Super Admin:" followed by your name. The program makes this account the first time you open the company. Nobody can log in with it (its password is random and never shown), and it never appears in the company's user lists. Every change you make is in the company's audit trail under that name. The menu under your name at the top right reads Super Admin, managing this company and offers Back to the platform and Log out . Step by step On Companies , click Open on the company's row. The company's Home page opens with the yellow strip. Work as you would in any company. Click Back to the platform in the strip (or in the menu under your name). You return to the Companies page. Good to know Log out in the company's menu ends your Super Admin session as well and takes you to the log-in page. Use Back to the platform to leave the company only. Opening any platform page while you are inside a company (for example with the browser's Back button) takes you out of the company first. A company whose database needs an update cannot be opened: "The database of ... needs the latest update first. Use "Update databases" on the Companies page." Run the update on Database updates and open it again. Inactive companies can be opened, for example to check something before switching them on again. Every opening and closing of a company is in the Platform audit log ( company opened , company closed ).

When a new version of the program is installed, it may bring upgrade scripts : files that add the new tables and columns the new version needs. Every company database has to receive them. This page shows which companies still need which scripts and runs them for you. Where to find it: Companies > Database updates, or the Database updates button on the Companies page. A company's details page also warns "This company's database needs ... update(s)." with a link here. The line at the top says how many upgrade scripts the program knows ( 9 in the picture). A company database is up to date when every one of them has been run on it. New companies are created up to date. The columns Column What it means Company The company (click to open its details page) and its status. Database The company's database. Updates to run The names of the scripts still to run, oldest first, or Up to date . A red message means the database could not be read. Last column Run , for a company with scripts to run. Step by step After copying the files of a new version of the program onto the server: Back up the company databases and the platform database (see "When something goes wrong" below). Log in as the Super Admin and open Database updates . Click Update all companies (shown only when something is waiting) and confirm "Run every pending update on every company database? Back the databases up first." To update one company only, click Run on its row. Read the message: "... update(s) run. Every company database is up to date.", "Every company database was already up to date.", or "Some updates could not be run." followed by the company and the reason. Good to know The scripts run oldest first. For each company, the program stops at the first script that fails and leaves the later ones for the next attempt. The scripts keep every record and can safely be run again. Until its database is updated, a company cannot be opened by the Super Admin or switched on again, and a new company copied from it fails its check. Its users see a Database update needed page after log-in instead of their work: users of the other companies are asked to contact the Super Admin, while administrators of Company 1 also see the files to run by hand. Each update run is recorded in the Platform audit log as database updated , with the names of the scripts. The server administrator can also run every pending update from the command line: php tools/platform.php update-all .

The accounts that manage the platform. A Super Admin can open and change every company, so keep this list short, and keep at least two active Super Admins so one can help the other. Where to find it: Platform > Super Admins. The columns Column What it means Name Full name, You for your own account, and the e-mail address. Username The log-in name. Status Active , Inactive or Locked . temporary password under it means the person has not yet replaced a temporary password. Last log-in Date and time of the last log-in. The buttons at the end of each row, for the other Super Admins: Unlock (for a locked account), Deactivate or Activate , and a Temporary password box with Reset . On your own row there is Change my password , which opens My account . Fields The New Super Admin box: Field What to enter Full name The person's full name. Required. Username 3 to 50 characters: letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore. Saved in small letters. It must not be used by any Super Admin or any company user. E-mail Optional. Temporary password At least 10 characters with upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a symbol, not containing the username. Step by step To add a Super Admin: Fill in the New Super Admin box. Click Create . The message reads "Super Admin ... created. They must change the temporary password at the first log-in." Give the new Super Admin their username and temporary password. At their first log-in My account opens and they cannot use any other platform page until they have chosen their own password. To reset another Super Admin's password: Type a temporary password in the Temporary password box on their row. Click Reset . The message is "Temporary password set for ..." A locked account is unlocked at the same time, and the person must change the password at the next log-in. To unlock, deactivate or activate another Super Admin, click Unlock , Deactivate (and confirm) or Activate on their row. Good to know "You cannot deactivate your own account." and "This is the last active Super Admin." protect the platform from being left without anyone to manage it. "That username is already used on the platform (by a Super Admin or a company user)." means the username is taken somewhere on the platform. Super Admin passwords follow their own rule (at least 10 characters with upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a symbol), whatever the companies' password rules are. Every change here is in the Platform audit log .

The few settings that belong to the platform as a whole rather than to one company. Where to find it: Platform > Platform settings. Fields Field What it means Name of new company databases: prefix The start of the name of each new company database; the company number follows it ( 002 , 003 ...). Letters, digits and underscores, at most 50. Left empty, the program uses the first company's database name followed by _company_ (shown in grey in the box). On shared hosting, use the prefix your control panel requires (for example cpuser_ ). New companies: employees who join wait for approval The starting value of the approval box on New company . Each company can change it afterwards on its own page. Super Admin session ends after (minutes without activity) How long a Super Admin can be idle before being logged out. At least 5. Super Admin failed log-ins before the account locks How many wrong passwords in a row lock a Super Admin account. Wrong Company Codes allowed from one address in 15 minutes How many wrong codes one computer may type on the join page. After that, the join page stops that computer for 15 minutes. Step by step Change the values you need. Click Save . The message says how many settings were changed, for example "1 setting(s) changed." Good to know The box under the settings, Platform database , names the platform database (for example gsmart_master ) and reminds you that the MySQL user of config/config.php needs the right to create and drop databases and to create tables, keys and triggers in them. It also explains the emergency switch described in "When something goes wrong" below. Changing the prefix affects only companies created afterwards; existing databases keep their names. Messages: "The database prefix may only have letters, digits and underscores (at most 50)." and "The Super Admin session needs at least 5 minutes." Every change is in the Platform audit log as platform settings , with the new values.

A permanent record of what happened on the platform and to which company: log-ins of Super Admins, companies created, opened, changed, switched off and on, codes regenerated, employees who joined, were approved or rejected, database updates and settings changes. Entries cannot be changed or deleted. Where to find it: Platform > Platform audit log. The filters Filter What it does Company One company, or All companies . The list changes as soon as you pick one. What happened One kind of entry, or Everything . Only the kinds recorded so far are listed. From and To The period. It starts as the last 30 days. Click Show after changing the dates. The columns Column What it means When Date and time. Who The username, and under it what kind of person: super admin , owner , user , guest (someone on the join page) or system (the command-line tool). Company The company concerned, when there is one. What happened The kind of entry (see below). Details What exactly was done, for example "Set-up finished: database gsmart_company_002, 70 tables". From The address of the computer it came from.
