Some of the entries you will see: What happened Meaning platform setup Multi-company was switched on and Company 1 registered. login, login failed, logout, session timeout A Super Admin logged in, failed, logged out or timed out; login failed is also written for unknown usernames on the log-in page. login refused A user of an inactive company tried to log in. company created, company activated A company record was made; its set-up finished (or it was switched on again). company setup failed, company setup retried, company deleted A set-up failed, was run again, or a failed record was deleted. company opened, company closed A Super Admin opened a company or went back to the platform. company edited, company deactivated, owner changed The company's details, status or owner were changed. company code regenerated, company code state, company join rules The Company Code or the joining rules were changed, by the owner or a Super Admin. employee joined, join refused An employee made an account with a code; someone typed a code that was refused. employee approved, employee rejected A Company Owner decided on a join request. database updated, restore Upgrade scripts were run; a company database was restored from a backup. super admin created, super admin password reset, platform settings Changes to Super Admins or to the platform settings. Good to know The page shows the latest 500 entries of the period. Narrow the period or pick a company to see older ones. What happens inside a company is also in that company's own audit trail ( System Administration > Audit Trail ), in much more detail. The platform audit log records the platform's view: who did what to which company.

Where a Super Admin changes their own password. Where to find it: Platform > My account; also Change password in the menu under your name, and Change my password on Super Admins. It opens by itself when you log in with a temporary password. The line at the top gives your full name, username and last log-in. When you have a temporary password, a yellow line asks "Please replace your temporary password before continuing." Step by step Type your Current password . Type the new password in New password and again in Confirm new password . It needs at least 10 characters with upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a symbol, must not contain your username and must differ from the current one. Click Change password . The message is "Your password has been changed." and the Companies page opens. Messages: "Your current password is incorrect.", "The new passwords do not match.", "Choose a password different from your current one." and "The new password must have ..." followed by what is missing.

A Super Admin is locked out Another active Super Admin can unlock the account or reset its password on Super Admins . If there is no other Super Admin (or all are locked out), the server administrator can give the account a new temporary password from the command line, in the program folder: php tools/platform.php reset-superadmin USERNAME "NEWPASSWORD" Replace USERNAME with the Super Admin's username and NEWPASSWORD with the temporary password to give; keep the quotes, because the password contains a symbol. The password must follow the Super Admin rule. The account is unlocked and made active, and the Super Admin must choose a new password at the next log-in. The reset is written in the platform audit log. The same tool has three more commands for the server administrator: php tools/platform.php list : lists the companies with their status, database and Company Code; php tools/platform.php sync 2 : rebuilds the platform's list of the usernames of company 2 (or the number you type), like Sync user list ; php tools/platform.php update-all : runs the pending upgrade scripts on every company database, like Update all companies . A user cannot log in although the account exists Open the company's details page and click Sync user list . If a username is used in two companies (this can happen after restoring an old backup), the message names it; rename the user in one of the companies and sync again. Backups Each company backs up and restores its own database only, on its own Backup & Restore page. The files are kept in the company's own folder, and the files of companies other than Company 1 are named after the company number ( company_002_... ), not after the database. A restore can only rebuild the company's own tables. Statements in a backup file that switch to or name another database, create databases, users, triggers, routines or views, read files or copy data with a SELECT are refused and listed. The audit trail protection is put back afterwards, and the company's list of usernames on the platform is rebuilt; a username that now clashes with another company is reported. The platform database (for example gsmart_master ) is in no company's backup. Back it up yourself, for example with phpMyAdmin > Export, at the same time as the company databases, and keep a copy off the server. Switching multi-company off in an emergency If the platform database cannot be reached, no company can be opened. In an emergency the server administrator can move the file storage/platform/multi_company.json out of its folder: the program then runs as Company 1 alone, with Company 1's users only, and the other companies cannot be reached. Put the file back (or run Multi-Company Setup again) to return to several companies. Nothing is lost either way. Before going live with several companies Keep the Super Admin password safe, and create a second Super Admin. Check on Companies that every company has a Company Owner. Back up the platform database together with the company databases, and do it before every database update. Scheduled report e-mails are sent for every active company from the same daily task; nothing extra is needed per company.

t: Appendix A. What each transaction records
x: Every transaction you save is turned into general ledger lines and, for stocked items, into inventory movements. The rules are fixed in the program: you choose the accounts (through Module Default Accounts, items, tax codes and asset categories), but you never type the posting of an invoice or a bill yourself. This appendix lists, for every kind of transaction, the accounts it debits and credits, what it does to stock and to customer or vendor balances, and the page where you enter it.

The account names are those of the standard chart of accounts of a contractor delivered with the program. Your company posts to the accounts chosen under Module Default Accounts , on each item in the Item List , on each tax code in Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists and on each asset category. Prices and amounts on sales and purchase forms are VAT-exclusive. VAT is worked out on each line and posted to the account of the line's tax code (in the demo, 2100 Output Tax on sales and 1300 Input Tax on purchases). Stocked items are items of the types Inventory part and Inventory assembly . Only they have a quantity on hand and a value. Non-inventory parts, services and other charges post to accounts only. A stocked item leaves stock at its weighted-average cost : the book value of the item divided by the quantity on hand, over all sites. A sale that brings the quantity to zero takes all the value that is left. A customer balance is what 1100 Accounts Receivable holds for that customer and its jobs. A vendor balance is what 2000 Accounts Payable holds for that vendor. Every ledger line carries the class of the transaction (see The class on a transaction, at the end of this appendix). Tip To see the entry of any saved transaction, open it. The box General ledger entries created automatically lists every line with its account, memo, class, debit and credit. On sales documents (invoices, sales receipts, statement and finance charges, credit memos, POS sales and returns) the box is shown only to users who have the special permission View costs and margins , because it shows the cost of goods sold.

The table lists every setting of Module Default Accounts , the account it points to in the demo company, and what uses it. no posting rule reads it Cash on Hand (Register) 1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers Proposed as the cash account of new POS terminals Cash Over and Short 6200 Cash Over and Short Drawer differences when a register is closed Card Clearing 1060 Card Clearing Card and other non-cash tenders whose payment method names no account E-wallet Clearing 1065 E-wallet Clearing E-wallet tenders whose method names no account Bank / Merchant Charges 6080 Bank and Merchant Charges Service charges, merchant fees on settlements Interest Income 4200 Interest Income Interest earned entered in Reconcile Retained Earnings 3200 Retained Earnings Earlier years' profit on the balance sheet Opening Balance Equity 3900 Opening Balance Equity Opening stock and opening asset balances Gain / Loss on Disposal of Assets 4300 Gain (Loss) on Disposal of Assets Asset disposals Important If a default account the transaction needs is not set, saving stops with the message The default account "..." is not set. Set it under Financial Set-up & Reports > Module Default Accounts. Nothing is saved until the account is chosen. There is no year-end closing entry to make. The balance sheet shows the net income of earlier fiscal years inside Retained Earnings, and the income statement starts again at the beginning of each fiscal year.

Transaction Entered on Number Posts to the ledger Estimate Create Estimates EST- No Sales Order Create Sales Orders SO- No Invoice Create Invoices INV- Yes, unless pending Sales Receipt Enter Sales Receipts SR- Yes, unless pending Statement Charge Enter Statement Charges SC- Yes Finance Charge Assess Finance Charges FC- Yes Customer Payment Receive Payments PMT- Yes Credit Memo Create Credit Memos/Refunds CM- Yes Customer Refund Create Credit Memos/Refunds Check series Yes Purchase Order Create Purchase Orders PO- No Item Receipt Receive Items IR- Yes Bill Enter Bills BILL- Yes Supplier Debit Memo Supplier Debit Memos DM- Yes Bill Payment Pay Bills Check series (AAP- when it applies an advance) Yes Advance to Supplier Advances to Suppliers ADV- Yes Check Write Checks Check series Yes Cash Voucher Cash Voucher CAV- Yes Deposit Make Deposits DEP- Yes Transfer Transfer Funds TRF- Yes Journal Entry Make Journal Entries JE- Yes Opening Balance Make Journal Entries JE- Yes Inventory Adjustment Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand ADJ- Yes Inventory Transfer Transfer Inventory IT- Stock only Build Assembly Build Assemblies BLD- Yes, unless pending Processing Order Disassemble / Process Items PRC- Yes, unless pending Depreciation Run Depreciation JE- Yes Asset Disposal Dispose of Assets JE- Yes POS Sale POS Register POS- Yes, unless suspended POS Return POS Receipts, Returns & Voids POS- Yes Cash Over/Short Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings JE- Yes Service Charge Reconcile JE- Yes Interest Earned Reconcile JE- Yes The names in the first column are the ones the program shows in lists, in Find and in the Type column of reports. Numbering is explained in Appendix C .

Estimate and Sales Order Entered on Create Estimates and Create Sales Orders . Ledger: nothing. The view of the document says Non-posting document: it records a commitment and does not affect the ledger. Stock: nothing moves. The quantities of an open sales order that are not yet invoiced count as on sales order in the stock status reports and the Inventory Center. Balances: no effect on the customer's balance. Status: an estimate is Pending , becomes Accepted when it is turned into a sales order or partly invoiced, and Closed when it is fully invoiced or closed with Close . A sales order is Open , then Partially filled , then Closed when every line is invoiced or closed. Invoice Entered on Create Invoices . Invoices are also made by Create Batch Invoices and by a charge sale on the POS Register . Account Debit Credit 1100 Accounts Receivable Invoice total, VAT included Income account of each item (for example 4000 Sales, 4010 Service Income) Line amount 2100 Output Tax (the tax code's account) VAT of the lines 5000 Cost of Goods Sold (the item's cost account) Average cost of stocked items 1200 Inventory (the item's asset account) Average cost of stocked items Stock: stocked items leave the Inventory site of the invoice (or the site of the line) at their average cost. The cost is stored on the line and shows in the Cost column for users who may view costs. Balances: the customer's balance goes up by the invoice total. The invoice stays open until payments or credits are applied to it. Special lines: a discount item is posted as a debit to its own income account (4060 Sales Discounts for DISC-10 and DISC-AMT); a payment item such as DOWNPMT (Down Payment Received) debits 1050 Undeposited Funds and lowers the amount charged to Accounts Receivable; billable costs added from bills and checks credit 4110 Reimbursable Expense Income; a subtotal line posts nothing; a group item is entered as the separate items it holds. Pending: an invoice saved with Pending (non-posting until marked final) ticked posts nothing (see Pending transactions, later in this appendix). Example ABC Trading Corp. is invoiced for one LAP-001 Laptop 14-inch i5 16GB at ₱39,990.00 plus 12% VAT, and the laptop's average cost is ₱32,000.00. The invoice debits 1100 Accounts Receivable ₱44,788.80, credits 4000 Sales ₱39,990.00 and 2100 Output Tax ₱4,798.80, and debits 5000 Cost of Goods Sold and credits 1200 Inventory ₱32,000.00. One laptop leaves the Main Warehouse, and ABC Trading Corp.'s balance goes up by ₱44,788.80. Sales Receipt Entered on Enter Sales Receipts . Ledger: the same as an invoice, except that the total is debited to the Deposit to account instead of Accounts Receivable. The default is 1050 Undeposited Funds; you can also choose a bank account or another current asset. Stock: stocked items leave the Inventory site at average cost. Balances: no effect on the customer's balance: the sale is paid on the spot. Later: a sales receipt deposited to 1050 Undeposited Funds waits in Make Deposits until you deposit it. Statement Charge Entered on Enter Statement Charges . Ledger: debit 1100 Accounts Receivable, credit the income account of each item (for example 4100 Finance Charge Income for LATE-FEE Late Payment Fee, 4020 Delivery Income for DEL-FEE Delivery Fee), and credit Output Tax for any VAT. Stock: statement charges are meant for services and other charges. A stocked item on one would leave stock like on an invoice. Balances: the customer's balance goes up. The charge appears on the next statement and can be paid in Receive Payments. Finance Charge Made on Assess Finance Charges , one for each customer you select. Ledger: debit 1100 Accounts Receivable, credit 4100 Finance Charge Income. No VAT. Stock: none. Balances: the customer's balance goes up. The charge is due on the assessment date. Customer Payment Entered on Receive Payments , or as a payment at the counter on the POS Register . Account Debit Credit Deposit to account (default 1050 Undeposited Funds) Amount received 4060 Sales Discounts Early-payment discount 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax (or the tax's own account) Income tax withheld by the customer (1% / 2%) 1315 Creditable VAT Withheld (or the tax's own account) VAT withheld by the customer (5%) 1100 Accounts Receivable Amount received plus discount plus withholding Stock: none. Balances: the customer's balance goes down by the amount received plus the discount and withholding. The invoices the payment is applied to become Partially paid or Paid . An amount received but not applied stays on the payment as an unapplied credit. Taxes withheld: each type ticked in the Withholding box is kept with its base, rate and ATC; the 1% / 2% and the 5% go to different accounts, as the BIR requires (an income-tax credit, and a VAT credit for 2550Q Item 16). A payment saved before the types were kept posts its withholding to 1310. Applying credits: using an existing credit memo or unapplied payment on the same screen posts nothing new; it only records which invoice the credit pays. At the POS: a payment taken at the counter debits the terminal's cash account for cash, or the clearing account of the payment method, and is applied to the customer's oldest open invoices first. Example ABC Trading Corp. pays the ₱44,788.80 invoice by check and withholds 1% of the VAT-exclusive amount, ₱399.90. You enter Amount received ₱44,388.90, and on the invoice line Withholding ₱399.90 and Payment ₱44,388.90. The payment debits 1050 Undeposited Funds ₱44,388.90 and 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax ₱399.90, and credits 1100 Accounts Receivable ₱44,788.80. The invoice is paid in full. Credit Memo Entered on Create Credit Memos/Refunds . Account Debit Credit 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances Line amounts 2100 Output Tax VAT of the lines 1100 Accounts Receivable Credit memo total 1200 Inventory Average cost of goods returned to stock 5000 Cost of Goods Sold Average cost of goods returned to stock Stock: only when Return goods to stock is ticked: stocked items come back into the Return to site (or the inventory site of the credit memo) at the item's current average cost. Without the tick, only the first three lines are posted. Balances: the customer's balance goes down. What happens to the credit depends on the choice under What to do with this credit : keep it as an available credit, apply it to an invoice now, or give a refund. Customer Refund Recorded with the Refund button of a credit memo or of a payment that has an unapplied credit, on Create Credit Memos/Refunds . Ledger: debit 1100 Accounts Receivable, credit the Pay from account (a bank or cash account). Stock: none. Balances: the customer's balance goes back up by the refund, which uses up the credit. Rules: the refund cannot be more than the available credit. A refund cannot be edited: void it and record a new one. A refund above your amount limit needs supervisor approval.

Purchase Order Entered on Create Purchase Orders . Ledger: nothing. It is a non-posting document. Stock: nothing moves. The quantities not yet received count as on purchase order in the stock status reports. Balances: no effect on the vendor's balance. Status: Open , Partially filled as items are received, Closed when every line is received or closed. Item Receipt Entered on Receive Items , when goods arrive before the vendor's bill. Ledger: debit 1200 Inventory (the item's asset account) for stocked items, or the item's expense account for other items, and credit 2000 Accounts Payable. An item receipt carries no VAT. Stock: stocked items come into the receiving site at the cost on the receipt, and the average cost is worked out again. Balances: the vendor's balance goes up at once: open item receipts are part of Accounts Payable and of the A/P aging. Editing: an item receipt not billed yet can be edited; it is posted again (stock, Inventory and Accounts Payable) and the purchase order follows the new quantities received. Later: Enter Bill for Received Items turns the same record into a bill with a new BILL- number. The quantities stay as received; the cost and the VAT can change, and inventory value and the payable are adjusted to the billed cost. Bill Entered on Enter Bills , Receive Items and Enter Bills or Enter Bill for Received Items . Receipt Management , the Fixed Asset Register and Asset Maintenance can also create bills. Account Debit Credit Account of each line on the Expenses tab Line amount 1200 Inventory, for stocked items on the Items tab Line amount Expense account of other items (else their cost account, else 6110) Line amount 1300 Input Tax VAT of the lines 2000 Accounts Payable Bill total Stock: stocked items come into the site of the line (or the Default site for items ) at the bill's cost, and the item's average cost is worked out again. Balances: the vendor's balance goes up. The bill stays open until it is paid in Pay Bills or a debit memo is applied to it. Billable costs: a line marked billable to a Customer:Job is offered on that customer's next invoice. Example TechDistributors Inc. bills 5 MOU-001 Wireless Mouse at ₱350.00. The bill debits 1200 Inventory ₱1,750.00 and 1300 Input Tax ₱210.00, and credits 2000 Accounts Payable ₱1,960.00. Five mice come into stock, and the vendor's balance goes up by ₱1,960.00. Supplier Debit Memo Entered on Supplier Debit Memos , for goods returned to a supplier, price or billing corrections and allowances. Ledger: debit 2000 Accounts Payable for the total; credit the account of each expense line, 1200 Inventory for stocked items returned, and 1300 Input Tax for the VAT. Stock: stocked items leave the site of the line at the amount on the debit memo. Balances: the vendor's balance goes down. The available amount is applied to the supplier's bills on the debit memo's own page or under Credits in Pay Bills; applying it posts nothing further. Bill Payment Made on Pay Bills . One bill payment is recorded for each vendor. Account Debit Credit 2000 Accounts Payable Payment plus discount plus taxes withheld Payment account (bank or credit card, default 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking) Payment 5050 Purchase Discounts Discount taken 2110 Withholding Tax Payable (or the tax's own account) Income tax withheld (1% / 2%) 2115 VAT Withheld Payable (or the tax's own account) VAT withheld (5%) Stock: none. Balances: the vendor's balance goes down, and the bills paid become Partially paid or Paid . Supplier credits used on the same screen only link the credit to the bill. Rules: a bill payment can be edited (date, account, check number, the bills it pays, the amounts and the taxes withheld); the vendor stays the same. A payment above your amount limit needs supervisor approval. Taxes withheld: each type ticked in the Withholding column is kept with the bill, its base (net of VAT), rate and ATC, for BIR Form 2307 and the BIR Reports . Advance applied: when Use advance is used, the advance is applied as a bill payment of its own (AAP-00001 ...): debit 2000 Accounts Payable, credit 1410 Advances to Suppliers. Example a ₱112,000.00 bill (₱100,000.00 plus VAT) paid less 1% and 5% withheld: debit 2000 Accounts Payable ₱112,000.00; credit 1010 Cash in Bank ₱106,000.00, 2110 Withholding Tax Payable ₱1,000.00 and 2115 VAT Withheld Payable ₱5,000.00. Advance to Supplier Entered on Advances to Suppliers . Account Debit Credit Advance account (default 1410 Advances to Suppliers) Amount paid Paid from (bank or credit card) Amount paid Balances: not part of Accounts Payable: the vendor's balance and the A/P aging do not change until the advance is applied to a bill in Pay Bills. Rules: it can be edited, but not below what was applied; it is voided only after its applications are voided. Check Entered on Write Checks or as a quick entry in Use Register . Receipt Management , the Fixed Asset Register and Asset Maintenance can also write checks. Ledger: debit the lines exactly as on a bill (expense accounts, 1200 Inventory for stocked items, the expense account of other items) and 1300 Input Tax; credit the Bank / credit card account the check is drawn on. A "check" drawn on 2050 Company Credit Card records a card charge. Stock: stocked items on the Items tab come into stock like on a bill. Balances: a check does not go through Accounts Payable, so the vendor's balance does not change. Pay open bills with Pay Bills instead. Rules: a check above your amount limit needs supervisor approval. Lines to accounts marked With SL need a name, or a payee on the check. Cash Voucher Entered on Cash Voucher , for petty cash, revolving fund and other cash payments. Asset Maintenance can also make one. Ledger: the account lines exactly as entered (debit or credit), plus one credit to the Cash account (for example 1005 Petty Cash Fund) for the cash amount. The debits less the credits of the lines must equal the cash amount. Stock: none. Balances: a line to 1100 Accounts Receivable must name a customer and changes that customer's balance; a line to 2000 Accounts Payable must name a supplier and changes that supplier's balance.

Deposit Entered on Make Deposits or as a quick entry in Use Register . Account Debit Credit Deposit to bank account Total less cash back Cash back goes to account Cash back amount 1050 Undeposited Funds Each payment and sales receipt deposited Terminal cash account (1001) Cash of each POS shift deposited Clearing account (1060, 1065, 1070) Card or e-wallet settlement 6080 Bank and Merchant Charges Merchant fee deducted Account of each other receipt Amount of the receipt Stock: none. Balances: no effect on customer balances: the payments deposited already lowered them. POS cash: the amount of a closed POS shift is the counted cash, less the opening float (which stays in the drawer), plus the cash drops. When the shift's closing entries are corrected later, the deposit's line for the shift follows. Later: a deposit can be edited (payments and shifts taken off or added, other receipts, date, account); it is posted again. Transfer Entered on Transfer Funds or as a quick entry in Use Register . Ledger: debit the Transfer funds to account, credit the Transfer funds from account. It does not touch income or expenses. Stock and balances: none. Service Charge and Interest Earned Recorded by Reconcile when you finish a reconciliation with a Service charge or Interest earned amount. Service Charge: debit the account chosen beside it (default 6080 Bank and Merchant Charges), credit the bank account. Interest Earned: debit the bank account, credit the account chosen beside it (default 4200 Interest Income). Both are dated on the dates you enter beside them, take their numbers from the JE- series, and are marked cleared in the reconciliation straight away. A reconciliation saved for later keeps the two amounts but posts nothing. Undo last voids the two entries and keeps their amounts on the reopened reconciliation, so they are posted once more when it is finished.

Journal Entry Entered on Make Journal Entries . Ledger: every line exactly as entered, debit or credit. The debits must equal the credits, and an entry needs at least two lines. Names: a line to 1100 Accounts Receivable needs a customer and changes that customer's balance; a line to 2000 Accounts Payable needs a vendor and changes that vendor's balance; a line to an account marked With SL needs a customer, supplier, employee or other name. Stock: none. A journal entry to 1200 Inventory changes the ledger but not the quantities or values of items, so the inventory valuation reports will no longer agree with the ledger. Use Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand for stock. Opening Balance Entered on Make Journal Entries with Opening balance entry ticked. It posts like a journal entry and is listed with the journal entries. The Fixed Asset Register also makes one when a new asset is saved with Record the purchase set to Existing asset (opening balance) : debit the category's asset account for the cost, credit 3900 Opening Balance Equity for the cost less the opening accumulated depreciation, and credit the accumulated depreciation account for the opening accumulated depreciation. Import from CSV does the same for imported fixed assets. Opening stock is not an opening balance entry: it is an inventory adjustment against 3900 Opening Balance Equity (see below). Tip For customers' and vendors' opening balances, enter one line per customer to 1100 Accounts Receivable (or per vendor to 2000 Accounts Payable) with the name on the line, balanced against 3900 Opening Balance Equity. The names are required on those lines.

Inventory Adjustment Entered on Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand . Physical Inventory Count posts its differences as an inventory adjustment, and the Item List posts one when a new stocked item is saved with a Quantity on hand . Quantity added: debit 1200 Inventory, credit the Adjustment account (default 5100 Inventory Adjustments and Shrinkage), at the item's average cost. Quantity removed: debit the adjustment account, credit 1200 Inventory, at the item's average cost. Value changed (Total value): debit or credit 1200 Inventory against the adjustment account for the difference, with no change in quantity. Only users who may view costs can adjust values. Opening quantity from the Item List: debit 1200 Inventory for the Total value entered, credit 3900 Opening Balance Equity. Stock: the quantity changes at the site of the adjustment, and the average cost is worked out again. Editing: an adjustment can be edited; it is taken off the books, worked out again against the stock without it, and posted again under the same number. Inventory Transfer Entered on Transfer Inventory . Ledger: nothing, because both sites use the same inventory account. The page confirms Quantities moved without changing total inventory value. Stock: the quantity leaves the from site at the item's average cost and arrives at the to site with the same value. Editing: a transfer can be edited (date, sites, lines); the stock moves again. Build Assembly Entered on Build Assemblies . Account Debit Credit 1200 Inventory, assembly item Total cost of the components 1200 Inventory, stocked components Average cost of each component Expense account of non-stock components Quantity times the item's cost Stock: the components leave the build site and the assembly comes in at their total cost. Example: building one SET-OFFICE Office Monitor Set takes one each of MON-024, KEY-001, MOU-001 and CAB-HDMI out of stock at average cost, and credits 5200 Direct Labor Absorbed ₱150.00 for LAB-ASM Assembly Labor (per set). Pending: a build saved with Save as pending build posts nothing until Complete build . Editing: a build can be edited (assembly, site, quantity, date); a completed build is posted again, a pending one stays pending unless it is completed on the same save. Processing Order Entered on Disassemble / Process Items , for disassembly, de-kitting and co-product processing. Account Debit Credit Asset account of each input item Average cost of the inputs Expense account of non-stock inputs Quantity times the item's cost Account of each additional cost line (for example 5200) Amount of the cost Asset account of each output item Cost allocated to the output Processing variance account (default 5100) Difference, if any Difference, if any Stock: the inputs leave the processing site and the outputs come in at their allocated cost. Variance: only the valuation methods (current average cost, manual amounts) leave a difference between the total cost and the value of the outputs. Pending: an order saved with Save as pending posts nothing until Complete and post .

Depreciation Posted by Run Depreciation , dated the last day of the month. Ledger: for each asset category and class, debit the category's depreciation expense account (6090 Depreciation Expense in the demo) and credit its accumulated depreciation account (for example 1555 Accumulated Depreciation - Computer and POS). Assets: the month is marked as run for each asset. An asset whose net book value reaches its salvage value becomes fully depreciated. Undoing: voiding or deleting the entry frees the month, so it can be run again. Asset Disposal Posted by Dispose of Assets . Account Debit Credit Accumulated depreciation account All depreciation to date Asset account Cost of the asset Received into account (default 1050) Proceeds received 4300 Gain (Loss) on Disposal of Assets Loss Gain Assets: the asset is marked disposed. When asked, the page first runs the missing months of depreciation up to the disposal date. Undoing: voiding or deleting the disposal makes the asset active again. Asset purchases and maintenance A new asset in the Fixed Asset Register is recorded as a check ( Paid now (Write Checks) ), a bill ( On account (Enter Bills) ) or an opening balance, each debiting the category's asset account; or nothing, with Already recorded elsewhere . A record in Asset Maintenance is paid through a bill, a check or a cash voucher that debits the Parts charged to and Labor charged to accounts (proposed: the account whose name contains "Repair", 6030 Repairs and Maintenance in the demo) and, with VAT, 1300 Input Tax.

POS Sale Completed on the POS Register . Account Debit Credit Account of each tender Amount paid with it Income account of each item Line amount 2100 Output Tax VAT of the lines 5000 Cost of Goods Sold Average cost of stocked items 1200 Inventory Average cost of stocked items Tenders: cash is debited to the terminal's cash account (1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers for both demo counters). Other payment methods debit their own clearing account: in the demo, Credit/Debit Card to 1060 Card Clearing, GCash and Maya to 1065 E-wallet Clearing, Gift Voucher to 2120 Gift Vouchers Outstanding, P.O. Card to 1070 P.O. Card Clearing and Bank to 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking. Stock: stocked items leave the site of the terminal at average cost. Balances: no effect on customer balances, even when a customer is named on the sale. Suspended sales ( Suspend ) post nothing until they are recalled and completed. A sale completed with Charge to account is saved as an invoice instead (see Invoice), and a payment at the counter as a customer payment. POS Return Processed on POS Receipts, Returns & Voids , always with supervisor approval. Ledger: debit 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances and 2100 Output Tax; credit the account of the refund method (cash: the terminal's cash account). Stock: when Goods can be resold (back to store stock) is ticked, the items come back into the store's site; when it is not, they go to the damaged-goods site. Either way they come back at the current average cost: debit 1200 Inventory, credit 5000 Cost of Goods Sold. If no damaged-goods site exists, items that cannot be resold do not come back into stock. Cash Over/Short Posted by Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings when a register is closed and the cash counted differs from the expected cash. Short: debit 6200 Cash Over and Short, credit the terminal's cash account. Over: debit the terminal's cash account, credit 6200 Cash Over and Short. Example: Makati Counter 1 is ₱50.00 short: 6200 Cash Over and Short is debited and 1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers credited ₱50.00.

Both are done from the view of a saved transaction with the Void and Delete buttons. Both need the Delete/Void right on the page, a reason ( Reason (required, recorded in the audit trail) ), and a date after the closing date. What happens Void Delete The document Stays, marked VOID with the reason, date and user Is removed Ledger and stock Everything it posted is taken out Everything it posted is taken out Its number Stays in use Is not given out again Available for Posting transactions only All, except POS sales, returns and over/short Audit trail Full copy with the reason Full copy with the reason A voided transaction cannot be edited or voided again. It still appears in lists and reports as void, and in Voided and Deleted Transactions Detail . Estimates, sales orders and purchase orders cannot be voided (they post nothing); delete them, or use Close to stop expecting the rest. Voiding or deleting is refused while: payments or credits are applied to the invoice, statement charge, finance charge or bill (remove them first by editing the payment or credit); the payment or sales receipt is included in a deposit (void the deposit first); the credit memo or payment has been refunded (void the refund first); the estimate, sales order or purchase order has been converted or received in part (close it instead). Voiding or deleting a payment or credit releases the invoices it paid, which become open again. Voiding or deleting a check, bill payment or customer refund above your amount limit, and voiding any POS sale or return, needs supervisor approval. A transaction cleared in a bank reconciliation can be changed, voided or deleted only by a user with the closed-period permission. The change is listed on the Reconciliation Discrepancy report. Note Item receipts, inventory adjustments, inventory transfers, builds and finance charges cannot be changed after they are saved, so they have no Edit button. To correct one, void it and enter it again. Deposits and bill payments can be edited.

Some transactions can be saved first and posted later. While they wait they are pending : they post nothing to the ledger and move no stock. Transaction How to save as pending How to post it Invoice, sales receipt Tick Pending (non-posting until marked final) Mark as final , then save Build assembly Save as pending build Complete build Processing order Save as pending Complete and post POS sale Suspend Recall , then Complete sale A pending invoice is not part of the customer's balance or the A/R aging, is not offered in Receive Payments, and is not checked against the credit limit until it is marked final. A pending sales receipt is not offered in Make Deposits. The view of a pending invoice or sales receipt says This transaction is pending. It does not affect the books or inventory until it is marked final. Pending invoices and sales receipts are listed on the Pending Sales report and counted on the Home dashboard; pending builds on the Pending Builds reports; pending processing orders on the Processing & Disassembly Register. A pending build or processing order can be saved even when the components or inputs are short; completing it checks the stock again. Pending documents take their number when they are first saved.

The closing date protects the periods you have finished. It is set in Company, Security & Closing Date in the box Books closed through (blank = open) . Once a closing date is set, a user without the special permission Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled cannot: save a transaction dated on or before the closing date; edit, void or delete a transaction dated on or before it, or move it to a later date; import transactions or opening stock dated on or before it. The messages are The books are closed through 07/08/2026. You do not have permission to record transactions dated on or before the closing date. and This transaction is dated on or before the closing date (07/08/2026) and cannot be changed. Administrators, the Company Owner and the Super Admin always have the permission; of the installed roles, no other role has it. A memorized transaction set to be entered automatically on a date in the closed period stops, and is set back to Remind me when it is due . The same permission is needed to change a transaction cleared in a bank reconciliation, whatever its date. Tip After each month-end close, make a backup, check the reports, and then move the closing date to the last day of that month.

A class is your own way of splitting the books (branches, departments, projects). The classes are kept in the Class List . Every transaction form has a Class box. The class is copied to every ledger line the transaction posts, so every financial report can be filtered by class and the "by Class" statements show one column per class. On journal entries and cash vouchers a line can have its own class; a line without one takes the class at the top. When you save a transaction without a class, a window No class selected warns that it will be saved as Unclassified . Choose Choose a class to go back, or Continue saving . The window does not appear while the Class List is empty. On the POS Register a sale starts with the user's default class (set in Company, Security & Closing Date) or else the terminal's default class, and the class is kept for the next sale. Run Depreciation posts each asset under its own default class when no class is chosen on the run. A class already used on transactions cannot be deleted; make it inactive instead. Reports list entries without a class as (Unclassified) .

t: Appendix B. Default roles and what they can do
x: A new installation starts with nine roles, and a company created on the platform copies the roles of the company it is copied from. Administrators can change their page access in Page Access Configuration and their rights and special permissions in User Role Configuration , but the installed roles cannot be deleted. Effective Access (View as User) shows what one user can really do and why.

Open: the user can open the page and see its records (the page is allowed for the role). Create , Edit , Delete/Void , Print/Export , Approve: what the user can do on a page they can open. Approve lets the user approve other users' actions that need supervisor approval, and their own. A user with several roles gets everything any of the roles gives. A user override set for one user and one page always wins over the roles.

Role What it is for Demo user Administrator Everything in every module, including user accounts, roles, page access, the closing date and the audit trail admin (System Administrator) Accountant Financial Set-up & Reports, Fixed Assets, Banking and reconciliation, all module reports and the financial statements accountant (Ana Cruz) A/R Clerk Customers module transactions and the Customer and Receivables reports arclerk (Ben Garcia) A/P Clerk Vendors module transactions, Pay Bills and the Vendors and Payables reports apclerk (Carla Lim) Inventory Clerk Items, sites, receiving, adjustments, builds, processing, stock counts and quantity reports invclerk (Dan Villanueva) Sales Representative Estimates, sales orders, invoices and the Sales reports salesrep (Maria Santos) Cashier POS sales, returns and cash drops at the assigned terminal only cashier1 (Ella Ramos) POS Supervisor Everything a cashier can do, plus approvals and X- and Z-readings supervisor (Fred Tan) Auditor View-only access to all transactions, reports and the audit trail auditor (Grace Uy) In the demo company the admin user logs in with the password Admin@12345 (and must change it at once) and the other demo users with Demo@12345. Change these passwords, or deactivate the users you do not need, before real use.

Note A few pages open on a new entry when you click them in the menu: Receive Payments, Pay Bills, Make Deposits, Transfer Funds and Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand. A user who may only view them (the Accountant, the Auditor) sees Access denied there. Open those transactions from the Customer Center, the Vendor Center, a report or Find instead.

Special permissions are set per role in User Role Configuration . The labels are the ones shown there. Special permission What it allows View costs and margins See item costs, average costs, cost of goods sold and margins in reports, the Inventory Center, the Item List, the price pages and processing orders; adjust inventory values; see the ledger entries of sales documents View bank balances outside Banking See bank balances on the Home dashboard, in the Chart of Accounts, on Transfer Funds and in the bank-balance columns of reports Max discount % without approval The largest discount a user may give on a line (or with a percentage discount item) on estimates, sales orders, invoices, sales receipts and at the POS Max price change % without approval How far a line's price may differ from the item's standard or price-level price on the same documents Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval The largest check, cash voucher, bill payment, customer refund, inventory adjustment, count difference or processing order a user may save alone, and the largest check, bill payment or refund they may void or delete Can exceed customer credit limits Save an invoice (with a reason) or a POS charge sale that takes a customer over the credit limit Can change the Chart of Accounts and default accounts Add, change and delete accounts, and change Module Default Accounts (with Edit on that page) Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled Work in the closed period and change transactions cleared in a bank reconciliation Can design report layouts (fonts, headings and footers, columns and rows) and save or share them Use the Modify Report button on reports, save and share layouts, and choose the layout a report opens with How the values work: A Yes/No permission is granted when any of the user's roles grants it. A limit is the highest value among the user's roles. A blank limit in any role means no limit. A limit that none of the user's roles sets counts as 0: every discount, price change or amount then needs approval. Going over a limit does not stop the user: the form asks for Supervisor approval , and a user who has Approve on that page types their username and password. A user who has Approve on the page approves their own action. Nobody can approve with their own password otherwise ( You cannot approve your own transaction. ). Of the installed roles only the Administrator and the POS Supervisor (on the POS pages) have Approve . Approvals for the clerks therefore come from an Administrator, unless you give Approve to another role. Administrators, the Company Owner and the Super Admin have every special permission with no limits. The values each role is installed with: Role Granted Limits Accountant View costs, View bank balances, Chart of Accounts changes, Design report layouts Amount: no limit; discount 0%; price change 0% A/R Clerk None Amount ₱50,000.00; discount 10%; price change 5% A/P Clerk View costs Amount ₱100,000.00 Inventory Clerk None Amount ₱20,000.00 Sales Representative None Discount 5%; price change 0% Cashier None Discount 5%; price change 0%; amount 0 POS Supervisor None Discount 30%; price change 20%; amount ₱20,000.00 Auditor View costs, View bank balances None set

When a user (or a role) would be able to create or edit on both pages of one of these pairs, User Accounts and User Role Configuration show a segregation-of-duties warning, and you must tick a box to save anyway: Vendor Center and Pay Bills (creating vendors and paying bills); Receive Payments and Reconcile (receiving customer payments and reconciling the bank account); Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand and Physical Inventory Count (adjusting inventory and counting it); Enter Bills and Write Checks (entering bills and writing checks); POS Register and Make Deposits (selling at the POS and depositing the cash).

A role can cover all sites or only the sites ticked for it, and a user can be limited to certain sites and POS terminals in User Accounts . When both are set, the user works only in the sites that both allow. Users limited to sites see only those sites in lists, site pickers and site-based reports, and saving a transaction for another site is refused.

t: Appendix C. Number series and document numbers
x: Every transaction and a few records get a number from a series : a prefix, then a running number filled with zeros. Each company has its own series.

Series First number Used by EST- EST-00001 Estimates SO- SO-00001 Sales orders INV- INV-00001 Invoices, including batch invoices and POS charge sales SR- SR-00001 Sales receipts SC- SC-00001 Statement charges FC- FC-00001 Finance charges PMT- PMT-00001 Customer payments CM- CM-00001 Credit memos PO- PO-00001 Purchase orders IR- IR-00001 Item receipts BILL- BILL-00001 Bills DM- DM-00001 Supplier debit memos ADV- ADV-00001 Advances to suppliers AAP- AAP-00001 Advances applied to bills (bill payments made out of an advance) (none) 1001 Checks, bill payments and customer refunds CAV- CAV-00001 Cash vouchers DEP- DEP-00001 Deposits TRF- TRF-00001 Fund transfers JE- JE-00001 Journal entries, opening balances, depreciation, asset disposals, cash over/short, service charges, interest earned ADJ- ADJ-00001 Inventory adjustments, physical counts, opening stock IT- IT-00001 Inventory transfers BLD- BLD-00001 Assembly builds PRC- PRC-00001 Processing orders POS- POS-000001 POS sales and returns FA- FA-00001 Fixed asset numbers MNT- MNT-00001 Asset maintenance records

A number is taken when the transaction is first saved, never when the form is opened. The form shows the next number as a hint, for example INV-00024 (auto) in the Number box. If saving fails (a message in red), no number is used up. The counter only goes forward. A voided transaction keeps its number; a deleted one leaves a gap, and the number is not given out again. A suspended POS sale removed with Cancel suspended sale is deleted, so it also leaves a gap in the POS- series. Because checks, bill payments and customer refunds share one series, a bill payment made by bank transfer or card also takes the next check number. Changing a transaction's date does not change its number. When an item receipt is turned into a bill with Enter Bill for Received Items , the record gets the next BILL- number in place of its IR- number. A new company created on the platform starts every series again from 1.

On these forms you can type a number instead of taking the automatic one, both when entering and when editing: Number on estimates, sales orders, invoices, sales receipts, statement charges, credit memos, purchase orders, bills and supplier debit memos; Check no. on Write Checks; Entry no. on Make Journal Entries; CAV entry no. on Cash Voucher. Leave the box blank to get the next number. A number you type does not move the counter. Important Only the cash voucher checks that a typed number is not used already ( CAV entry no. ... is already used. Leave the number blank to get the next one. ). On the other forms the program accepts a number that is already in use, and a typed number that is ahead of the counter will be given out again later. Type your own numbers only when you must match a pre-printed form, and check the list first. All other transactions (payments, bill payments, deposits, transfers, item receipts, adjustments, transfers of stock, builds, processing orders, POS transactions and the entries the program makes) are always numbered automatically.

t: POS receipt numbers and Z-reading numbers
x: Every POS terminal has its own receipt series: the Receipt prefix set in POS Terminals followed by an 8-digit number, for example MK1-00000001 for Makati Counter 1 and CB1-00000001 for Cebu Counter 1. New terminals are offered the prefix OR-. Sales, returns, charge sales and payments taken at the counter each take the next receipt number of the terminal, in addition to their own transaction number. Z-readings are numbered per terminal (#1, #2 ...) when the register is closed. The prefix can be changed on the POS Terminals page. The running number cannot be reset there ( Receipt numbers are sequential per terminal and cannot be reset here. ).

Not from within the program. There is no page for the prefixes or the next numbers of the series; they are kept in the sequences table of the company database. A system administrator with access to the database (phpMyAdmin or Navicat) can change a prefix or the next number there, for example to start at the next number of your pre-printed invoices. Important Make a backup before changing the table, and never set a next number at or below a number already used: the program would give out duplicate numbers.

Company Code: with several companies, each company has a code such as ABD-7K2QX (see Appendix F ). It is not a document number and cannot be chosen; the Company Owner or the Super Admin can only regenerate it. Codes you choose yourself: account codes, item codes, customer and vendor names, site codes and terminal codes are typed by you and must be unique.

t: Appendix D. Messages and what to do
x: Messages appear in three places: in a red box at the top of the form you were saving (nothing was saved, and what you typed is still on the form), in a coloured bar at the top of the next page, and on the log-in page. The table lists the messages you are most likely to meet first. Where a message contains a name, number or amount, it is shown here with an example or with "...". Message or problem Why What to do Invalid username or password. 3 attempt(s) left before the account is locked. The username or the password is wrong Check Caps Lock and type again. t: Appendix E. For the system administrator
x: This appendix is for the person who installs and looks after the program. It needs access to the server, the database and the program folder.

Component Requirement PHP 8.1 or newer (8.2 or newer recommended), with the pdo_mysql and mbstring extensions Database MySQL 5.5.3 or newer, or MariaDB 5.5 or newer Web server Apache (the .htaccess files are included) or nginx Browser Any current browser Internet Only to load Bootstrap from a CDN; see Offline use PHP and MySQL versions are separate: old XAMPP packages with MySQL 5.5 come with PHP 5, which cannot run this program. Install a current XAMPP, or point a PHP 8 installation at your MySQL 5.5 server.

With XAMPP and phpMyAdmin: Unzip the folder into C:\xampp\htdocs\ , so that you have C:\xampp\htdocs\gsmart-construction\index.php . Start Apache and MySQL in the XAMPP Control Panel. Open phpMyAdmin at http://localhost/phpmyadmin and choose Import . Choose database/gsmart_construction_clean.sql to start real work (the set-up lists and the user accounts, no client, project or transaction), or database/gsmart_construction_sample.sql for the sample contractor with four projects and a year of work. Click Go . Either file creates the company database gsmart_construction and the platform database gsmart_construction_master . If your MySQL user has a password, or you used another database name, edit config/config.php . Open http://localhost/gsmart-construction/ and log in as admin with the password Admin@12345 (the other accounts are listed in README.md; the Super Admin is superadmin with Super@12345). From the command line, php tools/install.php does the same (see Command-line tools).

Setting What it holds db: host, port, name, user, pass, charset The database connection (utf8mb4) app: name The program name shown on screen; left as "Accounting System", the program shows GSMaRT Construction System app: timezone The company time zone, Asia/Manila by default app: currency The currency sign, ₱ app: debug Detailed error pages, switched on only by the environment variable APP_DEBUG=1 app: upload_dir Where uploaded receipts are kept (storage/receipts) master: name (optional) Another name for the platform database when several companies are set up The environment variables DB_HOST , DB_PORT , DB_NAME , DB_USER and DB_PASS override the values in the file. Important config/config.php holds the database user and password. Never send it to anyone, never attach it to a support e-mail or a screenshot, and never place a copy where the web server can serve it. The .htaccess files (or the nginx rules) stop browsers from opening the config, app, database, modules, storage, tools and views folders; keep them in place. Settings that users change inside the program (company details, password rules, lockout, session timeout, finance charges, negative stock, the closing date) are in Company, Security & Closing Date , not in this file.

Make a backup of the database ( Backup & Restore , phpMyAdmin Export, or tools/export_sql.php ), and a copy of the program folder including storage/ and config/config.php . Copy the new program files over the old ones. Keep your config/config.php . In phpMyAdmin (Import) or Navicat (Execute SQL File), select your company database and run the files in database/migrations/ that you have not run yet, oldest first. Log in. If a file is still missing, the program stops after log-in with the page Database update needed , which names the files still to run, in order. GSMaRT Construction System 1.0 is delivered with the complete database and needs no upgrade file. Later versions put theirs in database/migrations/ , each written for MySQL 5.5, keeping every record and safe to run twice. Important Never import database/gsmart_construction_sample.sql or database/gsmart_construction_clean.sql over a database that is in use. Both drop and recreate every table: all your records would be replaced by the sample data. Upgrade only with the files in database/migrations/ . With several companies, every company database needs the update. The Super Admin runs them with Companies > Database updates on the platform pages, or you run php tools/platform.php update-all . After upgrading from a version with the older average costing, you may run Rebuild data once in Utilities: Verify & Rebuild Data to recost past sales. It is optional: new transactions use the current costing at once. Make a backup first, because the cost of past sales may change.

Run them from the program folder, for example php tools/install.php . They refuse to run from a browser. Command What it does php tools/install.php Creates the database (if missing), the tables, the audit trail protection triggers and the setup data. Stops if the database already has tables php tools/install.php --demo The same, plus sample transactions dated around the day you run it php tools/install.php --drop Drops and recreates the database first: deletes all data php tools/export_sql.php --out=backup-2026-09-30.sql Writes one complete, importable SQL file (tables, data and triggers) php tools/send_scheduled_reports.php E-mails the memorized reports that have a schedule; add --company=N for one company php tools/platform.php list Lists the companies, their status, database and Company Code php tools/platform.php reset-superadmin (username) (password) Gives a Super Admin a new password, unlocks the account and asks for a new password at log-in php tools/platform.php sync (company id) Rebuilds the platform's list of that company's usernames php tools/platform.php update-all Runs the pending upgrade files on every company database tools/seed.php (the chart of accounts, roles, users, lists and number series of a new installation), tools/demo_data.php (the sample transactions) and tools/lib.php are used by install.php and are not run on their own. export_sql.php without --out writes to database/gsmart_construction.sql : give --out to choose the file. With several companies it also exports the platform database; --no-master leaves it out. Add --no-create-db to leave out the CREATE DATABASE and USE lines. It exports the database named in config/config.php (Company 1). platform.php works only after multi-company has been set up. Scheduled report e-mails send_scheduled_reports.php sends every memorized report that has a daily, weekly or monthly schedule and an e-mail address, as a CSV attachment. Each report runs with the access of the user who memorized it; a report that user can no longer open is skipped. It uses PHP's mail() , so configure SMTP in php.ini (XAMPP: sendmail.ini ). With several companies, one run sends the reports of every active company. Run it once a day: Linux (cron): 0 6 * * * php /path/to/gsmart-construction/tools/send_scheduled_reports.php Windows (Task Scheduler): create a daily task with the program C:\xampp\php\php.exe and the argument C:\xampp\htdocs\gsmart-construction\tools\send_scheduled_reports.php .

Everything users upload and every backup made inside the program is kept under storage/ , which the web server must be able to write to and which browsers cannot open directly. Folder What it holds storage/backups Backups made on Backup & Restore (.sql or .sql.gz), the safety backups made before each restore (before_restore_...) and uploaded backup files (uploaded_...) storage/receipts Receipts uploaded in Receipt Management storage/receipts/inbox E-mailed receipts waiting to be imported storage/company The company logo storage/maintenance Pictures of parts attached to maintenance records storage/imports CSV files that passed Check the file on Import from CSV, kept for a day so they can be imported storage/platform multi_company.json, the switch that turns multi-company on storage/companies/c002, c003 ... The same folders for every company after the first With several companies, Company 1 keeps the folders above and each other company has its own folder, named after its number (c002 for company 2). Include the whole storage/ folder in your file backups. Note Moving storage/platform/multi_company.json away switches multi-company off in an emergency: the program then runs as Company 1 alone. Put the file back to return.

Inside the program: Backup & Restore writes the whole company database to one file in storage/backups , lists and downloads the backups, and restores one. A restore always makes a fresh backup of the current data first, and asks you to type RESTORE. From the command line: php tools/export_sql.php --out=FILE . phpMyAdmin: Export. With several companies, back up the platform database ( accounting_system_master , or the name set in the config) together with the company databases. Whichever way you use, keep a copy away from the server.

The pages load Bootstrap 5.3.3 and Bootstrap Icons 1.11.3 from cdn.jsdelivr.net. To run without internet, download both and place these files, as listed in assets/vendor/README.txt : assets/vendor/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css assets/vendor/bootstrap/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js assets/vendor/bootstrap-icons/font/bootstrap-icons.min.css assets/vendor/bootstrap-icons/font/fonts/bootstrap-icons.woff2 assets/vendor/bootstrap-icons/font/fonts/bootstrap-icons.woff The program uses the local copies automatically when they are there.

Apache: the included .htaccess files block the program's internal folders and .sql and .md files. nginx: deny the folders app, config, database, modules, storage, tools and views, hidden files, and .sql and .md files, and pass .php files to PHP-FPM. The README has a sample configuration. Printing receipts to a Bluetooth roll printer needs the page to be opened on an https:// address or on http://localhost/ .

Import accounting_system_clean.sql , or run php tools/install.php without --demo . Change the admin password, and change or deactivate the demo users you do not need. Create a MySQL user just for this program (instead of root) and put it in config/config.php . Use HTTPS. The session cookie becomes secure automatically. Keep APP_DEBUG off. Enter the company details, password rules and session timeout in Company, Security & Closing Date . Check the Chart of Accounts and Module Default Accounts , the tax codes, terms, sites, POS terminals and payment methods. Review the roles, page access and special permissions (Appendix B), and give every user their own account. Enter the opening balances and opening stock, then set the closing date to the day before you start. Make a backup before each month-end close and keep a copy off the server. With several companies: keep the Super Admin's password safe (a second Super Admin is a good idea), check that each company has a Company Owner, and back up the platform database with the company databases.

Term Meaning in GSMaRT Construction System Accumulated depreciation The depreciation recorded so far on a fixed asset, kept in the asset category's accumulated depreciation account Approve (right) The right to approve, on a page, the actions of other users that need supervisor approval Assembly (Inventory assembly) A stocked item made from other items listed as its components; you make it with Build Assemblies Audit trail The permanent record of every change, void, deletion, log-in, denied page, approval and permission change; entries cannot be edited or deleted Average cost The book value of an item divided by its quantity on hand over all sites; stock leaves at this cost Billable cost An expense or item line on a bill or check marked for a Customer:Job, offered on that customer's next invoice Bill of materials The components of an assembly and the quantity of each needed for one unit Build point The quantity of an assembly at or below which more should be built By-product A secondary output of a processing order, valued at a fixed value per unit that is taken out of the cost first; the co-products share the rest Cash drop Cash taken out of a POS drawer during a shift and recorded on Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings Cash voucher A payment of cash from a petty cash, revolving fund or other cash account, printed as a voucher Class A label of your own (branch, department, project) put on a transaction and on every ledger line it posts, so reports can be split by it Clearing account An account that holds card or e-wallet sales until the provider pays them into the bank Closing date The date through which the books are closed; transactions on or before it cannot be recorded or changed without special permission Co-product A main product of a processing order; co-products share the cost left after by-products and scrap Company Code With several companies, the code (such as ABD-7K2QX) an employee types to join a company; it is never a password Company Owner With several companies, the user who manages a company's employees, join requests and Company Code, with full authority in that company Credit limit The largest balance a customer may owe; an invoice above it needs the permission to exceed limits and a reason Creditable withholding tax The part of a payment a customer withholds for the BIR, entered in Receive Payments and debited to 1310 Customer:Job A customer with a job under it, shown as "ABC Trading Corp.:Office Renovation Project"; a job's balance counts in its customer's Delete Removing a transaction; its full copy stays in the audit trail Effective access What one user can really open and do, with the reason, shown on Effective Access (View as User) Employees & Other Names The list of people and bodies that are neither customers nor suppliers, used as payees and on subsidiary ledgers Find The search for transactions in every module at once, by any combination of filters Fiscal year The accounting year; the month it starts is set in Company, Security & Closing Date Forecast Expected sales per customer for a year, compared with actual sales in Forecast vs Actual by Customer Group item An item that stands for several items; on a form it is entered as those items Input tax VAT paid on purchases, debited to 1300 Input Tax Item receipt A record of goods received before the vendor's bill; it is later turned into a bill Job A project or sub-account of a customer (see Customer:Job) Layout A saved design of a report (columns, headings, fonts, footer, page); it can be shared and made the default Memorized report A report saved with its filters, which can be sent by e-mail on a schedule Memorized transaction A transaction saved as a model, entered again automatically or after a reminder on a schedule Module default accounts The accounts each module posts to when an item, tax code or form does not name one Negative stock A quantity on hand below zero, allowed only while the setting "Allow selling or moving stock below zero" is on, and listed on the Negative Inventory Listing Net book value The cost of a fixed asset less its accumulated depreciation Non-posting document An estimate, sales order or purchase order: it records a commitment and does not touch the ledger Opening Balance Equity The equity account (3900) that takes the other side of opening balances and opening stock Opening float The cash put in a POS drawer when a shift is opened Output tax VAT charged on sales, credited to 2100 Output Tax Page access Whether a role may open a page at all, set in Page Access Configuration Pending A saved invoice, sales receipt, build or processing order that does not post until it is marked final or completed Price level A named price list (such as Wholesale or VIP) given to a customer, as a percentage or as a price per item Processing order A transaction that turns input items into output items (disassembly, de-kitting, co-products) and shares the cost among the outputs Progress invoice An invoice for a percentage of an estimate Reconcile Matching an account's cleared items to the bank statement; cleared lines are protected afterwards Reorder point The quantity at or below which an item should be ordered again Role A set of page access, rights, special permissions and sites given to users Sales rep The person credited with a sale, used in the Sales by Rep reports Scrap Waste from a processing order, valued like a by-product at a fixed value per unit, often zero Segregation of duties Keeping apart duties that one person should not hold together; the program warns when roles combine them Shift A cashier's working period on a POS terminal, from opening float to Z-reading Site A place where stock is kept (warehouse, store, stockroom, van, damaged goods); quantities are kept per site Special permission A permission beyond page rights, such as viewing costs or a maximum discount, set per role Statement charge A charge added to a customer's account without an invoice, shown on the next statement Subsidiary ledger The entries of one name on the accounts marked With SL, shown by the Subsidiary Ledger report Super Admin With several companies, the platform administrator who manages every company and can open any of them Supervisor approval A second person's username and password, typed on the form, for an action above a user's limits Suspended sale A POS sale put aside to be recalled later; it posts nothing Tax code A VAT treatment on a line (VAT12, ZR zero-rated, EX VAT-exempt, NT non-taxable) with its rate and accounts Tender One way a POS customer pays (cash, card, e-wallet, voucher); a sale can have several Terminal A POS counter, with its site, cash account, receipt prefix and assigned users Terms The payment terms of a customer or vendor (such as Net 30 or 2% 10 Net 30), which set the due date and early-payment discount U/M set A set of units of measure for items, with a base unit in which stock and costs are kept (such as pc, dozen, box of 24) Unclassified A transaction or ledger line with no class Undeposited Funds The account (1050) that holds payments and sales receipts until Make Deposits moves them to the bank User override A page setting for one user that wins over all of that user's roles VAT-exclusive Prices and amounts on forms are before VAT; VAT is added on each line Void Cancelling a transaction while keeping it, marked VOID, with its effect on the ledger and stock removed With SL A mark on an account in the Chart of Accounts: every entry to it must name a customer, supplier, employee or other name X-reading A mid-shift summary of a POS terminal's sales and tenders; the register stays open Z-reading The closing reading of a POS shift, with the cash counted and the over or short; it is numbered per terminal
